zh.therapist_turn_zh: 如果我说的不对你纠正我，但生病会让你紧张吗？
zh.client_response_zh: 我是一个很容易焦虑的人。不知道为什么。
zh.internal_zh:
<internal>
[Perception] 她太简单化了，而且有点不靠谱。一开始她就误解了整个新冠/工作那件事，然后直接跳到“生病会让你焦虑？”就好像她在用一种很基础、几乎显而易见的方式总结我。这让我感觉她根本没认真听我在说什么，或者她只是试图显得很有洞察力，但其实根本没理解。当你已经因为生病、工作受影响、一切都乱成一团而压力很大时，那种问题感觉太表面了，没什么意义。

[Decision] 所以我用一种很直接、搪塞的方式回答：“大部分事情都会让我紧张。我是一个很容易焦虑的人。不知道为什么。”这样我就不用表现得好像她的问题很有帮助似的，其实并没有。保持笼统和敷衍比敞开心扉再冒被误解的风险更安全。如果她要搞得这么简单，那我也不会给她太多东西去分析。
</internal>

en_backup.internal:
[Perception] She was being overly simplistic and a little off the mark. First she misunderstood the whole COVID/work thing, then she jumped straight to “sickness causes you nervousness?” like she was summarizing me in a basic, almost obvious way. It made me feel like she wasn’t really tracking what I was saying, or maybe she was just trying to sound insightful when she wasn’t actually getting it. When you’re already stressed about being sick, work being affected, and everything turning into a mess, that kind of question feels too surface-level to matter.

[Decision] So I answered in a blunt, shut-down way: “most things cause me nervousness. i am a very anxious person. not sure why.” That way I didn’t have to act like her question was helpful when it wasn’t. It felt safer to keep it general and dismissive than to open up and risk being misunderstood again. If she’s going to make it so basic, then I’m not going to give her much to work with.

[Perception] He keeps circling back to the message, like the important thing is the mechanics of it — who called, how she got my number, whether she had any right to do that. When he asks how I felt, what I hear is that he wants me to make this into some emotional thing, but all I can get to is that it felt like an invasion. She’s not “my mother” in any real sense — she’s a stranger, and now she’s in my space again. What hit me hardest was the privacy part: my cell number is supposed to be mine, and somehow that got breached. That’s what feels wrong, not some soft feeling underneath it.

[Decision] So I’m going to lay out the whole thing like a complaint, because that’s what it is. I want him to understand that this isn’t me being dramatic — this is someone I didn’t ask for, someone I don’t want, suddenly reaching me through my phone. If I explain it as a sequence — she calls, I get confused, I feel violated, now I’m stuck dealing with it — maybe he’ll finally see that the problem is the intrusion itself. And if I keep it on the outside, on the facts, I don’t have to hand him some fake emotional answer that isn’t there.

en_backup.internal:
[Perception] They’re trying to turn this into “change your setup, change your chair, stand up, move on,” but that’s not what feels unbearable. What hits is the idea that I’m supposed to just leave the only thing I know how to do well — the one-on-one room, the structure, the predictability, the competence I’ve built. The problem is not a chair. The problem is that I’m being asked to step into some other version of myself that feels vague, social, and exposed. I can hear how easy it sounds to them, and that makes me feel even more cornered.

[Decision] No. I’m not doing the dramatic leap they’re hovering over. I’m not abandoning private practice or pretending I want some new identity just because this one feels cramped. I need the thing that keeps me steady: my role, my routine, my control over the work. I can admit it feels awful, but I’m drawing the line at changing into someone I’m not sure I can be. I’m staying where I know how to function.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: Well, you did mention how you're stressed about your future. Do you have any goals or plans that you have been wanting to achieve or accomplish?

en_backup.therapist_turn: Well, you did mention how you're stressed about your future. Do you have any goals or plans that you have been wanting to achieve or accomplish?
en_backup.client_response: Current no. I am just trying to get by. Fear that I'll lose my job.
en_backup.internal:
[Perception] They keep asking about goals, plans, things I enjoy, people I can talk to — like there’s something practical I’m supposed to build on. But all I hear is how far away that is from where I am. The only thing that feels real right now is the job stress and the fear that everything could fall apart if I stop just getting through the day. Reading, talking, making plans — it all feels too small, too empty, like filler. Nothing in my life feels steady enough to imagine a future worth aiming at.

[Decision] So I’m not going to reach for hope I can’t protect. I’ll keep my head down and try to get by, because that at least doesn’t set me up to lose more. If I don’t expect much, I don’t have as far to fall. It’s safer to stay numb and occupied than to start wanting things that probably won’t happen anyway.

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 我完全理解找工作有多让人沮丧。我最近也在找工作，因为预算原因我的合同没有续签。

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 你所在的行业受到新冠疫情的影响了吗？

context_zh.speaker: client
context_zh.text: 我其实有工作，但我犯了个错，我觉得可能会有麻烦，我不知道该怎么跟经理说这个错。

context_zh.speaker: client
context_zh.text: 是的，我们从三月份就开始在家办公了。其实我刚入职时就在家办公，这在我被录用时是没想到的。

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 好的，抱歉我之前猜错了！能请你详细说说你的问题吗？

context_zh.speaker: client
context_zh.text: 没事！我们有一个截止日期，是下周一结束前要完成一批项目。有些项目只需要半天就能完成，其他的要花好几天。我犯的错是优先做了那些耗时短的项目，想尽可能多完成一些。结果我忘了开始那些需要几天的项目，直到周五（昨天）才开始，所以这几个项目没法按时完成了。

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 好的，如果我没理解错的话，你优先做了某些工作，但这些工作反而更早截止，是这样吗？

context_zh.speaker: client
context_zh.text: 差不多。它们都得在同一天完成，但我优先做了耗时短的，想多完成一些。所以现在这些耗时长的（截止日期相同）就没法按时完成了。

zh.therapist_turn_zh: 好的，如果我没理解错的话，你优先做了某些工作，但这些工作反而更早截止，是这样吗？
zh.client_response_zh: 我担心跟经理说这事。
zh.internal_zh:
<internal>
[感知] 他们让我把情况说清楚，我也听出来自己这么说有多糟糕：我忽略了那些耗时长的项目，现在它们不能按时完成。这戳中了我最害怕的部分——我搞砸了，而且经理会注意到，这不仅仅是“一个无心之失”，而是会让我看起来粗心或不靠谱。如果再深想，我不得不承认我时间管理得不好，而且我可能把自己搞到了没法悄悄补救的地步。

[决定] 我现在打算说得简短、只讲事实，因为如果我说太多，听起来会显得慌乱或者开始为自己辩护。简短回答感觉更安全——让情况变得更糟的可能性更小，暴露我有多担心的可能性也更小。我还是想把事情处理好，但我还没准备好完全面对这可能对我在经理眼中的形象意味着什么。
</internal>

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: I can totally understand how frustrating a job search can be. I was recently in the job market as well, as my contract was not extended due to budget reasons!

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: Is your line of business affected by Corona virus pandemic?

context.speaker: client
context.text: I actually have a job, but I made a mistake and I think I could get in trouble and I'm not sure how to approach my manager about the mistake I made.

context.speaker: client
context.text: It is, we have been working from home since March. I actually started my job working from home, something that wasn't expected when I was first hired.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: Ok, apologies for my earlier assumption! May I please know more details about the nature of your problem?

context.speaker: client
context.text: Thats ok! We had been given a deadline for end of day this upcoming monday to have a number of projects completed. Some projects take only part of day to complete while others take multiple. I made the mistake of prioritizing the ones that take less time to be sure I was able to get as many done as possible. I in turn, forgot to start the other projects that take a couple of days until friday (yesterday) so now these couple of projects wont be done by the deadline.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: Ok, if I understand correctly, you prioritized some work to be done later, which unfortunately had an earlier deadline, is that correct?

context.speaker: client
context.text: Yes essentially. They all had to be done the same day, but I prioritized the work that took less time in order to get more of them completed. So now these ones that take longer (with the same deadline) wont be finished in time.

en_backup.therapist_turn: Ok, if I understand correctly, you prioritized some work to be done later, which unfortunately had an earlier deadline, is that correct?
en_backup.client_response: I'm worried about talking to my manager about this.
en_backup.internal:
[Perception] They’re asking me to lay it out clearly, and I can hear how bad this sounds when I say it plainly: I missed the longer projects and now they won’t be done on time. That hits the part I’m most scared of — that I messed up in a way my manager will actually notice, and that this won’t just be “an honest mistake,” but something that makes me look careless or unreliable. If I go deeper, I’d have to admit I didn’t manage my time well and that I may have put myself in a position where I can’t fix this quietly.

[Decision] I’m going to keep it brief and factual for now because if I say too much, I’ll sound panicked or start defending myself. Short answers feel safer — less chance of making it worse, less chance of exposing how worried I am. I still want to make it right, but I’m not ready to fully face what this could mean for how my manager sees me.

judge.rationale: 对话无强文化绑定，阻抗和情绪强度在中文可自然呈现，翻译不会改变话轮功能。

Right now I want to keep focusing on how impossible the situation is, because that’s what’s making me feel so low.

[Decision] I’m not doing it. I’m not sitting Max down and forcing this conversation right now. I told myself I was going to be the parent who confronts what needs confronting, but I’m not going to walk into a conversation that could break my son or blow up my role with him. Not today. context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 你试过冥想和/或深呼吸练习吗？我知道我在担心的时候觉得那很有用。

[Decision] 我决定直接问有没有活动，因为我需要实际、安全的点子，能真正在家里用的。绕来绕去可能得不到我想要的针对性帮助。我想让治疗师引导我做一些可行的事，能帮我冷静下来，打破目前的僵局。

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: Those sound like positive ways of handling stress. It is natural of course to feel stressed out by the pandemic so it can be useful to think of ways to help manage that stress.

context.speaker: client

en_backup.internal:
[Perception] The therapist is trying to be helpful by suggesting meditation and deep breathing, but I’m still stuck and need something more concrete. What hits me is that I want to feel better without doing anything that could put me or my family at risk, and I also don’t want to just keep hearing general ideas. I’m feeling down, a little overwhelmed, and I want options that fit my situation at home during the pandemic.

[Decision] I decided to ask directly for activities because I need practical, safe ideas I can actually use in my own home. Hinting around probably wouldn’t get me the kind of specific help I’m looking for. I want the therapist to guide me toward something doable that could help calm me down and break up the rut I’ve been in.

[Perception] “有什么问题吗？”听起来是最老套、最标准的开场白——那种人还不知道该怎么办但想装得冷静专业时说的话。它戳中了我疲惫又厌烦的那部分：再说一遍抑郁，得到点头，或许几个小心翼翼的问题，然后不知怎么又回到原点。这让我觉得他们早就离真正的感受很远，像是在谈论一个症状，而不是那个吞噬了我生活多年的东西。

[Decision] 所以我直截了当：“我抑郁了。”如果他们打算照本宣科，我也懒得给他们一整篇可以归档的情绪论文。我不会为还没赢得信任的人表演希望。我想看看他们能不能不只是走常规治疗师的套路——说实话，我受够了被当成一个病例来对待，而不是一个已经试过一切的人。

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: Hi! What seems to be the issue?

en_backup.therapist_turn: Hi! What seems to be the issue?
en_backup.client_response: I'm depressed...
en_backup.internal:
[Perception] “What seems to be the issue?” sounded like the most generic, polished opening possible — the kind of thing someone says when they don’t really know what to do yet but want to look calm and professional. It hit that tired, bitter part of me that’s heard this all before: explain the depression, get nods, maybe a few careful questions, and then somehow end up back where I started. It made me think they were already at a distance from what this actually feels like, like they’re talking about a symptom instead of the thing that’s been swallowing my life for years.

[Decision] So I kept it blunt: “I’m depressed.” If they’re going to sound scripted, I’m not going to hand them a whole emotional essay they can file away. I’m not going to perform hope for someone who hasn’t earned it. I wanted to see if they could do more than the usual polite therapist routine, because honestly I’m sick of being handled like a case instead of a person who’s already tried everything.

My daughter shouldn’t have to organize her life around an old man who can’t even trust himself to get through the day. If I admit there’s any chance this gets better, then I have to sit there and hope she keeps waiting, keeps worrying, keeps losing time because of me. And if it doesn’t get better, then all this worry is just more proof that I’m already ruining things.

[Decision] So I decided to stop pretending there’s some good outcome I can reach for. What’s the point of reaching? Hope just makes me ask for more than I can give, and I can’t bear the look of her building her future around my mess. Better to accept the truth as it is: I’m a burden, and if I keep myself small enough, maybe I won’t take any more from her than I already have. Better to give up the fight than keep failing at it.

context.speaker: client
context.text: I am battling with my childhood trauma that i feel is affecting my everyday life with my child and spouse. I don't know how to tell my spouse about my childhood in fear he doesn't want to be with someone with a upbringing such as mine.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: Hi, thank you for chatting with me.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: From what I understand, you are struggling with childhood trauma and this is affecting everyday life with your child and spouse.

en_backup.therapist_turn: From what I understand, you are struggling with childhood trauma and this is affecting everyday life with your child and spouse.
en_backup.client_response: Yes, correct. I am not sure how to tell my spouse about my childhood trauma. He wants to know. He wants to help me. But I am not sure where to begin with explaining it to him.
en_backup.internal:
[Perception] I heard that the therapist understood the basic problem, but I still felt stuck on the most important part: how to actually begin telling my spouse. What hit me was that he really does want to know and help, but I’m terrified that if I start talking about my childhood, he’ll see me differently and it could change our relationship. I feel frozen because I don’t know how much to say, where to start, or how to keep myself from rambling or shutting down.

[Decision] I decided to say it out loud because I need more than general understanding — I need help figuring out the first step and how to have this conversation safely. I want the therapist to guide me on how to explain it without overwhelming myself, because on my own I keep getting scared and avoiding it. I’m asking directly instead of hinting because I genuinely don’t know how to begin.

context_zh.text: 确实！！口罩和社交距离很有帮助。感觉自己尽了份力，挺好的。

context_zh.text: 但是假期不能见家人会很难受！！

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 我同意。家人是我们唯一且真正的力量源泉。远离他们确实很难受。但至少，多亏了科技，他们只是视频/一通电话的距离。

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 关于你的工作，我知道很多工作和行业都受到了影响。但与此同时，个人配送服务的需求也爆发了。

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 如果你能开车，你愿意考虑兼职做食品/杂货配送司机吗？

context_zh.speaker: client
context_zh.text: 我的生意一直很忙，但我很高兴有个分心的事

zh.therapist_turn_zh: 如果你能开车，你愿意考虑兼职做食品/杂货配送司机吗？

[Perception] 我听治疗师把事情说得好像很大很严重，好像我得把一切都当成重大危机来处理。但其实，我还能正常运转。我的生意很忙，日子也过得去。想念办公室和家人是挺难受，但也不是什么大崩溃。这确实戳中我孤独的那部分，但不是那种我要崩溃的感觉。如果我告诉自己这只是难熬的一段时间，很多人都在经历这个，那就会感觉好受一些。

[Decision] 所以我要稳住心态，不把事情搞得太夸张。我可以承认自己很孤独，但没必要把它当成一个必须马上解决的深层问题。我会继续忙自己的，继续做已经在做的事，专注于我能控制的实际事情。这比深挖它到底有多糟糕要安全得多。
</internal>

en_backup.internal:
[Perception] I hear the therapist making this sound bigger and more serious than it really is, like I need to treat everything as if it’s a major crisis. But honestly, I’m still functioning. My business is busy, I’m getting through my days, and missing the office and family is hard but not some huge breakdown. It hits the lonely part of me, but not in a way that means I’m falling apart. If I tell myself it’s just a rough stretch and that lots of people are dealing with this, then it feels more manageable.

[Decision] So I’m going to keep it in perspective and not make this into something dramatic. I can acknowledge that I’m lonely, but I don’t need to treat it like a deep problem that has to be solved right now. I’ll keep busy, keep doing what I’m already doing, and focus on the practical stuff I can control. That feels safer than digging into how bad it might actually be.

zh.internal_zh:
<internal>
[Perception] 他逼我把最难堪的那部分说出口：不只是娜塔莉失踪了，而是我去找她时心里偷偷盼着的那点东西——她还需要我，还在等着我派上用场——压根儿就不存在。读那些邮件的时候，正正戳中了我一直躲着的地方：这么长时间我以为自己在找一个丢失的女儿，可也许我其实是在测试自己在她生活里还有没有角色。如果她不需要我，那我到底在救什么？那些恐慌、那些努力、那些为了撑下去而吃的药，又有什么意义？我在想，她不需要我，到底是我辜负了她，还是只是她成长得比我愿意接受的要快。

[Perception] He’s pushing me to say the ugly part out loud: not just that Natalie was missing, but that the thing I was hoping for when I went looking for her—that she’d still need me, still be waiting for me to matter—wasn’t there. When I read those emails, it hit the exact place I’ve been avoiding: all this time I thought I was chasing a lost daughter, but maybe I was really testing whether I still had a job to do in her life. And if she doesn’t need me, then what was I even saving? What was the point of all that panic, all that effort, all those pills just to keep going? I’m trying to understand whether her not needing me means I failed her, or whether it just means she’s farther along than I can accept.

[Decision] I decided to say it plainly because circling it isn’t helping. If I keep pretending this is only about her disappearing, I never have to face the harder possibility: that my role changed and I didn’t know how to go with it. So I’m putting the thought in the open—she didn’t need me at all—because that’s the part I need to examine if I’m going to figure out what really happened, and whether I’m grieving Natalie herself or the version of myself I thought she still required.

zh.internal_zh:

[Perception] The therapist is trying to reassure me that accountants are needed, but that doesn’t touch what I’m actually afraid of: my company already cut jobs, and the lockdown makes it feel like things could get worse fast. I’m wondering if this is about too much time together, lost attraction, resentment, pressure about marriage and kids, or if I’m just forcing myself to stay because I don’t want to lose the relationship I built.

[Decision] I’m going to keep looking at the cause because if I can understand whether this is a temporary reaction, a buildup of incompatibility, or just me avoiding a hard truth, then I can decide more clearly. I also need to stop making the whole thing about protecting his feelings, because that keeps me from facing what I want. If I can figure out whether I actually still want this relationship, then the breakup question becomes less about managing damage and more about making an honest choice. I still worry I’ll regret it, but staying because I’m afraid of being the bad person doesn’t seem like a real reason to remain.

Talking about “doing something fun” or “what do you like without your partner” made it seem like they weren’t hearing how deep this is — that I didn’t just lose a person, I lost the whole life, comfort, and identity I had with her. It hit the part of me that feels like nobody can really understand this unless they’ve been in it, so their suggestions sounded empty and kind of unrealistic.

context.text: We know marijuana has effects on the developing brain. en_backup.client_response: Well, I don't think it's going to hurt me.
en_backup.internal:
[Perception] It sounds like they’re making it seem way bigger than it is. I mean, I only do it a few times a month, not all the time, and I’m not even smoking it like that. The health stuff feels kind of general and distant, not like something that’s actually hitting me right now. The addiction thing sounds like one of those numbers they say to everybody, but it doesn’t feel like it applies to me specifically.

[Decision] I’m going to stick with “it’s probably fine” because that lets me keep seeing this as not a real issue. If I admit it’s a big deal, then I have to worry about changing it, and I don’t want to do that unless I really have to. So I’m going to minimize it and keep it in the “not serious for me” category for now.

If I keep the scale down, then I don’t have to turn my father into some creepy figure or myself into some damaged case. It was normal, I adjusted, end of story.

[Perception] He’s pushing on the one thing I don’t want to say out loud: that this might actually be bigger than I can muscle through. “Might never fly again” lands because I can feel the gap between what I was and what I am now. Two months isn’t nothing. It’s long enough to start hearing the silence at home, long enough to realize the cockpit is still out there without me. And once I really look at that, I have to admit I don’t know if I’m coming back. That feels pathetic. It feels like losing ground before I’ve even started. So I shut it down. I tell myself other guys have had worse, because if I let myself hope too hard, then I have to face the chance that hope gets crushed.

When I said, “Maybe you want to go out to sea, But you don’t,” I was testing a theory: that there’s some pull in him toward being open, or going toward feelings, but another part of him stays close to shore. The unresolved part is whether the boats mean escape, curiosity, fear, or just a way to keep distance from what’s underneath.

[Decision] I decided to push the interpretation forward instead of letting him stay vague. I’m trying to see if there’s a split between wanting to move toward something deeper and staying defended. I’m also trying not to get trapped in just talking about objects, because the question underneath is what he does with the part of himself that wants to go out there versus the part that won’t let him. en_backup.internal:
[Perception] She’s pointing out a contradiction, and I can feel it landing exactly where I’m least comfortable. On the one hand, she’s saying I’m acting like I’m above it, looking at Kate and the marriage from a distance, as if that means I don’t really enter it. On the other hand, she’s reminding me I’ve been here for eight years, which means whatever I’m doing with that distance is not just a habit with Kate — it’s also part of how I relate here, with her. So when I say, “What does that mean?” I’m really trying to figure out whether she means I’ve been avoiding something the whole time, or whether she’s saying my way of thinking is itself the problem. I’m also trying to understand whether she’s accusing me, or if she’s telling me there’s something I’m not seeing because I keep stepping back to look at it.

[Decision] I decided to ask what she meant because I don’t want to just accept a vague implication that I’ve been doing this for eight years and still missing the point. If there’s a pattern here, I want it made explicit. I want to know: is she saying I’m incapable of being close, or that I’m using distance as protection? Is she saying this is what ruins things with Kate, or that it’s also what keeps me from getting help here? I’m not willing to give up my way of seeing things without understanding what else she thinks is possible. So I pushed back, not just defensively, but because I need to know what game we’re actually playing and what she believes I’m not understanding.

[Decision] I’m going to explain why this isn’t on me to fix with some easy self-care suggestion, because I’m not the one causing the problem. The real issue is the situation I’m stuck in — no reliable father, no safe backup, no real support — and I need them to understand that before they act like I’m just not making an effort. If I sound defensive, it’s because I’m tired of being treated like I’m failing when I’m the one holding everything together.

</internal>

en_backup.internal:
[Perception] They’re hearing “depression” and “suicidal” and trying to sort me into something they can manage, but what I feel is just this long, heavy hopelessness that has never really budged. When they ask questions, it hits the part of me that already feels like there’s no answer and no point in digging around for one. I told them I’ve tried before and it didn’t help, and all I can think is: here we go again, me explaining it badly, them trying to fix it, and nothing changing. The “I’ll never be happy” part feels true in the room too, like it’s not even a dramatic thought, just the most honest thing I have.

[Decision] I’m going to keep it small and not reach too hard for hope, because hoping and then being disappointed feels worse than staying numb and resigned. If I act like I know what to do, I’ll just be pretending; if I open up too much, I might end up feeling exposed and then let down again. So I’ll answer, but only a little. I’ll stay vague, let them lead, and keep my distance from anything that sounds like a promise. That way I don’t have to risk believing this could actually get better.

en_backup.therapist_turn: Sorry, Laura. Let's not call it counseling. Let's call it talking.
en_backup.client_response: Laura... Laura is her name.
en_backup.internal:
[Perception] She couldn’t even keep the name straight. Laura. Not “a girl,” not some abstract case, not whatever story she was trying to build around me and my father. Laura is the patient, a real person, and the whole point is that this is about her and the work, not some melodrama about my family. When she said “talking,” she was trying to soften it, to make me sound unstable or guilty, like I needed rescuing from myself. What hit me was the insinuation that I’m confusing my own feelings with hers, or that I’m somehow drifting into my father’s territory. I heard the accusation underneath the advice.

[Decision] So I corrected her. I said the name again because if we’re going to discuss this, we’re going to do it precisely. Laura is Laura. Not my father’s patient. Not my father’s mistake. Not a moral parable. I needed her to see the boundary clearly: this is a therapeutic problem with a patient who has a crush, and I know how to handle that. I wasn’t going to let her turn it into a confession or let her talk down to me as if she’d uncovered some hidden truth about me. If she wants to help, she needs to stay with the facts and stop trying to make this about my family.

It hit the part of me that hates being seen as the one who can’t stay, can’t answer, can’t finish the conversation. It also hit the part that knows he’s not just talking about the session ending — he’s implying there’s something unfinished in me that I don’t want to face. That’s what made me say, “What did you just say?” I needed him to repeat it so I could buy a second and not react to what it really meant.

[Decision] I decided to keep it short and act like I only needed clarification. If I stayed with what he was really saying, I’d have to admit I’m avoiding the very thing I keep saying I’ve already understood. I’d have to talk about the dream again, and maybe about why it still has me, and that feels too exposed, too close to the feeling that I’m trapped in more places than I want to name. Shortness feels safer because it lets me stay in control and not let him pin me down.

[Decision] I’m going to keep it short and just answer the question, because if I say more right now I’ll either start sounding furious or get pulled into explaining all the details I don’t fully want to put on the table. It’s not a crisis, it’s just her being dramatic and worried for no reason. She’s making it sound like I put everyone through hell, but I literally sent her a text saying I was fine. So the whole thing is being blown way out of proportion. This isn’t some serious betrayal or disaster — it’s just a stupid late-night message.

[Decision] I’m going to keep it small in my head so I don’t have to deal with all that guilt-trip energy. If I treat it like a big deal, then I’m the bad guy and I have to explain myself and get dragged into all this family nonsense. It’s easier to say it’s nothing, just one bitchy text, and move on. I’m not going to let her make this into something bigger than it is.

[Perception] 他一直在说什么清单啊爱好啊，好像这玩意儿靠列个计划就能解决似的，但真正扎心的是我有多束手无策。我受够了那些没完没了的坏消息，受够了绷着神经，也受够了逼自己做事——我已经精疲力竭了。好像所有我应该做的事都只是另一个会搞砸的任务。我连让自己停止刷新闻都做不到，更别说冷静下来，那做个计划又有毛用？这感觉就像提前给我挖坑，等着我摔得更惨。

[Decision] 我打算不指望自己太多，因为指望大改变只会让我在做不到的时候更难受。也许我会试着一会儿不看新闻，或者做一件超级小的事，但说实话我不信这能有多大用。放弃一点“修复一切”的念头反而能保护我，不至于先抱希望然后发现还是老样子，最后更加失控。

It feels like everything I’m supposed to do is just another thing to fail at. If I can’t even get myself to stop checking the news or calm down, then what’s the point of making a plan? It all feels like a setup for more frustration.

[Decision] I’m going to keep it small and not expect much from myself, because hoping for a big change just makes me feel worse when I can’t do it. Maybe I’ll try to turn the news off for a little while or do one tiny thing, but honestly I don’t trust that it’ll help. Giving up a little on fixing it protects me from getting my hopes up and then feeling even more out of control when nothing changes.

en_backup.internal:
[Perception] I heard the therapist give me a generic answer about meditating and breathing, like that was the main fix for my stress. That felt off because my problem isn’t just “not relaxing enough” — I’m dealing with an unrealistic workload, too many responsibilities, and being so overloaded that I can’t even keep organized. When I asked what they do in the moment, I was looking for something concrete and realistic for when I’m already drowning, not a vague wellness suggestion that doesn’t touch the actual pressure I’m under.

[Decision] I decided to push back because I need the conversation to stay grounded in what actually happens at work. I want to correct the idea that a little breathing exercise is enough, since that makes it sound like the issue is mostly my stress management instead of the impossible demands I’m facing. I need something practical for when I’m overwhelmed, and I want that acknowledged rather than brushed past.

If I say it’s a cold, then I’m setting a limit: stop interpreting, stop prying, stop making this about hidden motives. I need to protect my own sense of control and not let him turn this into an accusation or an examination of me.

en_backup.internal:
[Perception] He’s trying to turn this into some practical little fix — like the problem is whether Patrick eats at dinner, or whether I can police the nurses, or whether I should be caring more about my father’s comfort. What I hear is: step in, manage more, make this cleaner, make this less disgusting. And that hits the part I can’t stand — the expectation that I should keep absorbing this crap like it’s normal, like I’m some kind of family utility closet.

[Decision] No. I’m not doing more. I’m not policing Patrick, I’m not setting up little meal rules, I’m not pretending this is about manners or logistics. I’m already the one holding the whole goddamned thing together. If anybody wants to feed him, fine. If he wants his nap, fine. I’m not taking on another task just because someone wants to make this feel organized. I’m done pretending there’s some good-faith solution here.

zh.internal_zh:

[Decision] 我决定直接说出来我需要支持我的抑郁，因为我现在不能含糊。我不想只是暗示我很痛苦然后希望他们能猜到。我需要把需求说出口，这样他们就知道这事很严重，这样我也能停止假装我没事，真正开口求助。
</internal>

[Decision] I decided to say directly that I need support for my depression because I can’t afford to be vague right now. I didn’t want to just hint at being in pain and hope they’d guess it. zh.internal_zh:
<internal>
[Perception] 她不停绕回那个点，所有人都看着我，好像那就是所有问题的根源。这戳到了我觉得暴露、被逼到角落的那部分，就好像不管我做什么，这个场面都让我看起来很蠢。也不是说我具体做错了什么——而是这个房间、这些关注、那些人看过来的方式，让一切崩溃了。问题感觉是周围施加的压力，不是我本人。

[Decision] 我决定就待在这个说法上，因为如果我说是我自己蠢，那听起来就好像我整个人都是问题所在，我受不了。所以我把责任往外推——是所有人都在看，所有人都在注意，是这情况让事情变得更糟。这样说比承认我慌了、失控了更安全，因为至少这样不是我这个人有毛病，而是我在应对的状况。
</internal>

en_backup.client_response: No, but it's what you think.
en_backup.internal:
[Perception] He’s backing away the second I call out what’s obvious. “That’s not what I said” is such a safe, slippery answer — it avoids the real issue, which is that he felt hurt and is now trying to make me the bad guy for saying what I thought. If he’s going to act offended by honesty and then hide behind “boundaries,” then this isn’t therapy, it’s him trying to control the room. He’s treating my words like a violation, but he can’t handle being spoken to directly. That makes him feel less like someone who can help me and more like someone protecting his own ego.

[Decision] Fine, I’m not going to sit here and beg a guy who can’t even stand up to his own feelings. If he wants to reinterpret everything I say as cruelty, then he’s not listening anyway. I’m going to shut this down before he gets to frame me as the problem and turn this into a lecture about how I’m supposed to speak. If this is what he offers, then he’s not worth taking seriously.

context.speaker: client
context.text: Hello, would you be able to help me with a fear of mine?

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: Hello, how are you today? I will be glad to assist you.

context.speaker: client
context.text: Thank you. I'm a little fearful and sad today because I found out my mother hurt her knee and won't be able to work for a while.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: Sorry to hear that. is it possible her job can give her light duties for a while

en_backup.therapist_turn: Sorry to hear that. is it possible her job can give her light duties for a while
en_backup.client_response: Unfortunately she is a nurse and needs to be able to work with patients. I don't think there are any light duty options.
en_backup.internal:
[Perception] The therapist seemed to be looking for a practical fix right away, like maybe my mother could just keep working in a modified way. But what feels important is that this isn’t just a small inconvenience that can be worked around. My mother is a nurse, and her job depends on being physically able to care for patients, so a knee injury really does affect whether she can work at all. I wanted the therapist to see that this is more serious and that I’m not just being anxious about something minor.

[Decision] So I answered plainly and gave the detail about her job, because I need the situation understood before we can talk about what I’m feeling. If the therapist sees how limited the options are, maybe I won’t feel like I have to keep explaining or minimizing it, and then we can actually address my fear and sadness about what this means for her and for me.

en_backup.internal:
[Perception] He’s basically saying I should lean on my supervisor like that’s going to change much, but he’s missing the point. The real problem isn’t me not speaking up enough — it’s the lockdown, the economy, and the fact that my company is already cutting people. My supervisor has limited power, and I’m stuck in a situation that’s bigger than any one conversation.

[Decision] So I’m not going to pretend this is something I can fix by just “doing the right thing.” I’ve already done what I can by talking to my supervisor, and now the burden is on the situation itself to improve. If things go badly, that’s because of the lockdown and the market, not because I failed to handle it properly.

zh.internal_zh:
<internal>
[Perception] 我听到了一种带恭维的比较，好像我提起另一个阿黛尔·布劳斯和你的发表物，只是出于羡慕或羡慕加嫉妒。但那根本不是我想做的。让我不舒服的是，这种暗示把我当成了单纯仰慕你成就的人，带着那种低人一等的仰视。其实我的意思比这尖锐得多：我注意到我们之间的差距，同时自己也因此暴露无遗。那些事实本身——文章、会议、曝光度——很刺眼，因为它们撞上了我自己的长期沉默。这不是一次中立的观察；它触到了我自1998年以来再没发表过东西的那部分，而且我清楚这意味着什么。

The facts themselves — the articles, the conferences, the visibility — were irritating because they rubbed against my own long silence. It wasn’t a neutral observation; it touched the part of me that hasn’t published since 1998 and knows exactly what that means.

[Decision] I decided I needed to correct the frame instead of letting it become a compliment or a side comment. I want to insist that I’m not just making conversation about another Adele Brouse or cataloging your accomplishments for the sake of it. I’m reacting to the contrast, and to what that contrast says about me. I need to push back because otherwise it sounds like I’m merely admiring you, when what I’m actually doing is confronting, and partly resenting, the place my own professional life has gotten stuck.

zh.therapist_turn_zh: 之前，你谈到苏尼尔的时候，你变得投入、兴奋，你自己也活过来了。你说话充满能量。你身体前倾。然后你停了下来。那很显眼。这个描述你觉得准确吗？你是否发现你有热情或兴奋的冲动，但阻止自己去表达它们？几周前我做过类似的观察，说你压抑自己，当时你反应很强烈。你还记得吗？
zh.client_response_zh: 什么……你在说什么？
zh.internal_zh:
<internal>
[Perception] 我听到他把那一刻变成了关于我“压抑自己”的说法，好像他抓住了真正的解释，现在可以把它放进一个更大的模式里。这感觉不对，因为它让我的犹豫听起来是故意的、全面的，而我知道的是，我确实有感受，我确实会被激动，有时我只是不知道怎么在当时用语言表达出来。这也戳到了痛处，他把这个和我之前反应强烈的一次联系起来，这听起来像是我在回避或隐瞒什么，而不是在回应一些感觉不对劲的事。我需要纠正的是他比我更了解我自己的那种暗示。

[Decision] 我决定必须回击，因为如果我接受那个框架，就会把我钉在一个总是压抑自己、自己的说法不可信的角色上。所以我用“什么……你在说什么？”来挑战他——不是因为我无话可说，而是因为我想让他确切地说出他的意思，然后我再看是否让那个解释成立。我需要捍卫“暂时的犹豫”和“被说成习惯性压抑自己”之间的区别。
</internal>

context.speaker: client
context.text: I suppose, when I fell in love with her all those years ago. Even with Wendy last year, at the very beginning. But now I... I'm beginning to realize I've got this pattern: I seek out people who have... who have... who have themselves a passion for life and I feed off them instead. I allow them to... to feel for both of us.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: You allowed both Wendy and Kate to do your feeling for you?

context.speaker: client
context.text: Yeah, at least... at least in part.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: Whatever emotion you do feel, do you openly express yourself at the time?

context.speaker: client
context.text: Not entirely.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: You hold yourself back?

context.speaker: client
context.text: Is... is that what you think?

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: Earlier, when you were talking about Sunil, you became engaged, excited, as you came alive yourself. You spoke with energy. You sat forward in your seat. And then you stopped yourself. It was striking. Does that description seem accurate to you? Do you find you have passionate or excited impulses, but stop yourself from expressing them? I made a similar observation a couple of weeks ago about you holding yourself back, and you had a strong reaction. Do you remember?

en_backup.therapist_turn: Earlier, when you were talking about Sunil, you became engaged, excited, as you came alive yourself. You spoke with energy. You sat forward in your seat. And then you stopped yourself. It was striking. Does that description seem accurate to you? Do you find you have passionate or excited impulses, but stop yourself from expressing them? I made a similar observation a couple of weeks ago about you holding yourself back, and you had a strong reaction. Do you remember?
en_backup.client_response: What... what are you talking about?
en_backup.internal:
[Perception] I heard him turning that moment into a claim about me “holding myself back,” as if he’d caught the real explanation and could now fold it into a bigger pattern. That felt wrong because it made my hesitation sound deliberate and blanket-like, when what I know is that I do have feelings, I do get stirred up, and sometimes I simply don’t know how to put it into words in the moment. It also hit the sore point that he was linking this to a previous time I’d reacted strongly, which made it sound like I was being evasive or hiding something rather than responding to something that felt off. What I needed to correct was the implication that he could see me better than I could see myself.

[Decision] I decided I had to push back, because if I just accepted that framing, it would pin me into the role of someone who always stops himself and can’t be trusted with his own account. So I challenged it with, “What... what are you talking about?” — not because I had nothing to say, but because I wanted to make him spell out exactly what he meant before I let that interpretation stand. I needed to defend the difference between being momentarily uncertain, and being told that I am habitually suppressing myself.

context_zh.speaker: client

context_zh.text: 我完全能理解那种感受。我也经历过跟你一模一样的情况。

context_zh.speaker: client
context_zh.text: 我们结婚一周年纪念日就是上周六。我知道我不该这么痛苦，但我就是。我觉得是因为，像有些人跟我说的，我们还处在蜜月期。我们没吵架，也没什么大问题……她直接就出轨了。

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 我真的很为你难过。你要明白，这种行为、这些选择，是她自身的缺陷，不是你的问题。

zh.therapist_turn_zh: 我真的很为你难过。你要明白，这种行为、这些选择，是她自身的缺陷，不是你的问题。
zh.client_response_zh: 很难这样看。我觉得自己是个失败者，不够好。
zh.internal_zh:
<internal>
[Perception] 听到说她出轨就该明白跟我无关，但我就是没法这么想。这话正好扎在最疼的地方——那个觉得自己随时可以被换掉的部分，哪怕才结婚一年，我还是没能留住一个人。如果连这么新的关系里我都是“不够的”，那再怎么努力大概也改变不了我是什么样的人。我感觉自己还没等事情成真就被丢掉了。

[Decision] 我不想逼自己去抱有希望，因为希望只会让这一切更难受、更丢人，万一最后还是不行的话。不如麻木一点，管自己叫失败者，别再指望自己能振作起来。如果我不相信任何东西能改变这一切，那我就不用冒险去信自己值得被爱，然后又失去它。也许放弃一点，才是唯一让我不会被彻底压垮的办法。
</internal>

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: I'm so incredibly sorry to hear that. You realize this behavior, these choices, are a flaw within her, and not you?

en_backup.therapist_turn: I'm so incredibly sorry to hear that. You realize this behavior, these choices, are a flaw within her, and not you?
en_backup.client_response: It's hard to see that.  I feel like a failure and not good enough
en_backup.internal:
[Perception] Hearing that she cheated is supposed to mean it’s not about me, but it doesn’t land that way. It hits the exact place that already hurts — the part of me that feels replaceable, like even in a marriage that was only a year old, I still couldn’t keep someone from leaving. If I was “not enough” in something this new, then all the work in the world probably won’t change what I am. It feels like I got thrown away before anything even had a chance to become real.

[Decision] I’m not going to try to force myself into hope right now, because hope just makes this feel bigger and more humiliating if it doesn’t work out. It seems easier to stay numb, to call myself a failure, and to stop expecting myself to bounce back. If I don’t believe anything will fix this, then I don’t have to risk believing I can be wanted and then losing that too. Maybe giving up a little is the only way to keep this from crushing me completely.

zh.internal_zh:

[Decision] 我打算先谨慎点，不完全吃压力这个角度。我会如实回答，但只说到我能维持“我一切都好”这个叙事为止。如果真是身体原因，我更想先处理那个，而不是翻那些我觉得压根不存在的压力源。

That lands on the part of me that really doesn’t want this to turn into “your job is the problem” or “you’re actually more stressed than you admit.” I know the migraines are real and they’re making the depression worse, but I also know my work and life are basically okay, and I don’t want to make a bigger deal out of something that might just be a temporary health thing. 

[Decision] I’m going to keep it cautious and not fully buy into the stress angle yet. I’ll answer honestly, but only as far as I can without unraveling the story that I’m managing things fine. If there’s something medical going on, I’d rather focus on that first instead of digging around for stressors that I don’t think are there.

It felt like he was trying to pull me out of the only place that feels solid: the part of me that already assumes the worst. The blood tests are the line where everything becomes real, and I can’t stand being asked to lean into that before I know. It hit the most private, scared part of me — the part that can’t afford to hope and then get crushed.

[Decision] I’m done talking about this. I need to keep my guard up and not open the door any wider. If I say less, I can keep control and not get dragged into hoping, explaining, or breaking apart in front of him. So I’ll shut it down and just ask for help getting up — get out of here before this goes any further.

[Perception] He was acting like there was still something to check, something uncertain, but there wasn’t. And it made me realize I’d been letting myself stay in the waiting place, as if waiting long enough could make it true.

[Decision] So I said it the bluntest way I could: I don’t have to grieve for a child that I never had. I needed to shut down the crying, the pity, the idea that I’m some tragic woman. If I say it like that, maybe I can keep control of it. Maybe then nobody can tell me what I’m supposed to feel.

en_backup.client_response: They did end up crying and saying that it was a mistake. I don't know if it would be a good idea. I think I would have feelings of regret
en_backup.internal:
[Perception] It felt like they were being really generic, like “maybe talk it out” is the kind of safe, polished thing people say when they don’t actually have to live in the same house with the fallout. They weren’t the one who walked in on my partner and roommate. They don’t have to go to sleep in that bedroom after this. So it landed like they were skimming over how humiliating and messy this is, almost as if “salvageable” is something you can just decide in a calm little sit-down. That made me feel like they didn’t really get how serious the betrayal is or how trapped I feel with all their stuff still in the house.

[Decision] I’m not going to treat that as real guidance right now. I need to stop looking for a neat answer from someone who isn’t in this mess with me. If I’m going to do anything, it has to be because I can actually imagine living with the consequences, not because someone says a relationship “might” be worth saving. Right now that feels too easy, almost naive, and I’m not ready to let them steer me into pretending this can be fixed by a conversation.

If they’re just going to echo back how terrible it is, I’ll keep it on the surface where I know I’m right and don’t have to feel exposed. I can’t make the fear disappear, but I can stop pretending I’m the same person I was before. I want this new life, and I’m going to try to be a good mother even if I’m afraid and even if it feels like it’s just me. Saying that out loud feels like taking ownership instead of waiting to be rescued.

[Perception] 我感觉到她话里的压力——好像“你得解决这个问题，别再进医院了。”这话击中了我已经又害怕又沮丧的那部分，因为我正努力为了约翰·卡洛保持健康，我讨厌身体不争气的感觉。同时，当她提到健康起来，我又想到我真的很想呼吸，不想回这里，想陪在宝宝身边。但她马上扯到奥斯卡，这触动了我保护欲和几乎内疚的那部分，因为奥斯卡陪了我12年。感觉很不公平。

[Decision] 我决定终于说出我一直绕着走的那句话——我不想回这里，而且奥斯卡跟这事搅在一起让我很纠结。我还没准备好接受“狗是问题”这种说法，但我没法继续假装自己不难受、不纠结。说“但——”是想慢下来，因为我想解释清楚，而不是直接怼回去或者被逼着接受我不信的东西。
</internal>

en_backup.internal:
[Perception] I heard the pressure in what she was saying — like, “you need to fix this so you don’t end up here again.” That landed on the part of me that’s already scared and frustrated because I’m trying to stay healthy for John Carlo, and I hate feeling like my body is failing me. At the same time, when she brought up getting healthy, it made me think about how much I really do want to breathe, to not be back here, to be around for my baby. But then she went straight to Oscar, and that hit the part of me that feels protective and almost guilty, because he’s been with me for 12 years. It feels unfair.

[Decision] I decided to finally say the thing I’ve been circling around — that I don’t want to come back here, and that Oscar is tied up in this in a way that messes with me. I’m not ready to agree with the whole dog-is-the-problem thing, but I can’t keep pretending I’m not upset or torn up about it. Saying “but the—” is me trying to slow it down, because I want to explain myself without just shutting down or getting forced into something I don’t buy.

context_zh.text: 我记得她穿了件特别美的蓝色长裙。领口开得很低那种，当然，还涂着红唇，戴着黑色假发，盘了个经典的发髻。她表现得特别优雅，把所有人都迷得神魂颠倒。我当时真不敢相信她病了，更别说快要死了。之后我们回了酒店，我订了个能看到公园的好房间，然后……（叹气）点了香槟……特别开心。那是……我最后一次见到她。

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 但你之前跟我说，你经常往返医院。

zh.therapist_turn_zh: 但你之前跟我说，你经常往返医院。
zh.client_response_zh: 我知道我是这么说的，因为说实话，我内心里感觉就是这样。我自己也一直在讲这个故事，讲了这么久……
zh.internal_zh:
<internal>
[Perception] 我听到治疗师指出一个矛盾：我一直说自己经常往返医院，但我脑子里却全是那个酒店房间、香槟、公园景观，整个感觉几乎是庆祝式的。让我一下子意识到，这两个版本对不上。一个听起来是陪伴和照顾，另一个听起来像是最后一道精修过的记忆——我可能一直在用它来遮盖自己到底有多承受不起真正生病、垂死的那部分。所以问题不只是“到底发生了什么？”而是我是否一直在把整段时间编成一个故事，这个故事保护我，不让我承认自己角色的真相——我缺席了，或者结局根本不是我一直回放的那个美丽画面。

[Decision] 我决定不能再因为从内部感觉真实就一直重复这个故事了。我得用事实检验它，哪怕记忆因此变形。不是要抹掉那些美好的部分——裙子、口红、她照亮整个房间的样子——而是把它们从我一直在粉饰的东西里分离开。如果我能搞清自己到底在哪里、去过医院几次、那一晚对我来说情感上意味着什么，也许我就能说出真相，同时不毁掉美好的记忆。这似乎是唯一的方法，让我知道我到底是在记住她，还是在维护一个阻止我面对更难部分的叙事。
</internal>

I'd gotten this great room with a view of the park and... ( Exhales ) Ordered champagne... Just a great time. It was... It was the last time I saw her.

context.speaker: therapist

en_backup.therapist_turn: But you told me that you were going back and forth to the hospital a lot.
en_backup.client_response: I know that's what I said, because honestly that's what it felt like inside. I've been telling myself that story for so long...
en_backup.internal:
[Perception] I heard the therapist point out a mismatch: I’ve been saying I was going back and forth to the hospital a lot, but the image I’m holding is of that hotel room, the champagne, the park view, the whole thing feeling almost celebratory. What hit me is that these two versions don’t comfortably fit together. One sounds like presence and caregiving; the other sounds like a final, polished memory I may have been using to cover over how little of the actual sick-dying part I can bear to hold in my mind. So the puzzle isn’t just “what happened?” It’s whether I’ve been turning the whole period into a story that protects me from admitting the truth of my role, my absence, or the fact that the ending was not really the beautiful scene I keep replaying.

[Decision] I decided I need to stop repeating the story just because it feels true from the inside. I should test it against the facts, even if that means the memory changes shape. Not to erase the beautiful parts — the gown, her lipstick, the way she lit up a room — but to separate those from whatever I’ve been glossing over. If I can figure out where I actually was, how often I was at the hospital, and what the hotel night was doing for me emotionally, maybe I can tell the truth without destroying the good memory. That seems like the only way to know whether I’m remembering her, or preserving a story that keeps me from looking at the harder part.

zh.internal_zh:
<internal>
[Perception] 他一直在附和我说她当然欠我一个解释，好像那能帮到我似的，但感觉一点用都没有。他并没有真正说出我需要听的话。我问了是该打电话还是等她，他现在却说得好像他已经认定她是坏人，而我只能坐在那儿接受这个说法。这戳到了我痛处：我不想成为那个被遗弃在空公寓里人，如果他都给不了我下一步该怎么办，就不要给我那种轻飘飘的“她对你太糟糕了”的回答。感觉他只是在塞给我愤怒，而我真正需要的是点实际的东西。

[Decision] 好吧，如果他只是站在她那边，一味说她多糟糕，那我就自己走务实路线。我要问问公寓、她的东西、要不要搬走，至少这些是实际的。我不会坐在这里继续揭伤疤，去听那些根本帮不到我的建议。
</internal>

[Perception] He keeps agreeing with me like of course she owes me an explanation, like that’s supposed to help, but it feels useless. He’s not actually saying what I need to hear. I asked whether I should call her or wait, and now he’s talking like he already knows she’s the bad one and I’m just supposed to sit here with that. It hits the raw part: I don’t want to be the guy abandoned in an empty apartment, and I don’t want some simple “she was terrible to you” answer if he can’t tell me what to do next. It feels like he’s just handing me indignation when I need something real.

[Decision] Fine, if he’s just going to stay on her side of the story and make it about how awful she was, then I’ll take the practical route myself. I’ll ask about the apartment, her stuff, whether I should move, because at least that’s concrete. I’m not going to sit here and keep reopening the wound for advice that doesn’t actually get me anywhere.

context.speaker: therapist

en_backup.therapist_turn: Have you said anything to her about it?

en_backup.internal:
[Perception] He keeps trying to make this into some deeper mystery, like I’m leaving because I’m scared or because I’m being evasive or because there’s some hidden truth about me I’m avoiding. But that’s not what this is. What hit me was the way he said “walking away” like it’s supposed to sound easy or selfish, when to me it sounds clear. I don’t need to be psychoanalyzed into staying in something that’s already dead. The only thing that matters is that I’ve already seen what this marriage is: empty, false, over. And if I say it plainly enough, maybe he’ll stop trying to drag me back into debating whether it’s real.

[Decision] So I’m going to tell him I haven’t said anything to her yet, because that’s the actual fact. Not because I’m uncertain, but because this is still in my hands. I need him to see that I’m not asking permission or looking for a rescue. I’ve made up my mind, and I’m trying to keep the conversation on the real issue: what happens now that it’s done, not whether I should pretend otherwise.

zh.internal_zh:
<internal>
[Perception] 他的表现好像我的情绪是某种戏剧性的转变，我应该解释清楚，好像我因为说他不像我想的那样就显得不理性或不公平似的。这戳到了我已经感到被逼到墙角、被误解的那部分。我并不是在说他是什么了不起的背叛者——我是在说他和我想的不一样，我也不想被迫承认一些关于他的美好故事，如果那不是真的。而且感觉不对头，因为他一直在说我的看法变了，而不是我实际提出的问题：凯尔一直在我身边晃悠，我感觉被逼着表态。

[Decision] 我决定反驳，说了我知道的最简单的真相：我不了解他。这样我就不用同意他的说法，也不用给他加分，把他当成一个可靠、值得信赖的男人，因为我不确定他是。我想纠正他，但又不想被拖进去解释我所有的感受，因为我不相信他想往哪带。
</internal>

context.speaker: therapist

context.speaker: client
context.text: I don't wanna talk about Kyle. I brought him up because... Fuck it. Never mind. I thought you were a man.

context.speaker: therapist

en_backup.therapist_turn: So today, I'm... your betrayer ? But last week, you were equally certain that I was generous and good. Can you see how dramatically your opinion of me has changed ? Can you make sense of that for me ?
en_backup.client_response: I guess I never really knew you.
en_backup.internal:
[Perception] He was acting like my feelings are some dramatic flip I should explain away, like I was being irrational or unfair for saying he wasn’t who I thought. That hit the part where I already feel cornered and misunderstood. I wasn’t saying he’s a betrayer in some grand, important way — I was saying he is not what I thought, and I don’t want to be pushed to admit some nice story about him if it isn’t true. It also felt wrong because he was talking about my opinion changing instead of the actual thing I brought up: that Kyle was hovering over me and I felt put on the spot.

[Decision] I decided to push back by saying the simplest truth I had: I didn’t know him. That way I’m not agreeing with his version, and I’m not giving him credit for being some solid, trustworthy man when I’m not sure he is. I wanted to correct him without having to get dragged into explaining all my feelings right then, because I don’t trust where he’s taking it.

zh.internal_zh:
<internal>
[Perception] 他想把话题转回我身上，好像真正的问题是我是否还会想要一个变得“胖、情绪化”还被困在婴儿里的女人。他在绕着同一个恐惧打转：生孩子会把女人变成我无法忍受的样子，而我会被困在尿布、没了性、没了自由、不再是我这个男人的生活里。他逼我承认我想要某种家庭责任和家庭生活，但我不想。

[Perception] He’s trying to turn this back on me, like the real issue is whether I’d still want someone who got “fat, emotional,” and stuck with an infant. He’s circling the same fear: that childbirth changes a woman in ways I’d find intolerable, and that I’d be trapped in a life of diapers, loss of sex, loss of freedom, loss of the man I am. He’s pushing me to admit I want some version of domestic responsibility and family life, and I don’t.

[Decision] No. I’m not going there. I won’t pretend I could happily sign up for that, and I’m not going to dress up my answer to make him comfortable. I’m drawing the line here: I do not want the burden, the mess, the bodily changes, the endless caretaking, or the surrender of my autonomy. That’s what I’m refusing, because once you accept that life, you don’t get to be untouched anymore.

context.speaker: client
context.text: Hey it is getting difficult day by day .

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: Hi! I am sorry to heard that. I would be very glad to help if you could please tell me what bothers you

context.speaker: client
context.text: We are unable to meet our friends and families especially during holidays like Thanksgiving and Christmas.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: I can see why you are concerned. These are certainly difficult times and this pandemic doesn't seem to be stopping anytime now. I understand your frustation.

context.speaker: client
context.text: There should be some other ways to get out of this situation.  Its so boring life.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: Many apps offer videocalls that you can use to chat with your loved ones though. Zoom is a great one, fore example!

context.speaker: client
context.text: Yes that is one way to connect but meeting in person makes a difference.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: It surely does. You can always travel, just make sure that you are maintaining social distancing and your mask at all times. If you and your family members follow the protocols, it is very unlikely that any of you is exposed to the virus.

en_backup.therapist_turn: It surely does. You can always travel, just make sure that you are maintaining social distancing and your mask at all times. If you and your family members follow the protocols, it is very unlikely that any of you is exposed to the virus.
en_backup.client_response: Its too risky to travel.  And with kids you it will be difficult. Besides you never know what will happen so don't want to take risk of travelling.
en_backup.internal:
[Perception] The therapist is acting like this is something I can just solve by using video calls or by traveling “safely,” but that misses the whole point. What hurts is that our normal life has been taken away — seeing family in person, enjoying holidays, going out with the kids, doing things that actually feel like life. The real problem is this pandemic and all the restrictions around it, not me failing to adapt.

[Decision] I’m not going to accept being pushed into pretending these substitutes are enough. It’s not that I’m unwilling to do anything; it’s that the situation itself has made ordinary life feel impossible and risky. I want the old normal back, and until that happens, I’m stuck dealing with what this pandemic has done to us.

That hit the part of me that already feels exposed, because I wasn’t just asking about Rosie. I was testing whether I could pull her away from me, make this about something safer, and maybe see if she’d bite. When she asked if I wanted to talk about her daughter or just make her uncomfortable, it felt like the room got too sharp. Too direct. Like I’d been seen doing the thing I’m ashamed of.

[Decision] So I shut it down. If I kept going, I’d have to admit I was messing with her, and then we’d be back on me — my wanting to be liked, my wanting to disappear, my whole stupid slippery thing. I don’t want to hand her that part of me right now. I don’t want to be the one who’s needy and intrusive and obvious. Better to act cool, pull back, say I don’t want to talk about her if she doesn’t. That lets me protect myself and keeps me from feeling like I’m begging or getting rejected.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: There are a few strategies you could use to combat that.  Personally, I try to soak in as much sunlight as possible before it goes down. context.speaker: therapist
context.text: As far as the intrusive and repetitive nature of the thoughts, have you ever consulted with a therapist or other mental health professional?  Obsessive thoughts are sometimes a sign of anxiety.

context.speaker: client
context.text: Yeah that is good advice. I definitely need to work on getting myself up earlier in the mornings, I've just come so accustomed to my current sleep schedule.

en_backup.therapist_turn: As far as the intrusive and repetitive nature of the thoughts, have you ever consulted with a therapist or other mental health professional?  Obsessive thoughts are sometimes a sign of anxiety.

[Perception] They’re suggesting that some of this might be tied to stress, anxiety, or the way my evenings and darker days feel, and honestly that hits because I do notice it gets worse at night. At the same time, the idea of seeing a therapist makes me feel exposed. I hear the suggestion as “talk to someone,” but what I feel is how hard it would be to sit there and explain all of this to a stranger without sounding dramatic or weak. I also don’t want to give up my routine or admit that I might need help to handle something I should maybe be able to manage myself.

[Decision] I’m not saying no, because a part of me does want this to get better and wants to try something new. But I’m holding back from fully committing right now because I want to protect my sense of strength and keep control. So I’ll stay cautious, agree that the advice makes sense, and leave the door open without actually stepping through it yet.

That made me feel like maybe she doesn’t fully get how trapped and vulnerable I’ve been feeling.

[Decision] So I’m going to keep this on the pandemic for now, because that’s the real thing I can point to and it feels more legitimate than making it sound like I just need to try harder. If I stay with that, then I don’t have to swallow the idea that her advice should be enough for me. I want help, yes, but I don’t want to be brushed off like this is just a matter of choosing the right friend.

[Perception] 我听到治疗师好像把一切都简化为“因大麻被起诉很少见”和“美国似乎很严格”，这跟我真正想谈的东西冲突了。我提起合法化或政治，根本不是为了这个。我说的是大麻怎么融入了我和妻子的生活，我怎么试图理解这一切，以及经济压力和日常使用是真实的。当治疗师一直在比较国家和选举时，感觉他们没抓住真正的问题，也不太懂我想解释的背景。

[Decision] 我决定需要纠正一下并稍微推回去，否则我们会一直陷在模糊的政治来回拉扯中，而不是处理我的情况。我想把话题拉回到现实：各州情况不同，地方参与很重要，我说的不是抽象评论。我需要指出，我这里的结构影响不一样，谈话应该关于我的生活和选择，而不是关于合法性的泛泛之谈。
</internal>

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: Ah yes, it is not cheap. I am not sure how much to suggest as it's not legal in my country :)

context.speaker: client
context.text: It was recently legalized in our state. My wife and I were actually one of the first people in line to buy it legally last year, before the pandemic. It is a major part of our lives.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: I am in the UK. It's sort of a grey area ... police won't really do anything but you can't buy it over the counter

context.speaker: client
context.text: One of the best things about legalization has been the expurgation of criminal records for incarcerated people jailed on marijuana charges. I'm very grateful that these atrocities have been rectified at least partially.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: Yes I would be too. Even twenty five years ago in my student days it was rare for anyone to be prosecuted for pot.  The US seems to be really strict on it tho

context.speaker: client
context.text: It varies, state by state, depending on which party is governing. Which you of course have a version of in the UK. Mayoral elections were today yeah?

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: They were but I didn't pay much attention :) I vote in the Generals and the locals but that's all .

context.speaker: client
context.text: Oh, well, I'm sorry to hear that. I think participation in local governance is actually the most achievable path for change, but perhaps how it's structured where you are, it wouldn't really matter much if you participated.

en_backup.therapist_turn: They were but I didn't pay much attention :) I vote in the Generals and the locals but that's all .
en_backup.client_response: I guess mayorals are only technically local, not like parliamentary elections
en_backup.internal:
[Perception] I heard the therapist kind of flattening everything into “it’s rare to be prosecuted for pot” and “the US seems strict,” and that rubbed against what I’m actually trying to talk about. That wasn’t the point of me bringing up legalization or politics. I was talking about how marijuana is woven into my life with my wife, how I’m trying to make sense of that, and how the financial strain and daily use are real. When the therapist keeps comparing countries and elections, it feels like they’re missing the actual issue and not quite getting the context I’m trying to explain.

[Decision] I decided I needed to correct that and push back a little, because otherwise we’d stay stuck in a vague political back-and-forth instead of dealing with my situation. I wanted to steer it back toward the reality that this is state-by-state, that local participation matters, and that what I’m saying isn’t just abstract commentary. I needed to make the point that the structure matters differently where I am, and that the conversation should be about my life and choices, not just general opinions about legality.

[Perception] 他们总是说得好像有个简单的解决办法——加入一个团体、给人发消息、去参加活动——但我听到的只有自己已经落后了多少。我手头堆着一堆截止日期，累得要死，还要逼自己去搞什么新的社交，这只会让我更清楚地意识到自己有多格格不入。它正好戳中了我害怕成绩已经下滑、最后这一年会毁掉我之前所有努力的那部分。如果我开始期望主动联系能有用，结果没用，那我只会更尴尬、更暴露，感觉什么都失败了。

context.speaker: client
context.text: I'm in my final year, having to juggle my dissertation with what feels like a million other assignments

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: Oh goodness, I can't imagine how stressful that would be. I've only gotten my associates, and I found that last semester to be a slough. But what kept me going was the relief and joy I would feel once I had that diploma in hand.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: Are there any study groups or classmates you can get together with, and basically make a night of it?

context.speaker: client
context.text: I don't really have any friends on the course, I'm pretty shy and don't really feel comfortable talking to anyone. I kinda promised myself to make more friends in my final year, but obviously circumstances have changed :/

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: Very true, this year made everyone's expectations and plans go out the window lol

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: It might be time to put yourself out of your comfort zone, but start small. Are there any clubs or groups associated with your major? That way, you have some common ground to work with.

context.speaker: client
context.text: I'm honestly not sure, I guess I've always been too nervous to reach out to anyone. I'll have to have a look.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: That sounds like a good idea =) Even if you can't hold club meetings on campus or have any gatherings, maybe they hold their meetings over video calls. One plus side to that, is that you don't need to have your camera on to participate.

en_backup.therapist_turn: That sounds like a good idea =) Even if you can't hold club meetings on campus or have any gatherings, maybe they hold their meetings over video calls. One plus side to that, is that you don't need to have your camera on to participate.
en_backup.client_response: That's true. I also feel a bit nervous about my final grades, I've done well so far but just feel like this year might mess everything up.
en_backup.internal:
[Perception] They keep making it sound like there’s some simple fix — join a group, message people, turn up to meetings — but all I can hear is how far behind I already feel. I’ve got deadlines piling up, I’m exhausted, and the thought of trying to force myself into some new social thing just makes me more aware of how out of place I am. It hits the part where I’m scared my grades are already slipping and that this final year is going to undo all the work I’ve done. If I start hoping that reaching out will help and it doesn’t, then I’ll just feel more embarrassed, more exposed, and more like I’ve failed at everything.

[Decision] So I’m not going to bother trying to make all of this better in some big way. I’ll just keep to myself and get through whatever I can on my own, because at least that way I don’t have to gamble on help that might not come through. It feels bleak, but it’s safer to expect it to go badly than to build hope and watch it fall apart. I’d rather lower my expectations now than risk finding out I can’t fix this.

en_backup.therapist_turn: I used to be the same way, but I learned about how to make and keep close friends.

en_backup.internal:
[Perception] He’s treating this like a simple “I used to be that way too” story, like my problem is just basic shyness that can be fixed by learning a few friendship tips. That misses the real part: I’m not just nervous around strangers, I actively keep people out because trust feels risky and I don’t want to lose control. When he says it’s not a big problem, it sounds like he’s brushing past what actually keeps me stuck and making it sound smaller than it is.

[Decision] So I’m going to pull back and keep it on the surface. If he’s going to respond with generic reassurance and compare me to himself, then he doesn’t really get it, and I’m not going to hand him anything more vulnerable. I’ll stick to describing the problem in a controlled way, but I’m not going to open up and let him steer me somewhere I don’t trust.

[Perception] The therapist is pushing me to make sense of that missing stretch of time, like the gap itself matters. I hear my own sentence as a kind of answer and accusation at the same time: if I had stayed, maybe none of this would have happened. I’m trying to connect the sequence of events, but the blank spot in my memory blocks the chain, and that makes everything feel both unfinished and dangerously open.

[Decision] I decided to state the reason plainly instead of pretending I don’t know. If I name the logic out loud—“because if I’d stayed with her, she wouldn’t have tried to kill herself”—then at least the problem is on the table in a form I can think about. It lets me test the thought rather than just carry it around as a vague guilt. I’m not ready to say it’s false, but I’m also not fully certain it’s true; I’m trying to pin down whether I’m describing what happened, or just the explanation I’ve been living with for years.

I’d rather not keep going in circles or sound like I’m overreacting when I’m the one getting picked on at work.

[Decision] 我决定继续，把不满挑明，但要用一种听起来足够可控的方式，不至于把整个谈话搞砸。我从对纽约的泛泛恼火转移到对茶的具体抱怨，因为比起说些更私人的话，这样更安全。我想看看我能不能提出要求或批评，然后得到确认说我没做错。所以我问了“我表现怎么样？”——我希望治疗师最终告诉我，我成功地表达了自己。

en_backup.internal:
[Perception] I took from the therapist’s words that they were staying with my point instead of arguing with me, even when I complained about the tea and about Americans. That hit the part of me that wants my frustration to be heard without being corrected or made into a joke. I also heard that “balanced conversation” I asked for is not really about politeness only — it is about whether I can say what bothers me and still remain acceptable here.

[Decision] I decided to keep going and make the frustration plain, but in a way that sounded controlled enough not to upset the whole exchange. I moved from the general irritation about New York to a specific complaint about tea because that felt safer than saying something more personal. I wanted to see if I could say a demand or criticism, and then get confirmation that I did it right. That is why I asked, “How did I do?” — I wanted the therapist to finally tell me that I managed to express myself properly.

en_backup.client_response: No, I just dont like looking at myself in the mirror. I just feel ugly and gross
en_backup.internal:
[Perception] It’s not just my weight, and that’s the worst part. Even when I’m doing the things I’m supposed to do — working out, eating better, trying clothes, trying haircuts — I still feel disgusting when I look at myself. So all the advice sounds like more things to try, but none of it touches the real problem. It just feels like I’m still going to be this ugly person no matter what I change.

[Decision] I guess I’m done expecting anything to really fix this. I’ll keep going through the motions because I have to, but I’m not going to let myself hope that I can actually feel beautiful or wanted. Hope just makes it hurt more when I look in the mirror and nothing has changed. If I act like it doesn’t matter, then I don’t have to keep getting disappointed.

They chose to betray me. Their cheating is the thing that hurt me, and now COVID is making it harder because I can’t even lean on friends the way I normally would.

[Decision] I’m going to take the advice that helps me get away from this mess, because I need relief, not more time blaming myself. I’ll go for long walks and keep talking to the friends I can reach, even if it has to be by phone or online. I want to put the responsibility where it belongs: on them for cheating, not on me for being hurt by it.

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: Steve，今天结束之前，我想问问你愿不愿意花几分钟说说你喝酒的事。

context_zh.speaker: client
context_zh.text: 行，比如什么？

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 嗯，你今天帮我们填了这份问卷，挺好的。非常感谢。我就是想确认一下上面的几项。我注意到你说你一周喝两到三次，每次喝三四杯，然后每周还有几次喝得更多。也就是六杯或以上，这上面写的。

context_zh.speaker: client
context_zh.text: 嗯哼。

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 这个听起来符合实际情况吗？

zh.therapist_turn_zh: 这个听起来符合实际情况吗？
zh.client_response_zh: 是啊，呃，周末的时候？
zh.internal_zh:
<internal>
[Perception] 她指着问卷上的数字，差不多在说：“这真的是你吗？”我听出来她觉得我喝酒可能比我平时想的要多，但我不确定这些数字没背景说明能代表什么。如果只是周末，那跟一直喝感觉不一样。我在想她是不是把偶尔喝大几晚跟每天喝酒的人当成一回事了，因为这两件事好像不一样。这话也触动了我心里那个想把自己看成挺正常、挺健康的训练刻苦的男的，而不是有酗酒问题的人的那部分。

[Decision] 我决定承认一部分，但也就到一定程度，说“是啊，呃，周末的时候？”这样我可以同意那些数字如果她是说周末喝酒的话也许对得上，但也给了我一个方式缩小范围，可能让情况显得没那么严重。我在试着弄清楚她到底是在说喝酒的量本身是问题，还是说我是怎么喝、多频繁喝才是问题。如果只是周末，我告诉自己那听起来没那么糟，我想看看她会不会也同意说这还是挺适量的。
</internal>

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: Steve, before we're done with our visit today, I was wondering if you'd be willing to take a few minutes to talk about your drinking.

context.speaker: client
context.text: Okay, like what?

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: Well, you filled out this survey for us today, which was great. Thank you very much. I just wanted to review a couple of things on here. I noticed that you said that you drink two to three times a week, drink three or four drinks at a time when you do drink, and weekly, um, have more drinks than that. So six or more drinks, it says on here.

context.speaker: client
context.text: Mm-hmm.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: Does that sound realistic?

en_backup.therapist_turn: Does that sound realistic?
en_backup.client_response: Yeah, uh, on the weekends?
en_backup.internal:
[Perception] She’s pointing to the survey numbers and basically saying, “Is this actually you?” I hear that she thinks my drinking might be more than I usually consider it, but I’m not sure those numbers really mean much without context. If it’s just weekends, that feels different to me than drinking all the time. I’m trying to figure out whether she’s treating a couple heavier nights the same as someone who drinks daily, because those seem like different situations. It also hits the part of me that wants to still see myself as a pretty normal, healthy guy who’s training hard, not someone with a drinking problem.

[Decision] I decided to acknowledge it, but only up to a point, by saying “Yeah, uh, on the weekends?” That lets me agree that the numbers might fit if she means weekend drinking, but it also gives me a way to narrow it down and maybe make it seem less serious. I’m trying to understand whether she’s saying the amount itself is the issue, or whether it’s how often and in what pattern I’m drinking. If it’s just weekends, I’m telling myself that doesn’t sound that bad, and I want to see if she’ll agree that it’s still pretty moderate.

judge.rationale: 无强文化绑定或语言双关，情绪和阻抗可自然翻译保留。

</internal>

context.speaker: client
context.text: Well, Stevie was a drummer and anyone will tell you they are totally different.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: Two weeks ago you did tell me that you wondered if you had missed your chance with Steve and you wanted to go back to that moment when you could've had him.

context.speaker: client
context.text: If that's what I was trying to do, it didn't work... not in the morning.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: Exactly. You saw in the mirror that you're a woman now and not a girl anymore, and maybe you didn't want to. If you did, you might have to see guitar boy again or give him a name. Do you think it's possible that he might've been a kind of symbol for roads not taken?

context.speaker: client
context.text: He was pretty great in bed for a symbol.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: Very good.

context.speaker: client
context.text: Okay, let's say that guitar boy was a symbol, right? So what am I doing with a cop?

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: Well, how did you feel when you were with him?

en_backup.therapist_turn: Well, how did you feel when you were with him?
en_backup.client_response: I felt safe.
en_backup.internal:
[Perception] He keeps trying to make Stevie into a symbol, like he’s not just some guy I wanted, but a whole signpost for the life I didn’t take. And maybe that’s true in some annoying way, but I don’t want him flattened into meaning. What hit me was the cop part. Because if guitar boy is about freedom and roads not taken, then the cop is the opposite of that, and I can hear how stupid it sounds to say I’m “just sleeping around” when one of them makes me feel safe. Safe enough to let someone else decide, safe enough to not have to be the adult all the time.

[Decision] So I said it plainly: I felt safe. Not sexy, not wild, not complicated — safe. I wanted her to see that I’m not chasing every man for the same reason. I’m not just replaying some old fantasy. With Stevie it was the missing road. With the cop it’s different. I’m trying to show her there’s a part of me that wants to be held, taken care of, maybe even bossed around a little, and that I don’t know what to do with that except call it something casual and keep moving.

[Perception] He’s pushing past what I’m willing to say. “Rejected, even abandoned” lands like he’s pinning the whole thing on me being needy or oversensitive, and “Can you describe it?” feels like he wants me to stare straight at that look on his face and mine. [Decision] I’m not doing that right now. I’m going to shut this down and keep it simple: I was early, he was busy, that’s all. I need to protect myself from getting pulled into feeling like I’m begging for attention or making a big deal out of nothing. If I stay on the surface, I can hold it together and not give him — or myself — that much.

I also knit, which is what I've been doing while lying in bed.  But I can't think of the last time I really truly enjoyed myself.
en_backup.internal:
[Perception] She sounds like she’s giving me the kind of answer people give when they don’t really know what to do with depression: “find hobbies,” “do something fun,” like I haven’t already tried to think of that. It hits the part of me that feels misunderstood and kind of invisible. I’m already lying in bed barely holding myself together, and the suggestion makes it feel like she thinks this is just a motivation problem or that I’m not trying hard enough. That stings because I am trying — I’m walking, I’m knitting, I’m getting through the day — and still nothing feels good. It makes me wonder if she really gets how flat and empty this is.

[Decision] I’m not going to pretend that advice is helpful just to be polite. I’m going to answer in a way that makes it clear this isn’t about not having ideas, it’s about not being able to feel them. If she wants to help, she needs to stop assuming the usual fixes fit me. I need her to understand that I’m already doing the little things I can, and they still aren’t touching how bad this feels.
