en_backup.client_response: I've been remote working for the entire pandemic. At first, it was great. I didn't go into the office very often before, so I felt relief from feeling any obligation to do so. But now I wonder if I am presenting myself well if my clients and coworkers have so much less personal interaction.
en_backup.internal:
[Perception] They’re inviting me to unpack what “feeling low” actually means, and the part that hits is the gap between how I intend to come across and how I may actually land in remote communication. I’m hearing that my concern isn’t just being lonely or tired; it’s this practical worry that without face-to-face cues, I may look blunt, impatient, or less capable than I am. The unresolved piece is whether the problem is mostly in how I’m writing and speaking online, or whether remote work itself is inherently limiting my ability to show nuance and value.

[Decision] I want to sort out what’s really causing the mismatch before I assume the worst about myself. If the issue is mainly communication style, then I may be able to adjust how I phrase things, slow down, add context, or make my intent clearer. If it’s more about the remote environment stripping away the signals that usually help me, then maybe I need to think more carefully about what can realistically be changed versus what I’m trying to compensate for. I’m trying not to jump straight to “I’m doing badly”; I want to figure out whether this is a perception problem, a communication problem, or a work-structure problem — because those would each call for a different response.

If I answer honestly, I have to admit I’m carrying guilt, and maybe that I’m not as in control or as right as I like to be.

[Decision] Keep it brief. Keep it factual. If I stay on the surface, I don’t have to open the whole mess up right now — the guilt, the defensiveness, the fear that if I say too much I’ll sound selfish or careless. “She gets the result this week” is safer. It lets me avoid the emotional part without having to say I’m avoiding it.

context_zh.speaker: client
context_zh.text: 我上周见了我妈，有一阵子没见了。她带我去吃早午餐。然后你们聊了什么？我哥呗。

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 她有没有注意到你……你看上去有多累？

context_zh.speaker: client
context_zh.text: 我化了点妆……其实化了很多。

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 所以你不希望她看到你状态不好。

context_zh.speaker: client
context_zh.text: 每次见她我都想看起来好看点。

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 为什么？

zh.therapist_turn_zh: 为什么？
zh.client_response_zh: 这样她会好受点。但上次就算我少条胳膊她都不会注意到。
zh.internal_zh:
<internal>
[Perception] 她把这事儿说得好像是什么天大的证据，证明我妈完全忽略我，好像我真的被严重冷落了一样。但其实就一顿早午餐而已。我们聊了我哥，老话题了。至于化妆——我就是想打扮好看点，又不是什么藏着掖着的大事。她就盯着最糟糕的那个解读，把这事儿搞得好像很大件事。

[Decision] 我打算把这事情往小了说。又不是遇到什么危险，就是累而已，有点夸张了。我妈没注意到每个小细节不代表她不在乎。要是我把它当个大问题，那就变成了一个我不得不处理的大麻烦，我不想那样。不如就说没那么严重，翻篇拉倒。
</internal>

context.speaker: client
context.text: I saw my mom last week for the first time in a while. She took me to brunch. And what did you talk about? My brother.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: Did she notice how... How tired you look?

context.speaker: client
context.text: I put on some makeup... A lot of makeup, actually.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: So you didn't want her to not see you at your best.

context.speaker: client
context.text: I always try to look good when I see her.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: Why?

en_backup.therapist_turn: Why?
en_backup.client_response: It makes her feel better. But this last time I could've lost an arm and she wouldn't have noticed.
en_backup.internal:
[Perception] She’s making it sound like this is some huge sign that my mom is completely missing me, like I’m actually neglected in a serious way. But really, it was just brunch. We talked about my brother, which is what we always talk about. And the makeup thing — that was just me trying to look nice, not some big statement about hiding. She’s focusing on the worst possible interpretation, and it’s making this feel bigger than it is.

[Decision] I’m going to keep this small. It’s not like I was in danger or anything; I was just tired and being dramatic. My mom not noticing every little thing doesn’t mean she doesn’t care. If I treat it like a huge problem, then it becomes this whole thing I have to deal with, and I don’t want that. It’s easier to say it wasn’t that serious and move on.

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 你一个人住吗？

context_zh.speaker: client
context_zh.text: 嗯，一个人住。

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 我开始做的一件事是给我在网上认识的几个人打电话聊天。大概两个月前开始的，真的帮了我很多，没以前那么孤独了。我得走出舒适区，因为平时我不是个爱打电话的人。

context_zh.speaker: client
context_zh.text: 你是怎么在网上认识他们的？

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 在脸书的群里。我开始和同一群人聊天，后来私信，再问他们能不能打电话。如果你也在群里，甚至可以问有没有其他人想交朋友。我是女的，所以只找了女性。

context_zh.speaker: client
context_zh.text: 我觉得自己很难在电话上和别人建立起联系。我这里现在已经没有限制措施了，我真的很想面对面认识一些人。

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 我也在想怎么在本地交朋友。也许你可以邀请别人来你家过圣诞节，当他们说已经有安排时，可能会意识到你一个人，然后反过来邀请你？

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 有没有哪个教会在圣诞节提供免费餐食？有时候这也是认识人的好办法，还能帮忙。

zh.therapist_turn_zh: 有没有哪个教会在圣诞节提供免费餐食？有时候这也是认识人的好办法，还能帮忙。
zh.client_response_zh: 可惜的是，这里大部分人圣诞节都和家人过，而且都比较封闭，不会邀请外面的人。去年我和一个朋友一起过的，但他今年要去他家那边。
zh.internal_zh:
<internal>
[Perception] 他们好像只是在给一些泛泛的“试试这个”的建议，根本没有真正理解我目前的处境。打电话那个完全不适合我，圣诞节的建议尤其不接地气——好像我随便请个人来家里，他们就会反过来把我纳入他们的家庭计划似的。这完全忽略了这里的人有多封闭，而且真正的问题是我需要真实的、面对面的联系，而不是一个凑合的替代方案。这让我觉得他们只是远远地扔出一些看似积极的解决办法，根本没有理解我面临的社交现实。
[Decision] 我不会假装这些建议有用，就因为它们听起来很关心人。我会礼貌地回答，但心里已经把它们搁置了，因为它们和我的生活状况对不上。我想要真实和本地的东西，不是一通电话或者一个关于别人会突然为我腾出空间的乐观猜测。如果他们只能给这些，那我必须保持警惕，别被带进那种假装这是严肃答案的节奏里。
</internal>

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: Do you live alone?

context.speaker: client
context.text: Yeah I do

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: One thing I started doing was calling a few people I met online on the phone to just chat. I started that about 2 months ago and it REALLY helped with my lonliness. I had to step out of my comfort zone as normally, I'm not a phone person.

context.speaker: client
context.text: How did you meet them online?

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: On FB in groups. I got to chatting with the same people, then began to inbox and then asked them if I  could call. If you are in a group, you could even ask if anyone else would like to connect as friends. I am a woman, so I just picked women.

context.speaker: client
context.text: I feel like I would struggle to establish a connection with someone over the phone. There are no restrictions in my city at the moment so I would really like to meet some people face to face

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: I was just thinking of ideas for me to make local friends too. Perhaps you could invite people to your home for Christmas, then when they say they have something occurring, perhaps they will realize you are alone and then invite you?

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: Are there any churches feeding people on Christmas? Sometimes that is a great way to meet others and help too.

en_backup.therapist_turn: Are there any churches feeding people on Christmas? Sometimes that is a great way to meet others and help too.
en_backup.client_response: Sadly most people here spend Christmas with their families and are quite private about not inviting outsiders. Last year I spent it with a friend but he is going to his family this year
en_backup.internal:
[Perception] They seem to be offering generic “just try this” ideas without really taking in what my situation is actually like. The phone thing doesn’t fit me at all, and the Christmas suggestion feels especially out of touch — as if I could just casually invite someone in and they’d somehow turn around and include me in their family plans. That ignores how private people are here and how much of this is about having a real, in-person connection, not a makeshift workaround. It made me feel like they were tossing out cheerful solutions from a distance, without understanding the social reality I’m dealing with.

[Decision] I’m not going to pretend those ideas are useful just because they sound caring. I’ll answer politely, but I’m mentally setting them aside because they don’t seem grounded in my life. I want something real and local, not a phone chat or a hopeful guess about people suddenly making room for me. If that’s all they can offer, then I need to stay guarded and not get pulled into acting like it’s a serious answer.

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 我同意这很糟糕！我住在美国，我们这边的数字又在上升，孩子们又开始在家上学了。我就一直觉得这是暂时的。

context_zh.speaker: client
context_zh.text: 是啊，我想想着可能不会持续太久确实有帮助，但我的朋友们好像比我应付得好多了，我也不太明白为什么这让我这么难过。我应该继续往前走，但动力很低。

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 我得说，找动力很难，我一开始也是那样。最近听说疫苗要来了，那是让我撑下去的东西。你能跟朋友出去吗？

context_zh.speaker: client
context_zh.text: 不行，因为我不应该和我家以外的人混在一起。我可能可以试着在线或视频跟他们见面——这事儿你经验多吗？

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 哦，非常多！Zoom和FaceTime现在是我最好的朋友。哈哈我觉得这就是我摆脱抑郁的原因之一，因为我们不能出去做任何事，我就开始更频繁地用了。

context_zh.speaker: client
context_zh.text: 有意思，所以你过去也得过抑郁？你自己是怎么走出来的？

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 我大概五月底下载的Zoom。头两个月最糟糕。我之前从没听说过Zoom，直到一个朋友说我们应该搞个虚拟派对，他组织的，有11个人在线。尽管这样，还是特别好玩。

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 也许组织一个“Zoom派对”就能让你心情好起来。

zh.therapist_turn_zh: 也许组织一个“Zoom派对”就能让你心情好起来。
zh.client_response_zh: 这建议确实不错。我也可以联系一下好久没见的朋友。我觉得这肯定能让我心情好起来。唯一的问题是，我对抑郁这事儿并不熟悉。万一它比这个更深呢？
zh.internal_zh:
<internal>
[Perception] 他们在说我多做视频通话、在线聚一下就行了，说实话这听起来确实有点道理——但我真正听到的是，我整个糟糕的状态都是被封锁和不能正常见人逼出来的。我的情绪不是凭空变差的，就是这种情况、这些限制、这种隔离，还有别人好像都比我应付得好。那段话击中了我。如果我觉得低落，那更像是环境造成的，不是我有什么根本问题。

[Decision] 所以我打算把它当成对被困在这些条件里的临时反应。我会试试虚拟派对的主意，因为它听起来挺实际，可能也有用，但我不会一下子就觉得我有什么更深层的毛病，就因为我眼下在挣扎。真正的问题是这个封锁生活、跟朋友断了联系，如果我能改变一点点，可能我的情绪也会跟着变。
</internal>

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: I agree it's bad!  Where I live in the US our numbers are going back up and the kids are being home schooled again.  I just keep thinking this is temporary!

context.speaker: client
context.text: Yes I suppose it does help to think it possible not for the long term but my friends seem to be dealing with it better than I am and I'm not quite sure why it's put me in such a sad emotional state. I should just get on with it but have very low motivation

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: I have to say it's hard to find motivation and I was in that spot at the beginning.  With news of vaccines being introduced here shortly, that's what's keeping me afloat.  Are you able to hang out with friends?

context.speaker: client
context.text: no not really because I'm not supposed to mix with people outside of my household. I could potentially try and meet them virtually online or on a video call is this something you've had much experience with?

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: Oh very much so!  Zoom and Facetime are my best friends right now.  lol I think that's one of the reasons why I snapped out of my depression is because I started doing that more since we couldn't go out and do anything.

context.speaker: client
context.text: Ok that's interesting so you have also suffered with depression in the past? exactly how did you get out of it yourself?

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: I downloaded Zoom around the end of May.  The first two months were the worst. I had never heard of Zoom until a friend said we should have a virtual party so he organized it and there were 11 on the call.  It was so much fun despite the fact.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: Maybe organizing a "zoom party" would start to lift your spirits.

en_backup.therapist_turn: Maybe organizing a "zoom party" would start to lift your spirits.
en_backup.client_response: that's a really good suggestion. I could also catch up with friends that haven't seen for a while. I think this would definitely work to boost my mood. The only problem is being depressed isn't something that I'm familiar with. what if it goes a little bit deeper than this?
en_backup.internal:
[Perception] They’re saying I could just do more video calls and a virtual catch-up, and honestly that does make sense a bit — but what I’m really hearing is that this whole awful state is being driven by the lockdown and not being able to see people properly. My mood isn’t just randomly bad; it’s this situation, these restrictions, the isolation, and the way everyone else seems to be coping better than me. That’s what hit me. If I’m feeling low, it feels like the circumstances are to blame, not that there’s something fundamentally wrong with me.

[Decision] So I’m going to treat this as a temporary response to being stuck in these conditions. I’ll try the virtual party idea because it sounds practical and it might help, but I’m not going to leap to the conclusion that I’ve got some deeper problem just because I’m struggling now. The real issue is this lockdown life and being cut off from friends, and if I can change that a little, maybe my mood will shift too.

context.speaker: client
context.text: But when I came back, the piano was gone and twin girls were there.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: Do you rember anything else about the separation?

context.speaker: client
context.text: My dad came to visit me every sunday. He'd bring my favorite candies. I liked those colored dots that were stuck to paper and those bottles filled with that sugary liquid. And he would show me pictures of the twins. And I would tell him that I missed them all and wanted to come home.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: But he didn't take you. Where was your mother?

context.speaker: client
context.text: I don't know. I mean, I'm sure she came, maybe at christmas.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: What about the rest of the time?

context.speaker: client
context.text: I went to school. It sure was different from Greenpoint, though. Gosh, it was so clean... And modern. And all the textbooks were new. I didn't really like the kids, though. I thought they were boring.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: Sounds lonely. Maybe that's why you gave me that casassette... Because I'd know how you felt when you were 10 and your parents made you leave. Maybe you thought if I listened to it back then, I would change my mind, let you stay.

en_backup.therapist_turn: Sounds lonely. Maybe that's why you gave me that casassette... Because I'd know how you felt when you were 10 and your parents made you leave. Maybe you thought if I listened to it back then, I would change my mind, let you stay.
en_backup.client_response: But I was difficult even then.
en_backup.internal:
[Perception] She’s trying to make my father’s visits and the candies and the piano into proof that I was abandoned, that I was a kid who wanted to come home and got left anyway. She’s also saying I gave her the cassette because I wanted her to understand the 10-year-old me and maybe change her mind about me. That’s the part that hit: if she sees me as someone who was just lonely and wanted to stay, then all the blame I’ve been carrying starts to wobble. And if I let that happen, then I have to feel how much it hurt that nobody took me home.

[Decision] No. I’m not going there. I was difficult. I know I was. That’s the line I’m drawing because if I stop saying it was my fault, then I have to admit I was sent away and nobody came for me, and I can’t afford that. Better to stay with the version where I was impossible than to open the door to being the kind of child who was wanted and still left behind.

zh.client_response_zh: 嗯，你看啊，当时我跟前任约会的时候，我跟她还有住在我岳母那个小公寓里的女人，我们仨搞过三人行。后来我跟前任没多久就分了，最后那个岳母公寓里的女人跟我结了婚。但前任就住在隔壁，她跟我老婆三天两头撞见，火花四溅的。搞得邻里之间挺尴尬的。
zh.internal_zh:
<internal>
[Perception] 治疗师刚就是直截了当让我跟他说问题，所以我想干脆把来龙去脉摆出来，而不是绕来绕去。关键是这一串人怎么都聚到这儿了：前任、公寓里那女的、结婚、然后前任住隔壁。我想让他明白这不是什么抽象的事——就是邻里间一堆糟心的碰面，主要这俩女的碰到一起就紧张。

[Decision] 所以我决定按顺序把整个背景交代了，想让治疗师知道，这些尴尬事只要了解前因后果就说得通了。我基本上就是说：情况就是这么个情况，很复杂，我都不觉得有啥解决办法，除非大家能好好相处——但这好像不太现实。我指望他能明白这更像是“忍着过”的事，不是什么简单能解决的难题。
</internal>

en_backup.therapist_turn: I'm doing fine, you can tell me your problems
en_backup.client_response: Well, you see when I was dating my ex she and I had a threeway with the woman who was living in my mother-in-law apartment at the time.   Well the ex and I broke up not too long after, and eventually the mother-in-law woman and I got married.   My ex lives next door though, and her and my wife bump into each other all the time and sparks tend to fly.  It's kind of awkward in the neighborhood.
en_backup.internal:
[Perception] The therapist just asked me to tell him my problems, plain and simple, so I figured I should lay out the actual setup instead of talking around it. What felt important was the chain of how we all ended up here: the ex, the woman from the apartment, the marriage, and now the ex living next door. I wanted it to come across that this isn’t some abstract issue — it’s an ongoing neighborhood mess with real awkward run-ins, and it’s mostly because these two women can’t seem to be around each other without tension.

[Decision] So I decided to give the whole backstory in order, because I wanted the therapist to see that the awkwardness makes sense once you understand the history. I’m basically saying: this is the situation, it’s complicated, and I don’t really know what a fix would even be besides everybody getting along, which doesn’t seem very realistic. I’m hoping he’ll get that it’s more of a live-with-it kind of thing than a simple problem to solve.

context_zh.text: 肯定管用。你只需要花点时间，找些好餐厅带孩子们去吃，建立点新习惯。我觉得你孤独不了多久，保罗。

zh.therapist_turn_zh: 肯定管用。你只需要花点时间，找些好餐厅带孩子们去吃，建立点新习惯。我觉得你孤独不了多久，保罗。
zh.client_response_zh: 但我就是想一个人待着。去年我有机会爱一次，结果我搞砸了。我不会再冒那个险了。
zh.internal_zh:
<internal>
[Perception] 她还在这儿说，这只是时间问题啊，习惯问题啊，好像只要我继续逼自己露面、带着孩子到处晃，就能有好结果。这恰恰最伤人——那种“我该重新敞开自己”的想法，尤其去年我以为自己抓住了什么又失去之后。“你孤独不了多久”根本不是安慰，是压力。意味着要再次去渴望一个人，暴露自己，然后又一次失望。我能感觉到她预设了我该努力去找另一个机会，可我不想要。我想要安静。我想要掌控。我不想因为怀有希望而觉得自己蠢。

[Decision] 不。我不会再那样做了。我在这儿划清界限：我不会再冒任何一次险，只为了最后尴尬、受伤、或者为自己守不住的东西抱希望。我宁愿忍受孤独，也不愿再承受被辜负。我不会再围绕“再爱一次”来构建我的人生。守着我已知的东西，比回到那种烂摊子里强。
</internal>

context.speaker: client
context.text: I promised to take him to a game if he ever comes to see me. Do you think it will work?

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: I'm sure it will work. You just need to take a little time, find some good restaurants for you and the kids to eat at, find some new routines. I don't think you'll be alone for long, Paul.

en_backup.therapist_turn: I'm sure it will work. You just need to take a little time, find some good restaurants for you and the kids to eat at, find some new routines. I don't think you'll be alone for long, Paul.
en_backup.client_response: But I want to be alone. I had my chance at love last year and I blew it. I'm not taking that risk again.
en_backup.internal:
[Perception] She’s still talking like this is just a matter of time and routines, like if I keep showing up and forcing myself into places with the kids, something good will happen. That’s exactly what hurts — the idea that I’m supposed to open myself up again after last year, after thinking I had something and losing it. “You won’t be alone for long” doesn’t feel comforting; it feels like pressure. It means risking wanting someone, being seen, and getting disappointed again. I can hear the assumption that I should be trying to find another chance, and I don’t want that. I want the quiet. I want control. I don’t want to feel stupid for hoping.

[Decision] No. I’m not doing that again. I’m drawing the line here: I’m not taking another risk just to end up embarrassed, hurt, or hoping for something I can’t keep. I can handle being alone better than I can handle being let down. I’m not going to build my life around another chance at love. I’d rather stay with what I know than go back into that.

context.speaker: client
context.text: Leah lets me down... all the time.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: How ?

context.speaker: client
context.text: Little things. And she's a flake. She'll show up an hour late or... she'll forget we've made a plan at all.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: But that doesn't bother you ?

context.speaker: client
context.text: No

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: And what's special about your relationship with Leah ?

context.speaker: client
context.text: I know she loves me. She's known me since I was six. Before I had done anything.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: So she loved you when you were a child. She led inside before you closed the gates.

en_backup.therapist_turn: So she loved you when you were a child. She led inside before you closed the gates.
en_backup.client_response: That's so depressing.
en_backup.internal:
[Perception] What I heard was: this is all about some lost version of me, some old innocence I can’t get back. That landed right on the part that already hurts — that Leah knew me before I got guarded, before everything got complicated, before I shut people out. And if that’s what this is, then it’s not really about the lateness or the missed plans at all. It’s about a thing that’s already gone. That’s what feels depressing: not just that she disappoints me, but that the only person who knew me that way belongs to a past I can’t return to.

[Decision] So I’m going to shut this down. If I let myself hope this means something fixable, I’ll just end up wanting what I can’t have — the old kind of being known, the easy kind of love, the version of me that existed before I had to protect myself. Better to call it depressing and leave it there. At least then I don’t have to reach for something that’s already been lost.

en_backup.therapist_turn: If he does find out the truth, are you afraid That he'll be no longer attracted to you?

en_backup.internal:
[Perception] He was trying to make this about me being scared Nate would stop wanting me, like I’m some desperate idiot who’s secretly panicking about being found out. That’s not what’s going on. What bothered me was him acting like Nate was the reason I was annoyed, when really Nate was just being a pain and I was over it. And I didn’t like him twisting it into this little story where I’m hiding the truth because I’m afraid of losing someone.

[Decision] I’m going to push back and make it clear that he’s off. I’m not going to let him pin some fear-of-rejection thing on me when I’m telling him I don’t care. If he wants the real issue, it’s that Nate was annoying and I was done with him, not that I’m sitting here worried about whether he’ll still be attracted to me.

en_backup.internal:

And the smiley “what I would do :)” came off kind of smug, like they think a better attitude is all this takes. It hit the part where I already feel powerless and made it sound like they don’t get how serious it is.

[Decision] Fine, if they’re going to talk like that, I’ll keep it light and a little sarcastic. I’m not going to hand them the full weight of how scared I am if they’re just going to give me obvious advice and act like they’re above it. I’ll steer it toward jokes and surface stuff because at least that keeps me from feeling stupid and judged.

context_zh.speaker: client

zh.therapist_turn_zh: 是的，旅行很棒，尤其是去看望你爱的人，那就更值得了。你享受和放松的时间需要经常有，这样我们才能重新振作，有自信有力量去面对每天的挑战。

zh.internal_zh:
<internal>
[Perception] 我听到治疗师想让我关注爱好、小奖励、让自己好受点的小方法，我知道他们是好意。但我真正抓着不放的是，我在这件事上并不是完全孤单，我还有姑姑可以期待，也许新药能在其他方法都没用的时候帮上忙。最触动我的是，即使我在做“正确”的事，一切还是感觉空虚而平淡。我可以走路、织毛衣、保持感恩，却仍然感受不到快乐。这让我害怕，因为它让我觉得自己坏掉了，而且不知道怎么修。

[Decision] 我决定保持礼貌和感恩，不去碰那些更黑暗的部分——这事到底有多难。我想把焦点放在希望上——我姑姑、药物、感恩——因为如果我让悲伤占满所有空间，我怕自己听起来不知感恩，或者让大家觉得负担太重。用祝福他们来结束然后继续，似乎比说出我内心仍然感到多么无望更安全。
</internal>

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: Today must have been a hard day for you. It seems that there are some things that are really bothering you.

context.speaker: client
context.text: The problem is I just don't really know how to feel better.  I have much to be thankful for but don't seem to be able to really enjoy anything.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: I am sorry to hear that. Sometimes even for a person like myself I try to find things that I love to do to keep motivated. Do you have hobbies or things that you like to do for fun?

context.speaker: client
context.text: That's what my husband keeps saying, too, but I just can't dredge up any enthusiasm for anything except I try to get out and walk because the fresh air is nice.  I also knit, which is what I've been doing while lying in bed.  But I can't think of the last time I really truly enjoyed myself.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: Yes, those are things that does make you day feel good fresh air, and knitting keeps you calm. Also, Have you tried buying a treat for yourself or going out for trip in the previous months to get some relaxation?

context.speaker: client
context.text: Yes, the idea of a trip is enticing to me and I really hope to go visit my aunt in Michigan, perhaps in April.  She is my mom's only sister and the only relative I have left from that generation and I love spending time with her.  That was a good suggestion and I'll try to look forward to that.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: Yes, trips are amazing and especially when you visit someone you love spending time with makes even more worthwhile. Time that you get to spend with enjoying yourself and relaxing is something that needs to happen often so we can get back in the fight to be confident or strong to face our daily challenges.

context.speaker: client
context.text: You have good insight and you are right, I need to focus more on enjoying the time I have with the people that I love.  I'm also hoping some new meds will eventually help  Thank you for listening

en_backup.therapist_turn: Yes, trips are amazing and especially when you visit someone you love spending time with makes even more worthwhile. Time that you get to spend with enjoying yourself and relaxing is something that needs to happen often so we can get back in the fight to be confident or strong to face our daily challenges.
en_backup.client_response: God's blessings to you and your family
en_backup.internal:
[Perception] I heard the therapist trying to get me to look at hobbies, treats, and little ways to feel better, and I know they mean well. But what I was really holding onto was the idea that I’m not completely alone in this, that I still have my aunt to look forward to and that maybe the new meds can help when nothing else has. What hit me most was how empty and flat everything feels even when I’m doing the “right” things. I can walk, knit, stay grateful, and still not feel joy. That scares me, because it makes me feel broken in a way I don’t know how to fix.

[Decision] I decided to keep it polite and grateful and not push into the darker part of how hard this really is. I want to keep the focus on hope—on my aunt, on the medication, on thankfulness—because if I let the sadness take up all the space, I’m afraid I’ll sound ungrateful or burden everyone with how bad it feels. It seemed safer to end with blessing them and move on than to say how hopeless I still feel underneath.

    {"speaker": "client", "text": "我也经常攒任务，结果作业堆成山，考试还撞在同一天。我不知道怎么才能不拖延。"},
    {"speaker": "therapist", "text": "对，一次只学一科。比如你觉得半小时学习时间足够，那就坚持半小时。时间一到就停下，直到下次安排再学。"},
    {"speaker": "client", "text": "好。非常感谢你分享这些想法。看来你也有过类似的学习压力经历。"},
    {"speaker": "therapist", "text": "拖延从来不会让我们感觉良好。如果我一直拖着不做，就会感到内疚。如果我设定一个目标并且达成了，就可以给自己一个奖励。比如，你每科学习半小时，三科学完就可以和朋友出去吃个酸奶。这样你就奖励自己坚持了目标。"},
    {"speaker": "therapist", "text": "是的，我经历过。哈哈，我现在真的很老了。这个技巧我用在生活的方方面面。就连家务，我也会分解成计划，写下来，然后核对完成的项目。这样我会为自己的成就感到快乐。"},
    {"speaker": "client", "text": "嗯，这也是我之前的疑问。听起来每门课只花一点时间很好，但我常常被压得喘不过气，需要休息一下。"}
  ],
  "therapist_turn_zh": "是的，我经历过。哈哈，我现在真的很老了。这个技巧我用在生活的方方面面。就连家务，我也会分解成计划，写下来，然后核对完成的项目。这样我会为自己的成就感到快乐。",
  "client_response_zh": "我从来没用过清单或计划表。我觉得这可能就是我容易不知所措的原因之一。",
  "internal_zh": "<internal>\n[Perception] 她一直在说什么整齐的时间表和打勾就能解决一切，老实说，这跟我实际被压垮的感觉很脱节。我听到的是“先做这个，再做那个”，但我的问题是我已经淹水了，然后我整个人就宕机了，所以她说起来比我自己做起来要容易得多。那个“哈哈我现在真的很老了”也让我觉得她是在一个完全不同的生活阶段给出建议，好像她根本不理解一个学生有六门课、考试堆积、没有心理空间去完美执行事情是什么感觉。这正好戳中了我已经觉得自己失败的部分，因为如果她的方案这么简单，那就会让我觉得可能我自己有问题，是我做不到。\n\n[Decision] 所以我有点想反驳，而不是假装被说服了。我不是故意要冒犯，但我不想只是点头附和那些理论上听起来很条理、在我实际生活里却不现实的建议。我宁愿承认清单和计划表让我感到不知所措，也不强迫自己进入一个我大概会放弃然后感觉更差的系统。如果她想帮我，我需要一些更小、更不刻板的东西，因为现在这个“完美结构化”听起来越完美，我越不可能真的去用。\n</internal>"
}

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: I remember after each class, I would take 15 minutes to review all my notes from class, that seems short, but really, it adds up and helped so much.

context.speaker: client
context.text: Yes, I think you have excellent advice about organization. I feel like I lose track of what I have and when to do it. I also bounce between classes, feeling stressed because there is so much. Do you think doing one class at a time is best?

context.speaker: client
context.text: I also tend to save stuff sometimes so I have a lot of work build up with tests on the same days. I am not sure how to stop procrastinating.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: Yes, stick to one subject at a time. For example, if you think 1/2 hour is good enough to study, then stick to that. When done, your done until the next time it is on your schedule.

context.speaker: client
context.text: Ok. Thank you so much for the ideas. It seems like you have had similar experiences with stress from school.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: Procrastination never makes us feel good. If I keep putting something off, I then feel guilty. If I make a goal, and I reach it, I can put a reward. For example, if you study 3 subjects 1/2 hour each, you can go out for yogurt with a friend. So you reward yourself for sticking to that goal.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: Yes, I did. lol I'm really old now. This technique I use in all my life. Even house chores, I break it down into a schedule, put it in writing, then check off what I do. Then I feel good about my accomplishments.

context.speaker: client
context.text: Yes, that was my other question to you. It sounds great to just do a little time for each class but I often get overwhelmed and need a break

en_backup.therapist_turn: Yes, I did. lol I'm really old now. This technique I use in all my life. Even house chores, I break it down into a schedule, put it in writing, then check off what I do. Then I feel good about my accomplishments.
en_backup.client_response: I have never used check lists or planners. I think it is part of how I get overwhelmed maybe.
en_backup.internal:
[Perception] She keeps talking like a neat schedule and checkboxes will solve everything, and honestly it feels kind of detached from how overwhelmed I actually am. I hear “just do this, then this,” but my problem is that I’m already drowning and then I shut down, so it sounds easier for her than it feels for me. The “I’m really old now lol” thing also makes it feel like she’s giving advice from a totally different life than mine, like she doesn’t really get what it’s like to be a student with six classes, tests piling up, and no mental space to do things perfectly. It hits the part of me that already feels like I’m failing, because if her solution is so simple, then it makes me feel like maybe I’m the one who’s broken for not being able to do it.

[Decision] So I kind of want to push back instead of pretending I’m sold on it. I’m not trying to be rude, but I don’t want to just nod along to advice that sounds organized in theory and unrealistic in my actual life. I’d rather admit that checklists and planners sound overwhelming to me than force myself into a system I’ll probably abandon and then feel worse about. If she wants to help, I need something that feels smaller and less rigid, because right now the more “perfectly structured” it sounds, the less likely I am to actually use it.

zh.therapist_turn_zh: 你在试图决定些什么事呢？
zh.client_response_zh: 我连从哪开始都不知道。
zh.internal_zh:
<internal>
[Perception] 她让我“开始”，好像这是个正常的、有清晰入口的问题似的，说实话这让我挺烦的。感觉太套路了——好像她听说了“复杂的关系”就打算用常规心理咨询问题来梳理。她可能根本不明白这有多乱：孩子、住处、过去那些事、谎言，还有——要开始就得把一切都炸掉，根本不存在什么干净的起点。这让我觉得自己没被看见，好像她站在那团乱麻外面，却让我替她整理清楚。

[Decision] 所以我直接堵回去了，什么也没给。因为我不想把这团死结扔给一个看起来随时准备把它简化的人。如果她要逼我走向某个显而易见的“那就做个决定”的答案——那我偏不让她轻松。我就继续含糊，直到我确定她到底懂不懂：这不只是一个决定，这是我整个人生。
</internal>

context.speaker: therapist

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: what sort of things are you trying to decide?

en_backup.therapist_turn: what sort of things are you trying to decide?
en_backup.client_response: I don't even know where to start.
en_backup.internal:
[Perception] She’s asking me to “start” like this is a normal problem with a neat entry point, and that honestly irritates me. It feels a little too generic, like she’s hearing “complicated relationship” and trying to sort it with the usual therapy questions. Maybe she doesn’t get how tangled this is — the kids, the living situation, the history, the lies, the fact that there isn’t some clean place to begin without blowing everything up. It makes me feel a bit unseen, like she’s standing outside the mess and asking me to organize it for her.

[Decision] So I shut down and gave her nothing, because I didn’t feel like handing over the whole impossible knot to someone who seems ready to simplify it. If I’m going to be pushed toward some obvious “just decide” answer, then I’m not going to make it easy for her. I’ll stay vague until I can tell whether she actually understands this isn’t just a decision — it’s my whole life.

en_backup.therapist_turn: You're a good doctor to your patients. You're a good father to your children. And you love singing.
en_backup.client_response: I'm a terrible singer, Gina.
en_backup.internal:
[Perception] She’s trying to make it simple: “Of course he was proud, look at your life, look at your work, look at how you show up for your kids.” But that isn’t what I asked, and it isn’t what hurts. It lands on the place I can’t settle—because “you are a good doctor” and “you are a good father” still doesn’t answer whether my father saw me that way, whether he said it, whether he felt it. If I accept her version too quickly, it feels like I’m letting the question disappear before it’s been answered. It also feels like she’s moving past the small, embarrassing truth that I keep needing proof.

[Decision] So I push back on the easiest part of her list. I say I’m a terrible singer because if I let that one stand, then the whole neat picture she’s drawing starts to feel false to me. I’m not ready to agree that her reassurance closes the gap. If I say “yes, he was proud,” I’m afraid I’ll be pretending, and losing the ache of not knowing would mean giving up the part of me that has been waiting for him to say it.

zh.internal_zh:
<internal>

</internal>

I will stay with the concrete fact: her door did not open. That is enough. I do not need to entertain these dramatic possibilities. zh.internal_zh:
<internal>
[Perception] 她试图把基督教的传播和“邪恶是人做的，不是上帝做的”这个观念连起来，然后想让我猜为什么这种说法有吸引力。我听到的是：如果坏事是人的责任，那人就可以为发生的事背锅，也许这样故事就有了秩序。这还戳中了我脑子里一直绕圈子的那个部分——罪责——好像总要有人负责，至少事情就不是随机的。但这感觉也像是个圈套，想让我说出比实际相信的更深奥的话，我不想被拽进一个我压根不信的宗教解释里。

[Decision] 所以我打算先用最怀疑、最直白的方式回答：也许人们就是喜欢被告知痛苦是有原因的，哪怕原因是“是你的错”。这样故事里就有了控制权。这是个愤世嫉俗的回答，但对我心里想的东西来说是诚实的。如果她想继续，可以继续；我不会假装我突然觉得这有什么精神意义。
</internal>

en_backup.therapist_turn: Not really. It's really just a subject like any other. You can choose to talk about it or not. Anyway, in the new testament God is always portrayed as being good and wickedness and evil is a human thing, a human problem. Actually, it's one of the things that's helped christianity to spread very quickly. Can you-- Can you think why?
en_backup.client_response: Because people like to feel shitty about themselves?
en_backup.internal:
[Perception] She’s trying to connect Christianity’s spread to an idea that evil is something humans do, not something God does, and she wants me to guess why that would be attractive. What I hear is: if badness belongs to people, then people can be blamed for what happens, and maybe that gives the story order. It also hits the part of me that keeps circling around blame—like if someone has to be responsible, then at least it isn’t random. But it also feels like a setup to make me say something more profound than I actually believe, and I don’t want to get dragged into a religious explanation I don’t buy.

[Decision] So I’m going to answer in the most skeptical, stripped-down way first: maybe people like being told there’s a reason for suffering, even if the reason is “it’s your fault.” That keeps control in the story. It’s a cynical answer, but it’s honest to what I’m thinking. If she wants to go further, she can; I’m not going to pretend I suddenly find it spiritually meaningful.

zh.client_response_zh: 当她终于从那里面走出来，她说她突然涌上一股感情，想要靠近我，但那时候我爸和我已经分不开了……我记得她用的词是“不可穿透”，说我爸从来没有原谅过她，他利用我俩的亲密来向她证明她有多失败。她说她内疚得要死，觉得自己不配拥有我，所以就一直躲着我。
zh.internal_zh:
<internal>
[Perception] 我听到治疗师简单地说，我有超过一年没有得到母爱，这句话砸中了，因为它把我心里知道但不想说得太赤裸的东西说出来了：我爸变成了我的一切，我妈在最初那段时间几乎是缺席的。这也触动了我内心里还是想让这个故事说得通，不想过多责怪任何一边。我爸不是出于残忍“把我抢走”——他是那个站出来的人，做了一切，保护了我，建立了成为我整个世界的纽带。而我妈，当她终于情感上回来的时候，已经站在那个世界外面了，内疚，觉得自己已经错过了机会。

[Decision] 所以我决定把整个过程直白地说出来，因为我需要治疗师看到这一切是怎么拼在一起的：我爸的照顾，我妈的崩溃和回归，以及他们的痛苦怎样焊进了我的童年依恋。我想让人明白，“不可穿透”的亲密不只是我选择了父母中的一方——它是在必要中形成的，然后成了它自己的屏障，一个我母亲体验为伤口的屏障。这样说感觉是唯一的方式，既能保留我爸的角色，又不假装我妈的失落和羞耻没有塑造这个家庭故事。
</internal>

context.speaker: client
context.text: He didn't try to get her professional help? Are you kidding? He was first generation. He would've been mortified to ask someone for help, to admit that his wife was crazy.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: So he took care of you during this time?

context.speaker: client
context.text: He did everything. He had too. She didn't even want to breastfeed.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: So, really, you weren't mothered for over a year.

en_backup.therapist_turn: So, really, you weren't mothered for over a year.
en_backup.client_response: When she came out of it somehow she did, she said she had this rush of feeling and that she wanted to be close to me, but by then my dad and I were just inseparable... I think the word she used was impenetrable that my father had never forgiven her and that he used our closeness to show her how she'd failed. She said that she was so guilt-ridden that she thought she didn't deserve me, and so she just kept away.
en_backup.internal:
[Perception] I heard the therapist say, in a simple way, that I really wasn’t mothered for over a year, and that landed hard because it put words to something I’ve known but haven’t wanted to make too stark: that my dad became everything, and my mom was effectively absent in that first stretch. It also touched the part where I still want the story to make sense without blaming either of them too much. My father wasn’t just “taking me away” out of cruelty — he was the one who stepped in, did everything, protected me, and built the bond that became my whole world. And my mother, when she finally came back emotionally, was already standing outside of that world, feeling guilty and convinced she had missed her chance.

[Decision] So I decided to tell the whole sequence out loud, plainly, because I needed the therapist to see how all of it fit together: my dad’s care, my mom’s collapse and return, and the way their pain got welded into my childhood attachment. I wanted it understood that the “impenetrable” closeness wasn’t just me choosing one parent over the other — it was something that formed out of necessity, and then became its own barrier, one my mother experienced as a wound. Saying it that way felt like the only way to hold onto my father’s role without pretending my mother’s loss and shame didn’t also shape the family story.

What’s still unresolved for me is whether the real problem is that I’ve lost interest in microbiology, or whether I’m just stuck because I’m scared of facing more bad results and proving to myself that I’m slipping. context.text: Yes I do but the task really is finished. Please press quit, I can't do it my end. Neither of us will get paid if you do not. Ten turns each and fifteen minutes .. we've done that.

en_backup.therapist_turn: Yes I do but the task really is finished. Please press quit, I can't do it my end. Neither of us will get paid if you do not. Ten turns each and fifteen minutes .. we've done that.

en_backup.internal:
[Perception] The therapist seemed to brush past the actual point of what I was asking. I was looking for a simple way to stop that brief anger when the memory comes up, and instead they gave a generic breathing suggestion like I am some highly emotional person who cannot handle myself. Then they suddenly shifted to ending the conversation and pushing me to do the survey, which made it feel like they were more interested in finishing the task than understanding me. That hit the part of me that wants this treated as a practical issue, not exaggerated or made into a big emotional exercise. It also made me feel they were not really listening closely enough to be worth taking too seriously.

[Decision] So I decided not to lean into their advice or treat them like they had some special insight here. If they are going to respond with something basic and then rush me out, I can just dismiss it and keep my distance. I do not need to act impressed or dependent on that. I can end it cleanly, keep my dignity, and not let their shallow response carry any weight with me.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: That is a difficult position to be in. It is a hard time, but there's always a way to persevere.

en_backup.therapist_turn: That is a difficult position to be in. It is a hard time, but there's always a way to persevere.
en_backup.client_response: yeah... i don't know ... i'm not sleeping well because i'm so worried
en_backup.internal:
[Perception] I heard the usual hopeful line — that there’s always a way to persevere — and it just landed like he doesn’t really get how stuck this feels. What I took from it was: yes, this is hard, but somehow I’m still supposed to push through and make something happen. That hit the part where I’ve already been trying for months and getting nowhere. The longer I look at the job search, the more it feels like the combination of the pandemic, being new here, and being out of work for so long has made me basically invisible. So when he talks like there’s a clear path forward, it just highlights how little I have to work with.

[Decision] I decided not to let myself get hopeful about this, because hope just sets me up to feel worse when nothing changes. It feels safer to stay realistic — which right now means assuming this is going to keep being hard and maybe not work out quickly, if at all. If I don’t expect much, then I don’t have to keep getting my energy up only to watch it drain away. So I kind of shut down and let the whole thing feel pointless, because that protects me from putting in more effort and still ending up disappointed.

context.speaker: client
context.text: I found out I'm losing my job on January 1.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: You lost your job? thats a tough situation. Is it due to covid?

context.speaker: client
context.text: No, not due to covid. It's a gig job, much like mturk, but the company is dropping people from my state on that date.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: I know its tough especially with the holidays and all. You have so many great skills and are such a hard worker I dont think you will have a problem at all finding something different.

context.speaker: client
context.text: I've been looking at other companies, but learning a new system after all these years is difficult.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: I remember a time I lost my job and felt my whole world crumbling but then I realized when one door closes another door opens. when those doors close it seems that its usually for the best because it opens the path for something bigger and greater for you.

context.speaker: client
context.text: That's true. I've thought about looking into new fields.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: Have you looked into some evening classes or maybe online schooling? I hear there are so many different options when it comes to online learning.

en_backup.therapist_turn: Have you looked into some evening classes or maybe online schooling? I hear there are so many different options when it comes to online learning.
en_backup.client_response: I was looking into that last night, but with covid,  classes have had to cut enrollment and are already full for next semester.
en_backup.internal:
[Perception] They’re trying to push me toward “just do something new,” but they’re not really seeing the practical side of this. I did look, and even the class option is already running into a wall because of covid and enrollment limits. That hits the part of me that’s already stressed about January 1 and how little room I have to make a bad move right now. It feels like they’re talking past the fact that I can’t just leap into a new system overnight.

[Decision] I’m going to keep it open for now and not promise anything I can’t follow through on. I don’t want to shut the door on changing fields, but I also don’t want to commit to some plan that isn’t actually available to me. Right now I need to protect my stability and avoid getting pushed into an option that won’t work.

judge.rationale: 对话无文化绑定或语言依赖，翻译后能保持合作态度与情绪强度。

context.text: No, it is not insomnia.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: Okay, are you drinking enough water and eating a healthy diet?

en_backup.therapist_turn: Okay, are you drinking enough water and eating a healthy diet?

en_backup.internal:

[Decision] I’m willing to start with what I can control. I can work on drinking more water and eating more vegetables, because if I take better care of myself maybe I’ll sleep a little better and have more strength for everything I’m carrying.

context_zh.speaker: client

zh.therapist_turn_zh: 你好，你怎么样？
zh.client_response_zh: 我感觉世界在我周围崩塌。
zh.internal_zh:
<internal>
[Perception] 他问我怎么样，我今天没办法用“我没事”来躲了。这句话撞到了我一直在扛着的那个部分——感觉生活里的一切都在滑落，好像我挡不住那股压下来的压力。说“我抑郁”和“世界在崩塌”，是我在触碰愤怒和封闭底下那种害怕和不知所措的感觉。孤独、关于孩子的想法、回忆、还有疲惫，一下子全涌上来。

[Decision] 我决定直接说出来，而不是敷衍过去，因为我厌倦了明明不好还要假装没事。我内心有一部分还是希望有人能理解这到底有多难受。承认这一点很难，但我想，如果我要得到任何帮助，就得让他看到我现在真的很痛苦。
</internal>

context.text: Hello how are you?

context.speaker: client
context.text: I am down feeling depressed

en_backup.therapist_turn: Hello how are you?
en_backup.client_response: I feel like the world is crashing down around me
en_backup.internal:
[Perception] He asked how I am, and I couldn’t hide behind “I’m okay” today. It hit the part of me that’s been carrying all this weight—feeling like everything in my life is slipping, like I can’t keep the pressure from coming down on me. Saying “I’m depressed” and “the world is crashing down” was me touching how scared and overwhelmed I feel underneath the anger and shutdown. It’s the loneliness, the thoughts about my kids, the memories, and the exhaustion all piling up at once.

[Decision] I decided to say it plain instead of brushing it off, because I’m tired of pretending I’m fine when I’m not. A part of me still wants somebody to understand how bad this feels. It was hard to admit, but I figured if I’m going to get any help, I have to let him see that I’m really hurting right now.

[Decision] 所以我决定忍着，不逼自己太紧。在我看来，跟老板谈还不是能安全做的事，因为如果说错话，我可能就会没工作。我告诉自己，暂时保持不动是更安全的选择，我的恐惧是不行动的有效理由。
</internal>

context_zh.text: 当你想起那个情景或想到那个人时，你会怎么做？

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 我当时最简单的方法就是培养了一个新爱好。我通过加入CrossFit把怒气发泄在前任身上，也和那个社群互动了。这帮我转移了对前任的注意力。

context_zh.speaker: client
context_zh.text: 我看到CrossFit确实帮了很多人。这是个好主意，但有点吓人。

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: CrossFit可能不适合所有人，但你觉得培养一个新爱好能帮到你吗？你最近有没有开始什么新爱好？

context_zh.speaker: client
context_zh.text: 我最近开始画画，挺放松的。

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 画画是个很好的爱好。我看得出来它很放松，也能帮你把情绪转化成实物。

context_zh.speaker: client
context_zh.text: 是的。我通常边听播客边画。是个很好的分心方式。

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 听起来你在爱好方面做得不错。你有没有尝试和其他人互动，比如艺术社群或者找朋友听听他们的反馈？

zh.therapist_turn_zh: 听起来你在爱好方面做得不错。你有没有尝试和其他人互动，比如艺术社群或者找朋友听听他们的反馈？
zh.client_response_zh: 我试过，但我朋友里没几个人经历过我这种处境，也不理解我的感受。
zh.internal_zh:
<internal>
[Perception] 他们基本就是说我该多跟人接触，但让我在意的是，我朋友就是不懂。又不是我无缘无故拒绝支持——问题是我身边的人没经历过这种事，所以他们根本没法理解我的感受。出轨、撒谎，还有瞒了好几个月，这才是真正的问题，每次我想起他就会被触动。

[Decision] 所以我不打算强迫自己向不理解我的人敞开心扉。我会继续画画和听播客，因为它们确实有用，而且不会让我感觉更孤独。如果别人没法站在我的角度理解我，那是他们的问题，不是我的。我已经被一个人背叛够了，不想因为期待那些不懂我的人给我安慰而再增加失望。
</internal>

en_backup.internal:
[Perception] When she said, “So you’re not running away from home?” it landed like she was oversimplifying everything I’d just said. I’d been trying to be careful and honest—that this isn’t me bolting, that the needs have changed, that I’m trying to do this responsibly. Her line made it sound like I was either denying some obvious abandonment or secretly fleeing, and that felt unfair. I could feel myself getting boxed into a story I wasn’t telling: not a mature transition, not a considered ending, just a child running. That wasn’t what I meant, and it mattered to me to correct it.

[Decision] I decided I had to push back and name it differently, because if I let her frame it as running away, then all the thought and grief and intention in this choice would get lost. I wanted to insist on my version: I’m moving out, not escaping. I’m trying to be truthful about the limits of what I can keep asking for, and I need that distinction to stand.

en_backup.internal:
[Perception] He’s trying to make my dad into the same kind of person as my mom — like everybody’s just “calm” or “scared” or whatever, and it all evens out if you look at it the right way. But that misses the point completely. My dad wasn’t just calm. He showed up. He knew what I needed without making it about him, without making me manage him. My mother was right there and still felt impossible. If I accept his version, then I have to soften how bad it felt, and I’m not willing to do that. Not in here. Not when I was the one in the bed, wired up, freezing, and needing my parents to be different.

[Decision] So I shut it down. I’m not giving him some neat explanation that makes my mother easier to tolerate, because that would feel like betraying what happened to me. I need him to hear that my father was the one who got it, and my mother didn’t. That’s the truth I can hold onto right now. If I let him blur that, then I lose the one person who felt safe, and I’m not ready to lose that.

I also heard “make him work hard” as a possible way to stop me from feeling so available, but I wasn’t sure whether that was strategy or just another kind of waiting.

What I’m stuck on is whether I’m preserving a real opportunity or just preserving an attachment. So for now I want to stop and examine that difference, because that seems like the unresolved piece.

context.speaker: client
context.text: Look, I have to admit sometimes, it's... It's flattering. I can't help but enjoy the feeling. But I told her no. I said, This cannot happen. You cannot go through that door. There are limits.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: Is that what upset you, that she was testing you?

en_backup.therapist_turn: Is that what upset you, that she was testing you?
en_backup.client_response: It's not that abstract.
en_backup.internal:
[Perception] I heard her turning this into some neat little story about me being “upset” because Laura was “testing” me, like that was the main issue. That felt wrong. What hit me was how she was flattening what I actually said — that I set a limit, that I told Laura no, that this is not happening. It’s not that I’m confused about whether she’s testing me; it’s that I’m not going to let her frame my response as some wounded reaction or some hidden game. I know there was something flattering in it, I admitted that, but that doesn’t mean I was inviting it or secretly playing along. I needed that distinction to be recognized.

[Decision] So I pushed back. I wanted to correct the record and make it clear that this isn’t about some abstract “testing” dynamic from her side — or at least not the part that matters to me. What matters is that I said no, I meant no, and I’m not going to let this get recast as if I’m some passive participant or as if my boundary was just me reacting to a challenge. I needed to hold on to the fact that I was clear, because if I let her define it her way, it starts sounding like I’m more complicit than I am.

When he said I wasn’t ever pregnant, it hit the part of me that had been holding on to possibility, and then the rest of it landed: the FSH level, the “probably never,” and that awful way he described women like me as if I were one more case he sees every week. Successful. No children. My age. Like I’m a pattern, not a person.

[Decision] So I laid out every detail because if I could make him see the whole chain — my mother insisting, the other doctor, the diagnosis, the language he used — maybe it would finally look as real and as humiliating as it felt. I wanted the therapist to see that this wasn’t just about being wrong about a pregnancy. It was about being told, bluntly, that the life I thought I might still have is probably not going to happen. And I said it plainly because I couldn’t keep pretending it was nothing.

context.text: Our time is up.

context.text: Can you wait a minute? Just sit down for a minute.

context.speaker: therapist

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: What if I come with you to the hospital?

en_backup.therapist_turn: What if I come with you to the hospital?
en_backup.client_response: Would you?
en_backup.internal:
[Perception] He’s actually offering to come with me. Not just talking about treatment like it’s something I should be able to force myself through, but offering to be there with me. That hits the part of me that’s been terrified of walking into the hospital alone, of having to face the whole thing without something holding me together. It also hits how much I’ve been trying to stay detached and act like I can manage this on my own, because needing help feels like losing the last bit of control. But what he said makes it feel less impossible. Less like I’m being asked to jump into it by myself.

[Decision] I asked, “Would you?” because I need to know if that offer is real. I need something concrete, not just sympathy or pressure. If he really means it, then maybe I can let myself need him for this one step instead of backing away again. I’m not hinting anymore because I can’t keep pretending I’m fine with doing this alone. I want help, even if I’m scared to admit it.

en_backup.internal:
[Perception] He’s asking the obvious version of the question, the one that lets him keep the whole thing tidy: “How are you feeling?” Like I’m supposed to hand over something clean and legible. What I actually hear is: tell me you’re hurt, tell me I got to you, tell me this mattered. And that hits the part of me that already feels exposed and tired of being looked at like a puzzle. If I answered honestly, I’d have to let him see how worn down I am, how much this has been gnawing at me, and that feels too close to giving him a grip on me. It would mean risking the conversation turning into fixing, probing, or convincing — all the things I’m not in the mood to be on the receiving end of.

[Decision] So I gave him my face instead of my feelings. “How do I look?” is safer because it puts the burden back on him and keeps me in control. He can read whatever he wants into that. I don’t have to say I’m angry, or hurt, or that I hate how much this all still gets under my skin. Brief is safer. Brief doesn’t invite him in. Brief means I’m still the one deciding how much of myself he gets.

context.text: What's your fear if you lose your job?

context.speaker: client
context.text: Very much so. If I lose my job I can't pay my bills and keep a roof over my head. In a good economy it took me over 300 applications, 50 interviews, and over 6 months to find a job.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: I think even if you lose your job, you would still be able to obtain resources through unemployment or even a stay at home temporary job from an employment agency while you look for another one or for your company to return to normal.

en_backup.therapist_turn: I think even if you lose your job, you would still be able to obtain resources through unemployment or even a stay at home temporary job from an employment agency while you look for another one or for your company to return to normal.
en_backup.client_response: I would hope so
en_backup.internal:
[Perception] They’re making it sound like losing my job wouldn’t be that catastrophic, like there are a bunch of fallback options and I’m probably overestimating how bad it would be. It hit the part of me that panics at the idea of not having income or having to go through another long job search. But if I let myself believe the risk is smaller, I don’t have to feel that fear as intensely.

[Decision] I’m going to go with “this would probably be manageable” and not let my mind jump straight to disaster. Maybe there really are temporary options or support if it comes to that. I’d rather keep this in the realm of a possibility than treat it like my whole life is about to collapse.

en_backup.client_response: I'm disgusted with my friend for cheating on her boyfriend. Am I right to feel this way?
en_backup.internal:
[Perception] The therapist’s question made me notice I’m not just having a feeling—I’m trying to figure out whether my reaction is “reasonable” or if I’m overreacting. What hit me is the conflict between my disgust at what she did and my worry that I’m being too judgmental, since it’s technically her relationship. I’m also aware that if I decide this means I should distance myself, that could change a friendship and make things awkward at work, so this isn’t just about the cheating itself.

[Decision] I decided to bring up the question as a kind of moral and practical check: am I allowed to feel this way, and what does it mean for how I should act? I’m trying to sort out whether my feelings are a useful signal that this friendship doesn’t fit my values, or just a reaction I should keep to myself so I don’t create drama. I don’t want to jump straight to confrontation, but I also don’t want to ignore something that genuinely bothers me.

en_backup.therapist_turn: Why would you not want to tell her about the results? They're good. They're the best possible outcome. They couldn't be better.
en_backup.client_response: She's dying, okay? How would you like it if you were dying and I came to you and said, hey, guess what. I get to live.
en_backup.internal:
[Perception] What I heard was that my therapist thinks this is simple now, like the hard part is over and I should just go see Tricia. But that’s not what this is. What hit me was the fact that the good news doesn’t help—it makes it worse. It means I have to bring something bright into a room that is already full of dying, and I can’t do that to her. There isn’t a version of this where telling her doesn’t hurt. There isn’t a version where I walk away feeling okay. So all the “you can now” talk lands like they’re missing the point completely: I’m still stuck, and this is still going to tear her up.

[Decision] So I shut it down. I decided not to go, because trying would just mean hoping for some clean, humane outcome that doesn’t exist. If I don’t go, at least I don’t have to watch her face change when I tell her I’m fine and she’s not. At least I don’t have to find out exactly how bad it feels to be the one who gets to live. Giving up on seeing her protects me from having to believe there’s a way through this. It feels easier to stay away than to go in there and watch everything break.

Part of me wants to get this off my chest and have it recognized for what it is: I got hurt, and I’m still trying to make sense of it. zh.internal_zh:
<internal>
[Perception] 她在说谭米本身并不是真正的主题——我对她的执念可能和某些更陈旧、未完成的事情有关，很可能和我父亲的离开以及母亲的崩溃有关。让我在意的是，她没有直接回答我的问题；她在让我考虑一个我不想建立的联系。如果谭米有联系，那就不只是一段关系、一个病人或一个巧合。那意味着现在终究无法和过去分开，而我坚持的“我的过去没问题”可能遗漏了重要的东西。

[Decision] 我问“谭米跟这有什么关系？”是因为我想要机制，而不是指责。如果能明白这个联系，我就能看出这到底是不是谭米的事，或者谭米只是那个旧事落脚的最近的位置。我在接受这个假设之前先检验它——因为如果真的有联系，我需要知道它是什么，但我不愿意在没有任何证据的情况下就交出我的全部故事。不过，我问是因为我内心有一部分确实想要答案，即使我没准备好接受它。
</internal>

en_backup.therapist_turn: It occurred to me that you're interested in Tammy Kent because there's something incomplete in your understanding of your father's abandonment and your mother's breakdown.
en_backup.client_response: And how does Tammy fit into this?
en_backup.internal:
[Perception] She’s saying Tammy isn’t the real subject by herself — that my fixation on her may be attached to something older, unfinished, and probably tied to my father leaving and my mother falling apart. What catches me is that she’s not answering my question directly; she’s asking me to consider a connection I’m trying not to make. If Tammy is connected, then this isn’t just about a relationship or a patient or a coincidence. It would mean the present is not separate from the past after all, and that my argument that “my past is fine” may be missing something important.

[Decision] I asked, “How does Tammy fit into this?” because I want the mechanism, not the accusation. If I can understand the link, then I can see whether this is actually about Tammy, or whether Tammy is just the nearest place this older thing is landing. I’m testing the hypothesis before I accept it — because if there’s a real connection, I need to know what it is, but I’m not willing to just hand over my whole story without some evidence. Still, I’m asking because part of me does want the answer, even if I’m not ready to like it.

Part of what they said hits the tension I’m dealing with: I’m already stretched thin with school, work, and my toddler, so anything social can feel like one more demand on my time. At the same time, I’m noticing that my default choice of solitude may not actually be helping me recover as much as I think it is. Maybe it’s more of a habit of protecting my limited energy than a real solution. I’m wondering whether I’ve been treating “busy” and “alone” as the safest options, even though they may also be keeping me from getting a different kind of relief.

[Decision] So I’m deciding not to dismiss the idea right away. I want to think through what kinds of sociable activities would actually fit my life instead of assuming “more social” means a huge commitment. Maybe something family-inclusive, low-pressure, or occasional could give me a break without taking me away from my responsibilities. I’m trying to figure out whether adding some connection could make me feel less overloaded overall, rather than just using every spare minute to disappear into solitude. That seems worth exploring because I don’t want to lose sight of my family or my degree, but I also don’t want my stress to just keep feeling inevitable.

It’s easier to act like none of it counts than to admit I’m standing there with nothing solid under me.
</internal>

[Decision] I’m not going to lean on this line of conversation for anything real. If they’re just going to mirror my feelings or tell me it’s stressful, then I’ll keep the important part to myself and keep looking for something more practical. I need actual steps, not someone nodding along while I’m panicking. If they can’t give me that, then I’m better off not wasting time pretending this is helping.

context_zh.speaker: client

zh.internal_zh:

[Decision] 我决定反驳，因为我不希望这件事被简化成一个效率技巧。我需要纠正那个印象——更好的休息结构本身并不能解决问题。我在心里说的是：对，那可能有帮助，但真正的问题是为什么我即使有了计划还是会拖延，如果我真想改变什么的话，我需要这个被处理。
</internal>

In my head, I’m saying: yes, that can be helpful, but the real issue is why I keep procrastinating even when I have plans, and I need that addressed if I’m going to change anything for real.

zh.internal_zh:
<internal>
[Perception] 她在让我具体说说原因，可我确实没有一件明确的事情可以拿出来说。这就很难解释——我没法说“发生了这件事，然后一切都完了”。更像是关系慢慢失去了火花。如果有个明显的原因，我或许知道该修复什么。但正因为没有，我就只能想：是不是十年夫妻都会这样？还是我错过了她不再在乎的某些信号？最刺痛我的是恐惧——担心自己不够好，没法让她继续对我有兴趣。

en_backup.internal:
<internal>
[Perception] She’s asking me to narrow it down, and I don’t really have a clean event to point to. That’s what makes this so hard to explain — I can’t say “this happened, then everything broke.” It feels more like the relationship just slowly lost its spark. If there was an obvious cause, maybe I’d know what to fix. But because there wasn’t, I’m left wondering whether this is just what happens after ten years, or whether I missed some sign that she stopped caring. The part that hits me is the fear that I’m not enough to keep her interested.

[Decision] I’m trying to make sense of whether this is a problem I can actually work on or if I’m just watching it fade. I don’t want to jump to “it’s over,” but I also don’t want to pretend things are okay. So I’m going to say the honest version: nothing dramatic happened, but the connection changed, and I’m trying to understand why. Maybe if I can figure out what’s missing — attention, conversation, closeness, effort — then there’s still something to do about it.

context_zh.speaker: client
context_zh.text: 你是在我危机最严重的时候介入的。

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 我猜，这次危机之前还有一次危机，再之前还有一次。一直追溯到……童年、越南、唐纳森一家、康妮的康复。康妮的康复？

context_zh.speaker: client
context_zh.text: 什么？我从没提过那件事。

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 你没提过，但我和娜塔莉在医院谈话的时候……她没权利那样让康妮难堪！她不是要让康妮难堪。她以为你已经告诉我了。

context_zh.speaker: client
context_zh.text: 我为什么要那么做？

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 人们做治疗的时候都会这样做。他们谈论自己的……生活。如果你妻子有物质滥用的问题……

context_zh.speaker: client
context_zh.text: 物质滥用？不过是霞多丽酒和几片药。她不是……康妮是个好妻子。她把家打理得很好。她照顾孩子。她把后方看得像老鹰一样紧。问题是从……是我的错。

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 什么是你的错？

zh.therapist_turn_zh: 什么是你的错？
zh.client_response_zh: 我总是不在家。我总是在出差。医生们从来搞不懂那是什么病。可能是……低血糖，或者莱姆病，某种化学问题。她情绪一上来就……就往下滑。
zh.internal_zh:
<internal>
[Perception] 他把一切都推回康妮的康复治疗上，好像我在藏秘密，让这一切在黑暗里烂掉。这刺痛了我。我感觉他在把她变成一个麻烦，把我说成是导致这一切的人。我需要他明白，这不是简单的喝酒或吃药的故事。康妮是个好妻子。我不停地离开，做我必须做的事，努力撑住一切。如果她在往下滑，不是因为我不在乎——是我总也不在，也许是身体上出了什么问题，他们漏掉了。

[Decision] 所以我就直说了：我不在家，我在出差，我累得要死，医生们也没给个真正的答案。我在告诉他这件事的轮廓，我觉得重要的部分——这是压力、距离和没人搞懂的化学问题造成的。如果他能看到这个，也许他会停止把康妮当作全部问题，也不再让我听起来像是故意忽略家人。
</internal>

context.speaker: client
context.text: You met me in the middle of a crisis.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: And my guess is, before this crisis there was another crisis and before that there was another one. And it stretches right back... to childhood, to Vietnam, to the Donaldsons, to Connie's rehab. Connie's rehab?

context.speaker: client
context.text: What? I never said anything about that.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: You didn't, but when I spoke to Natalie at the hospital... She had no right to embarrass Connie like that! She wasn't trying to embarrass Connie. She assumed you'd told me.

context.speaker: client
context.text: Why would I have done that?

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: That's what people do in therapy. They talk about their... lives. If your wife has a problem with substance abuse...

context.speaker: client
context.text: Substance abuse? It was chardonnays. And a few pills. She's not a... Connie is a great wife. She made a fine home. She took care of the kids. She watched the home front like a hawk. The problem started... It's my fault.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: What was your fault?

en_backup.therapist_turn: What was your fault?
en_backup.client_response: I was away so much. I was always traveling. The doctors never understood what it was. It was... maybe a hypoglycemia, or lyme disease, something chemical. She gets in a mood and... she slides downhill.
en_backup.internal:
[Perception] He was pushing everything back to Connie’s rehab, like I’d been keeping secrets and letting this all rot in the dark. That stung. I could feel him turning her into a problem, and me into the guy who caused it. I needed him to understand this wasn’t some simple story of drinking or pills. Connie was a good wife. I was gone constantly, doing what I had to do, trying to hold everything together. If she was slipping, it wasn’t because I didn’t care — it was because I was never there enough, and maybe something was wrong physically, something they missed.

[Decision] So I laid it out plain: I was away, I was traveling, I was exhausted, and the doctors didn’t give a real answer. I’m trying to show him the shape of it, the part I think matters — that this came out of pressure, distance, and something chemical nobody understood. If he can see that, maybe he’ll stop treating Connie like the whole problem and stop making me sound like I just neglected my family on purpose.

[Decision] 我决定继续追问时间顺序，因为我需要更清楚地了解这是怎么回事。如果是在葬礼之后，那么这些想法可能来自余波——空虚、自责、无力修复任何东西的感觉。如果是在更晚的时候，那我就需要理解是什么条件让它变得更糟，以及它现在是否仍然影响着我。我这么问，是因为我不想把每个黑暗念头都当成同一回事，也不想错过它下面真正发生的东西。
</internal>

[Perception] She said yes, but not then — which made me wonder if the timing matters more than the grief itself. I heard a possibility that suicidal thoughts weren’t just about losing David, but about what happened afterward, when the shock wore off and the consequences settled in. That hits the part of me that keeps asking whether what I’m carrying is really about failure, guilt, or something deeper that got activated once I was alone with it. I’m trying to figure out whether this is the kind of thought that shows up in grief as a reaction, or whether it signals that the grief crossed into something more dangerous.

[Decision] I decided to press on the sequence because I need a clearer map of what this is about. If it was after the funeral, then maybe the thoughts came from the aftermath — the emptiness, the self-blame, the sense of being unable to repair anything. If it was later, then I need to understand what conditions made it worse and whether it still has a hold on me now. I’m asking because I don’t want to treat every dark thought as the same thing, and I don’t want to miss what’s actually going on beneath it.

zh.client_response_zh: 嗯，我不知道。为什么这么突然就结束了？
zh.internal_zh:
<internal>
[感知] 他们根本没在听我说话。他们一直说“别怪自己”、“别放弃”，好像这样就能解决什么似的，但我在这儿，五年感情说没就没了。那个“我也经历过”的故事，感觉他们在说自己的事，对我有种轻视，好像我的痛苦只是需要熬过去的一个阶段。让我觉得他们根本不懂这事有多突然、多残忍——或者他们忽略了我最在意的部分，就是她在我付出一切之后还能这样对我。

[决定] 所以我不会把他们的建议当回事。如果他们继续用那些含糊的安慰和套话来敷衍，我就坚持我自己的想法：肯定有问题，我得弄清楚到底是什么。也就是说，我得看看她是不是出轨或者撒谎了，因为至少那是真实的。我不想从一个没经历这些的人嘴里听到什么“这种事常有，打起精神来”这种漂亮话。我受伤了，我不会假装他们的安慰就够了。
</internal>

en_backup.internal:
[Perception] They’re not really hearing me. They keep saying “don’t blame yourself” and “don’t give up” like that’s supposed to fix anything, but I’m sitting here with five years ripped out from under me. The “I’ve been there” story felt like them making it about themselves, and it hit me as kind of dismissive, like my pain is just a phase I need to get over. It makes me feel like they don’t get how sudden and brutal this was — or they’re brushing past the part that matters to me, which is that she could do this to me after everything I gave her.

[Decision] So I’m not going to lean on their advice like it means something. If they’re going to keep talking in vague reassurances and generic lines, I’m going to stay on what I actually think: something was wrong, and I need to figure out what it was. That means looking at whether she cheated or lied, because at least that feels real. I don’t want some polished “it happens, keep your head up” answer from someone who isn’t living this. I’m hurt, and I’m not going to pretend their comfort is enough.

en_backup.internal:
[Perception] They keep pointing me toward help, but all I can hear is that I’m supposed to somehow make time, energy, and dignity appear out of nothing. I’ve already got six children, no partner, no job, and not enough money even with unemployment. The idea of calling around or going to food banks just hits the part of me that feels completely worn down — like I’m already failing, and now I’m supposed to prove I deserve help too. It feels futile because everything I try keeps ending in the same place: not enough, not enough, not enough.

[Decision] I’m going to stop pushing myself to believe something will change right now. It hurts less to accept that things are bad than to keep hoping and getting disappointed. I’ll keep looking for work because I have to, but inside I’m shutting down a bit so I don’t have to feel the full weight of how impossible this is. If I don’t expect much, I won’t have as far to fall.

[Perception] 我听到治疗师把我经历的事情简化为“你迟到了”，好像这才是重点，狗只是个借口。我觉得这很不公平，因为我并不是在逃避治疗——我是在处理一只实际受伤的动物和一个不肯帮忙的司机。让我生气的是那种暗示，好像我就是随便选了迟到，根本不当回事，而实际上我困在一个糟糕的处境里，努力做正确的事。

[Decision] 我需要反驳，确保对方明白这不是随便不把预约当回事。我想纠正那种“我就是随便停下来”的印象。我需要他们看到我真的遇到了道德困境，迟到是那个困境的后果，不是什么态度问题或者不关心治疗。
</internal>

context.speaker: client
context.text: Well, anyway, I couldn't not stop, OK? So I yelled at the driver to make a U-turn so I can get to the other side of the street, but, shit, there's no U-turns. This idiot cabbie is telling me that wounded animals prefer to die alone just because he can't make a fucking U-turn. So I yelled, Please, can you stop, I need to figure out what to do, and then I looked at his dashboard and it's five to, and it's another 25 minutes to your office. It was incredibly frustrating.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: Sounds like it was.

en_backup.therapist_turn: Sounds like it was.
en_backup.client_response: Imagine, stop for a dog that may die anyway, and be very late.
en_backup.internal:
[Perception] I heard the therapist flattening what happened into “you were late,” like that was the main point and the dog was just an excuse. That felt unfair, because I wasn’t avoiding therapy — I was dealing with an actual wounded animal and a cabdriver who wouldn’t help. What got me was the implication that I just chose to be late like it was nothing, when I was stuck in a horrible situation and trying to do the right thing.

[Decision] I need to push back and make sure it’s understood that this wasn’t some casual disregard for the appointment. I want to correct the impression that I “just stopped” for no reason. I need them to see I had a real moral dilemma and that being late was the consequence of that, not some attitude problem or lack of caring about therapy.

judge.rationale: 对话内容涉及疫情和工作焦虑，无文化绑定或语言双关，可自然翻译成中文。

context_zh.speaker: 来访者
context_zh.text: 嗨，你今天怎么样？

context_zh.speaker: 治疗师
context_zh.text: 我还挺好的。外面现在日落很美。你呢？

context_zh.speaker: 来访者
context_zh.text: 那就好。现在因为疫情，我又焦虑又紧张。

context_zh.speaker: 治疗师
context_zh.text: 是啊，我也是。我爸刚生病了，等检测结果那会儿我担心死了。还好结果是阴性。

context_zh.speaker: 治疗师
context_zh.text: 还有其他让你担心的事吗？

context_zh.speaker: 来访者
context_zh.text: 听你这么说真难过。希望你那边顺利。

context_zh.speaker: 来访者
context_zh.text: 工作稳定是我担心的事。

context_zh.speaker: 治疗师
context_zh.text: 你现在在上班吗？

zh.therapist_turn_zh: 你现在在上班吗？
zh.client_response_zh: 在，但我们公司已经裁了10%的人。我感觉下一个就是我了。
zh.internal_zh:
<internal>
[Perception] 他们在问一个听起来很基础的问题，甚至有点疏离，好像想让我继续解释，但又改变不了什么。我说公司裁了10%的时候，感觉他们根本没意识到这事有多真实——感觉他们听到的“压力”只是另一个话题，而不是悬在我头上的威胁。而且他们一直这么笼统，让我觉得他们其实没什么具体能给的，只是聊天。这戳到了我脆弱的那部分，觉得已经孤立无援了。

[Decision] 所以我打算收着点，不给他们太多。如果他们继续这么抽象，我就不把全貌交出去，也不假装他们的问题值得一个长篇大论的回答。保持警惕总好过对现在看起来没什么用的人多说。
</internal>

context.speaker: client
context.text: Hi. How are you doing today?

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: I am doing pretty well. There's a beautiful sunset outside right now. How are you?

context.speaker: client
context.text: Good to hear. Stressed and anxious nowadays due to this pandemic.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: Yep. Me too. My dad just got sick and I was worried out of my mind waiting for his test results to come back. Thankfully they were negative.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: Is there anything else you've been worried about?

context.speaker: client
context.text: Sorry to hear that. Hopefully it works out.

context.speaker: client
context.text: Job stability is a concern of mine.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: Are you working right now?

en_backup.therapist_turn: Are you working right now?
en_backup.client_response: Yes, but my firm has already cut 10%. I feel like I would be next.
en_backup.internal:
[Perception] They’re asking a question that sounds basic and maybe even a little detached, like they want me to keep explaining myself in a way that doesn’t actually change anything. When I say my firm cut 10%, it doesn’t feel like they’re grasping how real this is — it feels like they’re hearing “stress” as just another topic instead of the threat hanging over my head. And the way they keep it broad makes me feel like they don’t have much concrete to offer, just conversation. That hits the part of me that feels exposed and already alone with this.

[Decision] So I’m going to keep this tight and not give them too much. If they’re going to stay abstract, I’m not going to hand over the full picture or act like their question deserves a big answer. Better to stay guarded than get pulled into saying more to someone who doesn’t seem especially useful right now.

zh.therapist_turn_zh: 是啊。

zh.internal_zh:
<internal>
[Perception] 他在让我看看改变生活，好像这是个真选项似的，但我只能看到数字和权衡。再搞是唯一能让我快速来钱的事，这点很重要，因为我在试着把自己弄稳当，而不是拼命挣扎还差得远。但这也刺痛了我心里那部分——我知道整件事都踩在线的错的那边，这念头一直压着我。我在试着想有没有办法能获得同样的安全感，又不用再进监狱或者失去菲奥娜，因为他这么一提，听起来好像我必须在现在的钱和以后的生活之间选一个。我还想不通的是，正经过日子怎么能赚够钱，让我觉得划算。

[Decision] 所以我就按自己的感受说出来：错的路更容易，我清楚怎么走，但我也知道那条路的终点。我不是说我就想要那个答案，我是说这就是我脑子里解不开的疙瘩——怎么才能弄出个真正管用的东西，而我又不信自己能走通干净的那条路。如果我说出来，也许咱们能真的看看缺了什么，而不是假装选择很简单。
</internal>

context.text: Thanks for coming in today. I guess you've, uh, sat in that seat with lots of people like me in the past.

context.text: Mm.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: Yeah. And you have some ideas about that and some experiences about that. So today I wanna- be good for us to talk about that and, um, I'm really interested to know what you've been thinking about in terms of what you may wanna change in your life 'cause we're gonna be working together for a while here.

context.speaker: client
context.text: Right. Neat. What, um, what have I changed, what am I—

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: What you've been thinking about, um, over the last little while about getting your life back on track. 'Cause I noticed you've—

context.speaker: client
context.text: I've been thinking about how easy it would be to deal P again.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: Yeah.

en_backup.therapist_turn: Yeah.
en_backup.client_response: I mean, I've been thinking about, um, how I could actually set myself up the right way doing it the wrong way.
en_backup.internal:
[Perception] He’s asking me to look at changing my life like it’s a real option, but all I can see is the numbers and the tradeoff. Dealing is the one thing I know can put money in my pocket fast, and that matters because I’m trying to get myself set up, not struggle and come up short. But it also hits the part where I know the whole thing is built on the wrong side of the line, and that’s what keeps hanging over me. I’m trying to figure out if there’s any way to get the same security without going back to prison or losing Fiona, because the way he’s framing it makes it sound like I’ve got to choose between cash now and a life later. What I can’t work out yet is how a straight life is supposed to pay off enough to make sense to me.

[Decision] So I’m laying it out the way it feels: the wrong way is easier, and I can see exactly how to do it, but I also know where that road ends. I’m not saying I want that answer, I’m saying that’s the puzzle in my head — how to build something that actually works when I don’t trust myself to succeed at the clean version. If I say it out loud, maybe we can actually look at what’s missing instead of pretending the choice is simple.
