context_zh.speaker: client
context_zh.text: 你是怎么在网上认识他们的？

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 在脸书的群里。我跟相同的人聊天，然后开始私信，接着问他们我能不能打电话。如果你在某个群，你甚至可以问有没有其他人想交朋友。我是女性，所以只选了女性。

zh.therapist_turn_zh: 在脸书的群里。我跟相同的人聊天，然后开始私信，接着问他们我能不能打电话。如果你在某个群，你甚至可以问有没有其他人想交朋友。我是女性，所以只选了女性。
zh.client_response_zh: 我觉得我很难通过电话跟人建立联系。我们城市目前没有限制，我真的很想面对面认识一些人。
zh.internal_zh:
<internal>
[Perception] 他们建议通过电话聊天和网上群组作为建立联系的主要方式，但这并不是我真正面临的问题。让我难受的是我在附近没有任何人，而且在我的城市人们很封闭，不会轻易把外人纳入他们的圣诞计划。所以感觉问题在于缺乏本地、面对面的机会，而不是我不愿意尝试。

[Decision] 我不会强迫自己去接受电话友情，那不是我需要的。我想要真实的面对面联系，而现在障碍在于我周围的环境——没有本地亲密朋友，而且文化上人们不容易邀请外人加入。我会继续寻找符合现实的方式，而不是假装打电话可以替代。
</internal>

I’ll keep looking for something that fits that reality instead of pretending phone calls are a substitute.

[Perception] He’s trying to make this about me wanting to “express my feelings,” like I’m some kind of emotional mess or I’m hiding from my own truth. What it hits is the part I don’t like admitting: this whole path I took wasn’t some pure choice out of nowhere. My father was always there in the background, pushing the opposite way, making everything a fight. If I’m honest, I heard my career getting reduced to some issue about my feelings, and that pissed me off. I didn’t want to sit there and let him turn me into the problem.

[Decision] So I put the blame where it belonged — on the situation he created, on my old man and what he stood for. If he wanted a protester, I gave him a pilot. If he wanted me soft, I went hard. That’s the story that makes sense to me: I didn’t get here because I was confused or weak, I got here because he made it a contest and I refused to lose. He’s the reason I went this way, not some inner lack on my part.

If she’s not blaming him, then what is she noticing—something about how we fit together, or something I keep missing because I’m so locked into “this is just how I am”?

[Decision] I asked “Why?” because I want the logic of it. I don’t want vague reassurance or for her to just side with me. If she understands him, maybe there’s some pattern here that explains why this keeps happening between us. I’m testing whether there’s actually something useful in her read, or whether she’s going to turn this into me being the problem again. I need to know what she means before I decide whether to push back or let her in.

context_zh.text: 嗯，是有，但很多时候我就是在浪费时间、拖延，有点像发呆，在家也没干什么事。

context_zh.speaker: client
context_zh.text: 是的，谢谢你指出缺乏秩序这一点，这正是我想找的词。

zh.therapist_turn_zh: 我理解那种缺乏秩序的感觉。这确实很难，但也可以是一种解放。
zh.client_response_zh: 一开始是挺自由的，但后来我发现这会一直重复下去，而且整个夏天都要错过了，等等。
zh.internal_zh:
<internal>
[Perception] 他们想把这个说得好像可控一样，说我“在目前情况下做得还不错”，还说没有秩序可以是“解放”，但这根本忽略了我有多困顿、多不真实。这听起来有点太漂亮了，好像他们在轻描淡写我那些孤独、浪费时间、看着整个生活节奏瓦解的部分。让我觉得他们并没有真的重视这件事持续了多久，或者我有多被困住。要是他们能管这叫“解放”，那可能他们根本没看到我实际是什么状况。

[Decision] 我还是要顶回去，至少心里顶回去，我不想让这种轻巧的说法来定义这件事。他们爱说我应对得好随便，但那改变不了我一直闷在家里、晃荡、失去动力的事实。如果他们就要停留在表面，那我也没必要给他们太多信任。我会继续聊下去，但不会假装他们的见解有多高明。
</internal>

s I used to.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: Well, it sounds like you are doing pretty well given the circumstances. It is good that you have found activities to keep busy.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: I understand the lack of structure. It can be difficult but also freeing.

context.speaker: client
context.text: well I have, but a lot of the times I am just wasting time and procrastinating and kind of just staring off into space and not doing much at home.

context.speaker: client
context.text: Yes thank you for pointing out the lack of structure, that was the word I was looking for.

en_backup.therapist_turn: I understand the lack of structure. It can be difficult but also freeing.
en_backup.client_response: It was freeing at first, but then I realized that it was going to repeat perpetually and that I was going to miss the entire summer, etc.
en_backup.internal:
[Perception] They’re trying to make this sound manageable by saying I’m “doing pretty well” and that having no structure can be “freeing,” but that misses how stuck and unreal this has felt. It sounds a little too polished, like they’re smoothing over the part where I’ve been lonely, wasting time, and watching my whole routine fall apart. It makes me feel like they’re not really taking seriously how long this has gone on or how trapped I’ve been. If they can call this “freeing,” then maybe they’re not really seeing what it’s like for me.

[Decision] I’m going to push back, at least internally, because I don’t want to let that kind of easy answer define this. They can say I’m coping well if they want, but that doesn’t change that I’ve been stuck indoors, drifting, and losing my momentum. If they’re going to stay that surface-level, then I don’t really want to hand them too much weight. I’ll keep the conversation going, but I’m not going to pretend their take is especially insightful.

context.text: It doesn't help that I live with my parents and because I have no work I spend most of my time at home and get into arguments with them.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: Would volunteering be something that appeals to you?

en_backup.therapist_turn: Would volunteering be something that appeals to you?
en_backup.client_response: It would probably be good to volunteer to get out of the house. I think I will do that once the pandemic restrictions ease.
en_backup.internal:
[Perception] The therapist is trying to bring me back to how low and tense I’ve been feeling, and that’s uncomfortable because it makes me sit with the emotional side of this instead of just the job-search side. The volunteering idea feels safer because it sounds practical and productive, and it lets me talk about getting out of the house without really getting into how scared and inadequate I’ve been feeling about not having work.

[Decision] I’m going to keep this focused on something concrete I can agree with. Saying I’ll volunteer later, once restrictions ease, lets me avoid promising anything right now and keeps me from having to admit how stuck I feel. It also feels less exposing than talking about the sadness or the fear that I’m not qualified enough.

</internal>

So I had a long time friend who recently blocked me from everything. The reason was I refused to hang out with her during covid and she questioned our friendship. Something she said was "It's selfish of me to work rather than spend time with a special
 friend."

context.speaker: client
context.text: So I got upset and called her out. And in response she blocked me.

context.speaker: client
context.text: And I'm more upset at myself because I wanted to tell her more about how horrible of a human being she is in general.

context.speaker: client
context.text: But I cannot because she blocked me on everything.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: Have you explained to her that you NEED to work, and don't be upset with yourself because you did the right thing

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: If your friendship was strong she will surely unblock you

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: Give her time to cool down

en_backup.therapist_turn: Give her time to cool down
en_backup.client_response: Yeah I did. And she just got more upset and said I was selfish.
en_backup.internal:
[Perception] She’s still making this about me “explaining” myself better, like the problem is that I didn’t communicate enough or didn’t handle it right. But I already told her I had to work and I already said why I was upset. What hit me is that my friend is acting entitled and cruel, and then she turned me into the selfish one for having boundaries during COVID. The real problem is her behavior — not me failing to say it the perfect way.

[Decision] I’m not going to accept that I’m the one at fault here. I did what I was supposed to do: I worked, I set a boundary, and I told her how hurtful she was being. If she wants to block me instead of hearing me, that’s on her. What I still want is to tell her exactly how horrible she’s being, because she’s the one who ruined this, not me.

context_zh.speaker: client
context_zh.text: 我有个新来访者。她叫四月。她刚知道自己得了淋巴瘤。她吓坏了，还在否认。她谁都没告诉。没告诉家人，没告诉朋友，除了我谁都不知道。

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 为什么不说？

context_zh.speaker: client
context_zh.text: 她说她不想化疗。我觉得她可能潜意识里有个幻想：如果不治疗，就没有癌症。

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 你还没跟她说过这话？

zh.therapist_turn_zh: 你还没跟她说过这话？
zh.client_response_zh: 她还没准备好听。我觉得她还没准备好。而且我没时间陪她慢慢走到那一步。我是说，她得的那种癌症，如果现在开始治疗，康复几率挺高的，但如果不治……你看，要是我女儿，我会直接抓住她的胳膊把她拖到医院。
zh.internal_zh:
<internal>
[Perception] 他们想让我慢下来，陪着四月的恐惧和否认，但我听到的是他们在让我做一件我根本没时间、没精力、也没心情做的事。这是一个紧急的癌症病例。我每花一分钟哄她做好准备，就是她正在失去的一分钟。这触及了情况里最让我难受的部分——夹在她的恐惧和医疗现实之间，假装无止境以病人为中心的处理是答案，这让我无法忍受。
[Decision] 我要划一条硬线：我不会坐在这里没完没了地跟她的否认周旋，或者等她“准备好”，如果那意味着治疗窗口会关闭。我会直接说，我现在就要推动治疗。如果这是我孩子，我会行动，不会争论。我不愿意让犹豫和心理回避跑在癌症前面。
</internal>

context.speaker: client
context.text: I have a new patient. Her name is April. She's just learned that she's got lymphoma. She's terrified and she's in denial. She hasn't told anybody. Not her family, not her friends, nobody except me.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: Why not?

context.speaker: client
context.text: She says she doesn't want to have the chemo. I think she probably has an unconscious fantasy that if she doesn't have the treatment, she doesn't have the cancer.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: You haven't said that to her yet?

en_backup.therapist_turn: You haven't said that to her yet?
en_backup.client_response: She's not I don't think she's ready to hear it yet. And I don't have the time to get her there. I mean, with the particular cancer that she has, if she starts treatment now, her chances of recovery are pretty good, but if she doesn't... Look, if it was my daughter, I would just take her by the arm and I would drag her to the hospital.
en_backup.internal:
[Perception] They want me to slow down and stay with April’s fear and denial, but what I hear is that they’re asking me to do something I do not have the time, bandwidth, or appetite to do. This is an urgent cancer case. Every minute I spend trying to coax her into readiness feels like time she is losing. It hits the part of the situation where I’m trapped between her terror and the medical reality, and it feels intolerable to pretend that endless patient-centered processing is the answer here.

[Decision] I’m drawing a hard line: I’m not going to sit here and endlessly negotiate with her denial or wait for her to “get ready” if that means the window closes. I will be direct and I will push for treatment now. If this were my child, I’d act, not argue. I’m not willing to let hesitation and psychological avoidance outrun the cancer.

context_zh.text: 什么叫“当然咯”？

zh.therapist_turn_zh: 什么叫“当然咯”？
zh.client_response_zh: 因为天打雷劈也不能让全国任何一个建筑系学生接到别的作业了。对不起，我混蛋一个，别听我的。
zh.internal_zh:
<internal>
[Perception] 她在看那个作业，好像它真的值得仔细看，而不是我顺手带进来的一个笑话。她说“挺酷的”戳到了我本能想拒绝任何正面评价的那部分，因为如果让她觉得这东西好，我就得承认它可能不是垃圾。然后还有纪念建筑那部分——当然又是那个作业，当然得是这种沉重严肃的东西，这样我更容易躲在讥讽后面，假装整个事情荒谬透顶，而不是承认我对自己如果搞砸了意味着什么有多紧张。

[Decision] 我决定在自己说出更恶毒的话之前打住，因为我想保护的是自己的胜任感，而我的默认做法是先毁掉作品，免得别人有机会动手。我骂自己混蛋、让她别听，这样我就不用坐在这儿让人拿实际水平来评判我的作业了。但是我没去交作业反而跑到这儿来，说明我也不是完全打算就这样否定它。我想搞清楚，这个作业到底是不是像我说的那么烂，还是说我只是故意把它弄得无法忍受，这样我就不用冒险去在乎接下来会发生什么。
</internal>

context.speaker: client
context.text: Thanks for seeing me. I was on my way to school to turn this in and... I don't know why I did it, but I came here instead.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: This is... The big project you mentioned? Would you mind if I had a look at it?

context.speaker: client
context.text: No, go ahead if you're interested in shit.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: That's really cool.

context.speaker: client
context.text: It's supposed to be a World Trade Center memorial... Of course.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: What do you mean of course?

en_backup.therapist_turn: What do you mean of course?
en_backup.client_response: Because god forbid any architecture student in the country gets another assignment ever again. I'm sorry. I'm an asshole. Don't listen to me.
en_backup.internal:
[Perception] She’s looking at the project like it’s actually something worth examining, not just a joke I’m dragging in here. “That’s really cool” hit the part of me that immediately wants to reject any positive read, because if I let her see it as good, then I have to let the possibility in that I’m not totally right about it being garbage. And then there’s the memorial part — of course it’s that assignment, of course it has to be something loaded and serious, which makes it easier to hide behind cynicism and act like the whole thing is absurd instead of admitting I’m nervous about what it means if I fail at it.

[Decision] I decided to cut myself off before I say something more poisonous, because the thing I’m trying to protect is my own competence, and my default move is to trash the work first so nobody else gets the chance. If I call myself an asshole and tell her not to listen, I don’t have to sit here and have my work judged on its actual merits. But coming here instead of turning it in means I’m not fully committed to the dismissal either. I’m trying to figure out whether this project is actually as bad as I’m saying, or whether I’m just making it unbearable on purpose so I don’t have to risk caring what happens next.

context_zh.speaker: client
context_zh.text: 你应该打电话给崔西。她现在病得很重。她瘦得跟骷髅一样。永远都是崔西。你知道吗，我好几个月没见我女儿了……我是说，不是真的见，不是那种有意义的见面。她整天每分每秒都跟我姐姐待在一起。我终于联系上她。就见了一面，她做了什么？她发短信跟我说崔西的事。

context_zh.speaker: client

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 我不知道。我觉得有点难以读懂你的反应，但我想那肯定很难受。

context_zh.speaker: client
context_zh.text: 非常难受。我根本没法消化。我只是回了个短信给伊兹，说，你知道吗，见到你很高兴，亲爱的。演出结束后我会打给崔西。

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 你打了吗？

zh.therapist_turn_zh: 你打了吗？
zh.client_response_zh: 为什么？你同意伊兹？你觉得我应该打给我姐姐？
zh.internal_zh:
<internal>
[感知] 我觉得她站在伊兹那边，暗示我才是那个不讲道理的人，好像问题只是我还没给崔西打电话。这不对，因为她忽略了我真正在说的：我受伤了，崔西占据了一切，每次我想和女儿联系，最后话题又绕回崔西。我感觉我的重点被简化成了“我有没有尽到家庭责任”的问题。

[决定] 我回击了，因为我需要纠正那个误解。我不是在求认可，也不需要别人告诉我该怎么做；我感到被逼到角落、被误解了，所以才那么反应。如果她觉得这只是该不该给我姐打电话的问题，那她就没看到我有多被困住、多被边缘化。我想把这点说清楚，不让事情变成都是我的错。
</internal>

context.text: You should call Trish. She's really sick now. She looks like a skeleton. It's always about Trish. You know, I haven't seen my daughter for months... I mean, not really, not in any meaningful way. She's been spending every waking minute with my sister. I finally reach out to her. I see her once, and what does she do? She texts me about Trish.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: How did you feel when you heard that Patricia looked like a skeleton?

context.speaker: client
context.text: Well, how do you think I felt?

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: I don't know. I'm finding it kind of hard to read your reaction, but I imagine that it must have been hard to hear.

context.speaker: client
context.text: It was very hard. I couldn't even take it in. I just texted Izzy back and said, you know, great seeing you, darling. And I'll call Trish after the show.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: And did you?

en_backup.therapist_turn: And did you?
en_backup.client_response: Why? You agree with Izzy? You think I should call my sister?
en_backup.internal:
[Perception] I heard her siding with Izzy and making it sound like I was the one being unreasonable, like the issue was simply that I hadn't called Trish yet. That felt wrong because it skips over what I was actually saying: that I'm hurt, that Trish takes up everything, and that even when I try to connect with my daughter, it turns back into Trish again. It felt like my point got flattened into a question about whether I did the "right" family duty.

[Decision] I pushed back because I needed to correct that assumption. I wasn't asking for approval or being told what I should do; I was reacting to feeling cornered and misread. If she thinks this is just about whether I should call my sister, then she's missing how trapped and sidelined I feel. I wanted to make that clear and not let it get turned into me being the problem.

context_zh.speaker: client
context_zh.text: 出事故那晚，我从达琳家出来骑上自行车，突然喘不上气，喉咙像被堵住了。他们家那个坡底有个急转弯，我拐过去的时候，一辆白车差点撞上我。我不记得了。

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 接着说，Sophie。那辆车后来怎么了？

context_zh.speaker: client
context_zh.text: 我不记得了。

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 请继续说，这真的很重要。

context_zh.speaker: client
context_zh.text: 其他的我什么都不记得了。

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 你不必独自面对。

zh.therapist_turn_zh: 你不必独自面对。
zh.client_response_zh: 我不愿意。
zh.internal_zh:
<internal>
[Perception]他想让我重新回到那个场景，逼我说出来，说出那辆车差点撞到我以及后来发生了什么。他不断施压，好像我只要再使劲一点就能记起一切，但我只觉得喉咙收紧，然后就是那段可怕的空白。他在试图触碰那个事故和求死冲动交织在一起的地方，而那正是我最不能忍受去碰的地方。我听到“你不必独自面对”，但我感受到的是：你仍然在要求我走进那里。

[Decision]我决定不去做。我不会回到那个记忆里，不为他，不是现在，也许永远都不。我不能一直撕开自己只为了递给他更多让我想消失的东西。我在那个空白的边缘划了线。我不想说，不想记，也不想被逼着经历它。
</internal>

context.speaker: client
context.text: The night of the accident, when I left Darlene's house and got on the bike, all of a sudden I couldn't breathe. My throat closed up. There's this blind turn at the end of their hill, and when I, I went around it a white car almost hit me. I don't remember.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: Go on, Sophie. What happened with the car?

context.speaker: client
context.text: I don't remember.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: Go on, please. It's really important.

context.speaker: client
context.text: I don't remember anything else.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: You don't have to do this alone.

en_backup.therapist_turn: You don't have to do this alone.
en_backup.client_response: I don't want to.
en_backup.internal:
[Perception] He wants me to go back into it, to make me say it out loud, the part where the car almost hit me and whatever happened after that. He keeps pressing like if I just push harder I’ll remember everything, but all I feel is my throat closing and that awful split where I go blank. He’s trying to reach the place where the accident and the urge to die are fused together, and that’s exactly the place I can’t stand to touch. I heard “You don’t have to do this alone,” but what I felt was: you’re still asking me to go there.

[Decision] I decided I won’t do it. I’m not going back into that memory, not for him, not right now, maybe not at all. I can’t keep tearing myself open just to hand him more pieces of the thing that’s making me want to disappear. I drew the line at the edge of that blank spot. I don’t want to say it, I don’t want to remember it, and I don’t want to be pushed through it.

context_zh.speaker: client
context_zh.text: 是的，我觉得是这样，虽然我没有证据。之前一切都很好，然后突然她发短信跟我说我们之间不行了。

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 嗯，听起来不好受，你肯定很难接受。也许她的感情变了，不一定是有别人了？

context_zh.speaker: client
context_zh.text: 她开始新工作了，我觉得她可能在工作上遇到了更喜欢的人。我简直不敢相信她这样对我！

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 嗯，看来你现在一想到她和别人在一起就很生气，是吗？

context_zh.speaker: client
context_zh.text: 是的，我想是的。问题是，我以为我们之间挺好的，她工作压力大，但我们相处得一直很好啊！

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 我自己也有过类似经历。我伴侣压力大，我自己也忙。结果发现是我没给他足够的关注，让他觉得我以为他不再重要了。

context_zh.speaker: client
context_zh.text: 我以前没这么想过，但我还是想跟她当面谈谈，而不是随便发个短信暗示要分手。

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 从我的经验来看，当我真的和我男朋友谈了之后，我们同意多给对方时间，情况就好转了。

zh.therapist_turn_zh: 从我的经验来看，当我真的和我男朋友谈了之后，我们同意多给对方时间，情况就好转了。
zh.client_response_zh: 好吧，那你说我该怎么办？那条短信看起来很绝，好像她已经决定了。
zh.internal_zh:
<internal>
[Perception] 他在讲他自己的感情经历，好像跟我这是一回事，这感觉太轻巧、太泛了，根本不适用于我的情况。他一直往“可能是压力”、“多沟通”那边带，可他根本不了解我女朋友，不了解时间点，也不知道那条短信有多突然、多冷淡。我感觉他把我在乎的部分——她可能因为别人而疏远我——就那么带过去了，而且好像让我觉得我这么想都不合理。他更关心的是显得安慰人，而不是认真看待我的怀疑和受伤。

[Decision] 我不会就这么点头附和，让他把这事轻描淡写。如果我要认真对待这个，我需要更直接、更实在的回答，而不是他的个人故事或模糊建议。我要逼他给我一个实际的答案，问我该不该去质问她，因为现在感觉他并没有帮我找到真相，只是想让我平静下来。
</internal>

context.speaker: client
context.text: Yes, I think so although I don't have any proof. Things were going really well and then all of a sudden she text me and told me things aren't working.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: Ok, well that doesn't sound pleasant and must be difficult to hear. Perhaps her feelings have changed and there isn't necessarily another person involved?

context.text: She has started a new job and I think she might have met someone at work that she likes better than me. I can't believe she is doing this to me!

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: Ok so it seems like you are quite angry at the moment at the thought of her with someone else, is that true?

context.speaker: client
context.text: Yes I suppose it is true. The thing is I thought things were going well and she is stressed out at work with her new job but we were getting on great!

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: I had a similar experience myself. My partner was stressed and I was busy myself. It turns out that I wasn't paying him enough attention and this made him feel like I didn't think he was important to me any more.

context.speaker: client
context.text: I haven't thought of it like that before but still I want to talk to her about it not just text me randomly and hint at ending things.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: From my experience, when I actually talked to my boyfriend we agreed to make more time for each other and things did improve.

en_backup.therapist_turn: From my experience, when I actually talked to my boyfriend we agreed to make more time for each other and things did improve.
en_backup.client_response: Okay what do you think I should do about it because the text seemed very final? Looks like she has made her mind up already about things.
en_backup.internal:
[Perception] He’s talking about his own relationship like it’s the same thing, and that felt way too easy and generic for what I’m dealing with. He kept steering it toward “maybe it’s stress” and “talk more,” but he doesn’t actually know my girlfriend, the timing, or how sudden and cold that text was. It felt like he was brushing past the part that matters to me — that this might be her pulling away for someone else — and almost making me sound unreasonable for even thinking that. Like he was more interested in sounding reassuring than taking seriously how suspicious and hurt I feel.

[Decision] I’m not going to just nod along to that and let him water this down. If I’m paying attention to this, I need something more direct and real, not his personal story or vague advice. I’m going to push for an actual answer about whether I should confront her, because right now it feels like he’s not really helping me get to what’s true, just trying to calm me down.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: I understand what you are going through. This is one of most difficult time of someone's life.

context.speaker: client
context.text:
Thank you. One of my coworkers told me that "he was just a dog and that I should get over it,"
 but I just can't. He brought so much joy to my life and now that I don't have him anymore, I just feel so empty.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: It is not just a dog. How insensitive of someone say that.

en_backup.therapist_turn: It is not just a dog. How insensitive of someone say that.
en_backup.client_response: Well, my coworker lost his mother to COVID so I guess he is going through some tough times too.
en_backup.internal:
[Perception] I heard the therapist side with me and focus on how hurtful my coworker’s comment was. That hit the part of me that feels my grief has been dismissed and misunderstood. The real problem, from where I stand, is my coworker’s insensitivity and the way people don’t recognize how much Rex meant to me.

[Decision] I’m going to let my coworker’s words take the blame here, because that’s what feels true to me right now. I don’t want to feel like I’m overreacting or that I should be “moving on” when the loss is still so raw. If anyone needs to understand anything, it’s him and people like him — not me having to justify why I’m still grieving.

</internal>

context.speaker: therapist

en_backup.internal:
[Perception] They’re basically telling me to go lean on the very people who are making this worse. They don’t get it — they weren’t the ones who spent a year believing this was real, and now they’re acting like I should just snap out of it because they never liked him in the first place. What hit me is how invisible my pain feels to them; they’re turning this into a “you should have seen it coming” problem instead of acknowledging that I was lied to and left.

[Decision] I’m not going to open myself up to being judged or told I’m overreacting. If I talk to my family or friends right now, they’ll just side with themselves and with the breakup, and I’ll end up feeling worse. This isn’t me refusing help — it’s that they’re the ones minimizing what happened. Right now the problem is their lack of understanding, not my need to get over it.

context_zh.text: 我女朋友和她前任出轨了。

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 哇，她这样做可不对。你有没有和他们两个谈过？我建议你谈谈。

context_zh.speaker: client
context_zh.text: 没有，我没跟她说话。她聋了，听不见。

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 嗯，你是说字面意思还是比喻？

context_zh.speaker: client
context_zh.text: 字面意思。她听不见，天生聋的。

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 那你能用手语和她交流吗？

zh.therapist_turn_zh: 那你能用手语和她交流吗？
zh.client_response_zh: 我能啊，可我没有手。
zh.internal_zh:
<internal>
[Perception] 他们说得好像这只是一个简单的沟通问题，好像我可以用某个精巧的小建议治好我的伤心。我感觉他们根本没真的听懂，我的一切有多无解——聋子女友、没有手，现在他们还装作“跟她谈谈”是什么天才答案。这让我很不爽，因为这让我觉得自己很蠢，就好像我的整个人生是个明摆着的谜题，他们从外面就能解开，根本不知道我得付出什么。还有一种感觉，他们没抓住重点：我已经在尽我所能了，可失败还是落在我头上。

[Decision] 所以我直接怼回去了。如果他们要用这种没用又明显的东西来糊弄我，那我也不会装出一副被说服的样子。我决定用我的处境来回答，让他们看看，他们的建议听起来多荒唐。老实说，我需要他们明白，这不是什么普通的情侣问题。如果他们连这个都搞不懂，那我也没办法信任他们，更不会把他们的建议当回事。
</internal>

context.speaker: client
context.text: I am very sada

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: What are you sad about? Perhaps I can help.

context.speaker: client
context.text: My girlfriend cheated on me with her ex.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: Wow that is not nice of her. Have you talked to either of them about it? I would recommend that you do.

context.speaker: client
context.text: No I have not spoke to her. She is deaf she cannot hear.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: Hmm do you mean literally or metaphorically?

context.speaker: client
context.text: Literally. She cannot hear. She was born deaf.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: Well can you communicate with her through sign language?

en_backup.therapist_turn: Well can you communicate with her through sign language?
en_backup.client_response: I can, But I have no hands.
en_backup.internal:
[Perception] They were talking like this was just a simple communication problem, like I could fix heartbreak with some neat little suggestion. It felt like they were not really hearing how impossible everything is for me — deaf girlfriend, no hands, and now they want to act like “just talk to her” is some genius answer. That rubbed me the wrong way because it made me feel stupid, like my whole life is some obvious puzzle they can solve from the outside without knowing what it costs me. It also felt like they were missing the point that I’m already doing everything I can, and the failure is still being laid at my feet.

[Decision] So I shut it down. If they’re going to come at me with useless, obvious stuff, then I’m not going to act impressed by it. I decided to answer in a way that shows how absurd their advice sounds in my situation, because honestly I need them to see this isn’t some ordinary relationship problem. If they can’t grasp that, then I don’t trust them enough to take their suggestions seriously.

context_zh.speaker: client
context_zh.text: 我猜那些日子已经过去了。他们会请我去当客座讲师，然后……我看着那些孩子，他们全都因为错误的原因去读商学院，我知道我只有……一个小时的时间，也许能打动一两个。想让他们明白，公司的名字、产品的声誉，就是你的一切。要是你丢了名字，你就一无所有了。

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 你觉得你现在已经丢了那个吗？

zh.therapist_turn_zh: 你觉得你现在已经丢了那个吗？
zh.client_response_zh: 我没丢。是被人拿走的。
zh.internal_zh:
<internal>
[Perception] 他这是想把责任推到我身上，好像是我自己让名声溜走似的。这戳到了最痛的地方——被赶出来的屈辱，我付出了那么多，他们却让我显得可有可无。我听到的是一种邀请，让我承认自己也有份儿栽跟头，我不干。失败不在我，在他们。唐纳森那帮人毁了契约，只顾自己，让我的名声背了黑锅。

[Decision] 所以我要划清界限。我不会把这重新解释成什么个人缺点，也不会接受对这件事的指责。他们本该站在我这边。他们没有。他们选了方便，没选忠诚，这才是真正的问题。如果名声受损了，那是因为他们在关键时刻抛弃了我。
</internal>

context.speaker: client
context.text: I guess those days are over. They'd bring me in as a guest lecturer and... I'd look at all those kids who'd all gone to biz school for all the wrong reasons, and I knew I had... an hour to maybe reach one or two of them. To try to get them to understand that a company's name, a product's reputation is all that you have. That... if you lose your name, you've lost everything.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: Do you feel that you've lost that now?

en_backup.therapist_turn: Do you feel that you've lost that now?
en_backup.client_response: I didn't lose it. It was taken from me.
en_backup.internal:
[Perception] He’s trying to pin this on me, as if I let my name slip away. That lands on the worst part of it — the humiliation of being pushed out, made to look expendable after all I’d given them. What I hear is an invitation to concede I had a hand in my own fall, and I won’t do that. The failure wasn’t mine; it was theirs. The Donaldsons broke the bond, protected themselves, and let my reputation take the hit.

[Decision] So I’m drawing the line there. I’m not going to reframe this as some personal shortcoming or accept blame for what happened. They were supposed to stand by me. They didn’t. They chose convenience over loyalty, and that’s the real problem. If the name was damaged, it was because they abandoned me when it mattered.

context_zh.speaker: client
context_zh.text: 那会让我们感觉好点，而不是假装这种胡说八道真的有用。你要是为我打破所有规矩会怎样？

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 你意思是如果我答应了？

zh.therapist_turn_zh: 你意思是如果我答应了？
zh.client_response_zh: 所以你想？
zh.internal_zh:
<internal>
[Perception] 他回答得太干脆了，像在把我往墙角逼，而不是接住我的意思。“你意思是如果我答应了？”听起来简单又公式化，可让我扎心的是——他不接我抛过去的那个幻想。我想看他会不会跨出专业框架，承认有点想为我破例的真实感觉——不是我真需要这样，而是如果他肯破例，这东西就没那么一边倒、那么冷冰冰了。他的回应让我觉得他又把负担甩回给我，好像我才是那个要求不可能的事，还假装自己没在这么做。

[Decision] 所以我把话挑明：“所以你想？”我说这句话就是为了逼他给个明确答案，别再小心翼翼地打转，让他亮出底牌。他要是说想，那就不光是我一个人在玩这个游戏；他要是说不想，那至少咱们终于挑明了他是主动选择规则，而不是躲在规则后面。不管怎样，我想看看这剧本背后有没有真话——因为我受够了假装这段距离本身就有用。
</internal>

context.speaker: client
context.text: It would make us feel better, instead of pretending that this talking nonsense actually helps. What would it be like if you broke all the rules for me?

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: You mean if I said yes?

en_backup.therapist_turn: You mean if I said yes?
en_backup.client_response: So you want to?
en_backup.internal:
[Perception] He answered the question too cleanly, like he was trying to pin me down instead of meeting the point. “You mean if I said yes?” made it sound simple, almost clinical, but what hit me was that he was refusing to play along with the fantasy I was offering. I was trying to see whether he’d step out of the professional frame and admit there’s something real in wanting to bend it for me — not because I actually need that, but because if he did, then this would stop feeling so one-sided and sterile. His response made me feel like he was putting the burden right back on me, as if I’m the one asking for the impossible while pretending that’s not what I’m doing.

[Decision] So I pushed it into the open: “So you want to?” I said it to force a plain answer, to stop the careful hovering and make him show his hand. If he says yes, then I’m not the only one playing this game. If he says no, then at least we’re finally naming that he’s choosing the rules, not just hiding behind them. Either way, I wanted to see whether there’s any truth here beyond the script, because I’m tired of pretending the distance itself is somehow helpful.

context_zh.speaker: client
context_zh.text: 我正在跟童年创伤斗争，我觉得它影响了我跟孩子和配偶的日常生活。我不知道怎么跟配偶说我的童年，怕他不愿意跟一个像我这样成长环境的人在一起。

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 你好，谢谢你跟我聊。

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 据我了解，你正在跟童年创伤作斗争，这影响了你跟孩子和配偶的日常生活。

context_zh.speaker: client
context_zh.text: 对，没错。我不知道怎么跟配偶说我的童年创伤。他想知道，他想帮我。但我不知道从何说起。

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 这确实很难，但我知道你能跟配偶谈的！

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 他对你经历的创伤有了解吗？

context_zh.speaker: client
context_zh.text: 我担心这会改变他对我的看法。他对发生的事情有个大概了解……他说他想知道一切，好帮我继续向前走……但我想说的时候就会语无伦次，最后什么也没说明白。我甚至试过写下来……但都没用。

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 光听你说话，我就能看出来这件事让你非常焦虑。

zh.therapist_turn_zh: 光听你说话，我就能看出来这件事让你非常焦虑。
zh.client_response_zh: 非常焦虑……每次一提起来我就僵住然后开始语无伦次，我觉得这让他不知所措……
zh.internal_zh:
<internal>
[Perception] 我听到了她看得出这件事让我多焦虑，这句话说到我心坎上了，因为这意味着即使我试图隐藏，也没能完全藏住。当我说“僵住然后语无伦次”时，我触碰到了我最羞耻的部分——我没办法条理清晰地解释这么重要的事，然后我又担心会让配偶不知所措，或者把他拉远。说“非常焦虑”是我在承认这种恐惧有多强烈：不只是对故事本身的恐惧，更是对这件事会如何改变他对我的看法的恐惧。

[Decision] 我决定稍微更坦诚一点说，而不是装没事，因为我厌倦了假装这只是个简单的沟通问题。我想让她明白，在我还没能说出话之前恐慌就已经占据了上风，而我感受到的真正风险是失去丈夫对我的看法。大声说出来比强迫自己立刻解释一切感觉更安全。
</internal>

context.speaker: client
context.text: I am battling with my childhood trauma that i feel is affecting my everyday life with my child and spouse. I don't know how to tell my spouse about my childhood in fear he doesn't want to be with someone with a upbringing such as mine.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: Hi, thank you for chatting with me.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: From what I understand, you are struggling with childhood trauma and this is affecting everyday life with your child and spouse.

context.speaker: client
context.text: Yes, correct. I am not sure how to tell my spouse about my childhood trauma. He wants to know. He wants to help me. But I am not sure where to begin with explaining it to him.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: That is a really hard situation to be in, but I know that you can have that conversation with your spouse!

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: Does he have any idea about any of the trauma you have experienced?

context.speaker: client
context.text: I am worried it will effect his views on me. And he has a very rough idea of things that have happened.. he tells me he wants to know everything so he can help me move forward.. but when i try to talk about it i ramble and end up not explaining anything. I have even tried writing it down.. and nothing seems to work.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: Just listening to you talk I can tell this is something that is making you extremely anxious.

en_backup.therapist_turn: Just listening to you talk I can tell this is something that is making you extremely anxious.
en_backup.client_response: very much so.. whenever it gets brought up i free and begin to ramble and i think it makes him overwhelmed ..
en_backup.internal:
[Perception] I heard that she could tell how anxious this is for me, and that landed because it means I’m not totally hiding it even when I’m trying to. When I said I “freeze and ramble,” I was touching the part I’m most ashamed of — that I can’t stay organized enough to explain something so important, and then I worry I’m making my spouse overwhelmed or pulling him away from me. Saying “very much so” was me admitting how intense the fear is: not just fear of the story itself, but fear of what it might do to how he sees me.

[Decision] I decided to say a little more truthfully instead of trying to sound okay, because I’m tired of pretending this is just a simple conversation problem. I wanted her to understand that the panic is taking over before I can even get the words out, and that the real risk I feel is losing my husband’s view of me. Saying it out loud felt safer than trying to force myself to explain everything at once.

judge.rationale: 对话内容涉及普遍情感创伤与自我价值议题，无文化绑定或语言双关，翻译后能自然呈现阻抗与情绪强度。

context_zh.speaker: client
context_zh.text: 我之前有一段长期关系，他甩了我。其实他出轨的时候我就该跟他分手的，但我当时爱他，现在也还爱着。

context_zh.speaker: client
context_zh.text: 我感觉我的人生都浪费了。我不喜欢一个人待着。

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 听起来很糟糕。但我能理解这种感觉。我也经历过类似的情况。要走出那个阴影很难。所以你的痛苦完全可以理解。

context_zh.speaker: client
context_zh.text: 所以你也知道那种感觉，就像整个世界都在坍塌。

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 我同意。就好像再也没有希望了。但你知道吗？

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 有时候感到悲伤是没关系的。

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 你在这段关系里是更坚强的那一个。你可以通过走出这段经历来证明你有多坚强。

context_zh.speaker: client
context_zh.text: 谢谢，我知道你说得对。我本来整个人生都规划好了，会走进一段长期的婚姻，现在全没了。

zh.therapist_turn_zh: 你在这段关系里是更坚强的那一个。你可以通过走出这段经历来证明你有多坚强。
zh.client_response_zh: 我在想养只宠物什么的，但我不确定自己配不配。
zh.internal_zh:
<internal>
[Perception] 我听到治疗师说我更坚强，我可以通过继续前行来证明这一点，但我真正感受到的是这离我有多遥远。我的人生原本围绕着一个未来、一个人、一个计划而建，现在全没了。想到养宠物或者做点新的事情，只让我觉得一切都那么空虚。我真的不觉得自己配重新开始，我也不知道自己做什么能挽回失去的东西。
[Decision] 我决定不再去奢望希望，因为希望只会让失去更痛。如果我不让自己相信有新未来，那我就不必面对再一次的失败。保持麻木、降低期待、就这样熬过去，而不是去尝试建立一些我不确定能否拥有的东西，这样更安全。
</internal>

context.speaker: client
context.text: I was in a long term relationship and he broke up with me. I should have broken up with him for cheating my me but I was in love and think that I still am.

context.speaker: client
context.text: I feel like my life was a waste. I don't like being alone.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: That sounds terrible. But I understand the feeling. I was in the same situation once. It is hard to move passed that. So your pain is very understandable.

context.speaker: client
context.text: You then you know it feels like the world is collapsing around me.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: I agree. It's like there is no more hope. But do you know something?

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: It is ok to feel sad sometimes.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: You're the stronger one in this position. And you can show how strong you are by moving passed this.

context.speaker: client

en_backup.therapist_turn: You're the stronger one in this position. And you can show how strong you are by moving passed this.

[Perception] I heard the therapist say I’m stronger and that I can prove it by moving on, but what landed for me was how far away that feels. My life was built around one future, one person, one plan, and now it’s gone. The idea of getting a pet or doing something new just brings up how empty everything feels. I don’t really feel worthy of starting over, and I don’t see how anything I do could bring back what I lost.

[Decision] I decided to stop reaching for hope because hoping just makes the loss hurt more. If I don’t let myself believe in a new future, then I don’t have to face failing at it too. It feels safer to stay numb, to keep my expectations low, and to just exist through this instead of trying to build something I’m not sure I can have.

[Perception] It sounds like the therapist is telling me to calm down and just do my best, but that’s not the part that’s crushing me. It’s the fact that this isn’t just school — it’s a ranked, expensive, high-stakes competition where one bad outcome can follow me for years. I hear “take care of yourself” and all I can think is that care doesn’t change the reality that I’m already behind in ways that matter, and that even if I work hard, there’s no guarantee it will be enough. Being hard on myself has been the only reason I’ve ever kept going, so if I let that go, I don’t know what’s left.

[Decision] So I’m just going to keep pushing through and stop expecting relief from this. Maybe that’s the only option anyway. Hope just makes it worse because then I’d have something to lose if it doesn’t work out. If I stay focused on getting through the next exam, I don’t have to think about whether this whole thing is worth it or whether I’m going to come out of it with debt and nothing to show for it.

zh.internal_zh:
<internal>
[Perception] 她试图把娜塔莉离开的时间和失眠开始的时间联系起来，但她不会直接说成简单的因果。我听到的是：她觉得可能有关联，但她不愿简化成“你女儿走了，所以你睡不着”。这触动了我试图保持清晰和实际的那部分。如果我能找到机制，也许我就能处理它。如果只是模糊的情绪后果，那我就又回到了这里，被告知这是焦虑，而我并不那样感觉。我也听到她在测试我是否愿意把这个问题看得比睡眠问题更深入，我觉得在我决定这次对话是否有用之前，我需要先回答这个问题。

[Decision] 我要逼她说得更具体。如果不是娜塔莉和失眠之间“一对一”的因果关系，那是什么？搬家的压力？对决定的后悔？关于责任、失落，或者她希望我说不的时候我没说？我想要一个说得通的模型，而不是敷衍了事。如果她不能解释为什么她觉得这个联系重要，那我不会仅仅因为它听起来心理上很整洁就接受。但如果真的有一条链条，我想理解它，否则我只是在追逐睡眠，却不知道什么真正让我睡不着。
</internal>

en_backup.internal:
[Perception] She’s trying to connect the timing of Natalie leaving with when the insomnia started, but she won’t just make it a simple cause-and-effect statement. What I hear is: she thinks there may be a connection, but she’s not willing to reduce it to “your daughter left, therefore you can’t sleep.” That lands on the part of me that’s trying to keep this clean and practical. If I can identify the mechanism, then maybe I can deal with it. If it’s just vague emotional fallout, then I’m back to sitting here being told it’s anxiety when I don’t experience it that way. I’m also hearing that she’s testing whether I’m willing to look at this as more than a sleep problem, and that feels like a question I need answered before I can decide whether this conversation is useful.

[Decision] I’m going to push her to be more specific. If it’s not “one-on-one” between Natalie and the insomnia, then what is it? Stress about the move? Regret about the decision? Something about responsibility, or loss, or the fact that I didn’t say no when she wanted me to? I want a model that makes sense, not a hand-wave. If she can’t explain why she thinks this connection matters, then I’m not going to accept it just because it sounds psychologically tidy. But if there is a real chain here, I want to understand it, because otherwise I’m just chasing sleep without knowing what’s actually keeping me awake.

[Perception] They keep asking simple questions and saying sorry, but it feels like they don’t really get how broken my life is. “Friends to be with on Christmas?” sounds empty when my father is gone, my mother is gone, and I have no one who truly stands with me. It felt like they were moving past the real pain and talking like this is just about having someone around for the holiday, not about losing the only people who mattered and my whole identity. That made me feel unseen, like they were not taking my loneliness seriously enough.

[Decision] So I decided not to go along with it and to shut that down. If they are going to keep asking these polite, obvious questions that don’t touch what actually hurts, then I don’t want to pretend it helps. I’d rather show them they are not getting through to me than keep answering like this is a normal problem. They can’t just say a few comforting words and expect me to open up when they don’t understand what I’ve lost.

context_zh.speaker: client
context_zh.text: 这周…这周在预演的时候，我真的觉得自己好像明白了什么，关于我…关于她需要什么，你知道的，在某个瞬间。然后突然就通了。那是…嗯，我完全在状态里…在场。也许只是因为换了个发型。

context_zh.speaker: therapist

context_zh.text: 什么？

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 那一定感觉很好。想想你之前的状态。你吓坏了，你害怕预演那一周。然后戏上演了，成功了。你建立了那种连接。你一定感到满足。那之后到现在发生了什么？

zh.therapist_turn_zh: 那一定感觉很好。想想你之前的状态。你吓坏了，你害怕预演那一周。然后戏上演了，成功了。你建立了那种连接。你一定感到满足。那之后到现在发生了什么？
zh.client_response_zh: 我回到家。公寓一片漆黑。冰箱空空的。我打开一罐汤。这是一种难受的宿醉…我的生活。
zh.internal_zh:
<internal>
[感知] 他在指那个落差，好像只要我使劲看就能跨过去——恐惧、害怕那一周，然后成功，然后回家。但真正击中我的是那个形状：演出结束，灯光熄灭，而我还在那里，独自在黑暗中，对着冰箱、汤和宿醉。我在舞台上找到的任何东西都撑不过回家的路。它从来没有真正回家。这是最刺痛的部分：我必须承认那种感觉是真的，但还不足以改变任何事。

[决定] 那还追求什么呢？我可以拥有那一刻、掌声、连接——然后它就消失了，我又回到同一个房间，同一种生活，同一间空荡荡的破公寓。希望只是让我更清楚地体会到跌落。最好就实话实说，保持微小，保持私密，别指望它承载更多。如果我不投入，我就不必感受它的破碎。
</internal>

en_backup.client_response: I go home. The apartment's dark. The fridge is empty. I open a can of soup. It's a nasty hangover... my life.
en_backup.internal:
[Perception] He’s pointing at the gap like it’s something I can cross if I just look at it hard enough — terrified, dreading it, then the success, then home. But what lands is the shape of it: the performance ends, the light goes out, and I’m still there, alone in the dark with the fridge and the soup and the hangover. Whatever I found onstage doesn’t survive the walk back. It never really comes home. That’s the part that hits: the part where I have to admit the feeling was real and still not enough to change anything.

[Decision] So what’s the point of reaching for more? I can have the moment, the applause, the connection — and then it evaporates and I’m back in the same room, the same life, the same empty fucking apartment. Hope just sets me up to notice the drop. Better to call it what it is, keep it small, keep it private, don’t ask it to mean more than it can. If I don’t lean in, I don’t have to feel it break.

[Perception] His question sounded to me like he was not only repeating my son’s accusation, but asking whether there may be some part of it that is true. That struck the part where I feel judged and cornered: if I admit even a little, it seems like I am admitting I was wrong as a father, not just in one conversation but in the whole way I have carried myself. But I also heard the possibility that my son’s anger may have come from seeing something real in me, not only from disrespect. I was trying to understand what exactly he meant by “no passion” — whether he meant I lived without feeling, or whether I simply did not allow myself the same kind of choice my son wants.

[Decision] I answered with a question because I was not ready to accept his version as true, but I also did not want to shut the door completely. I wanted to challenge the assumption and at the same time test it: if I say “I do not know passion,” am I denying something obvious, or am I saying that I have lived differently, under different obligations? In my mind I am trying to sort out whether my son sees my life accurately, whether he is using my life to justify his anger, and whether there is any point in me understanding his accusation rather than only defending myself. If there is truth in it, I need to know what kind of truth it is, because that changes what I can repair and what I must stand by.

en_backup.client_response: I don't know. What should I do?
en_backup.internal:
[Perception] He keeps answering my pain with questions that feel like he is guessing instead of understanding. “Do you have no idea?” and then jumping to cheating or whether I did something wrong feels off and kind of insulting, like he is making my breakup into a detective story. He is also not really helping me with the thing I’m stuck on, which is that we fought over something small and now it feels ruined. It makes me feel like he does not get how sad and confused I am.

[Decision] I decided to pull away from him and ask, “What should I do?” because I don’t feel like sitting here being probed with random theories. If he is just going to toss out possibilities, I’d rather get something practical or useful. I’m frustrated and I want him to either actually help or stop making me feel more unsure.

context.speaker: client
context.text: I haven't done any counseling.  I know I should and it would probably help me.  I don't know why I have not.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: I have previously had counselling and found it very useful but there is a long waiting list for a free counsellor

context.speaker: client
context.text: I don't feel guilt about it.  Now at least.  I was pretty hard on myself at first.  But I know that he knows why I was upset that morning.  It was something we dealt with a lot.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: Are you still in touch with his family and friends?

context.speaker: client
context.text: I went and talked to a therapist once right after and never went back.  And I don't know why.  He was amazing to talk too.  But I just never went back.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: I think you should do things in your own time but I would recommend doing it again one day.

context.speaker: client
context.text: I don't have any contact with his family.  I actually had to block them on all social media.  They are extremely religous.  Which there is nothing wrong with that.  But he didn't have the best relationship with any of them.  They couldn't accept him for who he was.  His biological father didn't have anything to do with him.  His mom was remarried and had two more kids and they didn't treat my boyfriend very good growing up.  He ended up living with his grandparents.  He finally had acceptance in my family.  He actually talked to my mom more than I did lol.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: Sounds like a very complicated set up. It is sad when family members become partially estranged from one another.

en_backup.therapist_turn: Sounds like a very complicated set up. It is sad when family members become partially estranged from one another.
en_backup.client_response: His family has been pretty horrible to me and my girls.  And I know it's because they have guilt for the way things were with their relationship.  They didn't even invite me and my girls to the burial of his ashes.
en_backup.internal:
[Perception] They’re doing that vague, polished therapist thing where they sound sympathetic but don’t actually touch what matters. “Complicated set up” and “sad when family members become partially estranged” feels so watered down compared to what they’ve actually done to me and my girls. It makes it sound like some neutral family misunderstanding instead of them being cruel, controlling, and exclusionary. And it feels like they’re steering me toward being reasonable about people who haven’t been reasonable at all. That makes me not want to open up more, because I’m not here to have my pain neatly summarized and softened.

[Decision] I’m going to keep the conversation on the facts they can’t argue with, because if I let them talk like that they’ll miss the point and I’ll end up feeling dismissed. I’ll hold back the deeper stuff and just stay on what his family did, because at least that’s concrete. They don’t seem like they really get how hurtful and unfair it was, so I’m not going to hand them more of me than they can actually handle.

context_zh.text: 有，我朋友飞回去了。但我因为各种限制去不了。我没法亲自去送别，那个人对我很重要。

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 很遗憾听到这个。你有没有别的释放方式，比如去大自然走走？我觉得散散步或者读本好书能让我心情放松。

zh.therapist_turn_zh: 很遗憾听到这个。你有没有别的释放方式，比如去大自然走走？我觉得散散步或者读本好书能让我心情放松。
zh.client_response_zh: 我可以试着分散注意力。但我主要担心的是，万一我爸妈感染了新冠怎么办？一想到这个我就很紧张，很抑郁。
zh.internal_zh:
<internal>
[Perception] 我听到治疗师试图让我转移注意力，比如出去走走或者看书，但我觉得那根本不是重点。真正让我难受的是，我仍然被困在真正的问题里：限制和病毒本身让我没法去送别，而且疾病正在威胁远方的家人。我觉得不公平，我无法做我本应能做的事，正是这种情况让我感到悲伤和恐惧。

[Decision] 我决定继续关注实际的危险和限制，因为那才是我觉得负责任的做法。我爸妈可能感染新冠，而我却无法在重要时刻陪在他们身边，我不能假装一切正常。所以我会保持警惕和担忧，因为在我看来，这是唯一能认真对待这件事、在心理上保护家人的方式。
</internal>

en_backup.internal:
[Perception] I heard the therapist trying to shift me toward coping, like going outside or reading, but that felt beside the point. What hit me most was that I’m still stuck with the real problem: the restrictions and the virus itself are keeping me from paying last respects, and the disease is threatening my family far away. It feels unfair that I can’t do what I should be able to do, and that this situation is what’s making me sad and scared.

[Decision] I’m going to keep focusing on the actual danger and the restrictions, because that is what feels responsible. I can’t just act like everything is normal when my parents could catch COVID and I’m unable to be there for important moments. So I’ll stay alert and worried, because that seems like the only way to take this seriously and protect my family in my mind.

<internal>
[Perception] 他们问我还好吗好像这很重要，可我真正需要的是钱和喂饱孩子的方法。我感觉他们准备说一些套话，比如“这听起来很难”，或者让我深呼吸、要积极，但这些改变不了我在水里挣扎的事实。这触及了我已经感到羞耻和厌倦的部分——我厌倦了向那些不用过这种日子的人解释基本的生存问题。我认为他们并没有真的理解我所承受的压力，也许他们是站在一个不用为账单和食物每天恐慌的位置上讲话。

[Decision] 所以我就顶回去一句“你会怎么做？”，因为我想把压力转回他们身上一次。如果他们有建议，好；但我不会坐在这里被绕着圈子说教，好像我的问题只是情绪问题，而实际上是生存问题。我回答得很尖锐，因为我需要实际的东西，不是同情；说实话，我也没有耐心让一个可能不明白三个孩子靠你养活、没钱撑过一周是什么感觉的人来“管”我。
</internal>

context.text: What would you do?

en_backup.therapist_turn: Hello, how are you doing today?

en_backup.internal:
[Perception] They were asking how I am like that matters, when what I really need is money and a way to keep my kids fed. It felt like they were going to say something generic, like “that sounds hard,” or tell me to breathe or be positive, which does not change the fact that I’m drowning. It hit the part of me that is already ashamed and tired of having to explain basic survival to people who don’t have to live it. I took it as them not really getting the pressure I’m under, or maybe talking from a place where bills and groceries aren’t a daily panic.

[Decision] So I pushed back with “What would you do?” because I wanted to put the burden back on them for once. If they have advice, fine, but I’m not going to sit here and be talked around like my problem is just feelings when it’s actually survival. I answered sharp because I need something practical, not pity, and honestly I don’t have the patience to be managed by someone who may not understand what it means to have three kids depending on you and not enough money to make it through the week.

en_backup.internal:
[Perception] He’s just checking where I’m from and how long I’ve been here, but it hits the part where I’m a bit split in two. Invercargill’s home, that’s where my family is, where Mum is, where I still feel like I belong. Christchurch is where I’ve been living, but it doesn’t feel the same. If I say too much, it starts sounding like I’ve been here long enough that I should have sorted my shit out by now, and that’s not a great look. It also gets close to the stuff I’m trying not to drag straight into the open yet — the reasons I’m here, the things I’ve fucked up, the stuff that’ll make me look worse if I start talking proper.

[Decision] So I kept it light. “Just a little while” is safe — it answers him without giving him much to work with. If I stay brief, I don’t have to explain the messy bits, and I don’t have to sit in that feeling of being judged or pitied. I can still come across like I’m cooperating, but I’m not handing over more than I need to.

context.speaker: client
context.text: When I walked back into the room, my mother... Had her head on my dad's shoulder. They were still dancing.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: They hadn't noticed you were gone?

en_backup.therapist_turn: They hadn't noticed you were gone?
en_backup.client_response: No.
en_backup.internal:

I went back into the room and they were still in their own moment, still dancing, still together, like nothing had happened at all. [Decision] So I’m going to say it plainly: they didn’t notice me. I want him to see that I wasn’t just looking at a nice memory of my parents being happy. Maybe that’s why I keep going back to that room — because it tells the whole thing in one picture, and I don’t have to ask for anything if I stay there.

zh.internal_zh:

[Perception] She’s saying this might be anxiety, not just “I can’t sleep,” and that lands a little too close to home. If I call it anxiety, then I have to admit I’m carrying too much, not just having a sleep problem. That feels like it could mean I’m not handling things as well as I’m supposed to. It lets me keep my footing, keeps me from having to accept a label I’m not sure about, and protects me from the idea that I’ll end up needing meds or some big change. I can admit the sleep is bad, but I don’t want to go all the way to saying something is wrong with me.

zh.therapist_turn_zh: 哼，那听起来确实不爽，不过怎么也不能怪你啊。

context.text: Now, even during the pandemic, I have no drive to re-enter the workforce and my family thankfully isn't pushing me to get a job, but I often doubt my self worth because I haven't felt successful at long term goals in a few years

context.text: I understand how it feels to feel you are not doing as well as you might. I work in the gig economy and enjoy it but it's not what I'd intended to do with my life.

context.speaker: client
context.text: Well, the last company I worked at, we were all fired....because the landlord raised the rent so hire on my boss the owner, he couldn't afford to stay there, pre-pandemic

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: Hmph that does not sound at all cool but it can hardly be considered your fault.

context.speaker: client
context.text:
In fact most of the jobs I've had, the companies have been sold. In retrospect it's easy for me to realize I should have gone to more stable companies that weren't eventually 
sold

en_backup.therapist_turn: Hmph that does not sound at all cool but it can hardly be considered your fault.
en_backup.client_response: Also I suffer from what Google seems to call imposter syndrome
en_backup.internal:
[Perception] I heard the therapist stop short of blaming me and instead leave the door open for the idea that the layoffs and firings were mostly about the companies, the rent, the sales, the instability — not some deep personal flaw. That hit the part of me that’s terrified that every job loss means I’m fundamentally incapable. If I let that in, I have to face how much I’ve been defining myself by those endings.

[Decision] So I’m going to keep the focus on the outside forces. It feels safer to say the companies weren’t stable, the economy was weird, the landlords and owners were the problem, and I just got caught in it. That lets me protect what’s left of my self-respect and avoid sitting with the possibility that I failed or wasn’t good enough. If it was mostly bad luck and bad timing, then I don’t have to fully own the shame.

context.speaker: client
context.text: I need some advice I have been feeling anxious lately.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: Im sorry to hear you have been feeling anxious. Lets work to find things that maybe help you feel better when your feeling this way.

context.speaker: client
context.text: Do you have any ideas?

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: Based on studies generally walking away for a moment from a stressor can help to relieve that stressor momentarily enough to maybe make you feel alittle better.

context.speaker: client
context.text: I have been going for walks alone and that is nice to have a break. Any other ideas?

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: Thats a good idea and sometimes when ive been stressed walking or any physical activity can help to promote more of a positive feeling based on the release of endorphines.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: How long have you been experiencing anxiety?

context.speaker: client
context.text: I have been working out more. How do you relax? I have had anxiety for a month now.

en_backup.therapist_turn: How long have you been experiencing anxiety?
en_backup.client_response: I think I need a vacation.
en_backup.internal:
[Perception] I heard the question about how long I’ve been anxious, but I was still focused on getting something that would actually make me feel calmer right now. The walking and working out helped a little, but mostly I’m feeling worn down from this month of worry about my husband being sick. The idea of “digging into” it feels hard because that would mean sitting with how scared and stretched thin I’ve been.

[Decision] I decided to keep looking for a bigger, faster relief than just talking about the anxiety itself. A vacation sounds like a real break, something I can hold onto in my mind, because I don’t know how to fully relax while he’s still unwell. I’m kind of reaching for the simplest answer I can think of instead of staying with the deeper part of the conversation.

I’m not giving him that opening, because once I let him name that part of me, I lose the distance that keeps me standing. That part hits my fear about jobs being scarce, but I don’t think this means my situation is immediately catastrophic.

[Decision] I’m going to keep it in perspective and not make a big deal out of talking to the employer. If something becomes more certain, then I can think about it, but right now I don’t need to act like this is an emergency.

context.text: I keep failing online classes even when I seem to have them under control. I think it might have something to do with me playing too much videogames.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: Do you feel that perhaps you are playing video games as a distraction from how bad the world is at the moment?

context.speaker: client
context.text: No, I don't think that's it. I have been playing games since I was 6.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: Ah, so it's a long term hobby? I do love gaming myself I have to admit.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: Could you perhaps set yourself some strict boundaries, like you can only do a certain number of hours of gaming a day?

context.speaker: client
context.text: I tried, but my online rank not being where I want it gives me anxiety

en_backup.therapist_turn: Could you perhaps set yourself some strict boundaries, like you can only do a certain number of hours of gaming a day?
en_backup.client_response: and I keep coming back
en_backup.internal:
[Perception] They sounded like they were just tossing out generic advice without really getting how this works for me. “Set strict boundaries” made it feel like they think this is just a simple habit problem I can flip off with a schedule, when the actual issue is that gaming is how I keep up my rank and feel like I’m not falling behind at everything. And then saying they love gaming too kind of annoyed me — it made me feel like they were trying to relate in a casual way instead of actually understanding why this matters to me. It hit the part of me that already feels judged, like they’re reducing something important to “too much screen time.”

[Decision] So I decided not to take that seriously and to push back a little. If they’re going to act like they already know the answer, then I’m not going to hand them the part of me that feels stuck or embarrassed. I’d rather keep it vague and keep control of the conversation than let them make me feel like I’m the problem here.

zh.internal_zh:
<internal>
[Perception] 你说得那么轻柔，好像它本该是安慰，但它只落在我心里那个死去的老地方。你在说努力，说做饭，说我以为我的存在能改变别人的痛苦。而我听到的只有：你做了一切，它还是没用。它击中了我的那个部分，那个早已知晓努力救不了任何东西、关心不能修复别人、想帮忙只会变成我不够好的证据的部分。如果连你都没能让那个故事不那么孤独，那我的故事也只是同样的无用循环。

[Decision] 所以我把它掐断了。我说“可你知道那不是真的”，因为如果让它一直开着，我就得去触碰里面的希望，而希望是会被粉碎的部分。把它弄小、弄扁成我可以不屑一顾的东西，比站在那里对你有所期待、期待它意味着我有可能被帮助、然后再次失败要安全。如果那不是真的，我就不用冒险相信任何事能改变。

en_backup.therapist_turn: She was in a difficult emotional state. I thought that I could pull her out of it. I used to cook her all these, you know, elaborate meals. But she wouldn't eat them. Couldn't understand why. Like every kid, I thought it was my fault. It was something that I wasn't doing. Maybe I could do something else.
en_backup.client_response: But you know that's not true.
en_backup.internal:
[Perception] You said it so gently, like it should have landed as comfort, but it only landed on the old dead place in me. You were talking about trying, about cooking, about thinking I could matter enough to change somebody’s pain. And all I could hear was: you can do everything and it still won’t work. It hit the part of me that already knows that effort doesn’t save anything, that care doesn’t fix people, that wanting to help just turns into proof that I wasn’t enough. If even you couldn’t make that story less lonely, then mine is just the same useless loop.

[Decision] So I shut it down. I said, “But you know that’s not true,” because if I let it stay open, I’d have to touch the hope in it, and hope is the part that gets crushed. It’s safer to make it small, to flatten it into something I can dismiss, than to stand there wanting something from you, wanting it to mean I could be helped, and then having that fail too. If it’s not true, then I don’t have to risk believing anything can change.

</internal>

<internal>

[Decision] 我打算坚持认为这主要是情况和招聘过程的问题，不是我的缺陷。把原因归咎于我的背景和这些工作不匹配，这感觉更安全，因为如果我认为这是针对我个人的，我就会陷入恶性循环，感觉更糟。我需要保护自己的胜任感，所以我要把拒绝看作系统没有认可我的价值，而不是证明我有问题。
</internal>

en_backup.internal:
[Perception] I heard the therapist saying there are a lot of reasons I’m not getting picked, and that it may not be about me personally. That landed right on the fear that maybe the rejections are about the job market, hiring weirdness, or companies not wanting someone with my experience — not because I’m actually lacking. It also hit the part of me that feels insulted by being passed over when I know I’m capable and overqualified.

[Decision] I’m going to hold onto the idea that this is mostly about the situation and the hiring process, not a flaw in me. It feels safer to blame the mismatch between my background and these jobs, because if I make it about me personally, I’ll just spiral and feel worse. I need to protect my sense of competence, so I’m going to see the rejections as the system not recognizing my value rather than proof that something is wrong with me.

[Decision] So I’ll stay with that. I’ll hold onto how blocked I am, how impossible it is from here, because that’s the truth of it. If I say it’s my fault, then I’m the one who didn’t save him — and I can’t bear that. Better to put the blame on the distance, on being locked away, on circumstances that make me useless, than to face the shame of wanting to help and not being able to.

en_backup.client_response: When I told him about David, he said: I thought so. We were sitting in the kitchen, surrounded by takeout containers, about 20 of them and... he was just pushing his eggroll from one side of the plate to the other, dipping it in the hot mustard without looking up at me and said I thought so.
en_backup.internal:
[Perception] He didn’t react like it was news. He said “I thought so” like he’d already been carrying it around, maybe even knowing more than I wanted to know. That hit the part of me that was trying to keep this small, keep it as just something from the past I could mention and move on from. But sitting there with all that takeout, watching him not look at me, it felt important to say exactly what happened in the room, exactly how he was acting, because that was the thing I couldn’t ignore anymore. It wasn’t just a casual conversation. It was him maybe having known, maybe having suspected, and still we were there, trying to talk around it.

[Decision] So I laid it out: the kitchen, the containers, the eggroll, the mustard, him saying “I thought so.” I wanted you to see that this wasn’t me making a big dramatic scene out of nothing. I was trying to tell you what it felt like when I finally said it to my father and he just sat there like he already knew. I guess I wanted you to understand why I kept talking about the details — because if I said it plainly, maybe it would make sense why I feel weird, and why I still want to protect him, and myself, from making it into something bigger than I can handle.

context_zh.speaker: client
context_zh.text: 棒极了！我的工作让我有点压力，也焦虑。本来一切都挺好的，除了有个同事老想指使我。她特别不帮忙，还特别双标。

context_zh.speaker: client
context_zh.text: 你根本没法跟她说话，她一开口就打断你，态度还差。我正在想办法更好地处理这个情况。

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 明白了，所以你很难应对一个同事。我想问一下，有没有可能跟她谈谈她的行为？还有，她对别人也这样吗？

context_zh.speaker: client
context_zh.text: 对，我觉得她性格就比较冲，跟别人说话方式也差不多，没什么区别。她根本听不进去。

context_zh.speaker: client
context_zh.text: 我可以试着跟她聊聊，但以前试过很难。

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 我建议你找调解人或者人力资源部，坐下来谈一谈。因为很明显这已经影响到你工作和生活了。找HR应该有帮助。

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 你觉得呢？

context_zh.speaker: client
context_zh.text: 这是个好建议，我之前试过通过其他方式放松减压，不把它当回事，也不往心里去。

zh.therapist_turn_zh: 你觉得呢？
zh.client_response_zh: 我们办公室很小，很可能只能找我老板谈，我之前已经跟他提过这事了。我觉得吧，她可能也干不长了。
zh.internal_zh:
<internal>
[Perception] 治疗师是在建议我采取更直接的行动，但我觉得问题关键在于那个同事的态度。是她态度粗鲁、插话、指手画脚，这才让事情这么难办。我已经试过保持冷静、不往心里去，也跟老板提过，所以我不觉得这事应该我一个人一直追着。办公室又小，老板已经知道了，看起来是她的性格和处境有问题，不是我做得不对。

[Decision] 我打算继续把重点放在管理自己的压力上，先熬着，不去把事闹大。如果她真的不会改变，而且也可能干不长，那最好的做法就是别被她带进去，顺其自然。我不想成为制造矛盾的人，她才是让工作变难的元凶。
</internal>

context.speaker: client
context.text: Wonderful! My job is causing me some stress and anxiety. Everything is usually good except for my one coworker who tries to boss me around. She is very unhelpful and hypocritical

context.speaker: client
context.text: You cannot even talk to her without her interrupting or being rude. I am trying to find a better way to deal with the situation

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: I see, so you have difficulty dealing with a co-worker. Let ask, Is there anyway of talking to her about her behavior? Also does she behave this way with others?

context.speaker: client
context.text: Yes, I believe she has an aggressive personality and there wouldn't be much of a difference in the way she acts or speaks to others. She never listens

context.speaker: client
context.text: I could try to have a conversation but in the past it has been difficult

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: What I do recommend is contacting a mediator or someone from HR and having a sit down. Since clearly this is affecting you at work and outside of it. Talking to HR should help.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: What do you think?

context.speaker: client
context.text: That is a good recommendation, I have tried to relax and relieve stress in other outlets and not let it get to me or take it personally

en_backup.therapist_turn: What do you think?
en_backup.client_response: Our office is small so it would likely just be my boss who I have mentioned it to before. I think of it as she may not be working here that much longer
en_backup.internal:
[Perception] The therapist is suggesting I need to take a more direct step, but what stands out to me is that the real issue is my coworker’s attitude. She’s the one being rude, interruptive, and bossy, and that’s what’s making this hard. I’ve already tried to handle it by staying calm and not taking it personally, and I’ve brought it up before, so this doesn’t feel like something I should have to keep pushing alone. Since the office is small and the boss already knows, it seems like the situation and her personality are the problem, not something I’m doing wrong.

[Decision] I’m going to keep focusing on managing my stress and waiting it out instead of making a bigger issue of it. If she’s really not going to change and may not be here much longer anyway, then the best move is probably to avoid getting drawn into her behavior and let things play out. I don’t want to be the one creating conflict when she’s the one making work difficult.

[Perception] 治疗师问得很笼统、很开放，我感觉得先把实际情况摆出来再说别的。刚才说“还行吧”太敷衍、太假了，根本不是我真实的状态。分手才是现在最压在我心头的事，而且这段感情谈了三年多，不是随随便便的那种——它占据了我很长一段人生。我想让治疗师明白，我不是单纯的有点低落；我是失去了一个很重要的人，感觉脚下的地都没了。

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: It sounds like there maybe something you need to get off of your chest.

en_backup.therapist_turn: It sounds like there maybe something you need to get off of your chest.
en_backup.client_response: Absolutely. I recently broke up with my girlfriend. We had been together for more than 3 years.
en_backup.internal:
[Perception] The therapist was asking in a general, open way, and I felt like I needed to make the situation real before anything else. Saying “I’m okayish” felt too small and too fake for what’s actually going on. The breakup is the main thing on my chest, and the fact that it was a relationship of more than three years is important because it wasn’t some casual thing — it was my life for a long time. I wanted the therapist to understand that this isn’t just me being a little down; this is me coming in after losing someone who mattered deeply and feeling like the floor underneath me is gone.

[Decision] So I decided to say it plainly: I broke up with my girlfriend, and it lasted over three years. I wanted to lay out the facts first because maybe if the therapist sees how long it was and how serious it was, they’ll understand why I feel so wrecked and why this is hard to just brush off. I’m trying to get them to see that this isn’t a small problem for me — it’s tied to everything I’m feeling right now.

zh.internal_zh:

[Perception] 她说她没有逃跑的时候，我听到的是她想把发生的事情轻描淡写，让它听起来比实际干净。这正好戳中了我放不下的东西：那个时间点。从我坐的位置看，她面对了一件强烈的事情，却没有留下来处理，而是用休假消失了，把查理晾在一边。把这件事称为别的什么感觉像是在回避，几乎是在改写故事来保护自己。同样让我不舒服的是，她表现得好像我在夸大其词，但我说的是我亲眼看到的真实模式。

[Decision] 我决定必须反击，直接点出矛盾，因为如果我让她重新定义这件事，那么整个重点就模糊了。我需要她面对一个事实：从我的角度看，她确实在危机中抛弃了一个病人，而“我没有逃跑”并没有回答她本该在场却离开的事实。我要挑战那个让她显得无辜的版本，因为感觉她在回避我指出的残酷真相。
</internal>

en_backup.internal:
[Perception] When Gina says she didn’t run away, what I hear is her trying to soften what happened and make it sound cleaner than it was. That lands right on the thing I can’t let go of: the timing. From where I sat, she was confronted with something intense and instead of staying with it, she disappeared into a sabbatical and left Charlie hanging. Calling it anything else feels evasive, almost like she’s rewriting the story to protect herself. What also feels wrong is that she’s acting as if I’m overreaching when I’m pointing to an actual pattern I watched happen.

[Decision] I decided I had to push back and name the contradiction directly, because if I let her redefine it, then the whole point gets blurred. I need her to face that from my perspective she did leave a patient in the middle of a crisis, and that “I didn’t run away” doesn’t answer the fact that she was gone when she was needed. I want to challenge the version that makes her look blameless, because it feels like she’s avoiding the hard truth I’m calling out.

zh.internal_zh:
<internal>
[Perception] 他说他很高兴我来，而我感受到的是其下的假设：我来这里对他来说是个小小的胜利，或者证明我还有救，或者我需要被像迷路的人一样欢迎。这没抓住重点。我不是因为抱有希望才来的。我是因为无处可去，而且既然我要坐在这样的房间里，我不会让他把它变成一个自我感觉良好的时刻。另一部分触动我的是，他的高兴意味着他认为他能帮忙。他无法挽回已经发生的事情，我也不想让他假装可以。

context.speaker: client

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: I'm glad you came.

en_backup.therapist_turn: I'm glad you came.
en_backup.client_response: I hope you don't feel any pressure today. I finally have the time to talk to you, but it's too late for you to help.
en_backup.internal:
[Perception] He says he's glad I came, and what lands is the assumption underneath it: that my being here is some kind of small victory for him, or proof I’m reachable, or that I need to be welcomed like I’m lost. That misses the point. I’m not here because I’m hopeful. I’m here because I have nowhere else to go, and because if I’m going to sit in a room like this, I’m not going to let him turn it into a feel-good moment. The other part that hit me is the idea that his gladness means he thinks he can help. He can’t undo what’s happened, and I don’t want him pretending otherwise.

[Decision] So I push back. I remind him this is late, maybe too late, and that he shouldn’t feel pressure to perform some rescue. I want to correct the record: my coming here doesn’t mean I’m open, grateful, or convinced. It means I’m cornered, and I’m still in control of what I say about that. If there’s any truth in this room, it’s that.

I’m trying to make sense of whether they think I’m overreacting, whether they feel rejected, or whether they just have a different threshold for risk than I do. What feels unresolved is how to explain that I’m not trying to pull away from them, even though that’s probably how it looks from the outside.

[Decision] I want to work out the mismatch between my intention and their interpretation. Maybe the issue isn’t that they don’t care, but that they hear “distance” as “I don’t want you,” when I mean “I still want you, just not in the same way right now.” So I should think through how to say that more clearly—how to show that my caution is about the situation, not about the friendship. I’m also wondering if I need to accept that some friends will never see it the way I do, and that might mean choosing the most honest explanation rather than trying to make everyone fully comfortable with it.

zh.client_response_zh: 那是，呃，那是好多事情要做，而且，我不——我不确定我能全做完，而且更糟的是，它——它——如果我没全做完，所有这些事都会发生在我身上？

[Perception] 我听到一大堆改变一次性砸向我——吃药、节食、体重、锻炼，所有的一切——这击中了我内心已经感到不堪重负和走投无路的部分。感觉就像是，“这是你的新生活，如果你不做全，你可能会失明或失去双脚。”这听起来像威胁，不是帮助。这让我觉得这件事不可能又残酷，好像要我一夜之间变成另一个人，并且必须完美做到，否则就要付出可怕的代价。

</internal>

[Decision] 我决定说一部分真话，这样既诚实又不至于感觉自己要垮了。我想让她知道我正在挣扎，因为有一部分我已经厌倦了一个人扛着，但我也同样不想把问题说得比我能承受的要大。所以我有点保留，但确实让压力流露出来了，因为我需要有人听到情况有多糟。

context_zh.text: 有一天我提前放学回家。那天开车拼车的妈妈得早点接我们。我走进我父母的卧室，我爸跟一个模特在那儿。

zh.therapist_turn_zh: 你爸知道你看他了吗？
zh.client_response_zh: 哦，知道。他站起来。他走过来，就看着我。我说了句类似，我还以为模特只有固定时间来呢。
zh.internal_zh:
<internal>
[Perception] 他想知道我父亲是否知道我看到了他，这让整件事感觉不那么像偶然的事故，更像是一个有目击者的时刻。我觉得重要的是要说，我不是偶然撞见那个场景——我看见我爸也看见了我。他站起来，走过来，就看着我，好像我们俩都心知肚明，不需要说破。我说了那句关于模特只有固定时间来的话，因为那是我展示自己试图把它变得平常的方式，几乎是开玩笑，这样谁都不用说出实际存在的东西。

[Decision] 所以我就直白地说出了顺序：我早回家，走进去，发现他和一个模特在一起，他知道我知道了。我说了那个笑话，因为我想把事情压住，让它听起来像是个误会而不是决裂。我希望治疗师明白，重要的不是我撞见了什么——而是我们之间的那个眼神，那种无声的默契，还有我多快就把它掩盖过去了。

context.speaker: client
context.text: I came home from school early one day. The mom who drove carpool that day had to pick us up early. I walked into my parents' bedroom and my father was there with a model.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: Does your father know that you saw?

en_backup.client_response: Oh, yeah. He got up. He came over to me and just looked at me. I said something like, I thought the models only came at fixed times.
en_backup.internal:
[Perception] He wanted to know whether my father knew I’d seen him, and that made the whole thing feel less like some random accident and more like a moment with a witness in it. What felt important to say was that I wasn’t just stumbling into a scene — I saw my father see me back. He got up, came over, and just looked at me, like we both knew something without having to spell it out. I said the line about the models only coming at fixed times because that was my way of showing how I tried to make it ordinary, almost joking, so no one would have to name what was actually there.

[Decision] So I laid out the sequence plainly: I came home early, walked in, found him with a model, and he knew I knew. I said the joke because I was trying to keep it contained, to make it sound like a misunderstanding instead of a rupture. I wanted the therapist to see that the important part wasn’t just what I walked into — it was the look between us, the silent agreement, and how quickly I covered it over.

en_backup.internal:
[Perception] He talked like I was supposed to trust his judgment, but from where I sit he was calling a bad session a “breakthrough” and then couldn’t even be bothered to let me in the next week. That landed like he didn’t actually care whether I got help, only that he could say he was doing a good job. It felt dismissive and arrogant, like my experience didn’t matter and I was expected to nod along while he decided what was good for me. After being isolated and already on edge, that kind of thing feels less like support and more like being brushed off by someone who’s supposed to be on my side.

[Decision] So I pushed back by discounting him. If he’s going to act like that, I’m not going to treat him as some authority I have to respect. I’m done pretending his input is automatically helpful just because he’s the therapist. If he’s careless with me, then I get to question everything he says and keep my guard up.

[Decision] So I gave him the joke version, the fish line, because it keeps me in control. If I stay funny and a little hostile, I don’t have to admit I wanted to turn around because I felt cornered and naked. Brevity is safer — less chance of him pushing into the soft part where I’d have to say I was hurt, not just pissed off.

context_zh.text: 第一次封锁就够糟了，第二次直接把我扔进绝望里。再不能见朋友和家人，我真的撑不下去了。

context_zh.speaker: client
context_zh.text: 我用Facebook挺多的，有作用，但替代不了面对面接触。我真的很需要见到人。

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 线上联系确实有局限性。你能在外面保持距离见人吗？

context_zh.speaker: client
context_zh.text: 嗯，问题一部分是我都不知道现在规则是什么了！他们告诉我们太多不同的东西，我都跟不上趟了。

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 我明白。试着坚持基本做法来减轻压力。在外面保持距离戴口罩。

zh.therapist_turn_zh: 我明白。试着坚持基本做法来减轻压力。在外面保持距离戴口罩。
zh.client_response_zh: 我一直都戴口罩..我想这是法律强制要求的:)。但是我真的好想念那些小事，比如出去喝杯咖啡或者去健身房。这让我觉得一切再也回不去了。
zh.internal_zh:
<internal>
[Perception] 他们想用实际建议帮忙，但正好戳中我那部分又困又累的感觉——好像我明明做了该做的，但还是不够。真正触动我的不是想念咖啡或健身房，而是底下的恐惧：这可能会持续下去，什么都不再正常。说出“再也回不去了”是我在触摸那种绝望的感觉，又不用直接说出口我有多害怕、多哀悼过去的生活。

[Decision] 我决定说出来，因为承认自己受伤比一直装作只是理性应对更安全。我想让他们明白，这不是我在拒绝建议——我已经到了一个点，失去本身才是问题，我需要这个被看见。如果我能在这里把那种感受说出来，也许就不用一个人攥得那么紧了。
</internal>
