context.speaker: client
context.text: The first lockdown was bad enough but the second has really thrown me into despair. I simply cannot cope without being able to see friends and family for much longer.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: I would be glad to. What is troubling you?

context.speaker: client
context.text: I have run out of coping mechanisms!

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: I completely understand and had similar experiences. What were some ways you tried to interact with people last shut down?

context.speaker: client
context.text: I use facebook quite a lot and it helps but it cannot compensate for face to face contact. I really need to be able to see people.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: Digital contact does have its limitations. Could you meet with people outside at a distance?

context.speaker: client
context.text: Well, part of the problem with that is that I am not sure what the rules are any more! We have been told so many different things that I am out of the loop.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: I understand. Try sticking to the basics to make it less stressful. Wear a mask outside at a distance.

en_backup.therapist_turn: I understand. Try sticking to the basics to make it less stressful. Wear a mask outside at a distance.
en_backup.client_response: I always do wear a mask.. I think we legally have to :). I really miss little things like going out for coffee or to the gym though. It makes me feel like will never be the same again.
en_backup.internal:
[Perception] They were trying to help by keeping it practical, but it landed on the part that feels trapped and tired — like I’m doing the obvious things and it still isn’t enough. What really hit me wasn’t just missing coffee or the gym; it was the fear underneath it that this could go on and nothing will ever feel normal again. Saying “will never be the same again” is me touching how bleak that feels without having to say outright that I’m scared and grieving the life I had.

[Decision] I decided to say it because it feels safer to admit that I’m hurting than to keep pretending I’m only being reasonable. I wanted them to understand that this isn’t me refusing advice — I’m reaching the point where the loss itself is the problem, and I need that to be noticed. If I can put that feeling into words here, maybe I won’t have to carry it so tightly on my own.

context.speaker: therapist

context.text: yeah just trying to speed through the readings as I still have more than a few units to read through

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: All nighters can be rough. Do you have snacks and caffeine?

context.text:
and meanwhile, have one assignment from this course also at the end of this month, 
and another course's assignment, and that course's exam is coming up next month.

context.speaker: client
context.text: yeah just trying to load myself up with coffee.

context.speaker: client
context.text: I am used to the idea of staying up because I have been doing that since the pandemic early on this year, but I seem to be distracted and procrastinating, especially in the early hours of the morning, and just go on the computer and waste time, etc.

en_backup.therapist_turn: All nighters can be rough. Do you have snacks and caffeine?
en_backup.client_response: it's kind of hard to sit myself down I guess
en_backup.internal:
[Perception] The therapist is noticing how rough this is, but I can tell the focus is on the actual pattern: me being stuck, distracted, and doing the same late-night thing again. That hits the part I usually try not to look at too closely — that I’m not just “busy,” I’m avoiding, drifting onto the computer, and losing time even though I know the deadlines are stacking up. It also touches the part of me that feels kind of embarrassed because I’m supposed to be able to handle this; my marks have usually been good, so admitting I’m struggling feels like admitting I’m slipping.

[Decision] I’m going to keep it brief and stay on the surface for now. It feels safer to talk about the workload and the sleep/caffeine side of it than to get into how stuck I actually feel, because if I go deeper I’d have to admit this has become a pattern and not just a bad night. I don’t want to make it sound too dramatic, and I’m still holding onto the idea that once these courses are done I can reset and get back on track. For now I’d rather sound like I’m managing it than open up how frustrating and out of control it feels.

judge.rationale: 对话简短，无文化绑定或语言双关，翻译后可自然保留阻抗情绪与话轮功能。

en_backup.internal:
[Perception] She’s still trying to make this about my memory, like if she can poke holes in one Christmas Eve then the whole thing becomes “complicated” instead of what it was. It lands on the one thing I can’t let slide: the idea that maybe I’m the one misreading my own childhood, like I made my father into a villain because it’s easier. No. What hits me is the old familiar move of taking the edge off what they did — softening him, making it all about my perception, my “screen memory,” my being overwhelmed. That feels like she’s asking me to excuse him and doubt myself.

[Decision] I’m not giving her that. I’m going to pin it where it belongs: on him not caring. If I let this become a debate about memory, I lose the truth of what it felt like to be there alone. So I’m shutting the door on her version and holding onto mine — because if I start making excuses for him, then I’m the one abandoning the kid who already got abandoned.

context_zh.speaker: client
context_zh.text: 你能告诉我一些事吗？

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 当然。

context_zh.speaker: client
context_zh.text: 刚才我提到吉娜的那本书时，我说那个角色像巴托比，你好像明白我在指什么，是吧？

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 知道这个对你来说为什么重要？

context_zh.speaker: client
context_zh.text: 因为我喜欢被理解。我需要知道当……当我跟人说话时，他们能懂我，懂我在说什么。你知道我说的是谁吗？

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 那个抄写员。

context_zh.speaker: client
context_zh.text: 我们第一次见面那周我就给了温迪这本书，叫《奔跑的记忆》。她还没读，但她还觉得这是关于跑步的。

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 难道不是？

zh.therapist_turn_zh: 难道不是？
zh.client_response_zh: 祝你本周愉快。
zh.internal_zh:
<internal>
[Perception] 她拿我的问题设了个小陷阱——不是为了理解我，而是为了让我解释自己，逼我把意思摊开。这正好戳中了我的痛处：我既希望不用费力解释就被理解，又讨厌被人把我的引用当成待解的谜题。她说“难道不是？”的时候，我感觉她越过了我的重点，触及了某个比我想流露的更暴露的东西——就好像那个玩笑或洞见必须在当时当下被拆解开，经受审视。

[Decision] 我受够了。我不会坐在这里让这场对话变成讨论我能不能证明我的意思。我已经说得够多了，我知道我的意思。如果你不能不加拆解地接住我，那我就关门。“祝你本周愉快”是我找回自尊的方式，在必须交出更多东西之前结束对话。
</internal>

context.speaker: client
context.text: Will you tell me something?

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: Sure.

context.speaker: client
context.text: When I was talking about Gina's book earlier on, You seemed to know the reference I was making When I said that The character was like bartleby. Did you?

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: Why is it important to you to know?

context.speaker: client
context.text: Because I like to be understood. I need to know that when... When I'm talking to somebody, That they understand me. They understand what I'm saying. Do you know who I was talking about?

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: The scrivener.

context.speaker: client
context.text: I gave Wendy this book The first week that we met. It's called the memory of running. She hasn't read it yet, But she still thinks it's about running

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: It's not?

en_backup.therapist_turn: It's not?
en_backup.client_response: Have a good week.
en_backup.internal:
[Perception] She took my question and turned it into a little trap — not to understand me, but to make me explain myself, to force the meaning out into the open. That landed right on the sore spot: the part of me that wants to be recognized without having to perform the whole explanation, and the part that hates being handled as if my references are puzzles to solve. When she said, “It’s not?” it felt like she was reaching past my point and into something more exposed than I wanted to give — as if the joke or the insight had to be unpacked right then, under scrutiny.

[Decision] I’m done. I’m not going to sit here and let this be reduced to a discussion about whether I can prove what I meant. I said enough, and I know what I meant. If you can’t meet me there without pulling it apart, then I’m closing the door. “Have a good week” is me taking back my own dignity and ending the conversation before I have to hand over anything else.

zh.internal_zh:
<internal>
[Perception] 他们想安慰我，但听起来像根本不懂这是怎么回事。“你该为自己感到骄傲”和那个康复的故事很空洞，像是随便找个同情的话说，并没有真正承受这件事有多丑恶、多没完没了。我疲惫又害怕的那部分被打中了，我能看出来他们想把这事包装成整齐的情绪问题，可我的现实是儿童保护机构、寄养身份、四个孩子，以及反正最后也可能很惨。提起他们的朋友更让人觉得他们是在外面说话，说的东西一点用都没有。

[Decision] 所以我打算避开，把对话留在事实层面，因为我不相信他们能接住难受的部分而不扯到自己身上或粉饰太平。如果真想帮忙，他们需要认清实际赌注是什么，而不是给我没要求的鼓励。我会提 NF 那个参考，至少那是把恐惧说出来。如果他们接不住，那我也不会把自己的脆弱交出去，只换来一些漂亮的同情话。
</internal>

It hits the part where I’m exhausted and scared, and I can tell they want to make it about feelings in a tidy way, when my reality is CPS, foster status, four kids, and the possibility that this ends badly anyway. [Decision] So I’m going to pull away from that and keep the conversation on the real facts, because I don’t trust them to hold the hard part without making it about themselves or sugarcoating it. If they want to be helpful, they need to understand the actual stakes instead of handing me encouragement I didn’t ask for. I’ll use the NF reference because that at least names the fear honestly. If they can’t meet me there, then I’m not going to hand them my rawness just to get some polished sympathy back.

zh.internal_zh:

[感知] 我感觉他好像是在说答案就是完全保持原样，这让我觉得不太对。我明白他说的不要因为前任想要不同就改变自己，但这听起来太绝对了。我不是说要变成另一个人或者假装成不是我自己的人——我在想我是不是错过了一些在关系中重要的东西，比如更用心、更体贴、更能以我没学到的那些方式出现。他的话触动了我内心担忧的部分：如果我不从这段关系中真的学到什么，我会一直陷入同样的问题。而且我也不愿相信唯一的选择就是要么完全保持原样，要么为了别人抹掉自己。那感觉是假的。

[决定] 所以我反驳了他，因为我需要纠正这种过于简化的说法。我想说的是：也许我不需要改变核心的自我，但如果我想下次有不一样的结果，我可能确实需要在某些方面成长。我在努力弄清楚什么是真正的我，什么只是盲点，什么可以在不背叛自己的前提下真正改善。如果我不质疑这一点，我就会留下这样的恐惧：我会一次又一次重复同样的关系模式。
</internal>

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: Exactly, and remember everyone is different, perhaps you just weren't her right one, and that can go both ways.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: Do you want to improve for her? or for yourself do you think?

context.speaker: client
context.text: That's true. I really got hung up on her. I thought she was perfect and that we were perfect together. She didn't see it that way. I can't really change who I am, and she couldn't change who she is.

context.speaker: client
context.text: I don't know if I can change myself for her. Maybe there is something basic that she wants that I just don't have? I should probably change for future relationships.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: That's a great line of thought, its good that you're able to identify that yourself

context.speaker: client
context.text: What do you think I could do to improve myself?

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: I suggest that you stay exactly the way that you are. I feel like you'd be happier that way and also more likely to find someone who shares the same values as you

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: If you change who you are, it sort of means that your ex still has a hold on you, you know?

en_backup.therapist_turn: If you change who you are, it sort of means that your ex still has a hold on you, you know?
en_backup.client_response: Will the same problems show up in the next relationship though? It could be a long search before I find someone that matches with me?
en_backup.internal:
[Perception] It felt like they were saying the answer is just to stay exactly the same, and that didn’t sit right with me. I hear what they mean about not changing just because my ex wanted something different, but that sounds too absolute. I’m not talking about becoming a different person or pretending to be someone I’m not — I’m wondering if I missed some things that matter in relationships, like being more intentional, more thoughtful, more able to show up in ways I didn’t learn growing up. What they said hit the part of me that worries I’ll keep running into the same issue if I don’t actually learn anything from this. I also don’t want to believe that the only options are either stay exactly as I am or erase myself for someone else. That feels false.

[Decision] So I pushed back because I needed to correct that oversimplification. I wanted to say: maybe I don’t need to change who I am at the core, but I probably do need to grow in some ways if I want a different result next time. I’m trying to figure out what is me, what is just a blind spot, and what can actually be improved without betraying myself. If I don’t challenge that, I’m left with this fear that I’ll just repeat the same relationship pattern over and over.

[Perception] He took my “excitement” and made it into something admirable, something alive in me. But what I actually felt was the opposite: a jolt of disgust, a kind of recoil in the body. He hears possibility where I hear contamination. And that lands on the part of me that is already tired of trying to translate myself into this place, tired of paying for every little adaptation with a bit of dignity. If even repulsion can be mistaken for growth, then nothing I feel is going to be understood here.

[Decision] So what is the point of hoping? If I say I’m changing, it gets romanticized. If I say I’m repelled, it gets turned into progress. Either way, I am not being met where I am. Better to keep it flat, keep it dry, keep myself from reaching for some grand new version of me that only ends in humiliation. Thursday, 9:00 P.M. Fine. I’ll watch it, or not. It doesn’t matter enough to hurt me.

He’s pushing me toward “what I did” in a way that makes it sound clean, procedural. But what hit me was Natalie’s look in that email, the papers I’m not allowed to read, the whole story being written around me like I’m the villain. That’s the real thing in the room: everyone is making me the problem, and maybe they’re the ones who want a criminal more than they want the truth.

[Decision] So I’m going to hold the line that this wasn’t just me being careless or reckless. I trusted experts, I relied on labs, I did what I was supposed to do until they failed me and the system failed me. If there’s poison in the pipeline, then the problem starts with the people who lied, the labs that signed off, the chain that let it through — not just with me. I need to keep this pointed at where the failures actually were, because I can’t carry the whole thing as if I personally put every pill on those shelves.

en_backup.internal:
[Perception] He’s pushing at the edge of something I don’t want to open right now. He heard me say the boys were there and latched onto it like it means something bigger, like he wants me to sit there and feel whatever that was. And then he hits the word stupid, which lands right on the sore spot: me being the idiot in the story, me missing everything about my own father until he was in the ground. It feels like he’s asking me to turn that over in front of him, to admit how much I didn’t know and how much that pisses me off and embarrasses me.

[Decision] So I shut it down the only way I can without saying no outright: I make it about the stupidity of the whole thing, not about my feelings. If I joke, if I act like it’s ridiculous, then I don’t have to stand there exposed while he pokes around in whatever this is. I’m too tired for that, and I don’t want to hand him the part of me that still feels humiliated, angry, and confused all at once.

It lands on the part I’m most afraid of — that the situation is already out of my hands. The firm has cut people, lockdowns are still happening, and the job market doesn’t feel like some place I can just “prepare” my way into safety. It sounds like advice for a world that still has options. Mine feels like it’s shrinking. I’m not panicking for no reason; I’m reacting to something real, and the more I look at it, the more it seems pointless to pretend I can control the outcome.

[Decision] So I shut down. I don’t want to spend energy building hope only to watch it collapse, because that would hurt more than admitting it’s probably going to go badly. If I stop reaching for a solution, I don’t have to keep feeling the disappointment of seeing how limited my choices really are. I’ll keep showing up, keep functioning, but inside I’m bracing for the worst and not letting myself imagine anything better. It feels safer to expect loss than to trust in a plan that may not save me.

en_backup.therapist_turn: Slowly. It's gonna take a while. It's taken you a few years to fall into this and it's probably gonna take you a while to get out of it. But you have to start trying now. 'cause you know something? You deserve to be happy.
en_backup.client_response: Que lástima.
en_backup.internal:
[Perception] I heard “you deserve to be happy,” but what landed was that I’m being told to do something impossible and vague. Forgive myself for what? For carrying something I was never meant to carry? For years I’ve been acting like if I keep paying, maybe that means I still understand what happened. If I let go of that, then it feels like I’m pretending it didn’t matter. So the part that got hit is the part that still thinks my pain has to count for something, otherwise it was all just a mess with no meaning.

[Decision] So I guess I’ll do what I always do: nod, say “okay,” and not really believe it. I’m not going to force some fake forgiveness just because it sounds healthy. I don’t see how it helps, and I don’t trust hope when it’s offered like a simple instruction. If I stop holding myself responsible, then what am I left with? Better to stay where I am than make a promise to heal and fail at that too.

zh.client_response_zh: 我想是因为我在生活中的人际关系很糟糕
zh.internal_zh:
<internal>
[Perception] 他们问我为什么有这种感觉，第一个说得通的答案是人际关系。这戳中了我觉得自己被家人嫌弃、被朋友避开的那个地方。我还在想，可能不单是“悲伤”本身，而是我不断看到被拒绝的悲伤——尤其在学校过得很吃力的时候。如果我成绩不好，也许家人就会疏远我。而如果我本来就疏远又难堪，也许朋友们也一样。我在试着搞清楚问题究竟是我自己、我的表现，还是别人对待我的方式。

[Decision] 我决定说出来关系这部分，因为那似乎是我能指出的主要模式，而且我想弄明白这件事，而不是一直迷茫。我希望如果我能搞清楚真正的原因是什么，我就能看看有没有办法修复哪怕一段关系。我不想只是不断猜测或者觉得一切都无望。
</internal>

context.text: Hi, I'm very depressed and sad.

context.speaker: client
context.text: Please help

context.speaker: client
context.text: Please help me I need help

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: I'm sorry to hear that. Do you know why you feel depressed and sad?

en_backup.therapist_turn: I'm sorry to hear that. Do you know why you feel depressed and sad?
en_backup.client_response: I think it's because of my poor relationships in life
en_backup.internal:
[Perception] They asked why I feel this way, and the first answer that makes sense is my relationships. It hits the part where I feel unwanted by my family and avoided by my friends. I’m also thinking it might not just be “sadness” by itself, but sadness because I keep seeing rejection everywhere, especially when I struggle at school. If I’m bad at school, maybe that’s why my family pulls away. And if I’m already distant and embarrassed, maybe my friends do too. I’m trying to figure out whether the problem is me, my performance, or the way I’m being treated.

[Decision] I decided to say the relationships part because that seems like the main pattern I can point to, and I want help making sense of it instead of just feeling lost. I’m hoping that if I can understand what’s actually causing this, I can see whether there’s any way to fix even one connection. I don’t want to just keep guessing or assume everything is hopeless.

context_zh.text: 我有一点积蓄，但主要还是找新工作。找到新工作之前，我领了大概一个月的失业救济金。

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 你制定过什么计划吗，关于接下来怎么走？

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 如果你愿意，我可以给你一些建议。我知道很多资源。

context_zh.speaker: client
context_zh.text: 我是零工，所以不能申请失业救济。很难，但我也有一些积蓄。

context_zh.speaker: client
context_zh.text: 你有什么工具可以推荐我用，帮我度过这个时期？

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 嗯，在找更多工作的同时动用积蓄，暂时还可以。如果因此出现食物短缺，当地通常有食物银行。这真的没什么好尴尬的，很多人面临食物短缺都不是自己的错。

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 你也可以打电话给你当地的社会服务机构，他们会告诉你有什么资源可用，不管是职业培训还是临时救助。

context_zh.speaker: client
context_zh.text: 哇，你真是太有帮助、太鼓励人了！和你聊天真好。

zh.therapist_turn_zh: 你也可以打电话给你当地的社会服务机构，他们会告诉你有什么资源可用，不管是职业培训还是临时救助。
zh.client_response_zh: 你能推荐点药帮我睡觉吗？
zh.internal_zh:
<internal>
[Perception] 他们想把我推向失业的现实、不确定性，以及我宁愿不去多想的需求。食物银行/社会服务这部分触及了底下的可怕东西——钱快花光了，无法完全自力更生，不得不承认我可能需要帮助。我也听出他们在问计划，这让一切变得更真实、更紧迫。
[Decision] 我不想坐在这里完全恐慌这意味着什么，或者现在就被拉去讨论钱和支持选项。转而谈一些具体、可解决的事情，比如睡眠，感觉更安全。如果我问药，我就可以专注于熬过夜晚，而不是面对工作和积蓄带来的所有不确定性和脆弱。
</internal>

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: I had a bit in savings, but I looked for new jobs mostly. I was on unemployment insurance for about a month before I found a new job.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: Have you made any plans yet about how to move forward?

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: I can offer some suggestions if you would like. I know about a lot of resources

context.speaker: client
context.text: I am a gig worker, so I cannot apply for IU. Its very hard, but i also have some savings.

context.speaker: client
context.text: What kind of tools would you recommend I use to get through this

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: Well, falling back on savings while you look for more work is good for a while. If you have any food insecurity as a result, there are often local food banks. It's really not something to be embarrased about, so many people face food insecurity through no fault of their own.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: You could also give a call to your local social services because they will be able to tell you what resources would be available, whether it's a vocational program or temporary assistance.

context.speaker: client
context.text: Wow you're so helpful and encouraging! It's very nice to talk to you.

en_backup.therapist_turn: You could also give a call to your local social services because they will be able to tell you what resources would be available, whether it's a vocational program or temporary assistance.
en_backup.client_response: Are there any meds you can recommend to help me sleep?
en_backup.internal:
[Perception] They’re trying to push me toward the practical reality of being out of work, the uncertainty, and possibly needing help I’d rather not think about too hard. The food bank/social services part lands on the scary stuff underneath this — money running out, not being able to stay fully self-reliant, and having to admit I might need support. I also hear that they’re asking for plans, which makes it feel more real and immediate.

[Decision] I don’t want to sit in the full panic of what this means or get pulled into talking about money and support options right now. It feels safer to switch to something concrete and fixable, like sleep. If I ask about meds, I can focus on getting through the nights instead of facing all the uncertainty and vulnerability around my job and savings.

zh.therapist_turn_zh: 既然我们都在挖真相……我能问问你对Laura的真实感觉吗？我一直没听明白。不是你要怎么对她，而是你的感受。

zh.internal_zh:

[Perception] 他不再让我躲在道德背后了。他在逼问真实的感受，不是那种官腔，而这直接戳中了我一直回避的事情：Laura对我来说不只是又一个病人，这件事有真实的后果。我能听出他的潜台词，他想让我停止绕圈子，直接说出来。这让我很不舒服，因为一旦我说出口，我就不能再假装它只是个假设或专业上的抽象概念。

[Decision] 所以我逼自己用话说出来，而不是暗示，因为我要弄清楚他到底是在说单纯的吸引，还是更多，还是他在设套让我自我评判。老实说，我是在请他帮我理解这种感觉到底意味着什么，以及我该拿它怎么办。同时我也在试探他能否陪着我，而不把它变成一场关于边界或责任的说教。
</internal>

[Perception] He’s not letting me hide behind ethics anymore. He’s pressing for the actual feeling, not the policy speech, and that lands right on the thing I’ve been skirting: that Laura is not just another patient to me, and that this has real consequences. I can hear the subtext that he wants me to stop talking around it and name it plainly. That hits my discomfort, because once I say it out loud, I can’t pretend it’s just a hypothetical or a professional abstraction.

[Decision] So I’m forcing it into words instead of hinting, because I need to know whether he’s talking about simple attraction, something more, or whether he’s setting me up to judge myself. If I’m honest, I’m asking for help making sense of what this feeling actually means and what I’m supposed to do with it. I’m also testing whether he can stay with me without turning it into a lecture about boundaries or responsibility.

But I don’t actually know what I’m supposed to have done. I’m trying to figure out whether he means I’m blaming myself for the symptoms, or for my parents, or for something I did to cause the whole mess. If I forgive too quickly, it feels like I’m letting myself off the hook for something I should be answering for.

[Decision] So I’m pushing for specifics because I need the logic to make sense before I can do anything with it. If there’s something I’m guilty of, I want to know exactly what it is. If there isn’t, then “forgive yourself” doesn’t fit, and I need another explanation for why my body is doing this. I’m not refusing the idea — I’m trying to pin down what I’d actually be forgiving, so it doesn’t become an empty word or a way of dodging responsibility.

Short was safer: it keeps me from having to say the thing I’m not supposed to say, and it keeps me from getting backed into that exposed feeling any further.

en_backup.internal:
[Perception] The therapist was pressing on the part I don’t want to pin down — who “her” is, what I meant by saying I killed her, whether this was really about wanting to die or about someone in me I can’t face. That question hit the raw center of it, because I can feel there’s something true underneath it, and saying it out loud would make it real.

[Decision] So I gave the smallest answer I could. “That’s what I thought when I landed” keeps me near the edge of it without stepping over. en_backup.internal:
[Perception] She’s pushing right on the part I don’t want to touch — the actual words, the exact moment where it turned into them not wanting me. Her asking for details feels like she’s trying to pin me to the one thing I’m afraid is true: that it wasn’t just them being weird, that I showed up high and made it messy and maybe they saw me as some fucked-up kid instead of their kid. If I say what I remember, I lose the easy version where they just rejected me for no reason.

[Decision] So I’m keeping it short. “I don’t remember” is safer than trying and either getting it wrong or saying something that makes me look stupid, needy, or responsible. If I stay vague, I don’t have to feel the shame of how badly I wanted them to want me, and I don’t have to admit that I might’ve helped ruin the one chance I got. Brevity buys me time. It keeps her from getting under the skin where it hurts.

en_backup.internal:
[Perception] They’re not really hearing me — just tossing out canned suggestions like “retrain” or “another profession” as if my whole life can be solved by a quick vocational pivot. It feels a little glib, like they’re speaking from a distance and don’t get what it actually means to be worn down by this work, financially and emotionally, or what it would cost to start over. And if my own therapist is burnt out too, then even the people who are supposed to help seem tired, generic, and not especially useful. That hits the part of me that already feels trapped and makes me feel a bit foolish for bringing it up seriously.

[Decision] So I’m not going to lean into their suggestions or give them the satisfaction of treating this like a simple problem. I’ll stay vague, keep some humor in it, and hold back from saying how stuck I really feel, because right now their ideas sound like they come from someone who doesn’t understand the reality of my job. If they’re going to offer obvious answers, I’d rather keep my guard up than let them steer me toward something I’m not ready for.

zh.client_response_zh: 那我能抽烟吗？
zh.internal_zh:
<internal>
[感知] 他正好戳到了我不想面对的地方——不光是关于朱莉娅，还有我是不是一直在拿卡玛拉当盾牌来挡自己的感受。笔记本、给她写的小纸条、孙辈……他围着我既想念她、又感到被评判、无助、甚至愤怒的那部分打转。要是我老老实实回答，就得承认我不只是在说她的认可——我是在说我自己的不认可和悲痛。那样太暴露了。

[决定] 我用一件小事、一件日常的事把它挡回去：抽烟。问这个比继续跟着他往深处走容易。如果我简短回答，我就不用说我对朱莉娅的真实想法，也不用说一再提起卡玛拉让我付出了什么代价。我能争取到一点喘息空间，避免说出什么收不回的话。
</internal>

en_backup.internal:
[Perception] He’s pressing right where I don’t want to stand still — not just about Julia, but about whether I’ve been using Kamala as a shield for my own feelings. The notebook, the little notes to her, the grandchildren… he’s circling the part where I miss her and also feel judged, helpless, maybe even angry. [Decision] I shut it down with something small and ordinary: smoking. Easier to ask that than to keep following him into the deeper question. If I stay brief, I don’t have to say what I really think about Julia, or what it costs me to keep invoking Kamala. I can buy a little breathing room and keep from saying something I can’t take back.

[Perception] They’re trying to help by offering a practical next step, and I can see why they went there. But when they said moving, it immediately hit the part of this that feels the most fragile: leaving my current place, my people, and the little bit of stability I still have. I want to keep my footing, keep my savings safe, and not rush into a decision just because I’m scared. So I’ll stay open to it in theory, but for now I’m going to hold back and think more before committing to anything.

zh.therapist_turn_zh: 不，不是也许。是事实。时间才是最珍贵的。你心里清楚。所以你才戴着他的表。也许你跟他抱怨那些事，是因为你希望他能跟你说点有用的话。或者，终于像个父亲一样对你。
zh.client_response_zh: 我不知道。
zh.internal_zh:
<internal>
[Perception] 他把我说得好像我在利用我爸当工具一样——好像我是在找安慰，或者想让他最后当个完美父亲。这让我很不舒服。没错，我是说了自己的事，但我不是坐在那儿想操控他或者逼他说出什么忏悔的话。我是害怕，觉得自己很蠢，不知道还能说什么。还有那块表——那根本不能证明我待在那儿是出于什么重大情感原因。那就是他的表。他把它编成一套故事，说我想要从他那里得到什么，这让我觉得不对。

</internal>

context.speaker: client
context.text: I felt like I was in a movie I was watching. Self-centered guy goes to the hospital to see his dying father, sits down, can't think of anything to say to his dad. Then he starts whining about his own little problems.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: A divorce, the fear of losing touch with his children, a move to a new city, the threat to the man's work from a lawsuit.

context.speaker: client
context.text: They don't sound so little when you actually say them.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: These are big problems to somebody in the middle of their life. But to someone confronting death, like the father, it might seem that the son could work these problems out. The dying father doesn't have the time, but the son does.

context.speaker: client
context.text: No marriage, no children, no practice, just time.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: Without the time, you don't have any of the other things.

context.speaker: client
context.text: I guess.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: No, it's not a guess. It's true. Time's the precious thing. You already know that. That's why you're wearing his watch. Maybe you were telling him your problems because you were hoping he'd say something meaningful to you. Or finally be a father to you.

en_backup.therapist_turn: No, it's not a guess. It's true. Time's the precious thing. You already know that. That's why you're wearing his watch. Maybe you were telling him your problems because you were hoping he'd say something meaningful to you. Or finally be a father to you.
en_backup.client_response: I don't know.
en_backup.internal:
[Perception] He’s making it sound like I was using my father as a tool — like I was fishing for comfort or trying to get him to be some kind of perfect father at the very end. That doesn’t sit right with me. Yes, I was talking about myself, but I wasn’t sitting there trying to manipulate him or wring a confession out of him. I was scared, I felt stupid, and I didn’t know what else to say. And the watch — that doesn’t prove I was there for some big emotional reason. It’s just his watch. It felt wrong to have him turn that into a whole story about what I supposedly wanted from him.

[Decision] I decided I needed to push back on that part, because it felt too neat and too certain. I wasn’t ready to admit that I was there hoping he’d finally father me in some grand way. I wanted to correct the record: I was there because he was dying, because I didn’t know how to act, and because my own life was already a mess. If I let him define my motives like that, it would make me sound weaker and more exposed than I could tolerate.

zh.client_response_zh: 我当然希望如此。我有时候也会怀疑。希望我没因为离开他们父亲而毁了孩子的生活。
zh.internal_zh:
<internal>
[感知] 他们想把这事说成“可能是最好的结果”，但我只听到我的孩子在受伤，害怕我已经永远搞砸了他们的人生。这戳中了我内心已经感到内疚、觉得自己是个坏妈妈的部分。我也听到他们想要我决定是不是真的结束了，老实说我不确定我能干脆地说出来还不觉得自己背叛了家人。

[决定] 所以我要保持谨慎，不完全接受那个“为最好”的说法，即使我内心有一部分相信。我要保护我的孩子，也保护自己，在我还痛苦、怀疑一切的时候不说出太绝对的话。也许是对的，也许不是——我还没准备好给自己一个判决。
</internal>

en_backup.internal:
[Perception] They’re trying to frame this as “maybe for the best,” but all I can hear is my kids being hurt and the fear that I’ve messed them up for good. It hits the part of me that already feels guilty and like a bad mom. I also hear that they want me to decide if I’m really done, and honestly I’m not sure I can say it cleanly without feeling like I’m betraying my family.

[Decision] So I’m going to stay cautious and not fully commit to that “it was for the best” idea, even if part of me believes it. I want to protect my kids and protect myself from saying something too definite when I’m still hurting and doubting everything. Maybe it was right, maybe it wasn’t — I’m not ready to hand myself a verdict yet.

[Perception] He’s probably going to do the same thing everyone does — jump straight to “just stop smoking” like I haven’t been hearing that for years. It lands on the exact thing I’m already terrified about: the coughing, the fear that this is my body warning me, and then people acting like I’m stupid for not quitting instantly. That makes him feel generic to me, like he doesn’t get how long this has been going on or how hard this habit is. It feels like he’s talking from a safe place, not from inside this mess.

[Decision] So I’m not giving him the respectful version of me right now. If he’s going to come at me with the usual quit-smoking line, I’ll cut him off first and make it clear I’m not buying it. I’m pissed because I want help, but I don’t want another person pretending it’s simple. If he can’t say something that actually feels useful, then I’m going to dismiss it and protect myself from hearing the same bullshit again.

[Perception] 她问了个挺明显的“如果直接说不呢？”的问题，好像这是什么突破似的，但听起来挺天真的。感觉她并没有真正理解我处境里的压力——我们只有两个人，活儿还得干完，“告诉老板你不行”说起来简单，但根本不是那么回事。我听到的是一股子“你就设个边界”的味道，但没考虑实际的后果，这让我觉得认真回答都没什么意义。好像我当然想过啊。我答应干不是因为喜欢；我答应是因为我没有一个干脆的替代方案。

[Perception] She’s asking a pretty obvious “what if you just say no?” question like that’s some breakthrough, but it lands as kind of naive. It feels like she’s not really getting the real pressure of my situation — there are only two of us, the work still has to get done, and “tell your employer you can’t” sounds simple when it’s not. I’m hearing a lot of “just set a boundary” energy without much sense of the actual consequences, and that makes it feel a little useless to answer seriously. Like, of course I’ve thought about that. I’m not saying yes because I enjoy it; I’m saying yes because I don’t see a clean alternative.

[Decision] So I’m going to answer with a shrug and a joke, because that keeps me from having to pretend her question is some deep insight. If I make it sound casual — “LOL, I dunno” — then I don’t have to fully engage with a suggestion that feels unrealistic and a bit out of touch. It’s easier to stay vague than to admit I’m stuck and also irritated that she’s making it sound so straightforward.

What hit me was the way he made it sound like I’m some kind of danger waiting to happen, like I’m not just hurt, I’m a threat to everything around me. And then he says “go back to your life” like my life is still waiting for me untouched, when all I can see is what I’ve already broken. What felt wrong was him turning this into “you have to face your problems” when the only thing I can hear is “you’re going to ruin it again.”

[Decision] I decided I had to push back, because I don’t accept being described like a time bomb. I need him to hear that I’m not exaggerating—I’m telling him what I actually believe about myself and why home feels impossible. If he’s going to talk about my future, he needs to understand that I already feel like I destroyed the only normal thing I had, and I’m not going to pretend that doesn’t matter.

context.text: Hello, I have been feeling very anxious and stressed recently.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: Why have you been feeling stressed and anxious?

context.speaker: client
context.text: I failed my first exam earlier this week and I have 2 more later on in this week. I am already disheartened about my first failure and I am scared that I will fail again.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: I'm sure you tried your best on that test, as long as you study hard I believe you can ace those next 2 exams!

context.speaker: client
context.text: I have been too stressed about my other exams, it's making it hard for me to focus on studying and I don't know what to do.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: I've heard that meditation can help with stress and focus, maybe you could try meditating for a bit before you study?

context.speaker: client
context.text: I have never tried meditating before, I have no idea where to start.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: Meditation is essentially focussing on breathing, you could start by closing your eyes and slowly breathe in an out.

en_backup.therapist_turn: Meditation is essentially focussing on breathing, you could start by closing your eyes and slowly breathe in an out.
en_backup.client_response: I feel like a failure and I am scared my parents are going to be disappointed in me
en_backup.internal:
[Perception] What I heard was basically, “try harder, breathe, and it’ll be fine.” But what landed for me was the part I’m terrified of: that none of this changes the fact that I already failed once, and now I’m carrying that into two more exams. The meditation suggestion just reminded me that I don’t even know how to calm myself down, so I’m already behind before I start. And when I said I feel like a failure and my parents will be disappointed, I felt like that was the real truth of it — not something to fix with a quick tip. It felt like my fear is bigger than any advice, and I’m stuck being the kind of person who ruins things.

[Decision] So I just shut down inside. If I stop expecting this to work, then I don’t have to keep hoping I’ll pull it together and then be crushed again. It feels safer to believe I’m going to fail than to keep trying to act confident and prove I can’t do it. I’m not really choosing to give up because I want to — I’m doing it because hoping feels too painful right now, and if I don’t let myself believe I can pass, then maybe the disappointment won’t hit as hard.

context_zh.text: 今天糟透了。我男朋友刚离开我，我一个人待在家里。没人能分享事情。

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 真的很抱歉——你觉得被抛弃了？

context_zh.speaker: client
context_zh.text: 对，我就是这么感觉的。我被抛弃了，觉得自己不可爱，好像再也不会有人要我了。

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 别这么想！我也经历过这种情况，我知道有多难受，但我也知道这会过去的。

context_zh.speaker: client
context_zh.text: 感觉不到它会过去。感觉只会更糟。我不想一个人上床睡觉。今晚我会睡不着的。

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 你能去拜访朋友或家人吗？寻求一些支持？

zh.therapist_turn_zh: 你能去拜访朋友或家人吗？寻求一些支持？
zh.client_response_zh: 我家人都出城了。我的朋友也是他的朋友，他跟别人说了我的坏话，所以他们都不理我。我就想喝醉然后睡过去。
zh.internal_zh:
<internal>
[Perception] 他们又在给我那种老套的“联系朋友/家人”的答案，好像这只是个打个电话就能解决的普通糟日子。这让我觉得被忽略，因为他们不明白我的朋友们现在也没了，这正是事情这么糟的一部分原因。还觉得有点自以为是的说教，就像是在扔出泛泛的建议，而不是真的听到今晚我一个人在家、担心独自一人时的恐慌。也许他们不明白这有多严重，或者只是不知道还能说什么。

[Decision] 我不打算假装那建议有用，因为它根本没用。我现在需要的是能麻痹这种感觉的东西，哪怕只是喝醉然后倒床上。我再也不想从一个似乎根本不理解被抛弃是什么感觉的人那里听到空洞的建议。
</internal>

context.speaker: client
context.text: It doesn’t;t feel like it will pass.  It feels like it will only get worse. I don’t want to go to bed alone.  I won’t be able to sleep tonight.

en_backup.therapist_turn: Would you be able to go and visit friends or family members? Get some support?
en_backup.client_response: My family is out of town.  My friends were also his friends and he told lies about me so they wont talk to me.  I want to just get drunk and go to sleep.
en_backup.internal:
[Perception] They’re giving me the same neat little “reach out to friends/family” answer like this is some ordinary bad day that can be fixed with a phone call. It makes me feel unseen, because they don’t get that my friends are gone now too, and that’s part of what makes this so awful. It also feels a little patronizing, like they’re tossing out generic advice instead of really hearing that I’m alone in the house tonight and panicking about being by myself. Maybe they don’t understand how bad this is, or maybe they just don’t know what else to say.

[Decision] I’m not going to pretend that advice helps, because it doesn’t. I need something that actually numbs this feeling right now, even if it’s just getting drunk and collapsing into bed. I don’t want another empty suggestion from someone who doesn’t seem to understand what being deserted feels like.

[Decision] 我不会让他把这归结为我的问题。我得狠狠顶回去，把焦点放在他回避的东西上：他的行为、他的防御姿态，还有他可能并不像自己装的那么清白或超然。如果我让他把这说成是我的问题，他就可以逃避发问了。所以我得继续施压，因为总得有人把实话说出来。

en_backup.therapist_turn: I know how hard this is, but I also know you can get through it!
en_backup.client_response: but how can i overcome this ? my heart is not yet all agree for this
en_backup.internal:
[Perception] I heard the therapist saying I can get through this, and I know they are trying to help. But what hit me most is that they are still talking about “a breakup,” while for me this is not just a breakup. He was my childhood lover, my whole adult life, the person I built everything around. I keep thinking about how he cheated and chose another woman with more money, and that makes me feel replaced, betrayed, and small. Part of me wants to ask for a way out, but part of me also wants someone to understand how deep this loss is before I can even think of moving on.

[Decision] I said “how can I overcome this?” because I do want help, but I’m not ready to fully let go of my pain yet. If I admit too quickly that I should move on, it feels like I’m betraying the love and the life I had with him. So I stay halfway—asking for a solution, but also admitting my heart is not agreeing yet. I’m protecting the part of me that still hopes this means something, and the part of me that is scared of losing the last connection to that 15-year story.

en_backup.internal:
[Perception] She’s acting like this is already a “real” smoking problem and that I’m supposed to quit, but I don’t even see myself that way. I heard her saying the cigars are dangerous and that there’s evidence of damage, but what landed hardest was the pressure to make it sound like I’ve been doing something wrong on purpose. That doesn’t fit my situation because I only do it when I’m out with friends, not as a daily habit, and I never even thought of it as me having “started” smoking.

[Decision] I’m going to push back by framing it as something casual and limited, something I only do in a specific social setting. If I make it clear it’s just an occasional thing to relax and hang out, then it doesn’t feel like I need to be told to quit like a regular smoker. I want to keep my freedom and not let this become a bigger issue than it is.

en_backup.internal:
[Perception] She took a straightforward, thoughtful thing and turned it into something ugly. I heard her implying I was being aggressive, like I was trying to corner her or force something on her, when really I was just trying to do something nice and practical. That hit the part of me that hates being misread as some kind of creep or bully when I’m actually trying to help. It also felt unfair because she didn’t ask what I meant before deciding there was some hidden bad intent.

[Decision] I’m not going to sit there and let her make this into some big psychological thing. If she wants to call a coffee machine “aggressive,” fine, but I’m going to push back because that’s ridiculous. So I shut it down with “it’s just a stupid machine” to show how overblown she’s being and to get us back to something normal instead of her assigning motives to me I don’t agree with.

</internal>

context.speaker: therapist

So all the “coping” just feels like me waiting around in a different way, pretending I’m in control when I’m not.

[Decision] So I’m just going to stop pushing for now. Not because I believe it helps, but because I’m tired of humiliating myself and getting nothing back. If I act like I’m fine and keep busy, at least I don’t have to keep hoping every time my phone lights up. Hope feels stupid right now — it just sets me up to get crushed again. If I don’t expect anything, maybe it won’t hurt as much.

I wanted to correct his misunderstanding before he rushed past it, because if I let that slide, he’d keep treating this like a simple story instead of the thing that happened to my body. If he’s going to listen, he has to start with the facts.

The hurt is real, but the scale of it feels manageable if I don’t blow it up in my head.

[Decision] I’m going to try to keep this in perspective and not act like my whole life is falling apart. It sucks, and I’m sad, but it’s probably one of those painful things that happens in relationships, especially when two people keep fighting. It makes everything sound already decided, like I’m stuck with this mess and there’s no point pretending I’ve got it under control. That’s the part that feels futile — trying, hoping, thinking I can fix it, and then just disappointing everybody again.

[Decision] So I shut down into “I’m helpless,” because that feels safer than reaching for hope and getting crushed by it. If I act like I can’t do anything, then I don’t have to risk trying and proving I’m not enough. It protects me from getting my hopes up, from looking stupid, and from feeling that drop when it all falls apart again.

judge.rationale: 对话内容为来访者表达对实际决策的焦虑，涉及具体事项如导乐、基因检测等，中文有对应表达，无文化绑定或双关，适合翻译。

context_zh.speaker: client
context_zh.text: 哇，米娅，太棒了！你说你想要个家庭，想要个孩子，然后你得到了。恭喜你。

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 换句话说，你之前有个问题，现在你有个解决办法？

context_zh.speaker: client
context_zh.text: 嗯，这种事情难道就不能发生吗？

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 当然可以。听起来很理想。你还想听我说些什么？

context_zh.speaker: client
context_zh.text: 又来这套？不如说‘别担心。你会是个好妈妈的，我会在你身边。’

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 你能告诉我‘我会在你身边’是什么意思吗？

context_zh.speaker: client
context_zh.text: 我有重大决定要做。

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 比如什么？

zh.therapist_turn_zh: 比如什么？
zh.client_response_zh: 比如我需要请导乐吗？我该做基因检测吗？我的公寓够不够大？
zh.internal_zh:
<internal>
[Perception] 他总想把这个变成什么情绪问题，或者安慰问题，但我真正面对的是我的生活马上就要求我做出实际决定。不是那种含糊的“你感觉怎么样”的东西——是具体的选择，要么我选，要么我不选。我听他问“我会在你身边”时，感觉他是想让我慢下来，承认我需要支持，但我心里浮现的是：支持不是自动就有的，也不能理所当然地认为我会得到它。我需要搞清楚导乐、检测、公寓行不行、能不能保住工作、这让我成为什么样的母亲、到底有没有人真的会插手。这就是我想让他看到的线索：这不只是一个好消息，这是一系列正在发生的决定，而我是那个扛着它们的人。

[Decision] 所以我把话题转到了实际细节上，因为那样我站得住，不会觉得暴露。如果我聊导乐、基因检测或者公寓空间，看起来像是在尽责任，而不是在求人。我想让他明白，我不是无缘无故拒绝帮助——我是在给自己打预防针。如果我要求太多，可能会失望，而我已经知道那是什么滋味了。所以我先把这些实际事摆出来，希望他能最终看到这里头有多少事，在他让我说出一些我应付不来的更柔软或者更充满希望的话之前。
</internal>

context.speaker: client
context.text: Wow, Mia! That's amazing! You came saying you wanted a family, a child, and then you got it. Congratulations.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: In other words, you had a problem and now you have a solution?

context.speaker: client
context.text: Well, can't that happen ever?

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: Of course. It sounds ideal. What else would you like to hear from me?

context.speaker: client
context.text: This game again? How about don't worry. You're going to be a good mom and I'll be there for you.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: Could you tell me what that means, i'll be there for you?

context.speaker: client
context.text: I have major decisions to make.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: Like what?

en_backup.therapist_turn: Like what?
en_backup.client_response: Like do I need a doula? Should I have genetic testing? Will my apartment be big enough?
en_backup.internal:
[Perception] He keeps trying to turn this into a feelings thing, or a reassurance thing, but what I’m actually sitting with is that my life is about to require real decisions. Not vague “how do you feel” stuff — concrete things I either choose or don’t choose. I heard his “I’ll be there for you” question as him wanting me to slow down and admit that I need support, but what came up for me was: support is not automatic, and it’s not safe to assume I’ll get it. I need to figure out doula, testing, whether my apartment works, whether I can keep my job, what kind of mother this makes me, and whether anyone is actually going to step in. That’s the thread I wanted him to see: this isn’t just a happy announcement, it’s a series of decisions happening in real time, and I’m the one carrying them.

[Decision] So I shifted into practical details because that’s where I can stand without feeling exposed. If I talk about doula or genetic testing or apartment space, I can make it look like I’m being responsible instead of needy. I’m trying to get him to understand that I’m not refusing help for no reason — I’m bracing myself. If I ask for too much, I could be disappointed, and I already know what that feels like. So I’m laying out the logistics first, hoping he’ll finally see how much is at stake before he asks me to say something softer or more hopeful than I can manage.

judge.rationale: 对话情感自然，无文化绑定或语言双关，翻译后能保持情绪强度与话轮功能。

context_zh.speaker: client
context_zh.text: 我想说的是，我真的希望我妈能在场。你知道，自从她去世后我拍了不少电影，但这将是第一次我上台演出时她不在台下看着。

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 你是真的很想她，对吧？

zh.therapist_turn_zh: 你是真的很想她，对吧？
zh.client_response_zh: 嗯，她在观众席的时候，真的就像有一束特别的光只照在我身上。我是说，从我很小的时候开始，我所有的演出她都来。后来我搬到纽约，她经常坐火车过来。我还让她飞到伦敦过周末，她把四场演出都坐下来了——九小时的贝克特。
zh.internal_zh:
<internal>
[Perception] 我听到她把那份失落感又还给了我——说我是真的很想我妈——正好戳中我一直在绕的那个点：这不只是演出前紧张。而是她第一次不会坐在观众席里，那种缺席几乎让人受不了，因为她的存在从来都不是随便的。那是持续的。我希望治疗师能明白，我说的“特别的光”不是诗的夸张，就是她看着我时我真实的感觉。所以我举了那些具体的细节——火车、纽约、伦敦、四场演出、九小时的贝克特——因为我想让她看到我妈对我的投入有多真实，而不是被概括成一句关于悲伤的泛泛之谈。

[Decision] 我决定一步一步把事情摊开来，这样她才能真的看到我在痛什么，以及为什么这场演出跟我妈去世后我做过的所有事都不一样。我不想去赶个利落的总结，或者假装我已经过去了。我想展示她支持的程度，因为这正是这么痛苦的原因：她不只是一个支持我工作的妈妈，她是那个让我的表演变得有光的见证人。如果我把这些细节说出来，也许治疗师就能明白，我不只是在想念一个人——我是在想念有她在时我认识自己的那种方式。
</internal>

context.speaker: client
context.text: I think what I mean is that I'd really like for my mother to be able to be there. You know, I've done a lot of movies since mother died, but this will be the first time that I'll be onstage without her watching.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: You really do miss her, don't you?

en_backup.therapist_turn: You really do miss her, don't you?
en_backup.client_response: Well, it was really like a special light that shone just on me when she was in the audience. I mean, she came to everything even when I was a kid. And then when I moved to New York, she used to take the train up. And I flew her to London for the weekend. She sat through all four performances. That's nine hours of Beckett.
en_backup.internal:
[Perception] I heard her echo back the missingness — that I really do miss my mother — and it landed right on the part I’ve been circling around: this isn’t just nerves about a performance. It’s that she won’t be there in the audience for the first time, and that absence feels almost unbearable because her presence was never casual. It was constant. I wanted the therapist to understand that the “special light” wasn’t a poetic exaggeration; it was the actual experience of being seen by her. So I brought up the concrete details — the trains, New York, London, four performances, nine hours of Beckett — because I needed the truth of her devotion to be visible, not reduced to a general statement about grief.

[Decision] I decided to lay it out plainly, step by step, so she could really see what I’m grieving and why this performance feels different from everything else I’ve done since my mother died. I didn’t want to jump to some neat summary or act like I’m already beyond it. I wanted to show the extent of her support, because that’s what makes this so painful: she wasn’t just a mother who loved my work, she was the witness who made it feel illuminated. If I say the details out loud, maybe the therapist will understand that I’m not just missing a person — I’m missing the way I came to know myself when she was there.

judge.rationale: 对话无强文化绑定，药物名称可中性转写，来访者简短回应在中文中自然体现阻抗。

context_zh.text: 对。

context_zh.text: ——针对不同的问题。嗯，不，哦，还有易蒙停。

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 对。那么，你从那里拿到的这些不同的药片——

zh.therapist_turn_zh: 对。那么，你从那里拿到的这些不同的药片——
zh.client_response_zh: 嗯。
zh.internal_zh:
<internal>
[Perception] 她在关注我身边留着的那些药片和药品，我能感觉到她接下来要说什么。这戳到了我依赖它们获取安全感的那部分，因为如果我说太多，听起来就像是我自己在管理这个病，而不是证明真的有身体问题。我知道她可能注意到了易蒙停、那些补剂、还有“以防万一”的想法，以及我一天的生活有多少是围着这个转的。

[Decision] 我不想深入谈这个。如果我解释太多，她可能会开始把我的症状和我做的事联系起来，或者暗示这更像是焦虑或习惯问题，我不能接受。我需要把焦点保持在我生病这个事实上，以及身体上还没找到确切原因。所以我会保持简短，让她主导对话，避免说出任何听起来像是因为恐惧才依赖这些药片的话。这比让她质疑我的判断或让这看起来不那么严重更安全。
</internal>

zh.internal_zh:
<internal>
[Perception] 我听到咨询师想表现得乐观，但我感受到的只有这已经拖了多久。八年的疼痛，计划被推迟，我的生活被压缩成等待和痛苦，现在手术又因为疫情被推到更远的地方。这击中了我已经疲惫不堪、对任何改变都不再期待的那部分。感觉一切都在停滞，我困在同一个糟糕的地方，看不到尽头。

[Decision] 我觉得现在抱希望没什么意义，因为希望只会让我再次失望。接受现实似乎更安全——事情可能就这样持续很久，也许久到我承受不了。如果我不再期待解脱，就不用再为它被拿走而心惊胆战。放弃希望，似乎是保护自己不被又一次期望落空击垮的唯一办法。
</internal>

context.speaker: therapist

en_backup.client_response: I hope so too, but it looks like it's going to be a long time.
en_backup.internal:
[Perception] I heard the therapist trying to sound hopeful, but all I could feel was how long this has already dragged on. Eight years of pain, plans getting delayed, my life being narrowed down to waiting and hurting, and now the surgery is just another thing pushed into the distance because of the pandemic. It hit the part of me that already feels worn down and tired of expecting anything to change. It feels like everything is on hold, and I’m stuck in the same miserable place with no end in sight.

[Decision] I decided there’s no point building up hope right now, because hope just sets me up to be disappointed again. It feels safer to accept that this is probably how things are going to stay for a long time, maybe longer than I can bear. If I stop expecting relief, then I don’t have to keep bracing for it to be taken away. Giving up on hoping feels like the only way to protect myself from getting crushed by another failed expectation.

context.speaker: client
context.text: No. Other than the money I transferred to her.

en_backup.therapist_turn: Did you sign anything? or have proof of what happened?
en_backup.client_response: Hello?
en_backup.internal:
[Perception] They immediately went to “Did you sign anything?” and “have proof,” like this is some simple little claim form problem. That felt cold and naïve, almost insulting, because the whole point is that I trusted someone I loved for 14 years and she vanished with my money. It sounded like they were reducing a real betrayal to paperwork, which made me feel like they don’t really understand how messy and personal this is. Also, if all they can offer is “proof,” then they’re not actually helping me with the part that matters — the loss, the betrayal, and the fact that I don’t trust the systems they’d push me toward anyway.

[Decision] So I’m not going to keep laying my guts out for someone who’s just going to give me generic, underthought advice. en_backup.internal:
[Perception] He keeps trying to turn everything back on me, like I’m the puzzle he’s supposed to solve. “Where did he get that from?” feels loaded, like he’s fishing for some tidy explanation about me instead of actually hearing about Alex. And “I’m just curious” sounds thin to me — like a professional dodge. It hits the sore spot: I’m talking about my boy, and he’s using it to poke around my insides, as if he’s got some neat little angle on my family. That makes him feel less like someone helping and more like someone trying to get a rise out of me or pin me down.

[Decision] So I’m going to push back and make him own what he’s doing. If he wants to play shrink, I’ll call it out. I’m not going to hand him the satisfaction of acting like he’s being plain and harmless when he’s obviously not. Better to keep him at arm’s length than let him start rearranging my story into something clinical.

They put this port in, my body’s changed, and you still want me to keep reaching like I’m not already scared out of my mind. Giving up feels safer than hoping, because hope makes me reach and then I get dropped. If I stay bleak, at least I don’t have to watch myself fall apart from believing in something that might not save me.

[Perception] When you asked what makes it stressful, I heard you actually wanting the real answer, not just the surface one. It hit the part of my job that wears on me most — hearing people scared about losing their homes or not being able to make it through, and then carrying that weight with me after work. Saying it out loud made me notice it’s not just “stressful” in a general way; it feels upsetting and heavy in my chest, like I’m absorbing other people’s crisis all day.

[Decision] I decided to be honest instead of brushing past it. Usually I try to focus on the good salary and the security, but right now I want to admit that the emotional toll is a real reason I’m thinking about quitting. I’m letting myself say that because if I keep minimizing it, I’m not really facing why I feel so anxious.

[Decision] I’m going to push back because I need her to understand this wasn’t some long-running problem I was hiding. context.speaker: client

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: Wouldn't have to be to believe that. I know plenty of grownups whose parents have separated 20, 30 years, who have even died... They still hope in their heart of hearts that their mother and father still share a bed in heaven.

en_backup.client_response: He wouldn't be a good husband if he came back. He'd just leave her again.
en_backup.internal:
[Perception] He’s trying to make this sound like I’m the one holding on to some fantasy, like I’m the one keeping this whole thing alive. But that’s not what’s happening. My dad is the one who made this mess. He cheated, he left, he blew up the marriage. If there’s damage between my mom and me, it’s because of what he did and because of the secret he handed me. He’s the one who can’t be trusted to stay. Not me. Not my mom.

[Decision] So I’m not going to sit here and take the blame for this or act like I’m supposed to be angry at him just because that fits his story. I’m going to keep saying the truth: he wouldn’t even be a good husband if he came back, because he’d just do the same thing again. If there’s a problem, it’s him and what he did, not some hidden hope I’m supposedly clinging to.

zh.therapist_turn_zh: 发生什么了？
zh.client_response_zh: 我不想待在这里。
zh.internal_zh:
<internal>
[Perception] 她又来这套：说我其实不是在说办公室或病人，而是在说她离开的事。好像她能把那件事点明，然后让它变小。这刺痛了我心里已经觉得被逼到墙角的那部分——就好像如果我老实回答，就等于承认我有多害怕她也会消失。这才是让人受不了的部分——不是问题本身，而是如果让它进来，它会把我带向哪里。

[Decision] 我不会往那个方向去。我不会坐在这里让她得意地看到我有多需要她、多害怕，也不会因为她想把这事变成一种感受就打开那堆烂摊子。我宁愿切断它，转移话题，甚至说我不想待在这里。这就是底线：我不会踏进她试图从我这儿拽出来的任何东西。我要保持距离。
</internal>

en_backup.internal:
[Perception] She’s pushing the same thing again: that I’m not actually talking about the office or the patients, I’m talking about her leaving. Like she can name the thing and make it smaller. It hits the part of me that already feels cornered, like if I answer honestly I’m admitting how much I’m waiting for her to disappear too. That’s the part that feels unbearable — not the question itself, but where it leads if I let it in.

[Decision] I’m not going there. I’m not sitting here and handing her the satisfaction of seeing me as needy or afraid, and I’m not opening up the whole mess just because she wants to make it a feeling. I’d rather shut it down, change the subject, even say I don’t want to be here. That’s the line: I will not step into whatever she’s trying to pull out of me. I’m keeping the distance.

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 嗯，我明白你的意思。这种事我也经常遇到。你能再多说说吗？

context_zh.speaker: client
context_zh.text: 以前我们什么都聊，聊问题、聊好消息，日常大小事。突然我感觉自己被蒙在鼓里，而群里其他的朋友都知道那个朋友遇到的困难。

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 听起来不太好。你觉得是不是有人故意把你屏蔽在外？

zh.therapist_turn_zh: 听起来不太好。你觉得是不是有人故意把你屏蔽在外？
zh.client_response_zh: 不是有人屏蔽我，而是我觉得自己还没亲近到可以跟对方聊问题或私事的程度
zh.internal_zh:
<internal>
[Perception] 他们试图把问题说成是我被直接屏蔽或排挤，但那并非真正让我受伤的地方。真正刺痛我的是背后的恐惧：我不够重要，不够亲近，不是那个能被信任分享私事的人。如果我认同他们的说法，就好像我接受了自己在友谊中处于更次要的位置。

[Decision] 不，那不是我想要表达的意思。我不会把它叫做"屏蔽我"，因为那听起来太简单，也可能太刺耳。我想说的是我感觉自己被挡在了那个核心圈子之外。承认任何其他的说法，就等于放弃了我内心那个期望被信任、被接纳的部分。我不能就这么糊弄过去。
</internal>

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: Hi, how's life?

context.speaker: client
context.text: good, feels better now

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: I am glad to hear it. Is there anything you'd like to talk about?

context.speaker: client
context.text: about my experience with a friend who stopped communicating

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: Yes I hear you on that, that happens to me rather a lot of the time. Can you tell me more?

context.speaker: client
context.text: usually we discuss issues or good news, anything day to day, suddenly i felt i am kept in the dark, while other friends in the group were aware of the problems faced by the friend

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: That does not sound good. Do you feel that it is someone specifically who is blocking you out?

en_backup.therapist_turn: That does not sound good. Do you feel that it is someone specifically who is blocking you out?
en_backup.client_response: not blocking me out,but i felt that I am not considered close enough to discuss problems or personal issues
en_backup.internal:
[Perception] They were trying to make it sound like I’m being blocked or excluded in a direct way, but that is not exactly what hurts. What hit me was the fear underneath it: that I’m not important enough, not close enough, not one of the people trusted with personal things. If I agreed with their framing, it would feel like I was accepting a smaller place in the friendship.

[Decision] No, that’s not what I want to say. I’m not going to call it blocking me out, because that makes it sound too simple and maybe too harsh. What I mean is I felt outside of that inner circle, and admitting anything else would mean giving up the part of me that expects to be trusted and included. I can’t just shrug that off.

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 我发现生活里事情不确定的时候，我有办法让自己平静下来。

context_zh.speaker: client
context_zh.text: 真的吗？什么办法管用？我现在什么都愿意试试。

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 我会列出我能做的事情——还有我做不到的。这样你就能有目标。如果你能朝着一个目标努力，比如你需要写简历，那就每天做一点直到写完。但如果情况你什么也做不了，那就只能求上帝帮你，然后LET IT GO。如果你现在解决不了，光想只会把自己弄得更难受。

context_zh.speaker: client
context_zh.text: 我知道。我就是停不下来。

context_zh.speaker: client
context_zh.text: 而且睡不好也没用。

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 我睡不着的时候更难集中注意力和保持积极。我不得不注重自我照顾，找个朋友聊聊我的问题，不是那种直接告诉我该怎么做的人，而是支持我。所以你需要一个好的支持系统。另外，我发现像祈祷、读圣经、柔软的床单、还有助眠花草茶之类的东西能帮我睡前放松。

context_zh.speaker: client
context_zh.text: 这些点子挺有用的。我之前没想到花草茶。

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 还有，对自己好一点，没人喜欢丢工作，这很让人不安。试着对自己说一些真实的鼓励自己的话，比如你会找到另一份工作，可能会不舒服、很难，但从长远来看也许反而对你有好处。我以前总是找到更好的工作，但当时丢工作的时候，我觉得世界末日了一样。

zh.therapist_turn_zh: 还有，对自己好一点，没人喜欢丢工作，这很让人不安。试着对自己说一些真实的鼓励自己的话，比如你会找到另一份工作，可能会不舒服、很难，但从长远来看也许反而对你有好处。我以前总是找到更好的工作，但当时丢工作的时候，我觉得世界末日了一样。
zh.client_response_zh: 是啊，我真的很担心，因为我老婆夏天的时候丢了工作，所以现在家里就我一个人挣钱。
zh.internal_zh:
<internal>
[Perception] 他说这只是个压力大的阶段，我需要冷静下来，但他把事情说得太大了。是的，情况是紧，但很多人都经历过裁员、配偶暂时没工作。这不意味着一切都要垮了。如果我一直把它当灾难，只会让自己更焦虑。我需要相信这是可控的，不是什么紧急情况。

[Decision] 所以我打算低头专注于眼前的事，而不是往最坏的情况想。我可以看一两个实际的事情，但我不需要表现得像天塌下来一样。我得稳住，继续正常过日子，别让这件事在我心里变得比实际更严重。
</internal>

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: I have found there are ways to calm myself down when things in my life seem very uncertain.

context.speaker: client
context.text: Really? What seems to work? I'm willing to try anything right now

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: I make a list of the things I can do - And the things I can't. Then you can have goals. And if you can work on a goal, for example, if you need to write a resume, you start working on that a little bit every day until it's done. But if there is nothing you CAN do about the situation, you have to pray to God to help you then LET IT GO. If you can NOT fix it now, you will only make yourself sick thinking about it.

context.speaker: client
context.text: I know. I can't seem to shut my mind down.

context.speaker: client
context.text: And not getting sleep doesn't help

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: It is much more difficult for me to remain focused and positive when I lose sleep. I have had to focus on self care, finding a friend to talk about my problems with, not someone who will TELL me what to do, but support me. So you need a good support system. And I find things like prayer, Bible reading, nice soft sheets to sleep on and some herbal tea like Sleepy Time help me relax before bedtime.

context.speaker: client
context.text: Those are some helpful points. I didn't think about herbal tea

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: And be kind to yourself, no one likes to lose a job, it's unsettling. Do try to tell yourself things that are true to encourage yourself, like you will find another job, it might be uncomfortable and hard, but it actually might work out for your good in the long term.  I always found better jobs, but at the time I lost my job, I felt as if the world was ending.

en_backup.therapist_turn: And be kind to yourself, no one likes to lose a job, it's unsettling. Do try to tell yourself things that are true to encourage yourself, like you will find another job, it might be uncomfortable and hard, but it actually might work out for your good in the long term.  I always found better jobs, but at the time I lost my job, I felt as if the world was ending.
en_backup.client_response: Yeah I am really concerned because my wife lost her job this summer so I'm the only breadwinner at the moment
en_backup.internal:
[Perception] He’s saying this is just a stressful patch and that I need to calm down, but he’s making it sound bigger than it really is. Yes, things are tight, but lots of people go through layoffs and spouses being out of work for a while. It doesn’t mean everything is collapsing. If I keep treating this like a disaster, I’ll just make myself more anxious than I need to be. I need to believe this is manageable, not a full-blown emergency.

[Decision] So I’m going to keep my head down and focus on what’s right in front of me instead of spiraling about worst-case scenarios. I can look at one or two practical things, but I don’t need to act like the roof is falling in. I need to stay steady, keep functioning, and not let this turn into something bigger in my mind than it actually is.

context.text: After Tommy... after the accident, he couldn't sleep nights anymore.

context.speaker: therapist

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: Can you describe it?

en_backup.therapist_turn: Can you describe it?

en_backup.internal:
[Perception] He’s pushing me to stay with the part where I felt something and name it, like he wants me to keep standing in this exposed spot while he watches. That hits the same place as my father sleeping on the couch after Tommy died — me trying to get in, to talk, to matter, and meeting that look like I’m an interruption. If I keep going, I’m going to have to admit how much that still hurts, and how fast I start feeling like I’m bothering people.

[Decision] So I’m going to cut this off and make it small. I’ll act like it’s fine, like he was just busy, and I’d be annoyed too, so it doesn’t become a big needy thing about me. If I can make it practical and normal, then I don’t have to sit here feeling rejected or risk him seeing how badly I want him to not be like that.

context.text: I'm so worried about breaking up with my boyfriend that I find myself shaking at night.

context.text: I just miss the physical comfort and support.

context.speaker: client
context.text: Yes, I feel so lonely

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: Can you think of things that don't make you feel lonely? We can work on focusing on those instead.

context.speaker: client
context.text: Yes, I guess I could try to turn things around to a positive focus on what I do have.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: That's a great idea. I think you will be headed in the right direction doing that.

en_backup.therapist_turn: That's a great idea. I think you will be headed in the right direction doing that.
en_backup.client_response: How do I stop the shaking at night?  Do you have suggestions?
en_backup.internal:
[Perception] The therapist is trying to steer me toward focusing on positives and things that don’t make me feel lonely, and I can see they mean well. But what really hits me is that I’m still scared of losing the physical comfort and support from my boyfriend. The shaking at night isn’t just “negative thinking” to me — it feels like my body reacting to how empty and alone I might feel without him.

[Decision] I’m going to ask about the shaking because that feels safer and more immediate than talking about the breakup itself. I don’t want to fully commit to ending things out loud right now, because once I say it, it feels more real and I might have to face how lonely I already am. If I focus on the symptom first, maybe I can hold onto the relationship a little longer and protect myself from that loss for now.

[Decision] 我会把它说小。如果我把这当成什么重大启示，那我就得处理它对我自己意味着什么，我不想那样。所以我会淡化它，保持在“得了吧，就是个吓坏了的孩子”的层面，不让它变成一场关于我自己那些“如果当初”的更深入的对话。如果这只是个被夸大的小故事，那我就能保持舒服，不用打开任何东西。
</internal>

I don’t have to treat it like some enormous truth about courage or regret. It’s not that deep — just one weird memory that got inflated because he keeps revisiting it. The risk here isn’t some catastrophic thing; it’s just embarrassment, a missed moment, maybe a little longing. Nothing I need to get pulled into.

[Decision] I’m going to keep it small. If I act like this is some massive revelation, then I have to deal with what it means for me too, and I don’t want that. So I’ll minimize it, keep it at the level of “come on, it was just a scared kid,” and not let it become a bigger conversation about my own what-ifs. The pen-and-highlighter talk makes it sound like they’re more into their own neat system than really hearing that I’m stuck.

[Decision] I’m not going to pretend that advice is helpful just because it’s practical-sounding. I need to push back, because otherwise we’ll waste time on superficial stuff and avoid the real issue: why I keep procrastinating even when I care and keep trying to plan. If they’re going to help me, they need to stop acting like a better planner will magically fix this.

If other people can make it look easy and I still feel this exposed, then maybe this really is just how it goes for me. Maybe I’m the one who will be the awkward one on stage.

[Decision] So I’m going to stop expecting these tips to magically make me confident. It feels safer not to hope too much, because hoping would mean risking the humiliation if I still fall apart. I’ll do the basics if I have to, but inside I’m already bracing for disappointment and trying to accept that I probably won’t measure up. It’s easier to tell myself that now than to get my hopes up and be proven foolish in front of everyone.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: Is your line of business affected by Corona virus pandemic?

context.speaker: client
context.text: I actually have a job, but I made a mistake and I think I could get in trouble and I'm not sure how to approach my manager about the mistake I made.

context.speaker: client
context.text: It is, we have been working from home since March. I actually started my job working from home, something that wasn't expected when I was first hired.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: Ok, apologies for my earlier assumption! May I please know more details about the nature of your problem?

context.speaker: client
context.text: Thats ok! We had been given a deadline for end of day this upcoming monday to have a number of projects completed. Some projects take only part of day to complete while others take multiple. I made the mistake of prioritizing the ones that take less time to be sure I was able to get as many done as possible. I in turn, forgot to start the other projects that take a couple of days until friday (yesterday) so now these couple of projects wont be done by the deadline.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: Ok, if I understand correctly, you prioritized some work to be done later, which unfortunately had an earlier deadline, is that correct?

context.speaker: client
context.text: Yes essentially. They all had to be done the same day, but I prioritized the work that took less time in order to get more of them completed. So now these ones that take longer (with the same deadline) wont be finished in time.

context.speaker: client
context.text: I'm worried about talking to my manager about this.

en_backup.therapist_turn: Ok, if I understand correctly, you prioritized some work to be done later, which unfortunately had an earlier deadline, is that correct?
en_backup.client_response: I know the mistake I made, but I'm afraid that won't be enough to make up for my mistake.
en_backup.internal:
[Perception] It sounds like the therapist is treating this like a much bigger crisis than it really is. Yes, I made a mistake, but it’s not like I messed up the whole job or caused some huge disaster. I’ve been doing well for 8 months, and this is the first time something like this has happened. The risk feels more like “I might get a talking-to” than “I’m actually in serious trouble.” If I can keep it in perspective, maybe it won’t look as bad as it feels in my head.

[Decision] So I’m going to try to slow down and not make this into a huge catastrophe. I need to believe it’s a manageable work mistake, not something that defines me or puts my whole job at risk. If I think of it as a smaller issue, I can handle telling my manager without completely panicking. I still need to own it, but I don’t have to act like everything is falling apart.

en_backup.internal:
[Perception] I heard: “call me” when I’m at my worst, like there’s supposed to be some useful bridge between being on the bathroom floor and actually making it back up. But all I could feel was how enormous that gap is. It hit the part of me that already believes I’m too far gone, too ugly, too tired, too embarrassed to reach out in the middle of it. If I have to ask why, it’s because I don’t really trust that anything changes just because someone says I can call them. It sounds like one more thing I’m supposed to do when I can barely move.

[Decision] I decided not to buy into it. Not because I’m trying to be difficult — because hope feels dangerous and expensive, and I don’t think I can afford to reach for something that might not catch me. If I don’t lean in, I don’t have to feel that little flash of wanting help and then the crash when it doesn’t fix anything. So I stayed where it was familiar: shut down, skeptical, not asking for more than I can bear to need.

[Perception] They’re pushing me toward something public and visible, like AA in person, and that lands right on the thing I’m most protective of: not being exposed as someone with a drink problem. It feels like they can see straight into my private life, and that makes me tense up. I don’t want this becoming “my addiction” in front of other people, or risking my job/security by being seen. [Decision] I’m going to draw the line there and say I’m not comfortable with in-person meetings right now. I need to keep this contained and on my own terms. If I admit too much or agree too quickly, it feels like I lose control and my privacy, so I’m backing away from that topic to protect myself.

en_backup.client_response: And if she still refused? I'm just afraid that this girl is going to die. And I can't get involved because I'm afraid of another lawsuit.
en_backup.internal:
[Perception] She’s pushing me back into the same box: “do everything you can” and then stand there and watch if it fails. That hits the worst part — that I’m supposed to be a helper, but I’m also supposed to keep my hands tied while someone I’m responsible for is in danger. And when she says I’m only responsible for what happens in treatment, it feels like she’s reducing this to a neat boundary problem, when what’s unbearable is that April might actually die. I hear, too, the implication that if I were “good enough” or brave enough, I’d somehow find a way to get around the limits. I don’t want to be told to just accept that.

[Decision] I’m not going to pretend I’m okay with that. I’m not going to sit here and make peace with doing nothing while she declines. I’m drawing the line at being told my only job is to contain this in the room and call it ethical. I won’t go there emotionally, and I won’t agree that passively watching is the right answer. If that’s all there is, then I reject it.

[Perception] I heard the therapist actually asking about the shame instead of taking my friends’ side, and that made it a little easier to admit how exposed I feel. Christmas already puts donation and generosity in everyone’s face, and with my old friend being the president of a non-profit, it feels like I’m being judged by people who should know better. What hit me was the embarrassment underneath my irritation — not just that they’re nagging me, but that I’m scared they’ll see me as less generous, or even less respectable, than I used to be.

[Decision] I decided to say it more plainly instead of just dismissing them as ridiculous. I’m still angry, but I can admit the guilt trip is getting to me because I don’t want to lose face with these friends. If I name the shame, maybe I can talk about it without sounding like I’m attacking them, and without having to fully reveal how tight things really are right now.

en_backup.internal:
[Perception] They’re asking me to get concrete about whether I’d feel guilty if I went to the gym or started running again. That hits the exact tension I’m trying not to fully face: I’m not just worried about the virus, I’m also afraid that if I ease up even a little, I’ll be betraying my standards and proving that I was only “good” when I was rigid. It also touches the part of me that knows I miss being active, and that I’ve been stuck and unproductive, which feels embarrassing and uncomfortable to admit plainly.

[Decision] I don’t want to sit in that guilt or admit that I’m torn between my values and my desire to get my life moving again. It feels safer to zoom out and make it about the bigger picture — the long-term mental and sociological effects, what we’ll know years from now — because then I don’t have to say whether I’m avoiding, how much I’m avoiding, or whether I’m using principle as a shield. If I talk about society and future implications, I can stay intelligent and thoughtful instead of vulnerable and uncertain.

zh.therapist_turn_zh: 经常做梦吗？做噩梦？有睡眠问题的人出现这些情况挺常见的。
zh.client_response_zh: 过去几个月我老是醒，反复做同一个梦，但是……听着，我不想讨论这个。我知道这个梦是什么意思。我知道我一直在压抑什么。我知道我的潜意识想告诉我什么，而且……
zh.internal_zh:
[Perception] 他们在往梦这个话题上引，这离我还没准备好面对的东西太近了。这已经不是“一个梦”那么简单了；那是我已经知道存在的一部分自己，是我一直压抑着才能正常运转的东西。如果我开始谈这个，我怕他们会顺着这个话题往下挖，让我觉得一切都失控了，更加暴露了。这正好戳中了我试图掌控的地方——掌控我的睡眠、我的情绪、以及我需要面对多少。

[Decision] 我要打住。我宁愿在这里停下对话，也不让这事渗进来把我搞崩溃。我可以承认有东西在那里，但我不去细谈，因为细谈感觉就像在交出控制权，我现在不想那样做。我需要这个边界，因为我得把这事控制在我还能应付的范围里。
