context.speaker: client
context.text: No, not anymore. I... I wake up after two or three hours.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: And what's your experience of that waking time?

context.speaker: client
context.text: No. Not particularly, no. I'm tired.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: What do you find yourself thinking about?

context.speaker: client
context.text: I find myself wishing that I had more Ambien. Listen, I've never slept well. I've always had a problem falling asleep.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: And once you are sleeping, do you sleep deeply? Are you restless?

context.speaker: client
context.text: Not really.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: Frequent dreams? Nightmares? They're not uncommon with people's sleep issues.

en_backup.therapist_turn: Frequent dreams? Nightmares? They're not uncommon with people's sleep issues.
en_backup.client_response: The past several months I have been waking up With a recurring dream but... Look, I'm not interested in discussing that. I know what the dream is about. I know what I've been suppressing. I know what my unconscious is trying to communicate with me and...
en_backup.internal:
[Perception] They’re moving toward the dream, and that feels too close to something I’m not ready to open. It’s not just “a dream” anymore; it’s the part of me I already know is there, the thing I’ve been keeping contained so I can keep functioning. If I start talking about it, I worry they’ll pull on it in a way that makes it all feel less controlled, more exposed. It hits the place where I’m trying to stay in charge—of my sleep, my emotions, and how much of this I have to face.

[Decision] I’m shutting this down. I’d rather stop the conversation here than let it get under my skin and unravel me. I can acknowledge that something is there without going into it, because going into it feels like handing over control and I’m not willing to do that right now. I need the boundary because I need to keep whatever this is from becoming bigger than I can manage.

context_zh.speaker: client

context_zh.speaker: client
context_zh.text: 还行吧，大概。就是分手了，很难过。

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 唉，听你这么说我也很难过。我们敞开自己去爱别人的时候都会经历这些。时间会慢慢冲淡这些感觉的。

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 我觉得分手从长远来看其实能让我们变得更好。它们让我们看清自己真正想要什么，不想要什么。

zh.therapist_turn_zh: 我觉得分手从长远来看其实能让我们变得更好。它们让我们看清自己真正想要什么，不想要什么。
zh.client_response_zh: 我知道，但我就是好像走不出来，你懂吗？不停回想我们在一起的那些美好时光，还有我有多爱他。
zh.internal_zh:
<internal>
[Perception] 那些话听起来都是平常那些安慰人的希望——“时间会过去”，“分手让人变得更好”——但偏偏戳中了我已经觉得困住、疲惫的那部分。是啊，我知道人们都这么说，可这改变不了我此时此刻还坐在这儿想他、反复回想一切、觉得我失去的是真正重要的东西。它击中了我一直希望这种痛能有意义的地方，可结果就是没完没了。

[Decision] 所以我现在干脆不挣扎了。就让自己难过着，跟“应该已经走出来”这种想法保持距离，因为硬逼自己去抱有希望又累又没用。如果我不期待任何改变，就不会一次又一次被自己的希望辜负。与其去够什么更好的东西然后眼睁睁看它溜走，不如就待在这个麻木又痛苦的事实里，还轻松点。
</internal>

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: Awl, I'm sorry to hear that. We all go through those moments when we open ourselves to love others. Time will allow these feelings to pass.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: I found that break ups make us better in the long run. They show us what we really want and what we dont.

en_backup.therapist_turn: I found that break ups make us better in the long run. They show us what we really want and what we dont.
en_backup.client_response: I know, but I just can't seem to move past it, ya know?  Replaying all the good times we had together, and how much I loved him.
en_backup.internal:
[Perception] It sounded like the usual hopeful stuff — “time will pass,” “breakups make us better” — but it just landed on the part of me that already feels stuck and tired. Like, yes, I know people say that, but it doesn’t change that I’m still sitting here missing him, replaying everything, and feeling like I lost something that actually mattered. It hit the place where I keep hoping the ache will make sense, and instead it just feels endless.

[Decision] So I’m not even going to fight it right now. I’ll just let myself stay sad and keep my distance from the idea that I’m supposed to be “moving on” already, because trying to force hope feels pointless and exhausting. If I don’t expect anything to change, then I don’t have to keep getting let down by my own hope. It’s easier to stay with the numb, miserable truth than to reach for something better and feel that slip away too.

context_zh.text: 他是个艺术家。那是他的工作。而且，裸体在我家完全正常。我早就习惯了。

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 裸体？

context_zh.speaker: client
context_zh.text: 裸体模特。女性的形体。就像素描基础课，Paul。艺术家必须从最纯粹的灵感出发。他的工作室就在家里，所以很多模特光着身子走来走去。没什么大不了的。我们很淡定。

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 所以对你来说，从小接触成年人的裸体是正常的，是吧？

zh.therapist_turn_zh: 所以对你来说，从小接触成年人的裸体是正常的，是吧？
zh.client_response_zh: 接触。啊，裸体。好可怕。乳房……吓死人了！
zh.internal_zh:
<internal>
[Perception] 他这么说就好像这是什么天大的、有伤害性的事——好像我住在一个瘆人的、充满性暗示的马戏团里，应该被搞出心理阴影似的。这话戳到了我想保护我爸、保护我自己对家记忆的那部分。如果我任由他把这事放大成“重大风险”，那我整个童年就被重新定义成病态的了，我不干。那只是裸体模特。艺术相关。在那个环境下很正常。不是什么灾难性的暴露。
[Decision] 所以我打算把它说得很轻。我要让他显得过度解读了，因为如果我承认这事很严重，我就得开始质疑我爸、质疑我的成长经历，还要质疑我现在是不是应该得创伤后应激障碍了。我没必要走到那一步。对他也许怪，但对我没啥。我能处理。不是什么大事。
</internal>

context.text: So this was normal for you, to be exposed to adults being naked, yeah?

en_backup.therapist_turn: So this was normal for you, to be exposed to adults being naked, yeah?
en_backup.client_response: Exposed. Ooh, nudity. How scary. Breasts... Terrifying!
en_backup.internal:
[Perception] He’s making it sound like this was some huge, damaging thing — like I was living in some creepy, sexually charged circus and should be messed up by it. That lands on the part of me that wants to protect my dad and my own memory of home. If I let it get inflated into “a major risk,” then suddenly my whole childhood gets recast as pathological, and I’m not okay with that. It was just nude models. Art stuff. Normal in that context. Not some catastrophic exposure.

[Decision] So I’m going to keep it small. I’m going to act like he’s overreading it, because if I admit it was serious, I have to start questioning my dad, my upbringing, and whether I’m supposed to be traumatized now. I don’t need to go there. It was weird to him maybe, but not to me. I can handle it. It’s not a big deal.

context.speaker: client
context.text: You have an entry door and an exit door?

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: It's for people's privacy. Some people don't like to... They don't like to run into each other.

en_backup.therapist_turn: It's for people's privacy. Some people don't like to... They don't like to run into each other.
en_backup.client_response: Are they ashamed?
en_backup.internal:
[Perception] That was the kind of question I could answer without really answering. “Ashamed” gives me somewhere to stand that isn’t about me. It sounds like a comment about the setup, about other people, about the door, about privacy. But it also brushes right up against what I don’t want to say: that I don’t like this kind of place, don’t like being seen, don’t like being the one who has to ask for help. It hit the part of me that wants to stay competent and detached, especially here, especially with something as personal as Alex.

[Decision] So I kept it short and a little sideways. If I say too much, I end up talking about my own discomfort, maybe my worry, maybe how hard this is for me to bring up at all. And once I start doing that, I lose control of the conversation and I have to feel more than I want to. It was safer to leave it as a question and let the therapist carry the meaning, instead of admitting that yes, maybe there is embarrassment here, and maybe that’s part of why I keep things brief.

The issue feels less like some deep personal failure and more like she’s overworried and making my being “a little sick” into a bigger deal.

[Decision] I’m going to keep it on her stress and the practical stuff, because that’s easier and safer than making this about me being actually messed up. If I talk like she was really stressed out, then it sounds reasonable and I don’t have to admit there’s something seriously wrong with me or that I’m the problem here. I can stay the grownup, the one who’s basically fine, and let her be the one who’s overdoing it.

[Decision] 我后撤了，因为我不信任他们能理解我。如果他们打算把这事儿说成是套路，或者替我说出我的意思，那我觉得再敞开心扉也没什么意义。我宁可直接简短回答，也不给他们更多机会误解。对一个好像有点太自信地告诉我我的冲突意味着什么的人，保持戒备反而更安全。

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 哦，新冠疫情现在确实对很多学生产生了负面影响。在家上网课对你有没有负面影响？

context_zh.text: 嗯，我觉得我没法集中注意力，因为我回到了家里和家人在一块，我就觉得干扰太多了。

context_zh.text: 是啊，有时候家庭确实很难理解边界这个概念。

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 我自己上大学时也出于类似原因去了外地，但说实话，我其实觉得大学生活更让人分心。

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 你有没有跟家人说过你现在遇到的这些问题？

zh.client_response_zh: 说实话，我担心他们会失望。也许这很傻。但我还记得我拿到奖学金时他们有多骄傲。我不想让他们怪我。
zh.internal_zh:
<internal>
[Perception] 他们基本上是在让我做我一直回避的那件事：告诉家人不要进我房间，认真对待学业。也许他们说得对，“边界”很重要，但我只听到这会引起一堆事——我要解释自己，让他们受伤或失望，可能让他们觉得我把一切都怪到他们头上。这触动了我已经觉得自己同时被家庭和奖学金困住的那部分。如果我连自己需要的空间都得不到，那就感觉没有什么真正的方法能解决这个问题，而不引发我不想要的麻烦。

[Decision] 所以我还是自己想办法应付，不提这件事。接受分心似乎比开一个口更容易，万一谈崩了，每个人都觉得我在失败。如果我还期望更多，我就得承认自己多需要帮助，但之后如果没改变，我会感觉更糟。不如保持沉默，告诉自己我会想别的办法，即使那基本就是凑合着过，不抱太多期望。
</internal>

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: Yeah sometimes families can struggle with the idea of boundaries.

context.text: I also went away to school for similar reasons, but I actually found college life way more distracting tbh.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: Have you told your family about the issues your having?

en_backup.therapist_turn: Have you told your family about the issues your having?
en_backup.client_response: I honestly am worried that they will be disappointed. Maybe that's crazy. I just remember how proud they were when I got this scholarship. I don't want them to blame me.
en_backup.internal:
[Perception] They’re basically asking me to do the one thing I’ve been avoiding: tell my family to stop coming into my room and to take my schoolwork seriously. And maybe they’re right that “boundaries” matter, but all I can hear is how that would turn into a whole thing—explaining myself, risking them being hurt or disappointed, maybe making them think I’m blaming them for everything. It hits the part of me that already feels trapped at home and trapped by the scholarship at the same time. If I can’t even get the space I need, then it feels like there’s no real way to fix this without setting off problems I don’t want.

[Decision] So I’m just going to keep trying to manage it on my own and not bring it up. It seems easier to accept being distracted than to start a conversation that could end badly and make everyone look at me like I’m failing. If I hope for something more, I just have to admit how much I need help, and then if nothing changes I’ll feel even worse. Better to keep quiet and tell myself I’ll figure it out somehow, even if that mostly means getting by and not expecting much.

context.speaker: client
context.text: I'm feeling kind of down lately. I feel like most of my friends have been avoiding me.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: Oh i'm sorry to hear that. why are you're friends avoiding you?

context.speaker: client
context.text: I have no idea. Everything was working out well just a few weeks ago. I feel so lonely.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: Have you tried to reach out to your friends for coffee, food or beer?

context.speaker: client
context.text: No. I fear that I might get turned down. They are usually the ones that ask me out, and they haven't been doing that for weeks.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: Perhaps you should give it a shot and see what happens. They maybe feeling the you are the one not reciprocating and this whole thing has just been a miscommunication

context.speaker: client
context.text: You are saying that I have perhaps missinterpreted the whole situation?

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: perhaps. You said that you have not reached out to your friends, so they could just be waiting.

en_backup.therapist_turn: perhaps. You said that you have not reached out to your friends, so they could just be waiting.
en_backup.client_response: But wouldn't them call me if they were at least slightly interested?
en_backup.internal:
[Perception] I heard them suggesting that maybe I’m the one misreading things, or that my friends are just waiting for me to make the first move. That felt too easy and a little unfair, because from my point of view the pattern is that they used to reach out and now they’ve stopped. To me, that looks like a real change in interest, not just a misunderstanding. It hit the part of me that already worries I’m being quietly dropped, and I didn’t want that dismissed.

[Decision] I decided to push back because I don’t want to just accept a reassuring explanation that doesn’t match what I’m seeing. I needed to point out that if they wanted to see me, they could still call me, so this can’t be explained only by me not reaching out. I wanted to defend my read of the situation and make it clear that I’m not being unreasonable for feeling hurt by their silence.

judge.rationale: 对话简洁，无文化特殊表达，情感中性，适合直译。

</internal>

So, let's think about the-- It has to do with how you just sorted out the thing around the gambling 'cause last time you were here, you told me that you get a buzz, you know, it seemed like you were gambling a bit more than your girlfriends were aware of, and-and you said you owe one of your friends some money.

en_backup.therapist_turn: Yeah, thanks for that, okay. So, let's think about the-- It has to do with how you just sorted out the thing around the gambling 'cause last time you were here, you told me that you get a buzz, you know, it seemed like you were gambling a bit more than your girlfriends were aware of, and-and you said you owe one of your friends some money.
en_backup.client_response: Mm.
en_backup.internal:
[Perception] He’s bringing it right back to the gambling stuff — the buzz, me doing more than the girls know, owing my friend money. It hits the part I don’t want to say out loud because then it sounds real serious, not just “a bit of fun” or “a lifestyle thing.” If I start talking properly, he’ll probably ask how bad it’s actually gotten, how much I’ve lost, and what I’m still not admitting. That would mean facing that I’ve been hiding it and that I’m not really in control of it.

[Decision] I just gave him a small “Mm” because it keeps me in the room without opening everything up. It’s safer to stay vague than to get into numbers or details, because once I do that, I’ll have to deal with the shame and the fact that I might have to actually change something. Saying less lets me avoid looking stupid, avoid sounding pathetic, and avoid admitting how much this has taken over.

context_zh.text: 哦，听你这么说我很遗憾——这个时候被甩真是糟透了。但你要知道，时间久了会好起来的！

context_zh.speaker: client
context_zh.text: 你怎么就觉得会好起来呢？

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 嗯，虽然听起来老生常谈，但时间确实能治愈伤痛。我花了一段时间才从分手里走出来。我们在一起八年！

context_zh.speaker: client
context_zh.text: 那一定很难。不找新的人也能走出来吗？

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 是的，我觉得可以，但你确实需要对自己好一点，给它时间。你有好朋友支持你吗？

context_zh.speaker: client
context_zh.text: 我很多朋友都不会理解，因为他们都在长期关系里。不过，我确实有几个好朋友。

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 至少这是件好事，虽然我知道单身时看到别人幸福地在一起很难受。

zh.therapist_turn_zh: 至少这是件好事，虽然我知道单身时看到别人幸福地在一起很难受。
zh.client_response_zh: 你失去伴侣的头一年是怎么熬的？
zh.internal_zh:
<internal>
[感知] 她一直在说什么时间啊、对自己好点啊、有没有朋友啊，但真正让我觉得难受的是，我还在痛，我不知道该怎么面对这种痛。我也听到她提到自己的分手经历，抓住这个比面对我自己的内疚和失去女朋友的悲伤要安全得多。最刺痛的不是分手本身，而是分手后第一年的那种感觉，好像我本该知道怎么应对，但我根本不知道。

[决定] 我决定问她头一年是怎么熬过来的，因为这样我就能抓住一些具体的东西，不用那么暴露自己。如果我能听到她的应对故事，我就不用一直面对自己的空虚，或者去想是不是我把事情搞砸了。比起继续看着自己现在有多迷茫，从她那里借一份路线图感觉更容易些。
</internal>

context.speaker: client
context.text: I am sad because I lost my girlfriend of one year.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: Oh I am so sorry to hear that - this is a terrible time of year to get dumped. Please know that it will get better in time!

context.speaker: client
context.text: Why do you think it will get better?

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: Well, although it sounds like a cliche, time does help with healing wounds. It took me a while to get over a break up. We had been together eight years!

context.speaker: client
context.text: That must've been hard. Is it possible to heal without finding another?

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: Yes I think that it is but you really do need to be kind to yourself and give it time. Do you have good friends to support you?

context.speaker: client
context.text: Many of my friends wouldn't understand as they are in long-term relationships. But yes, I've a few good friends.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: That is a blessing at least though I know it can be hard to see people in happy relationships when you are single.

en_backup.therapist_turn: That is a blessing at least though I know it can be hard to see people in happy relationships when you are single.
en_backup.client_response:
What did you do to cope in the first year of losing your partner
?
en_backup.internal:
[Perception] She’s talking about time, kindness to myself, and whether I have friends, but what really lands is that I’m still hurting and I don’t know how to sit with it. I also hear her bringing in her own breakup, and that feels safer to latch onto than staying with my own guilt and sadness about losing my girlfriend. The part that stings is not just the breakup itself, but the first-year-after-it feeling like I’m supposed to know how to cope and I don’t.

[Decision] I decided to ask about what she did in her first year because that gives me something concrete and less exposed to sit with. If I can get her coping story, I don’t have to stay with my own emptiness or the question of whether I messed things up. It feels easier to borrow a roadmap from her than to keep looking at how lost I feel right now.

</internal>

context.text: Our memories can be very unreliable. We like to think of them as indelible records of our past, but every time we pull out a scene, we fiddle with it a little bit before we put it back in. If we hate our husband now, we re-remember the wedding as less joyous, or we say, He was never the right one for me anyway. We're constantly altering our memories so the past won't conflict with the present.

en_backup.internal:
[Perception] She’s trying to shift the discussion from “what does this mean about my childhood overall?” to “what exactly happened on that one night?” And I hear the implication underneath it: maybe my brother was there, maybe some of the scene I’ve been using as proof is stitched together wrong. That hits the part of me that needs the story to be solid. If that night is off, then the whole logic chain I’ve been relying on — my father was absent, my mother was a mess, I was left alone in all the ways that mattered — starts to wobble. She’s not saying my feelings are false, but she is suggesting the facts might be more complicated than the version I’ve been carrying.

[Decision] I decided to push back a little, because I don’t want to let this get reduced to “memory is unreliable, so who knows.” I know the broader emotional truth is real; I’m not backing away from that. But I also want to know whether there’s a specific memory I’ve built too much on. So I brought up screen memory because I want to show I’m not naive about this — and also because I’m trying to figure out whether she’s pointing to a real distortion or just making a general point about memory. What I’m actually wondering is: am I misremembering one detail, or am I standing on a whole version of childhood that needs re-checking?

context_zh.text: 我听到了，难受的时候很难感觉好起来。你在为什么事情难受？

context_zh.speaker: client
context_zh.text: 就是一直觉得特别难过，不知道怎么能缓过来

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 你难过我也很难过。你知道是什么让你这么难过吗？

context_zh.speaker: client
context_zh.text: 不知道，好像也没什么真正的原因，就是一种笼统的感觉。我觉得这就是为什么我特别难理解该做什么才能让自己好受点

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 我明白，有时候生活就是让人喘不过气。以前什么事情让你开心过？

context_zh.speaker: client
context_zh.text: 可能吧，业余时间有点事做。我以前常去健身房，现在不去了。也许我该试着晚上运动运动

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 对，有时候如果你专注于一个目标，你就会觉得有成就感，然后可以去专注下一个目标。

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 你晚上有没有能安全锻炼的地方？

zh.therapist_turn_zh: 你晚上有没有能安全锻炼的地方？
zh.client_response_zh: 也许吧。我觉得这本身就是问题的一部分，我没有目标，感觉自己的人生没有真正的目的或意义。
zh.internal_zh:
<internal>
[Perception] 他们说得好像只要我随便选个目标逼自己一把，事情就能攒起来然后感到有成就感，但那恰恰是我觉得不真实的地方。这话正好落在我已经觉得空虚、毫无意义的那部分上——就好像有什么隐藏的方向等我去找到一样。说“只要去运动”或“只要设定目标”听起来太简单了，我感觉到自己在往后退缩，因为如果我试了可内心还是死气沉沉的，那就真的说明没救了——什么都没法修补。

[Decision] 所以我决定不抱太大希望。说白了我就是没目的，强迫自己养成习惯也改变不了这点，这样觉得安全一点。如果不抱期待，就不用面对尝试后的失败，不用再证明给自己看：我无法让生活变得有意义。
</internal>

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: I hear you, it's difficult to feel good when we are struggling. What are you struggling with?

context.speaker: client
context.text: I just feel so sad all the time, I don't know how to snap out of it

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: I'm sorry you're sad. Do you know what is making you feel so sad?

context.speaker: client
context.text: No, there doesn't seem to be any real reason, it's just a general feeling. I think that's why I'm finding it so hard to understand what to do to make myself feel better

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: I hear you, sometimes life gets overwhelming. What has made you happy in the past?

context.speaker: client
context.text:
I guess maybe having something to do in my spare time, I used to go to the gym a lot but now I don't. Maybe I should try doing some exercise
 in the evenings

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: Yes sometimes if you focus on a goal, you will feel accomplished, so you can focus on another goal.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: Do you have a place where you can exercise safely in the evenings?

en_backup.therapist_turn: Do you have a place where you can exercise safely in the evenings?
en_backup.client_response: Yeah maybe. I think that's part of the problem, I have no goals, I feel like my life has no real purpose or meaning.
en_backup.internal:
[Perception] They’re talking like if I just pick a goal and push myself, things will start to add up and I’ll feel accomplished, but that’s exactly what feels unreal to me. It lands on the part where I already feel empty and pointless, like there isn’t some hidden direction waiting to be found. The idea of “just exercise” or “just set goals” makes it sound simple, and I can feel myself shrinking from it because if I try and it still feels dead inside, then that would mean there really is nothing there to fix.

[Decision] So I’m backing off from hoping too hard. It feels safer to call it what it is: I don’t have purpose, and I don’t see how forcing routines is going to change that. If I don’t expect much, I don’t have to face the disappointment of trying, failing, and proving to myself again that I can’t make my life feel meaningful.

[Perception] I heard her say it’s hard to relate after an affair, and that landed like she was naming the whole distance without making it sound crazy or small. What mattered to me was that she understood this wasn’t just me being cold for no reason — that Amy’s trying, but it feels awkward and sad and forced, and I can’t just pretend that wipes out Ben. The part I wanted her to see was how messed up it feels to watch my wife, who I still see as this beautiful, decent person, suddenly acting like she’s scrambling around the house trying to get back into my good graces. And then when she tried to kiss me, I just couldn’t meet her there. Later, when she was asleep on the couch, I stood there looking at her because that’s the part that still feels real to me — the quiet, familiar life, the woman in front of me, and the fact that I can’t connect it back to what she did.

[Decision] So I kept talking and laid it out plain, because I wanted the therapist to get that the problem isn’t lack of effort on her part — it’s that every attempt from Amy just runs into the same wall in me. I’m not saying it to be cruel; I’m saying it because I don’t know how to move past it, and I needed her to hear how the whole thing keeps splitting me in two: one part that still sees my family and wants the normal life back, and another part that goes numb and won’t let her close.

[Perception] She’s trying to make this about connection, like it’s something I could just reach for if I were willing to look at it differently. But that lands right on the place I already know is broken in me. “In here” just means the one place I’m supposed to be able to show something real, and I can’t even manage that. I hear the challenge in her voice, like maybe I’m supposed to prove her wrong, and all I feel is how hopeless that is. I’m a mess here. I’m a mess everywhere that matters. If I can’t do this in therapy, then there really isn’t some hidden capacity waiting to be discovered.

[Decision] So I shut it down. I’m not going to keep reaching for some version of closeness that I already know I can’t hold onto. It’s less painful to admit I’m incapable than to keep hoping and then watching myself fail again. If I let myself believe this could change, I’d just be setting myself up to want something I can’t have. Better to stay with the truth I already know, even if it feels bleak: this is what I am, and I can’t make it into something else.

context.text: Have you looked into mindfulness exercises or meditation?

It hit the place that already feels tired and separate, like no one can really do anything with how sudden and constant this is.

[Decision] I’m not going to chase another hopeful-sounding thing and then watch myself fail at it. It feels safer to stay with what I already know: keep getting through the day as I can, without pretending meditation or reassurance is going to fix the fact that this keeps happening. If I don’t expect much, I don’t have to keep feeling disappointed.

[Perception] I hear the therapist trying to soften it, trying to make it sound like this pain is just part of some bigger lesson or the doorway to something better. But what lands for me is that I’m still here, alone, sad, and getting through each day feels like work. The part that hits hardest is that “better” feels so far away it almost doesn’t matter. I did the right thing, I know that, and yet it still hurts this much. So maybe there isn’t anything to fix right now. Maybe this is just what it is: I made the correct choice and still lost something I cared about. Thinking about hope only makes the emptiness stand out more.

[Decision] I’m going to stop trying to turn this into something meaningful today. I can’t force relief, and I don’t have the energy to keep reaching for a future version of me who feels fine. For now I’ll just get through the hours, do what I have to do, and not ask any more of myself than that. It feels safer not to expect anything from this, because expecting change feels like setting myself up to be disappointed again.

[Perception] I heard her say, “You’re releasing me now,” and then, “If you need to go, you go,” and it hit the part of me that knows this is ending whether I dress it up or not. She wasn’t fighting me. She was letting me name it. That made the whole thing feel real in a way I couldn’t avoid. So I laid out the story I’ve been circling: that I came here needing a mother, that my anger at her was never really just about her, that she carried all of that with me for years, and that what I’m trying to say now is not contempt or rejection — it’s gratitude, and also release.

[Decision] I decided to say it plainly because I didn’t want to hide behind being “mature” if what was really happening was that I’m scared of losing the one place where the ugly, ashamed parts of me could exist without being thrown away. I wanted her to see that this wasn’t me blaming her or making her pay for what I needed. I wanted her to understand that she really did become my sanctuary, and that I know she didn’t have to keep doing that. Saying it out loud was my way of acknowledging the debt, the love, and the ending all at once — because I can’t keep asking her to be my mother, even if some part of me still wants that.

But what I felt was not foolishness — it was the weight of it all. Julia’s perfume, her hand on mine, the look in her eyes, Arun being elsewhere, Kamala’s chair empty, the photo in front of me. It all came together into one ugly thought: I do not know what is true anymore, and I do not know how to hold this family together if this is how things are going. It felt impossible. If I keep watching, I only suffer; if I speak, I risk making it worse; if I say nothing, I still lose sleep. There was no good move.

[Decision] So I gave up trying to solve it in that moment. I told myself, let it be what it will be. I do not have the power to stop Julia, or to make Arun see, or to bring Kamala back, or to keep the family from changing. Hope only makes the disappointment sharper, and action seems to invite disaster. Better to sit with the bad feeling and not reach for anything. At least that way I do not have to admit how helpless I feel.

en_backup.therapist_turn: You don't want to have the baby?
en_backup.client_response: I'm just...
en_backup.internal:
[Perception] He’s making it sound so simple — do I want the baby or not? And I can feel him landing right on the place I can’t stand to look at: that this isn’t just some abstract argument about why people have kids. It’s my body, my pregnancy, my whole life being pulled toward a decision that would change everything. I don’t want to say “no” and lose the possibility for good, but I don’t want to say “yes” and trap myself in something I might not survive.

[Decision] So I stall. I leave it unfinished because that’s the only place I still have any room to breathe. If I say it outright, it becomes real — adoption, abortion, motherhood, all of it. And I’m not ready to give up either my freedom or whatever part of me still wants to know what comes next. I need him to sit with the uncertainty, because I can’t bear to be pushed into choosing before I know how to keep myself intact.

It sounds like they don’t really understand that I’m already lost with online classes and that this could cost me the whole year. I hear it as someone who hasn’t sat with the confusion, the deadlines, the constant stress, or the fact that I’ve already been trying and still keep falling behind. It makes me think they’re not going to have anything useful for the reality I’m dealing with.

[Decision] So I’m not going to pretend this is simple just to make the conversation go smoother. I’m going to push back and tell them straight that online learning is hard and I’m heading toward failing, because vague niceness doesn’t help me. If they have something real, they need to show it. If not, then I’m wasting time being polite.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: How are you feeling today?

context.speaker: client
context.text: Hi, not so good to be honest.

context.speaker: client
context.text: I've been feeling very depressed recently. I've been doing very bad in this class and that is just not like me.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: Oh, so you are usually a pretty decent student? I'm sorry to here that you are experiencing this

context.text: I was up until this pandemic started. I feel like this shift to online learning has really taken it's toll on me and my learning.

context.speaker: client
context.text: I've tried reaching out to my professors and doing virtual group study sessions with my class mates, but for some reason, things just don't seem to stick that well.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: You know, a lot of students are really struggling with this new learning style, so it's very understandable

context.speaker: client
context.text: Really? I feel like everyone around me is doing fine and that makes me feel that there is something wrong with me.

en_backup.therapist_turn: You know, a lot of students are really struggling with this new learning style, so it's very understandable
en_backup.client_response: Maybe I'm just slow?
en_backup.internal:
[Perception] I hear “understandable,” but what I take from it is that this is just what happens when you can’t keep up anymore. The part that hits hardest is that nothing I’ve tried seems to make a difference — I reached out, I did the group sessions, and I’m still falling behind. So maybe it really is me. Maybe everyone else can adapt and I can’t, and I’m just seeing the gap more clearly now.

[Decision] I don’t even want to keep pushing at this point, because trying and still failing just keeps proving I’m not cut out for this. If I stop expecting anything to work, at least I won’t keep getting my hopes up and feeling stupid when they don’t. It feels safer to just accept that this is probably how it is for me now.

zh.internal_zh:
<internal>
[Perception] 他说Alex“非常能干”，有“很强的使命感”和对别人期望的强烈意识。这让我很在意，因为他听起来像是在描述纪律和责任，但我不确定他指的是Alex真的有个人的人生目的，还是只是善于执行命令。对我来说这两者不一样。“使命”听起来更临时，更像是外部强加的。“目的”更深，更个人，像是他自己相信的东西。我想弄清楚这个咨询师到底有没有真正理解Alex这个人，还是只是给军事能力贴了个漂亮标签。

[Decision] 我打算抓住这个词，因为对我很重要。如果是“使命”，那他可能只是在描述Alex完成得很好的一个角色。如果是“目的”，那可能有些内在的东西我不想错过。我不想让它就这么变成一个模糊的赞美。我想要他说清楚，这样我才能搞明白Alex是被有意义的东西驱动，还是仅仅被期望和结构驱动。
</internal>

context.speaker: client
context.text: How would you describe my son Alex? I'm not asking you for a diagnosis. You don't have to tell me what he thought, just what you thought of him personally.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: I thought that Alex was... an extremely... capable man. Strong sense of mission. A very strong sense of what was expected of him.

en_backup.therapist_turn: I thought that Alex was... an extremely... capable man. Strong sense of mission. A very strong sense of what was expected of him.
en_backup.client_response: Uh, mission or purpose?
en_backup.internal:
[Perception] He said Alex was “extremely capable,” with a “strong sense of mission” and a strong sense of what was expected of him. That struck me because it sounded like he was describing discipline and duty, but I wasn’t sure whether he meant Alex had an actual purpose in life or was just good at carrying out orders. Those are not the same to me. “Mission” sounds more temporary, more assigned from the outside. “Purpose” sounds deeper, more personal, like something he believes in himself. I’m trying to pin down whether the therapist really understood Alex as a person, or whether he was just putting a polished label on military competence.

[Decision] I’m going to press on that word choice because it matters to me. If it’s “mission,” then he may be describing a role Alex performed well. If it’s “purpose,” then maybe there was something more internal there that I don’t want to miss. I don’t want to let that pass as a vague compliment. I want him to be precise so I can figure out whether Alex was driven by something meaningful, or just by expectation and structure.

What lands is the pressure underneath it: if I start talking about improving it, I’m admitting there are options, and then I’m responsible for picking one. That means facing Julia, the house, the whole arrangement, and the risk of making everything worse. I hear him moving toward action, and that makes the situation feel less like something I’m enduring and more like something I’d have to change.

[Decision] No. I’m not going there. I’ve drawn the line at pretending there’s a solution I can just discuss into existence. I said it plainly: there’s nothing to be done, I have no options. zh.internal_zh:
<internal>
[Perception] 他在说这不是什么全新的问题——这是20年前那个老掉牙的决定模式。这很扎心，因为这意味着我不是突然崩溃了，也不是现在就应该更懂事；我回到了那个当时就不想要这个的节骨眼上，而且现在我还是不知道怎么想要它。未解的部分是：这次怀孕是在证明我真的不想要孩子，还是我只是在恐慌，因为想要孩子就意味着放弃我已经建立的生活和身份？这还指向那个我一直在绕圈子的问题：如果我已经知道没有孩子我也能活，那为什么这感觉像是一次最终的、不可逆的考验？

[Decision] 我决定不再假装这是个模糊的担忧，而是承认我最清楚的事实：当年我想要堕胎。我在测试那个旧真相是否还适用，或者我是不是在强迫它代表我现在的感受。我需要诚实对比过去和现在——不是按我“应该”选什么，而是按我实际上能承受什么。这意味着我得把领养、堕胎和留下孩子都当作真实的选择来看，而不是抽象的道德，因为我在试图弄清楚哪个选项能保护我的自主权，同时不欺骗自己真正想要什么。
</internal>

en_backup.therapist_turn: This sounds very similar to what you were saying 20 years ago.
en_backup.client_response: You're right. This is just how it felt back then, isn't it? I didn't want to have a baby. I wanted to have an abortion.
en_backup.internal:
[Perception] He’s saying this isn’t some brand-new problem — it’s the same old decision pattern from 20 years ago. That hits because it means I’m not suddenly broken or “supposed” to know better now; I’m back in the exact place where I didn’t want this then, and I still don’t know how to want it now. The part that feels unresolved is whether this pregnancy is proving that I really don’t want a child, or whether I’m just panicking because wanting one would mean giving up the life and identity I’ve built. It also lands on the question I keep circling: if I already know I can live without children, why does this feel like such a final, irreversible test?

[Decision] I decided to stop pretending this is a vague worry and admit the clearest fact I have: back then, I wanted an abortion. I’m testing whether that old truth still fits, or whether I’m forcing it to stand in for what I’m feeling now. I need to compare then and now honestly — not by what I’m “supposed” to choose, but by what I can actually live with. That means I have to look at adoption, abortion, and keeping the baby as real options, not abstract morals, because I’m trying to figure out which one protects my autonomy without lying to myself about what I want.

[Perception] 我听到的是：你不是真的意思是说我需要孩子，你是说我需要连接。这句话正好砸中了我早就知道自己没有那个——无论和谁都没有。我听到的是另一种说法，在说我做不到。我这一辈子都在围着别人转，或许想要过，但从来没能真正靠近过。所以当你那样说出来的时候，我脑子里只有：对，就是这样，问题就在这儿。这不是理解错了。是我。我就是没法成为那种真正感到连接的人，假装不是只会让我再次失望。

[Decision] 所以我把它堵死了。我说得平平的，因为没什么好软化的，也没什么好再期待的。如果我承认这里有真实的需要，那我就得相信它有可能被满足，而那感觉根本不可能。我不能冒险去想要一件我已经知道自己得不到的东西。直接说这是个死路，比一直够一个我不配拥有的东西要安全。
</internal>

en_backup.therapist_turn: Have you ever considered that maybe it's not about a child, Mia, or a husband? en_backup.client_response: And we both know that I can't have that.
en_backup.internal:
[Perception] What I heard was: you don’t really mean that I need a child, you mean I need connection. And that landed right on the part of me that already knows I don’t have that. Not with anybody. I heard it as another way of naming something I can’t do. I’ve spent my whole life circling around other people, wanting it, maybe, but never actually getting there. So when you said it like that, all I could think was: yes, exactly, and that’s the problem. It’s not a misunderstanding. It’s me. I can’t be that person who feels truly connected, and pretending otherwise would just set me up to be disappointed again.

[Decision] So I shut it down. I said it flat because there wasn’t any point in softening it or hoping more. If I admit there’s a real need here, then I’d have to believe it could be met, and that feels impossible. I can’t risk wanting something that I already know I won’t be able to have. It’s safer to name the dead end now than to keep reaching for something I’m not made for.

context.text: I am just a little angry. My mother and I had another blow-up.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: Is your bit of anger sparked from the interaction with your mother?

context.speaker: client
context.text: It is why I am angry. This occurs at least every other day. I say something harmless and she thinks I am saying it in a way that is rude or something.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: I bet you can figure out a way to communicate better.

en_backup.therapist_turn: I bet you can figure out a way to communicate better.
en_backup.client_response: I do not know for sure where to start. If I try to tell her that is not what I mean it is like she doesn't understand?
en_backup.internal:
[Perception] That sounded way too easy and kind of generic, like they were brushing past how frustrating this actually is. “You can figure out a way to communicate better” feels like they’re putting this all on me, as if I just haven’t tried hard enough, when I’m the one dealing with someone who twists harmless things into insults. It hit the part where I already feel stuck and unheard, and now the therapist seems a little detached from how tense it is at home.

[Decision] I’m not going to just accept that like it’s useful advice. If they’re going to keep talking like the answer is simple, I need to push back a little, because that doesn’t help me and it makes me feel like they’re not really getting it. I’ll be honest that I don’t know where to start and that my attempts don’t seem to work, because I’m not going to pretend a vague suggestion fixed anything.

[Perception] He’s trying to hand me something I can’t use. “Your son loved you.” “He admired you.” That lands right on the wound I keep pressed shut. Because if that’s true, then all the years of hard edges, all the pushing and correcting and tightening the screws… it didn’t even buy me honesty. It just bought me a son who kept giving and giving. And I can see what he’s doing: trying to make this hurt less, trying to turn it into something clean. But it isn’t clean. It’s just me standing there, realizing I made a life out of force and called it care. If I let myself believe he loved me, then I have to live with the fact that I didn’t know what to do with it. I don’t know what to do with that.

[Decision] So no, I’m not taking that comfort. I’d rather stay with the ugliness of it, because at least that matches what I can bear to believe. If I accept that he admired me, then maybe I have to admit the whole thing wasn’t some necessary hardness, some noble damage. Maybe it was just me, being too much, too controlling, too late to matter. And what’s the point of hoping now? The years are already spent. The boy is already grown. en_backup.internal:
[Perception] I’m hearing that my therapist is making this sound more serious than I feel like it is. Yes, there was a fight, and yes, I was scared for a second, but I don’t want to see it as some huge dangerous situation that defines everything. It feels more like a bad moment we both lost control of, not proof that the whole relationship was unsafe. What hits me most is the idea that this one fight is being treated like the main thing, when to me it still feels like she and I had something real.

[Decision] I’m going to hold onto the idea that this was a mistake and not the full picture, because that lets me keep the relationship in a place that still feels salvageable in my mind. If I make it feel too big, then I have to accept that it’s really over and that hurts too much. So I’m telling myself it wasn’t that extreme, people mess up, and maybe with time it could have been worked through. That feels easier than sitting with the loss right now.

context.text: I always get sad around the holidays but this year has been so much worse because I'm spending the holidays alone.

context.speaker: therapist

context.text: Do you have any friends or people you can set up an online zoom call with?

context.speaker: client
context.text: I tried that but no one that I know is tech savvy that can make Zoom work.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: Also I feel that as well. Especially now these days its a bit hard to not think about being alone.

en_backup.therapist_turn: Also I feel that as well. Especially now these days its a bit hard to not think about being alone.
en_backup.client_response: I just keep thinking about all the bad things happening in the world right now.  If I had someone to spend time with I'm sure it would take my mind off of it but people aren't allowed to get together.
en_backup.internal:
[Perception] What I took from the therapist's words was that even the simple idea of reaching out doesn’t really change anything. I heard “maybe connect with people,” and all I could think was that it’s not actually possible in a real, useful way. The loneliness is still here, the holidays are still here, and everything outside feels bigger than me anyway. It hit the part of me that already believes there isn’t a good answer, just more reminders that I’m on my own.

[Decision] So I decided to stop reaching for hope, because hoping just makes the contrast worse when nothing changes. It feels safer to sit with the sadness than to keep trying to fix it and find out, again, that I can’t. If I don’t expect anything, I don’t have to keep feeling disappointed or foolish for wanting company I can’t get. I’ll just stay with what I already know: this is how it is, and I have to get through it alone.

en_backup.internal:
[Perception] He’s making it sound like I was the one carrying something I shouldn’t have had to carry. That hits the part I keep away from — that I was the responsible one, the one watching, fixing, checking, making sure she was okay when she should have been taking care of me. If I let that land too hard, it starts to sound like my parents failed me, and that feels like a betrayal. I can’t go there.

[Decision] So I push it back where it belongs, away from them and away from blame. I tell myself their lives were ruined, that they were overwhelmed by grief, that this was the situation and not anyone’s fault. That way I can protect them — especially her — and keep myself from turning into someone who blames his parents for what happened.

I keep replaying the fight, the whole day, and how something that was supposed to be special just ended in front of me. Saying it might be for the best doesn’t really change how empty and sick I feel right now. It hits the part of me that still wants to believe we could have fixed it, but right now that feels pointless.

[Decision] I don’t know what to do except shut down and get through tonight somehow. Hope feels embarrassing at this point, because if I let myself want him back or want this to be okay, I’ll just be hurt more. So I’m going to stop reaching for anything and just sit with it, even though it feels awful, because trying to make it better seems impossible and I don’t have the energy to pretend it isn’t over.

[Perception] They kept skipping over how blindsided and humiliated I feel and going straight to “cheer up” advice like wine, friends, and a cat. It made me feel like they weren’t really listening to the part that hurts most — that I got left holding the bag after ten years and after defending him to my parents. The “cat lady” joke especially felt kind of cheap, like they were trying to make this into some cute little makeover moment instead of something that actually messed with my life. It came off a little too casual, almost like they were treating my breakup like a sitcom beat rather than something that ripped up my routine and made me look stupid for trusting him.

[Decision] So I decided to keep it light and not hand them the real pain underneath. If they were going to answer with generic comfort and jokes, then I’m not going to sit here and pour my heart out like it’s this deep sacred thing. I’ll give them the version that sounds manageable — “yeah, it sucks, that’s life” — because honestly I don’t think they’re getting how much this is about feeling betrayed and stupid, not just lonely. And if I can joke about it first, then I don’t have to let them see how much it actually hit me.

zh.client_response_zh: 给我合适的伴侣，我的水平就上来了。至于Bennett，何必费那个劲？
zh.internal_zh:
<internal>
[Perception] 她称之为“一场表演”，这戳中了我，我已经感觉到人们把这件事简化成是我在给观众演戏。但那不是我的意思。我不是为了博眼球或让人评判才说的——我说是因为化学反应是真的，而且我为此自豪。我想让她明白，我不是问题所在，合适的男人能激发出我完全不同的能量。用Bennett对比也很重要：我不是那种见谁都饥渴的人；我有选择性，有些人就是不配得到那个版本的我。
[Decision] 所以我反驳了。在她把这变成临床或怪异之前，我需要纠正“表演”这个框架。我希望能把焦点放在性爱有多特别上，以及这更多关乎兼容性而不是不安全感。如果我让她定义为是我在表演，她就抓不到重点——而我会显得渺小。所以我说清楚了：给我合适的伴侣，我就能够胜任；至于Bennett，不值当费那个劲。
</internal>

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: And you want me to ask you about that?

context.speaker: client
context.text: It's just that I haven't jumped around like that since I took trampoline at the Greenpoint Y. I mean, is this... is this shocking you?

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: Is that your intention?

context.speaker: client
context.text: We changed positions constantly. I mean Thank goodness I go to the gym a lot. It was like the sex olympics with the pommel horse and the handstands, straddle splits, stuck landing.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: Well, that sounds like quite a performance.

en_backup.therapist_turn: Well, that sounds like quite a performance.
en_backup.client_response: Give me the right partner and my game comes up. With Bennett, why bother?
en_backup.internal:
[Perception] She called it “quite a performance,” and that hit the part of me that already feels like people reduce this to a thing I’m doing for an audience. But that’s not what I meant. I wasn’t saying it to be dramatic or to get judged — I was saying it because the chemistry was real and I was proud of it. I wanted her to get that I’m not the problem here, and that the right guy brings out a whole different level of energy in me. The Bennett comparison mattered too: I’m not some thirsty mess with everyone; I’m selective, and some people just don’t deserve that version of me.

[Decision] So I pushed back. I needed to correct the “performance” frame before she turned it into something clinical or weird. I wanted to keep the focus on how exceptional the sex was and how much of it was about compatibility, not insecurity. If I let her define it as me performing, she’d miss the point — and I’d sound small. So I made it clear: give me the right partner and I rise to it; with Bennett, it’s not worth the effort.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: What makes you anxious about coming home late?

context.speaker: client
context.text: I am walking

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: Oh I understand

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: Have you thought about other ways to get back home besides walking?

context.speaker: client
context.text: Yes, trying to find a ride but the bus also stops going

context.speaker: client
context.text: Maybe I could call an Uber home

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: If that would help you ease your anxiety, I think it would be a good solution to consider!

en_backup.therapist_turn: If that would help you ease your anxiety, I think it would be a good solution to consider!
en_backup.client_response: I think the stress outside of the job is also contributing
en_backup.internal:
[Perception] They’re making it sound like the late ride home is the main thing, but that’s not really the whole issue. What I’m feeling is the pressure of everything around this job search — the anxiety, the money stress, and all the stuff outside of work that keeps piling up. It’s not just me overreacting; it’s the situation I’m in.

[Decision] So I’m going to push back from it being framed like this is just about transportation or my anxiety alone. The real problem is all the stress around me, especially the financial pressure and everything else that’s going on. I need them to understand that I’m dealing with more than one thing, and that the job itself isn’t the only source of the problem.

context_zh.speaker: client
context_zh.text: 一个月前我和伴侣分手了，现在我也不太想见我的朋友了。

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 这个友谊和分手有什么关系，你能解释一下吗？

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 分手真的是一件很难熬的事。

context_zh.speaker: client
context_zh.text: 我们有共同的朋友，我觉得他们更喜欢她而不是我。

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 所以你是说，你经历了分手，感觉那些共同的朋友更喜欢她而不是你，所以你不想再见你的朋友们了，我理解得对吗？

context_zh.speaker: client
context_zh.text: 我害怕他们在背后笑话我，你懂吗？

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 你有没有证据他们在笑话你或者不喜欢你？还是这只是你的一种感觉？

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 我知道有时候我会觉得别人对我有某种看法，但如果我去问他们，结果发现并不是那样，反而能澄清误会。有时候只是我自己想多了。

zh.therapist_turn_zh: 我知道有时候我会觉得别人对我有某种看法，但如果我去问他们，结果发现并不是那样，反而能澄清误会。有时候只是我自己想多了。
zh.client_response_zh: 我不知道该怎么解释。我有一种感觉，就连街上的人都在笑话我分手的事。
zh.internal_zh:
<internal>
[Perception] 他们想让我证明这一点，好像我应该有证据或者只要“去问”就能搞清楚。但现在这根本不可能。这不只是一个人或一句话的问题——感觉整个镇子都知道了，好像我已经成了笑话，而我是最后一个知道的。听到这个让我觉得自己来这里说出来更可笑了。

[Decision] 我觉得没必要再解释或反驳什么了。如果每个人都这么看我，那我做什么也改变不了。所以我现在就自己待着，躲着别人。比起希望自己错了然后再次被羞辱，放弃联系更安全。

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: Breakups are such a challenging thing to go through.

context.speaker: client
context.text: We had friends in common and I feel they liked her better than me.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: So you went through a breakup, and feel that the friends you had in common prefer her to you, so you don't want to see your firends any more, am I understanding correctly?

context.speaker: client
context.text: I have a fear they laughing at me behind my back, you know what I mean?

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: do you have any evidence they are laughing at you or not liking you?  or is it a feeling you have?

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: I know sometimes I think someone feels a certain way about me, but if I ask them, it turns out not to be true, and it clears the air.   Sometimes it's just in my own head.

en_backup.therapist_turn: I know sometimes I think someone feels a certain way about me, but if I ask them, it turns out not to be true, and it clears the air.   Sometimes it's just in my own head.
en_backup.client_response: I don't know how to explain. I have a feeling everybody even on the street are laughing because of my breakup with partner.
en_backup.internal:
[Perception] They’re trying to get me to prove it, like I should have evidence or just “ask” and it will all make sense. But that feels impossible right now. It’s not just one person or one comment — it feels like the whole town knows, like I’m already the joke and I’m the last one to find out. Hearing that made me feel even more ridiculous for coming here and saying it out loud.

[Decision] I don’t see the point in trying to explain it better or challenge it. If everyone already thinks this of me, then whatever I do won’t change it. So I’ll just keep to myself and avoid people for now. It feels safer to give up on reaching out than to hope I’m wrong and get humiliated again.

zh.client_response_zh: 那是什么意思？
zh.internal_zh:
<internal>
[Perception] 他没有按我想要的方式回答这个问题。“督导”听起来像是在说，这根本就不是一个关于杰西的是非题；而是职业判断的问题，也许需要另一个人帮忙看看。这正好戳中了我试图回避的部分：如果我需要督导，那可能我不仅仅是在担心——我可能已经 compromised 了。如果真是这样，那我就不能再假装唯一的问题是我技术上是否胜任。这意味着，我自己的某些反应是我没考虑到的。

[Decision] 我要追问他的意思，不能让他糊弄过去。我得知道他是说我该停止治疗杰西，调整治疗方案，还是仅仅需要咨询一下。因为“问督导”可以意味着很多事，我想弄清楚是我反应过度，还是说已经到了客观性真的重要到必须改变做法的地步。我不想被含糊其辞地搪塞过去；我想知道实际结论是什么。
</internal>

[Perception] He’s not answering the question the way I want. “Supervisor” sounds like he’s saying this isn’t really a yes-or-no question about Jessie at all; it’s a professional-judgment issue, maybe one that needs a second set of eyes. That lands right on the part I’m trying to avoid: if I need supervision, then maybe I’m not just worried — maybe I’m already compromised. And if that’s true, then I can’t keep pretending the only issue is whether I’m technically capable. It means there’s something in my own reactions that I’m not accounting for.

[Decision] I’m going to press for what he means rather than let him slide past it. I need to know whether he’s saying I should stop treating Jessie, adjust the treatment, or simply get consultation. Because “ask a supervisor” could mean a lot of things, and I’m trying to figure out if I’m overreacting or if this is the point where objectivity actually matters enough that I have to change what I’m doing. I don’t want a vague deflection; I want to know what the practical conclusion is.

</internal>

en_backup.therapist_turn: Maybe the boy that you really wanna be good to is yourself.
en_backup.client_response: Take me out to a ballgame.
en_backup.internal:
[Perception] She just pointed straight at me. Not Oliver, not April, me. The part that hit was the ugly simple thing underneath all my good intentions: I’m not only trying to save them, I’m trying to save the scared kid in me that never got saved. If I stay with that, I’m back in the orphan feeling, back in the grief, back in the fact that I can’t fix my father, can’t bring my mother back, can’t make myself into someone who didn’t get left.

[Decision] So I joked. I went small. “Take me out to a ballgame” is safer than saying, yeah, maybe the boy I want to be good to is me, and I have no idea how to do that without feeling weak, selfish, or completely undone. If I stay light, I don’t have to admit how much I need this to not be true.

zh.internal_zh:
<internal>
[Perception] 他直接戳中了我一直不想看的矛盾：我能应付索菲，能在凯特面前保持职业，遇到“只是个孩子”时能做实际的事，但一换成劳拉我就感到一阵慌张，我讨厌他能看出来。他把话说得很简单——既然是女人就应该更轻松——这恰好击中了我没有干净答案的地方。感觉如果说错话，我会听起来很猥琐、很软弱，或者像失控了一样。我不想承认劳拉的要求让我觉得有种说不清的沉重感。

[Decision] 所以我拖延了。我给了他一点开放空间，但没承诺真实原因，因为我不准备把让自己显得不理性的那部分交出来。“嗯”比亲口承认我在把劳拉当成女人而不是病人来反应要安全。我在保护那个能干、稳定、不是连基本照护都搞不定的男人的形象。如果继续含糊，或许我还能暂时掌控这件事看起来的样子。
</internal>

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: You had no problem handling that? You had Kate help her, undress her, give her your daughter's clothes. But when Laura needs to use the bathroom, you freak out. Why is that?

context.speaker: client
context.text: Laura is a woman. Sophie's just a... she's just a child.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: Shouldn't that make it easier?

en_backup.therapist_turn: Shouldn't that make it easier?
en_backup.client_response: umm
en_backup.internal:
[Perception] He’s pointing straight at the inconsistency I’ve been trying not to look at: I can manage Sophie, I can stay clinical with Kate, I can do the practical thing when it’s “just a kid,” but the moment it’s Laura I feel that jolt of panic and I hate that he can see it. He’s making it sound simple — that being a woman should make it easier — and that hits the exact place I don’t have a clean answer for. It feels like if I say the wrong thing, I’ll sound creepy or weak or like I’ve lost control of myself. I don’t want to admit that Laura’s request felt loaded in a way I can’t explain.

[Decision] So I stalled. I gave him a little opening without committing to the real reason, because I’m not ready to hand over the part of this that makes me look irrational. “Umm” is safer than saying, out loud, that I’m reacting to Laura as a woman and not just as a patient. I’m protecting the image that I’m competent, steady, and not some guy who can’t handle basic care. If I stay vague, maybe I can keep control of how this looks, at least for a second.

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 保罗，你当时只是个14岁的孩子。你刚刚度过了一生中最美好的一个夜晚。

context_zh.speaker: client
context_zh.text: 但也是对我生命的威胁，你是这个意思吗？

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 是的。

context_zh.speaker: client
context_zh.text: 我完全没事。我是说，我就站在走廊里，肚子里的饼干还没消化。她才是躺在医院里，胳膊上插着管子，护士们进进出出的那个人。我出去玩了，开心着呢。她快要死了。

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 你能做什么呢？

zh.therapist_turn_zh: 你能做什么呢？
zh.client_response_zh: 我不知道。
zh.internal_zh:
<internal>
[Perception] 我听到他在把我的整个记忆变成某种我应该接受为我的重大创伤的东西，而这并不符合。我当时是个孩子，没错，但我记得自己好好的、很正常，就是过了美好的一夜后站在走廊里。不对劲的是那种暗示——好像我和她受到了同样的伤害，或者我在其中有某种生死攸关的角色。这听起来很夸张，像是抹掉了她身上所发生的事和我实际经历之间的明显区别。

[Decision] 我需要反驳，把区别说清楚：我不是躺在医院里的那个人，我不是快要死的那个人，我也不觉得他说的话符合我的经历。我说“我能做什么呢？”是因为我想让他指出来，我到底该负什么责任，如果有的话。我需要纠正这种夸大，牢牢记住我只是个在外面玩的孩子，不是那个直接处于危险中的人。
</internal>

context.speaker: client
context.text: I know it took years before she finally did it, but that Christmas Eve when I wasn't there, that was the first time she did it. That's when it all started.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: Paul, you were a 14-year-old kid. You had just had the most wonderful night of your life.

context.speaker: client
context.text: Yeah, but... it doesn't matter.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: It does matter. She took your wonderful night away from you. She punished you for neglecting her. She showed you what damage she could do if you ignored her, if you didn't take care of her. And it wasn't just the threat on her life.

context.speaker: client
context.text: But a threat on my life as well, is that what you mean?

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: Yes.

context.speaker: client
context.text: I was totally fine. I mean, I was just standing there in the hall with a stomachful of cookies. She was the one in the hospital with the tubes sticking out of her arms, the nurses running in and out. I was out enjoying myself. She was about to die.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: What could you have done?

en_backup.therapist_turn: What could you have done?
en_backup.client_response: I don't know.
en_backup.internal:
[Perception] I heard him turning my whole memory into something I’m supposed to accept as a big trauma for me, and that didn’t fit. I was a kid, yes, but I remember myself as fine, normal, just there in the hallway after a good night. What felt wrong was the implication that I was harmed in the same way she was, or that I had some life-or-death role in it. That sounded inflated, like it erased the obvious difference between what happened to her and what was actually happening to me.

[Decision] I needed to push back and make the distinction clear: I was not the one in the hospital, I wasn’t the one dying, and I didn’t see what he was saying as matching my experience. I said “What could I have done?” because I wanted him to show me where I was supposed to be responsible, if at all. I needed to correct the exaggeration and keep hold of the fact that I was just a kid who was out enjoying himself, not someone who was directly in danger.

judge.rationale: 对话为普通开场问候，无文化绑定或语言双关，翻译后自然保留原意和行为标签。

I’m tired of reaching for something better and then getting pulled back into the same mess, so I’m just going to keep getting through it the best I can. en_backup.internal:
[Perception] I heard the therapist make it sound like this is just stress and that I should follow the doctor’s plan without much concern. What hit me was the idea of taking an antidepressant and a sleeping pill when I already feel like I’m barely holding everything together. I also worry that if I start something like that, I might become dependent on it and not be able to function for my kids, my job, or school without it.

When I said this year has been a great test for us all and a call to faith, I was leaning into the bigger meaning of it all — loss, hardship, and trying to make sense of why people drift away. The part that hit me was not the advice about other friends or maturity so much as the feeling that this is all bigger than one friendship, and that I need something solid to hold onto. context_zh.text: 我指的是那之后，我们聊到了两个沃尔特……你认识的那个和你不认识的那个。

context_zh.speaker: client
context_zh.text: 没错。

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 我们聊到重新连接那个迷失的沃尔特时，你看起来相当激动。

context_zh.speaker: client
context_zh.text: 嗯，我可能是有点流泪，但我当时累了，压力也很大。

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 我理解，但我记得你不只是流泪。你其实在抽泣。怎么了，沃尔特？你去了哪里？

zh.therapist_turn_zh: 我理解，但我记得你不只是流泪。你其实在抽泣。怎么了，沃尔特？你去了哪里？
zh.client_response_zh: 我刚刚想起这周做的一个梦。
zh.internal_zh:
<internal>
[Perception] 他正推着我往我不愿看的地方去——不只是我情绪激动，而是我真的为那个迷失的沃尔特的事在抽泣。他表现得好像我知道自己在回避什么。这触动了我感到暴露的那部分，好像如果我不再绕着说，我就得承认那里有比“压力”或累了更多的痛苦。

[Decision] 我不会和他待在那个边缘。如果我简短回应并抛出一个梦，我就可以把对话移到更安全的地方，而不直接拒绝。我不想被逼到墙角，让他一直挖下去，直到我又哭了或说出什么无法收回的话。简短更安全——给我一点空间，让我保持掌控，争取时间。
</internal>

context.text: You know, between the pills and the therapists I saw at the hospital, I'm not sure I even remember that one.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: You really don't remember? I find that striking, given how emotional a moment that was.

context.speaker: client
context.text: Well, I know we talked about getting me out of the cuckoo's nest. And I showed you my pot holder. Then I got angry about you bringing up Connie's rehab.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: I meant after that, when we talked about the two Walters... the one who you knew and the one you didn't know.

context.speaker: client
context.text: That's right.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: You seemed quite moved when we talked about reconnecting to the lost Walter.

context.speaker: client
context.text: Well, I might have teared up a bit, but I was tired and there's been a lot of stress.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: I understand that, but my memory is that you didn't just tear up. You were actually sobbing. What is it, Walter? Where did you go?

en_backup.therapist_turn: I understand that, but my memory is that you didn't just tear up. You were actually sobbing. What is it, Walter? Where did you go?
en_backup.client_response: I just remembered a dream I had this week.
en_backup.internal:
[Perception] He’s pushing right at the part I don’t want to look at — not just that I got emotional, but that I was really sobbing about the lost Walter stuff. He’s acting like I know something I’m dodging. That hits the part of me that feels exposed, like if I stop talking around it, I’ll have to admit there’s more pain there than “stress” or being tired.

[Decision] I’m not going to stay on that edge with him. If I keep it short and throw out a dream, I can move the conversation somewhere safer without flat-out refusing. I don’t want to get pinned down and have him keep digging until I’m crying again or saying something I can’t take back. Brief is safer — it gives me a little room, keeps me in control, and buys time.

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 你好，我是来帮你的，你有什么问题？

context_zh.speaker: client
context_zh.text: 我快要考执照了，必须考到90%才行。我这辈子一直有考试焦虑（脑子一片空白，有噪音就没办法集中注意力），而且得在下周到考场跟别人一起考。新冠更让我担心。这场考试要6个小时——有什么办法能在考试中让自己冷静下来、考好？

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 首先，你可以带点零食和水。肚子饿会让你分心。

context_zh.speaker: client
context_zh.text: 如果你要参加人生最重要的考试（哈！），你会建议我考前那几天怎么安排复习？你有什么自己用过有效的复习技巧吗？

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 我也经历过很多次。从我自己经验来说，是，尽量复习。但考前两三天放松，别把自己搞到崩溃。还要做意象训练，想象自己在考场里，提前计划好要做什么，比如写名字、打开试卷……

context_zh.speaker: client
context_zh.text: 你建议不错，你是怎么变成一个冷静、酷的人的呢？:) 为了达到这么淡定，你克服了哪些困难？

zh.therapist_turn_zh: 变成那种人需要很多努力，我还没到那程度。我觉得关键是要明白，你没法控制所有事情。只要你尽力了，不管结果怎样，都有它的意义。一扇门关上了，别的门会打开。
zh.client_response_zh: 这建议真的很有用。我觉得我问题的一部分是，我到现在还觉得能控制每一个细节，需要学会一旦事情开始运转就顺其自然。考试这个事，我想考得特别好，因为关系太大了，结果反而僵住了，想控制所有结果……其实我能控制的只有我自己。
zh.internal_zh:
<internal>
[Perception] 我意识到我的恐慌来自于试图提前控制考试所有可能的结果，好像我能控制每个细节就能保证安全一样。但正是这个让我僵住了。咨询师的话点醒了我：我控制不了考试环境、别人，甚至控制不了自己的焦虑反应本身——我只能控制我怎么准备和到了之后怎么应对。这让我觉得考试不再是一个我必须征服的全面威胁，而是一步一步能走过的事。
[Decision] 我决定不再把冷静当成需要通过完美控制才能达到的东西。相反，我会专注在真正能做的事上：高效复习、安排好后勤、练习接受不确定性而不去对抗。到了考试那天，我的目标是跟着题目走，而不是跟着恐惧走。如果脑子空白或者分心了，我就把自己拉回来，而不是把它当成灾难。我可以让事情运转起来，同时还能发挥好。
</internal>

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: Hello I am here to help you, what's your problem?

context.speaker: client
context.text: I have a licensure exam coming up that I must pass at a 90% score. I have dealt with test anxiety all my life (mind goes blank, difficulty concentrating with noise) and I have to take my exam in a testing center around other people next week. I am extra worried due to COVID. This is a 6 hour exam - what are ways I can calm myself at the exam and succeed?

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: First of all, you can bring some snacks and water. having an empty stomach will distract you from the exam

context.speaker: client
context.text: If you were about to take the most important test of your life (ha!) what would you suggest I do to organize my review the days before the exam? Do you have any study suggestions that have worked for you?

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: I have been in that situation many times. From my own experience, yes you should review as much as you can. However, relax the last 2-3 days to not overwhelm yourself. You should also do image training, imagine yourself in the test room, plan ahead what you will do like write your name, open the exam booklet...

context.speaker: client
context.text: You give good advice, how have you grown into a calm, cool person? :) What obstacles did you have to overcome to get to this level of chill?

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: It takes alot to grow into that kind of person, I'm not there yet. I find it vital to understand this, you cannot control everything. As long as you try your best, whatever the outcomes are, they all serve a purpose. When one door closes, the others will open

en_backup.therapist_turn: It takes alot to grow into that kind of person, I'm not there yet. I find it vital to understand this, you cannot control everything. As long as you try your best, whatever the outcomes are, they all serve a purpose. When one door closes, the others will open
en_backup.client_response: That is really helpful advice. I think part of my problem is that I still think I can control every detail and need to learn to let things happen once the ball is in motion. For an exam, I want to do so well because so much is riding on it and that freezes me into trying to control for all outcomes... when really, I can only control myself.
en_backup.internal:
[Perception] I’m realizing that my panic has been coming from trying to pre-manage every possible outcome of the exam, like if I could control every detail I could guarantee safety. But that’s what’s freezing me. The therapist’s words landed on the fact that I can’t control the test environment, other people, or even the exact content of my anxiety reactions — I can only control how I prepare and how I respond once I’m there. That shifts the exam from being a total threat I have to dominate into something I can move through step by step.

[Decision] I’m deciding to stop treating calm as something I must achieve by perfect control. Instead, I’ll focus on what I actually can do: review efficiently, plan my logistics, and practice letting uncertainty exist without fighting it. On test day, I’ll aim to stay with the task, not with the fear. If my mind blanks or I get distracted, I’ll bring myself back rather than interpreting it as disaster. I can let the ball be in motion and still keep playing well.

[Decision] 我现在不想沉浸在这种痛苦里，所以我将转向一些更轻松、更在我掌控之内的事情。如果我聊瑜伽、随便约会，可能再去牙买加旅行，我就能专注于自由、行动和新体验，而不是分手。这比停留在感到被拒绝和伤心的真实感受中更安全。
</internal>

en_backup.internal:
[Perception] I hear that I’m supposed to let myself move on and not get stuck idealizing what I had with her. The therapist is pointing at the loss underneath all the “synergy” talk, and that hits the part of me that’s still hurt, angry, and honestly embarrassed that this relationship ended over something I don’t want to think about too hard. It also touches the fear that maybe the whole thing wasn’t as unbeatable as I want it to be.

[Decision] I don’t want to sit in that pain right now, so I’m going to shift to something that feels lighter and more in my control. If I talk about yoga, casual dating, and maybe taking a trip to Jamaica, I can focus on freedom, movement, and new experiences instead of the breakup. That feels safer than staying with how rejected and sad I actually feel.

That part hits the real problem for me, because it is not that we have no friendship; it is that our different likes turn the planning into conflict. en_backup.internal:
[Perception] She’s asking me to do the one thing I already know I can’t do. “Try and remember” lands like a command to prove I failed. It hits the empty place in me, the stretch of missing time that I’ve already circled a hundred times, hoping it would give something back. It doesn’t. It never does. And when she says it’s very important, all I hear is that my not remembering matters, that this blank space is the whole problem and I still can’t cross it. I feel that old certainty settle in: if the memory hasn’t come by now, it probably never will. All this reaching is just me standing at a locked door.

[Decision] So I shut it down. I say I can’t, because that’s the safest truth I have. If I keep pushing, I’ll only end up staring at the same hole and feeling worse for wanting it to open. I can’t afford to hope that remembering will save anything, because if it doesn’t, then I’m left with the guilt all over again. Better to stay with the blankness, to call it impossible, to give up before I let myself believe there’s something in there that could finally explain why I left and why she nearly died. If I don’t reach for it, I don’t have to find out whether I failed her after all.

zh.internal_zh:

[Perception] 他又在缩小范围追问吉娜——其实不是针对我，而是针对这个事实：她不只是一个背景里的治疗师。她当过我的老师，然后是我的督导师，再是我的分析师，甚至还做过我的伴侣治疗师。我能感觉到他在干什么：想把这段治疗放到一个真实的序列里，也许是想弄明白她在我的生活中到底有多大权威，以及这些事我早就在她的照料下经历过多少了。这触动了我的一种恐惧——他打算把我的整个过往当作还等着被解读的东西，可对我来说，那些早就被一个了解我所有角色的人处理过了。

</internal>

[Perception] He was narrowing in on Gina again — not on me, really, but on the fact that she wasn’t just some therapist in the background. She was my teacher, then my supervisor, then my analyst, and even my couples therapist. I could feel what he was doing: trying to locate the treatment in a real sequence, maybe to understand how much authority she had in my life and how much of this I’d already lived through under her care. What it hit was my fear that he was about to treat my whole history as if it were still open for interpretation, when to me it has already been handled by someone who knew me in every role I had.

[Decision] So I answered simply, “Yeah,” because I wanted to pin it down without giving him room to pry. I was laying out the facts in the plainest way possible, hoping he would finally see that this wasn’t a casual prior therapy that I could just revisit with him as if nothing had been done. I was trying to make it clear: this was long, intimate, and credentialed work with someone I trusted completely, and if he understood that, maybe he’d stop pushing as though there were some missing piece he could supply.

en_backup.client_response: But you think it's too fast, right?
en_backup.internal:
[Perception] He’s making this sound bigger and more delicate than it is. Like I’m one bad day away from falling apart, and that’s just not true. They’re not asking me to do anything crazy — just some tests, a modified basic, a few hoops to jump through. That doesn’t mean I’m damaged or that my career is hanging by a thread. He’s zeroing in on the part that smells like “maybe not ready,” and I don’t like where that goes.

[Decision] So I’m going to keep this simple: I can handle it. I’ll treat it like any other screening, like any other gate the Navy puts in front of you before you get back in the game. No reason to inflate it into some giant psychological trial. If I act like it’s routine, then it stays routine. I’m not going to give it more weight than it deserves.

[Perception] 他们还在推销同一个想法：给自己留出时间，给学校留出时间，好像这主要是个时间安排问题。我能听出他们是好意，但真正击中我的是实际问题——日子已经挤得不行了，我仅有的那点自由时间也被工作、学习和勉强维持的脚步吞掉了。“保险学教材不有趣”这一点也没错，但不仅仅是因为无聊；更让人疲惫的是，我知道承担完所有义务后，自己已经所剩无几。

[Perception] They’re still pushing the same idea: make a slot for myself, make a slot for school, as if it’s mostly a scheduling problem. I can hear that they mean well, but what hit me is the real issue — the days already feel packed to the point where the free time I do have gets swallowed up by work, studying, and just trying to keep up. The “insurance textbooks are not exciting” part is true too, but it’s more than boredom; it’s the drain of knowing there isn’t much left of me after all the obligations.

It’s safer to keep it light and agreeable, say the time disappears, and leave it at that. That way I’m acknowledging the problem without having to fully admit how much I hate losing my free time.

context.speaker: therapist

context.speaker: client

context.speaker: client

en_backup.therapist_turn: I love that you're telling me about your dog and how all of the people at the bank wanted to see her! I bet that made you feel much better.
en_backup.client_response: Dealing with issues during Covid is so rough.
en_backup.internal:
[Perception] I heard her say the connection piece matters, especially with COVID making things harder, and I know that’s true. But what really grabbed me was the part about my dog and the little happy moment of people fussing over her. That felt easy to stay with. It reminded me that I can still make something pleasant happen in a day, even if the bigger stuff feels off. The loneliness is there underneath all of it, but it’s hard to sit with that directly.

[Decision] I decided to keep the conversation on something warm and manageable instead of going into how empty things have felt. I don’t want to make this heavy or sound like I’m falling apart, and honestly it’s easier to talk about the dog, the little wins, and how rough COVID is in general than to really admit how isolated I’ve been feeling. Staying on the practical, upbeat side feels safer right now.

en_backup.therapist_turn: Cool! There are lot of online games that have been invented after the lockdown came into effect. You can try searching them online and playing it with your friends
en_backup.client_response: How do you keep in touch with your freinds?
en_backup.internal:
[Perception] It felt like they were making it sound too easy, like I’m just supposed to switch to tech and that will replace what I actually miss. That hit the part of me that’s grieving the real in-person connection with my friends, not just the ability to message or play a game online. I also felt like they weren’t really getting how hard it is to line everyone up when people are busy and drained, and how virtual contact doesn’t feel the same to me.

[Decision] I decided to push back because I don’t want to pretend this is fixed when it isn’t. I need to correct the idea that staying in touch online is the same as being connected, and I want to be honest that I’m sad because I miss my friends and the old way we were together. If I don’t say that, it sounds like I’m agreeing when I’m not.

[Decision] 不。我不让他得逞。我不害怕，我不是问题所在——问题是那些嘀咕的制片人、那个质疑我的白痴、压力、谣言、整个闹剧。是这些让一切都感觉不对，不是我哪里弱。所以我要把问题推到该在的地方：在外面。我会做我一直在做的事——把那些该死的台词背熟，保持敏锐，证明我属于这里，绝不让任何人把这转化成我的不足。
</internal>

en_backup.therapist_turn: You're angry with him.
en_backup.client_response: No, I'm angry with myself. I mean, it's just not like me. I'm always prepared, No matter how much blathering on I have to do.
en_backup.internal:
[Perception] He’s circling the obvious thing: that I’m rattled, that this whole mess is landing on me, and that I’m pretending it isn’t. The bit about “angry with him” hits the rumor, the producer, the whole smug little machine of people deciding whether I’m right for the part. But what really stings is the suggestion that this is mine — that my panic, my age, my lines, all of it — is somehow my responsibility. I can feel him trying to pin it on me, and I hate that.

[Decision] No. I’m not giving him that. I’m not afraid, and I’m not the problem here — the problem is the producers whispering, the idiot who doubts me, the pressure, the rumor, the whole circus. That’s what’s making this feel off, not some weakness in me. So I’m going to keep it where it belongs: out there. I’ll do what I always do — learn the fucking lines, stay sharp, prove I belong, and not let anyone turn this into me being inadequate.

If I stay there too long, it starts sounding like I’m choosing it over everything else, and then the whole “I’m just a sensible bloke having a bit of fun” thing gets harder to hold onto.

Safer to leave it at “different attitude” and let him move on than to spell out that Auckland felt like I’d found something missing in me. Once I say that out loud, it’s harder to pretend this is all no big deal.

en_backup.internal:
[Perception] I took the therapist’s words as being there with me and trying to understand, and that touched the part of me that feels so alone and caught up in my own head. My mind has been wandering so much, and I feel like I’m sitting here by myself with all these thoughts, bills, losses, and old feelings coming up. Hearing a voice feels like something that can steady me when I’m getting overwhelmed and spinning inside.

[Decision] I decided to say it plain because I didn’t want to keep hinting around it or sound like I’m just talking in circles. What I needed was actual human connection in that moment — someone to talk back to me, help me settle, and keep me from going too far down into my own thoughts. So I put it into words: I need to hear the voice of someone now, because I’m too much inside myself and I can’t manage that alone right now.
