zh.internal_zh:
<internal>
[Perception] 他在逼着我说我觉得他们怎么想的，而不是让我停留在“他们生气”这个层面，以及底下更大的恐惧。这戳中了那个部分——我正在试图搞清楚这到底只是暂时的愤怒，还是更长久的东西——我是不是已经在变成那种让我孩子带着同样的怨恨来记住我的父亲。当我说“要是我就跟他一样呢？”的时候，我在检查对自己不利的证据：我的病人，我的注意力，我儿子一个人被留下，我可能以不同的形式重复了同样的缺席。

[Decision] 我正试着弄清楚我的恐惧到底是事实，还是只是我在给自己讲一个灾难性的故事。我不知道孩子们完整的感受，但我能指出的证据是：他们在生气，而且我的确做过一些事情，可能让他们觉得自己被排到第二位。所以我在试着连线：如果我想不一样，就不能只是假设自己已经完蛋了，或者等到太晚。我需要看看我实际做了什么，他们可能怎么体验的，以及我是不是还能在它变得像我跟我父亲之间那种距离一样固化之前，改变这个模式。
</internal>

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: They're mad at you, Paul? That's what they feel?

en_backup.therapist_turn: They're mad at you, Paul? That's what they feel?
en_backup.client_response: And what if I'm just like him? I mean, did they feel that they had to compete with my patients for my attention? Have I too left my young son home alone with his mother?
en_backup.internal:
[Perception] He’s pushing me to say what I think they feel, instead of letting me stay at “they’re mad” and the bigger fear underneath it. That hits the part where I’m trying to figure out whether this is just temporary anger or something more permanent — whether I’m already becoming the kind of father my kids will carry around in the same resentful way I carry my father. When I say “what if I’m just like him,” I’m checking the evidence against me: my patients, my attention, my son left alone, the possibility that I’ve repeated the same kind of absence in a different form.

[Decision] I’m trying to work out whether my fear is actually true or just a catastrophic story I’m telling myself. I don’t know my kids’ full feelings, but the facts I can point to are that they’re angry, and I have done things that could have felt like being put second. So I’m trying to connect the dots: if I want to be different, I can’t just assume I’m already doomed or wait until it’s too late. I need to look at what I’ve actually done, how they might have experienced it, and whether I can still change the pattern before it hardens into the same kind of distance I feel with my father.

context_zh.text: 就是——太难了。我一直在想那些我跟他意见不合或者没好好珍惜他的时候，我都没来得及告诉他我有多爱他。

context_zh.text: 我知道他知道的:)。我只是没想到会在这么年轻的时候就失去他。他都没来得及享受退休！

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 真是可惜，他把时间都花在照顾家人上，却没能享受自己的空闲时间。

context_zh.speaker: client
context_zh.text: 是的。我觉得如果他退休后没有立刻身体变得很差，还有时间享受一些乐趣的话，处理起来会容易一些。

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 你想过找心理治疗师吗？我们几乎很少想到这个服务，但在很多情况下，人们在悲伤时确实需要专业人士的帮助。

zh.therapist_turn_zh: 你想过找心理治疗师吗？我们几乎很少想到这个服务，但在很多情况下，人们在悲伤时确实需要专业人士的帮助。
zh.client_response_zh: 我现在真的负担不起心理治疗。而且我知道我爸爸会觉得这完全是浪费钱——他对钱特别在意。
zh.internal_zh:
<internal>
[Perception] 他们基本上是在推荐最明显、最贵的东西，好像我还没想过似的。“找治疗”听起来很泛泛，而且跟我实际面对的问题有点脱节——不只是“伤心”，而是想念爸爸的沉重、钱的问题，还有这种悲伤和他紧密相连。这听起来也很不好，因为感觉他们绕过了真正的障碍，把我当成一个还没尝试过常规方法的人。这让我觉得他们没什么帮助，几乎像是在说套话，而不是真正理解我。

[Decision] 所以我要用现实情况来堵住他的嘴：我付不起，就算付得起，我爸爸也会讨厌在这种事情上浪费钱。这样我就掌握了主动权，也保护了那个知道这不是一个简单解决办法的自己。如果他们非要提出这么脱离我生活的东西，我不会为了礼貌而假装它有用。
</internal>

context.speaker: client
context.text: It is just - very hard. I keep thinking about all the times I disagreed with him or did not appreciate him enough and I never got to tell him how much I loved him.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: Your dad wouldn't want to see you grieving everyday either. You should live the way you know he'd love to see

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: I believe he knew you loved him regardless how much you two argued

context.speaker: client
context.text: I know that he did :). I had just not expected to lose him at such a comparatively young age. He did not get to enjoy his retirement!

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: That's sad when he spent all his time taking care of the family and yet could not enjoy his free time

context.speaker: client
context.text: Yes. I think it would have been easier to deal with had he not immediately descended into very bad health as soon as he retired and had had time to have some fun.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: have you considered seeking therapist? We almost never think of that service, but in a lot of case, people actually need help from professionals when grieving

en_backup.therapist_turn: have you considered seeking therapist? We almost never think of that service, but in a lot of case, people actually need help from professionals when grieving
en_backup.client_response: I can't really afford to have therapy at the moment. Also I know that my dad was just have considered it to be a waste of money - he was very careful with money.
en_backup.internal:
[Perception] They’re basically recommending the most obvious, expensive thing as if I hadn’t already thought of that. “Seek therapy” feels generic and a little out of touch with what I’m actually dealing with — not just “being sad,” but the weight of missing my dad, the money problem, and the fact that this grief is tied to him. It also lands badly because it sounds like they’re brushing past the real barriers and treating me like someone who just hasn’t tried the usual solution yet. That makes them feel less helpful, almost like they’re speaking in canned advice instead of really understanding me.

[Decision] So I’m going to shut that down with the practical reality: I can’t afford it, and even if I could, my dad would have hated wasting money on something like that. That lets me keep control and protects the part of me that knows this isn’t a simple fix. If they’re going to offer something so disconnected from my life, I’m not going to pretend it’s useful just to be polite.

context_zh.text: 这就是尴尬的地方。好像除了我之外，其他人都特别高兴能继续在家办公。我不太敢说出我的感受，因为怕经理改变主意，那样的话对团队里其他人（看起来）来说就太扫兴了。

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 我明白了。这是个担心。所以你感觉如果一个人去办公室，其他人就都得去？没有任何灵活性？

context_zh.speaker: client
context_zh.text: 嗯，也有可能我经理会说我们可以灵活安排。但如果是那样的话，我觉得到头来可能只有我一个人在办公室上班……那就跟在家办公一样孤单，还白白丢掉了在家办公的一些好处，比如省油钱。而且，我觉得我公司可能最后会把我们的办公室挪作他用。

context_zh.speaker: client
context_zh.text: 哈哈，不好意思，刚才那句话说得又臭又长。:\

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 嗯。有点两难。不过这种情况能一直持续下去吗？也许老板会延长在家一段时间，但等别的公司都回办公室了，这个预期就会变成所有公司的要求。

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 其他同事可能也会慢慢改变想法。

context_zh.speaker: client
context_zh.text: 这倒确实有可能。但我办公室所在的城市有很多高科技公司，那些公司在疫情之前就已经在往更多居家办公的方向走了。所以就感觉这可能是我们这地区的一个“文化转变”似的。不过肯定也有很多人跟我一样的感觉。也许我们应该自己开个公司，哈哈。

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 没错。我觉得你不是一个人。有没有什么办法能让在家办公对你来说更好一点？多休息几次？改善工作空间？

zh.therapist_turn_zh: 没错。我觉得你不是一个人。有没有什么办法能让在家办公对你来说更好一点？多休息几次？改善工作空间？
zh.client_response_zh: 这个问题问得好。我住的州现在还是基本上处在封锁状态。我抑郁的一部分原因肯定也跟所有这些晚上和周末的活动一年前就全停了有关。
zh.internal_zh:
<internal>
[Perception] 咨询师好像在暗示这主要是我工作环境的问题，好像我只需要调整一下家里的日常安排，其他事情就能自己解决好。这让我觉得我一直在说的那种孤独和低落，其实没那么严重。感觉更像是一段暂时的低谷，我可能把事情夸大了。反正很多人都要面对同样的封锁状况。

[Decision] 所以我打算保持平常心，不当成什么需要大动干戈的大事。我现在先应付着，再等一等，看看等更多地方开放之后情况会不会自然好转。我不想把情况说得太糟，也不想把它搞成什么大事，很可能只是目前的环境让我有点难受而已。
</internal>

context.speaker: client
context.text: That's where it gets awkward. It seems like everyone besides me are super happy that we'll continue working from home. I hesitate to share my feelings because maybe my manager will change her mind, which would be a big bummer for everyone else on the team (seemingly).

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: I see. That's a concern. So you feel that if one person goes in to the office, then everyone else will have to? There won't be any flexibility?

context.speaker: client
context.text: Well, it's possible that my manager will say we can be flexible. But if so, I think I'd end up being the only one in my office working... which would be just as lonely as working from home while throwing away the few perks of working from home, like saving on gas. Plus, I think my company will probably want to repurpose our office space eventually.

context.speaker: client
context.text: lol, sorry, that was an ugly run-on sentence. :\

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: Hm. A bit of a dilemma. Can this situation go on forever though? Maybe the boss will extend the stay-at-home for a while, but when other companies go back to the office, the expectation will be there for all companies.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: Other employees might change their minds bit by bit as well.

context.speaker: client
context.text: That is indeed a possibility. But my office is in a city that has a whole lot of high-tech companies, which were moving towards doing more work from home even BEFORE the pandemic. So it kind of feels like this might be a "cultural shift" in my area in general. Although there has GOT to be a whole lot of other people who feel like I do. Maybe we should start our own company, lol.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: True. I don't think you are alone. Is there something that you can do to make working at home better for you? More frequent breaks? Better work space?

en_backup.therapist_turn: True. I don't think you are alone. Is there something that you can do to make working at home better for you? More frequent breaks? Better work space?
en_backup.client_response: That's a good question. My state is still one of the ones that's mostly shut-down. Part of my depression surely stems from the fact that all evening/weekend activities ended a year ago as well.
en_backup.internal:
[Perception] The therapist is making it sound like this is mainly about my work setup, like I just need to tweak my home routine and the rest will sort itself out. That lands on the part where I’ve been feeling lonely and kind of down, but honestly it’s not like I’m in some huge crisis. It feels more like a temporary rough patch, and I’m probably making a bigger deal out of it than it is. Lots of people are dealing with the same shutdown stuff anyway.

[Decision] So I’m going to keep it in perspective and not treat this like some major issue that needs a big intervention. I can just manage it for now, wait it out a bit, and see if things naturally improve once more stuff opens up. I don’t want to overstate how bad it is or make it into a whole thing when it’s probably just the current circumstances getting to me.

context_zh.text: 你好，今天怎么样？

context_zh.text: 因为我很难过，很崩溃，分手了。

context_zh.text: 哦不！分手太难受了！我分手已经很久了（我结婚了）。但我还记得那有多崩溃！不过我跟你说，这事儿你挺得过去的！

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 你和你对象在一起多久了？

context_zh.speaker: client
context_zh.text: 嗯，我感觉不是这样。我很抑郁，情绪很糟……生活一团糟。我订婚两年，在一起快三年了。

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 我懂你的感受！你可能觉得整个世界都塌了，觉得浪费了时间再也回不来了，而且精疲力竭。虽然我没经历过解除婚约，但我经历过抑郁、情绪糟糕、生活崩溃的感觉。我那时候总是努力关注未来的积极面。

zh.therapist_turn_zh: 我懂你的感受！你可能觉得整个世界都塌了，觉得浪费了时间再也回不来了，而且精疲力竭。虽然我没经历过解除婚约，但我经历过抑郁、情绪糟糕、生活崩溃的感觉。我那时候总是努力关注未来的积极面。
zh.client_response_zh: 嗯，也许是吧。但现在没有一件事感觉好，感觉积极……就算努力想别的，给自己时间，都没用……我试着去理解为什么发生……真希望我能把对他的爱关掉……那样我现在会好很多。
zh.internal_zh:
<internal>
[Perception] 他们说得好像很懂，但其实根本没接住我。老说“关注积极面”“你能挺过去”，感觉很敷衍，像是想把我的痛苦带过去，因为他们自己不舒服。一个连将近三年感情、两年订婚是什么滋味都不知道的人，说得倒是挺自信。这正好戳中我那种支离破碎、渴望真实回应的地方，而不是打鸡血。让我更觉得孤单，好像我的崩溃被简化成他们能随便糊弄过去的事。
[Decision] 我要怼回去，不再给他们客气的版本了，因为他们根本就没听进去。如果他们非要给那些显而易见的、乐观的答案，那我也不用假装那些有用。我想让他们明白，现在没有一件事是好的，我连今天都熬不过去，更别提什么“关注未来”了。如果他们接不住，我就不让他们把我的真实痛苦给绕过去。
</internal>

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: Hello, How are you doing today?

context.speaker: client
context.text: Not good,and you?

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: That is a bummer! I have actually had a very good morning so far! Why aren't you doing good today?

context.speaker: client
context.text: Because I am sad,and devastated about my break up

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: Oh no! Breakups are so hard! It has been a long time since I have had a break up (since I am married). I can remember how devastating it was though! I can tell you though this is something you can get through!

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: How long were you and your partner together?

context.speaker: client
context.text: well,it doesn't feel that way. I am so depressed and emotional...Life is falling apart. I was engaged for 2 years,and together almost 3.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: I know how you are feeling! It probably feels as if the world is crashing in all around you, You probably feel like you've wasted time you will never get back, and you are probably feeling just plain exhausted. While I can't say that I have ever been apart of a broken engagement. I can say I felt both Depressed and emotional and like my life was falling apart. I always tried focusing on the positives of the future.

en_backup.therapist_turn: I know how you are feeling! It probably feels as if the world is crashing in all around you, You probably feel like you've wasted time you will never get back, and you are probably feeling just plain exhausted. While I can't say that I have ever been apart of a broken engagement. I can say I felt both Depressed and emotional and like my life was falling apart. I always tried focusing on the positives of the future.
en_backup.client_response: Yes,that can be true. But at the moment nothing feels good,or positive...even trying to focus on other things,taking me time,nothing helps..i try to understand why it happened...and i wished I could turn my love for him off...i would be in a much better place now.
en_backup.internal:
[Perception] They kept talking like they understood, but they really weren’t meeting me where I am. “Focus on the positives” and “you can get through this” felt generic and kind of dismissive, like they were trying to steer me away from the actual pain because it made them uncomfortable. They sounded a little too sure of themselves for someone who doesn’t know what it feels like to lose a nearly 3-year relationship and a 2-year engagement. It hit the part of me that feels wrecked and desperate for something real, not pep-talks. It made me feel even more alone, like my devastation was being simplified into something they could brush past.

[Decision] I’m going to push back and stop giving them the polite version of how bad this is, because it feels like they’re not hearing me. If they’re going to keep offering obvious, upbeat answers, then I don’t need to pretend that helps. I want them to sit with the fact that nothing feels good right now and that I can’t just “focus on the future” when I’m still trying to survive today. If they can’t handle that, then I’m not going to let them talk over the real grief I’m in.

[Decision] So I shut it down. I started talking in caricatures and guesses because I needed distance, not more intimacy with that picture. I don’t want to give that scene more life or let it take over the room. If I keep it vague and mocking, I can protect myself from feeling the full force of how rejected and small this makes me feel.

[Perception] She’s saying she’s going to speak up for me, that she’ll tell them I did everything I could, that I was trying to help. But that lands right on the thing I can’t face: the whole lawsuit, the whole question of whether I should’ve done more, whether I’m the kind of man who lets something like this happen. It feels like if she starts explaining me, then I have to sit there and hope words can fix something that’s already gone too far. I’ve spent my whole life not being alone with this kind of thing, not having to carry it by myself, and now I’m being asked to stand there and trust somebody else’s version of me.

[Decision] No. I’m not going to buy into that. I’m not going to pretend that what she says will matter, because I don’t think it will. It feels like one more attempt to make this legible, to make it sound better, and I can’t go there. I draw the line at being reassured by talk when the damage is already done. If they want to decide, let them decide. I’m not opening myself up to more of this.

context_zh.speaker: client
context_zh.text: 这确实让我焦虑。其他部门有些裁员了。

context_zh.text: 而且，有些选择去办公室几天的人得了新冠。

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 我完全理解那种感觉，因为疫情刚开始时我也很担心自己的工作。

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 你和你的经理谈过这件事吗？也许可以从经理那里确认一下你的工作稳定性？

context_zh.speaker: client
context_zh.text: 这是个好建议。实际上我一直在担心，怕自己得到的答案不好，或者根本得不到真正的答案。

zh.therapist_turn_zh: 你和你的经理谈过这件事吗？也许可以从经理那里确认一下你的工作稳定性？
zh.client_response_zh: 现在的真相很吓人
zh.internal_zh:
<internal>
[Perception] 治疗师问我和经理谈话的建议，正中我一直在回避的那个点。我知道获取澄清是“负责任”的做法，但这也意味着我必须直接面对一些真实的东西。如果答案不好，那么我一直在承受的担忧就成真了；如果答案模棱两可，我仍然被困住。无论哪种情况，感觉都得不到任何有用的东西。只感觉像是打开了更多恐惧的门，害怕失去工作、失去房子，对接下来要发生的事毫无控制感。

[Decision] 所以我决定现在不去推进。待在已经知道的模糊里，比去追求一个可能击垮我的答案更安全。我厌倦了伸手去抓希望然后被伤到，所以我现在允许自己不行动。如果我不问，就不用直接听到最坏的结果，也许我能撑过今天，而不用让恐惧变得更大。
</internal>

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: Just from the few messages we have exchanged I can tell this is making you very anxious.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: Have there been any lay off's at your job due to COVID?

context.speaker: client
context.text: It is making me anxious. There have been some layoffs in other departments.

context.speaker: client
context.text: And, some people who decided to go in the office a few days have gotten CoVid.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: I completely understand that feeling, as I was also very worried about my job when the pandemic started,

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: Have you spoken with your manager about this? It might help to get some clarification from your manager about your job security?

context.speaker: client
context.text: That is a good suggestion. I have actually been worried about the answer I would get or that I would get no real answer at all.

en_backup.therapist_turn: Have you spoken with your manager about this? It might help to get some clarification from your manager about your job security?
en_backup.client_response: the truth right now is scary
en_backup.internal:
[Perception] The therapist’s question about talking to my manager landed right on the part I’ve been trying not to touch. I know that getting clarity would be the “responsible” thing to do, but it also means I’d have to hear something real. If the answer is bad, then all the worry I’ve been carrying is true; if the answer is vague, I’m still stuck. Either way, it doesn’t feel like there’s anything useful to gain. It just feels like opening the door to more fear about losing my job, my house, and having no control over what happens next.

[Decision] So I decided not to push for it right now. It feels safer to stay with the uncertainty I already know than to go after an answer that could crush me. I’m tired of reaching for hope and getting hurt by it, so I’m letting myself not act for the moment. If I don’t ask, I don’t have to hear the worst thing directly, and maybe I can get through today without making the fear bigger.

zh.internal_zh:
<internal>
[Perception] 她还在逼我接受一个想法：我妈也许真有某种真实的原因，某种真实的内心转变，而不只是操纵。但最让我难受的并不是这个理论本身——而是它背后的那个更大的暗示：就算她病了，就算她变了，她还是没有为我争取过。所以问题不是『她当时怎么想的？』而是『为什么我不值得她努力？』这是我无法释怀的部分。因为如果我让自己相信她是有某种情有可原的动机，那离原谅她所做的事就又近了一步。我不愿意那样做，除非它能解释为什么没有人留下来。

[Decision] 所以我跳过关于她动机的表面争论，直接切入更深的逻辑：如果她真的在乎，为什么她停下来了？为什么她没有回来找我？我在试图验证这个故事有没有任何版本，最后不是以『我是那个被人离开的人』收场。我想要一个能解释这个模式的答案——不光是我妈的行为，而是被人抛弃这个大模式。如果没有，那我就只剩下最坏的结论，我需要知道那到底是真的，还是只是我的感觉。
</internal>

en_backup.therapist_turn: No no no no no, I understand your anger. She didn't take care of you, she lied, she was never there for you, then suddenly she wants to be close.
en_backup.client_response: Why... Did she give up? Okay, she was sick for a year, but after that... Why didn't she fight harder to be my mother? How, how come nobody sticks by me?
en_backup.internal:
[Perception] She’s still making me sit with the idea that my mother might have had some real reason, some actual internal shift, instead of just being manipulative. But what lands hardest isn’t that theory by itself — it’s the bigger implication behind it: that even if she was sick, even if something changed, she still didn’t fight for me. So the question isn’t “what did she feel?” It’s “why wasn’t I worth the effort?” That’s the part I can’t resolve. Because if I let myself think there was some understandable motive, then I’m one step closer to excusing what happened. And I’m not willing to do that unless it explains why nobody stayed.

[Decision] So I pushed past the surface argument about her motives and went straight to the deeper logic of it: if she really cared, why did she stop? Why didn’t she come back for me? I’m trying to test whether there is any version of this story that doesn’t end with me being the person people leave. I want an explanation that makes sense of the pattern — not just my mother’s behavior, but the larger pattern of being abandoned. If there isn’t one, then I’m left with the worst conclusion, and I need to know whether that’s actually true or just what it feels like.

zh.internal_zh:
<internal>
[Perception] 他说“那个女演员”，好像只是个冷门小知识，但让我猛地一沉的是，这一切这么快就能被简化成八卦。然后他又说那是个敏感话题，立刻就把话题扯到伊莎贝尔——不对，伊莎贝尔，我女儿——好像真正的故事只是点家庭琐事。但压在我心头的不是这个。压在我心头的是，我妈妈用弗朗西斯·法默的名字给我取名，这个女人那么美，却一生不幸，她的心智被人夺走，而我妈妈只想到这名字的光鲜。感觉就是这样：她在乎美、形象、事物的光鲜，却不在乎把这样的负担交到一个孩子手里意味着什么。我希望他能明白，这不只是“我名字奇怪”，而是我的整个过去都纠结在我妈妈爱什么和她忽略什么里。

context.text: Isabel. Her full name is Isabel. I mean, she's named after my mother. I always thought it was a beautiful name. Glamorous. Not like my name... Frances. I asked my mother, why did you name me Frances? She said, oh, don't you know? I named you after Frances farmer.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: The actress.

en_backup.therapist_turn: The actress.
en_backup.client_response: Yes. Yeah, Frances. Well, what happens to her?
en_backup.internal:
[Perception] He said “the actress,” like it was a neat little fact, but what hit me was how quickly this could all get reduced to trivia. And then he said it was a sensitive subject, and immediately he went to Isabel—no, Isabel, my daughter—as if the real story was just some passing family issue. But that isn’t what’s sitting in me. What’s sitting in me is that my mother gave me this name after Frances Farmer, this beautiful woman whose life was terrible, whose mind was taken from her, and my mother thought only about the glamour of the name. That’s what it feels like: she cared about beauty, image, the shine of things, and not what it meant to hand that burden to a child. I wanted him to see that it wasn’t just “my name is odd,” it’s that my whole history is tangled up in what my mother loved and what she overlooked.

[Decision] So I told him the name and made him follow the thread all the way to Frances Farmer, because I needed the room to hold the whole story, not just the polished surface of it. I’m not ready to say “my mother did this to me,” because I promised myself I wouldn’t blame her, but I can lay out the facts and let him see the shape of it: the beautiful name, the ugly fate, and what it means that I was given that name. If I say it plainly enough, maybe he’ll understand why I’m so defensive when he points toward my mother. Maybe he’ll finally see that I’m not being difficult for no reason.

I’ll keep it clipped and a little sharp, because I don’t want to sit here and explain my life to someone who answers with canned empathy. Better to stay on my guard and make it clear I’m not one of those people who can be talked down with generic reassurance.

[Decision] I’m going to keep it brief and just say I went once. That way I’m answering her without having to commit to a verdict, defend myself, or get into all the reasons it’s hard. context_zh.text: 但我们可以在小事里找到安慰。你有什么能给你安慰的东西吗？哪怕再小的事。

context_zh.speaker: client
context_zh.text: 她活着的时候，我觉得是她让我活着，因为我不想让她承受我自杀的痛苦。

context_zh.speaker: client
context_zh.text: 我会有几分钟觉得好一点，但之后一切又都显得毫无意义。

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 我相信我们这辈子都有目标。我知道没有我们珍爱的人很难活下去。我觉得让他们活在我们心里的一种方式，就是把他们对我们的好传递给其他人。

context_zh.speaker: client
context_zh.text: 你说到点子上了。我很难找到自己活着的意义。我没有孩子，而且我的焦虑让我不敢和别人接触。

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 我也有同感，我在别人面前也会焦虑。

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 也许一步一步来是最好的办法。有时候别人只需要一个微笑，即使我们自己笑不出来，也可以给别人一个微笑。

context_zh.speaker: client
context_zh.text: 每次我说服自己去寻求专业帮助，我都骗自己相信这次终于能修好自己了。当然，到现在也还没修好。

zh.therapist_turn_zh: 也许一步一步来是最好的办法。有时候别人只需要一个微笑，即使我们自己笑不出来，也可以给别人一个微笑。
zh.client_response_zh: 我承认在网上看到那么多人都有跟我一样的“症状”确实有帮助。
zh.internal_zh:
<internal>
[Perception] 听到那么多人都有跟我一样的“症状”，我心里有些变化。我一直把这当成证据，证明我特别烂，一直没法修好自己，但也许这并不只是我一个人的缺陷。也许我一直在说的“骗自己”其实是我一次又一次地想找到一条出路，而这条路别人也走过。这让问题不再像是个人失败，更像是真实存在、可以被理解的东西。

[Decision] 我不需要假装突然好了，或者再多试一次就能奇迹般地修好自己。但我可以不再那么严苛地把自己孤立在脑子里。如果别人也能说出这种感觉，那也许我可以继续寻找帮助，不意味着我又在骗自己。我可以把这当成一个小小的开口，而不是又一次失望。
</internal>

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: I believe we all have purpose in this life.  I know that it's hard to live with-out the ones we hold dearly.  I think a way we can keep them alive in our hearts is to pass on the good things about they did for us to others.

context.speaker: client
context.text: You hit the nail on the head. I struggle to find purpose for my life. I have no kids & my anxiety keeps me from reaching out to people.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: I feel the same way, I get anxious around others as well.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: Maybe little steps are the best way.  Sometimes all someone needs is a smile, even when we can't find our own, we can give one to others.

context.speaker: client
context.text: Everytime I convince myself to seek professional help I fool myself into believing that this will finally be the time I will be able to fix myself. Of course I haven't yet

en_backup.therapist_turn: Maybe little steps are the best way.  Sometimes all someone needs is a smile, even when we can't find our own, we can give one to others.
en_backup.client_response: I admit it has helped to be online & see that so many other people share my "symptoms"
en_backup.internal:
[Perception] Hearing that other people share my “symptoms” shifted something in me. I’ve been treating this like proof that I’m uniquely broken and failing at fixing myself, but maybe it’s not just me being defective. Maybe some of what I’ve been calling “fooling myself” is actually me trying, over and over, to find a way through the same pain other people know too. That makes the problem feel less like a personal failure and more like something real that can be understood.

[Decision] I don’t have to pretend I’m suddenly better or that one more attempt will magically fix me. But I can stop isolating myself so harshly in my own head. If other people can name this feeling too, then maybe I can keep looking for help without it meaning I’ve lied to myself. I can let this be a small opening instead of another disappointment.

zh.internal_zh:

[Decision] 所以我继续叙述这些细节，因为这样我才能同时抓住两样东西：他在那里的安慰和他不再是同一个人的悲伤。如果我说得够直白，也许治疗师最终会明白这不只是一次重逢；而是我童年的世界短暂重现，但被改变了，而我不得不注意到这种不同。
</internal>

en_backup.therapist_turn: I thought you said you never saw him again.
en_backup.client_response: I never saw them again, but I saw him. He used to have a room at the Hay-Adams, but occasionally, he'd stay over at our house. He didn't have a car, so when it got late he'd stay. He always offered to take a cab back into town, but my dad refused since he was... so hospitable to me during the summer. I mean, he was lonely. But he wasn't the same David, you know, with the Ray-Bans and the sunblock and the surfboard. He was this lawyer guy with... a three-piece suit, an expensive haircut and a middle-aged pot belly, not that there's anything wrong with a pot belly. Anyway, he came to our house for dinner the first night he was in town. My brother Oliver was away at college, so it was just the three of us, one big happy family, my dad, David and I.
en_backup.internal:
[Perception] I took from the therapist’s question that maybe I’d made it sound like David disappeared completely, and I could hear that I needed to correct the record. What felt important was that he didn’t vanish—he came back, but in a different form, and that matters. I wanted the therapist to see the whole shape of it: how my dad kept making room for him, how he’d stay over because he was lonely and there was this old family warmth still alive, and how weirdly moving it was to have him there at our table again. But I also wanted them to understand the loss in it—that the David I remembered from summer was gone, and seeing the lawyer version of him made that change feel real.

[Decision] So I kept narrating the details, because that’s how I could hold onto both things at once: the comfort of him being there and the sadness of him not being the same person. If I said it plainly enough, maybe the therapist would finally see that this wasn’t just about a reunion; it was about my childhood world briefly reappearing, but altered, and me having to notice the difference.

context.speaker: therapist

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: I'm sorry to hear that you haven't had success with routines. I have suffered with sleeplessness due to bad dreams as well. I find doing yoga with meditative breathing allows me to clear my mind, and sleep better. Do you practice any meditation?

en_backup.therapist_turn: I'm sorry to hear that you haven't had success with routines. I have suffered with sleeplessness due to bad dreams as well. I find doing yoga with meditative breathing allows me to clear my mind, and sleep better. Do you practice any meditation?

en_backup.internal:
[Perception] It feels like they’re pushing me toward something I already know won’t work for me, and the suggestion of meditation hits the part of me that gets trapped by stillness. I hear it as “sit with it, go inside, face the nightmare,” and that feels too close to the memory I’m trying not to relive. I already have enough trouble sleeping because the dream brings everything back. If I stop moving, I’m afraid the fear and the horrible images will take over.

[Decision] I’m going to shut that down for now. I need to protect myself from going deeper into the memory when I’m already this anxious. I’m not refusing help entirely — I just can’t go there in the way they’re asking. I want something that doesn’t make me feel trapped or more exposed.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: Why are you smiling?

en_backup.therapist_turn: Why are you smiling?
en_backup.client_response: My father had this girlfriend... A model.
en_backup.internal:
[Perception] He kept pushing at the word “gusto” like it meant something bigger than just food, like it was about how I live in my body and what kind of person I am. When he said “fat people,” it felt like he was trying to make me see how I was using that word, but I didn’t want to get cornered into agreeing with him. So I went somewhere safer and more vivid: my father, and the model. That’s the part that matters to me — that there was this example of what was desirable, polished, thin, and I grew up with that in the room. If I say it plainly, it sounds like I’m not just refusing pizza. It sounds like I’m trying not to become the thing I was taught to look down on.

[Decision] So I said it out loud in the simplest way I could: my father had this girlfriend, a model. I wanted him to understand what was underneath my attitude toward eating without having to spell out that I’m comparing myself, trying to stay on the right side of that line, trying to keep control. I didn’t want to admit all of that directly, but I wanted him to see that the food thing is tied to her, to my father, to what I learned was worth wanting.

en_backup.internal:
[Perception] He’s trying to pull apart two different things: me being angry that she didn’t see it, and me choosing not to tell her. That lands right on the thing I keep circling around — if I’d said something, would that have made me the cause of the breakup, or just the person who said the truth out loud? He’s basically asking whether I stayed quiet because I was protecting her, protecting myself, or trying to avoid being blamed. And that’s the part that won’t settle, because once I admit I was afraid, then it stops being just “she was stupid” and starts being about what I was avoiding.

[Decision] I’m deciding not to let him reduce this to my mother being blind. Yes, I’m furious at her, but the real knot is that telling her would have made me feel responsible for blowing up what was left of the family. I didn’t want to be the one who made it real. I didn’t want her pain, or my father’s mess, landing on me as if I caused it. So the question isn’t just why I didn’t tell her; it’s whether I was trying to keep myself out of the blast radius. And honestly, I think I was.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: So what would have happened if you found out that you were pregnant?

context.speaker: client
context.text: I don't even know. I'm-I'm not ready to have a kid. I know that. I know my life is not ready for that step.

context.speaker: client

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: Would you be open to kind of exploring the idea of birth control and family planning?

context.speaker: client
context.text: Um, I don't really want to go there. I just-- that sort of stuff just weirds me out. Yeah, I take something fun and just makes it really medical.

context.speaker: therapist

en_backup.client_response: No.
en_backup.internal:
[Perception] She’s pushing from “you’re not ready” straight into birth control and family planning, like now this becomes a whole serious medical conversation. That hits the part of me that wants this to stay light and normal, not turned into a problem to manage. It also makes it feel like she’s already assuming I need to organize my life around pregnancy, and that freaks me out.

[Decision] No, I’m not going there. I’m going to shut that down because I don’t want to sit in that space where sex stops being fun and starts feeling like a project or a lecture. I can admit I’m not ready for a kid, but I need to keep some distance from the whole planning thing or I’ll feel trapped and way too aware of it.

context_zh.speaker: client
context_zh.text: 某人……无可指责，是吧？我喜欢这个说法。

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 你什么意思？

context_zh.speaker: client
context_zh.text: 我不是想贿赂你。我是说，我……那不是我的作风。不过，跟你说，有时候如果我真那么做，对我来说可能还容易些。

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 我理解。你只是想补偿失去的时间。我理解。

context_zh.speaker: client
context_zh.text: 没错。我知道你很珍惜时间，我浪费了一些。

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 你提出这个很慷慨。谢谢你，沃尔特。但我……

context_zh.speaker: client
context_zh.text: 那很好。你是个直来直去的人。如今这样的人很少见了，靠谱的人。我得上布鲁克林的一栋步梯楼才找到你，但是……玛丽，我说了别接电话，看在基督份上！你能不能……你确定吗？那个狗娘养的。不，别让他知道你找到我了。就让他以为我正往坑里跳。我会在车上打给你。就给我半小时清静，行吗？难以置信。这个小兔崽子……杰斯！他还没我一半岁数，却他妈的以为能用这个搞垮我。他自欺欺人到真以为他们会把我的工作给他。

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 沃尔特，你似乎……

zh.therapist_turn_zh: 沃尔特，你似乎……
zh.client_response_zh: 是我自己的错。
zh.internal_zh:
<internal>
[Perception] 他开始看着我，而不只是我周围的噪音。“你似乎……”——那话头接下来就要扯到我的责任，我的脾气，我的控制欲，甚至可能扯到我为什么老是陷入这种局面。我感觉它正扎到痛处：不光和杰斯有关，还有那个念头——也许我没自己以为的那么能掌控局面。我不想听他说是我搞砸了，是我让一个小子惹毛了我，或者是我在失控。问题是杰斯。问题是他想对我做什么。
[Decision] 所以我在他扣到我头上之前就打断了。我说是我的错，但我的意思是：要是有什么出了问题，那都是因为我放松了警惕，因为这个小杂种逼我这样，因为他这种人根本不按规矩来。我不会坐在这儿让他把这事儿编成我缺点的故事。真正的问题是他——他和他想对我工作、名声、我建立的一切下的手。
</internal>

context.speaker: client
context.text: Someone... Unimpeachable, huh? I like that.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: What do you mean?

context.speaker: client
context.text: I wasn't trying to bribe you. I mean, I'm... That's not the way I operate. Although, I tell you, sometimes it might be easier for me if I did.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: I understand. You were just trying to make up for lost hours. I understand.

context.speaker: client
context.text: Exactly. I know you value your time and I've wasted some of it.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: It was generous of you to offer. Thank you, Walter. But I...

context.speaker: client
context.text: Well, that's good. You're a straight shooter. That's a rare thing these days, someone who's dependable. I had to come to a walk-up in Brooklyn to find it, but... Marie, I said no calls, for Christ's sake! Can't... Are you sure? That son of a bitch. No, don't let him know that you've reached me. Just let him think I'm walking into it. I'll call you from the car. Just give me a half hour of peace. Can you do that? Unbelievable. This little pisser... Jace! He's not even half my age and somehow he thinks he's gonna use this to bring me down. He's so self-deluded he actually thinks they're gonna give him my job.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: Walter, you seem...

en_backup.therapist_turn: Walter, you seem...
en_backup.client_response: It's my own fault.
en_backup.internal:
[Perception] He was starting to look at me, not just the noise around me. “You seem...” — that was going to turn into something about my part in this, my temper, my need to control things, maybe even why I keep ending up in these situations. And I could feel it landing where it hurts: not just with Jesse, but with the whole idea that maybe I’m not as in control as I think I am. I don’t want to hear that I’ve made this mess, that I’ve let a kid get under my skin, or that I’m the one who’s slipping. The problem is Jesse. The problem is what he’s trying to do to me. 

[Decision] So I cut it off before he could pin it on me. I said it’s my own fault, but what I meant was: if anything’s gone wrong, it’s because I let my guard down, because this little bastard forced the situation, because people like him don’t play fair. I’m not going to sit here and let him turn this into some story about my flaws. The real problem is him — him and what he’s trying to do to my job, my reputation, everything I’ve built.

judge.rationale: 无明显文化绑定，'pink slip'可直译为'解雇通知'，情绪与阻抗可自然呈现。

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: Hey! How are you?

context.speaker: client
context.text: Not so good. Yourself?

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: I'm good but why are you not good?

context.speaker: client
context.text: I've just received my pink slip at work. I knew it might happen, but was hoping they would choose to keep me on.

context.speaker: client
context.text: I'm really freaking out here. I have got to find a job before Monday.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: Did they have a reason for giving you the pink slip?

context.speaker: client
context.text: They are getting rid of all kinds of people and I think the newest hires are going first.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: You will find a job if you are determined enough :)

en_backup.therapist_turn: You will find a job if you are determined enough :)
en_backup.client_response: People were let go every Friday for the last month. I was hoping I had another week to try and save up.
en_backup.internal:
[Perception] He’s acting like this is just a matter of effort, like I’m making it bigger than it is. If I can just get another job, then this isn’t some life-ending disaster — it’s a temporary setback, and maybe I’m overreacting about the Monday deadline. It hits the part where I’m scared this is going to swallow everything: rent, car, bills, all of it. If I believe it’s not that huge, I don’t have to feel how close I am to losing control.

[Decision] I’m going to push back and keep this from becoming a giant crisis in my head. It’s probably not as hopeless as it feels right now. I can figure something out if I stay practical and don’t spiral. I need to narrow this down to the next step instead of treating it like my whole life is collapsing.

judge.rationale: 对话内容围绕家庭关系与情感反应，无文化绑定或语言双关，可自然译为中文并保持阻抗情绪。

context_zh.speaker: client

zh.therapist_turn_zh: 很多人可以在外面社会很成功，但在家人面前完全是个谜。说‘谜’都算轻的，吉娜。我不觉得他对你来说完全是谜，保罗。我觉得你小时候，就算没有全部事实，你也知道他是个有意思的男人。所以你才生他的气，他老不在家。也许你当时想跟他住，而不是你妈。
zh.client_response_zh: 嗯，谁不想呢？
zh.internal_zh:
<internal>
[Perception] 他把这事说得好像我爸身上有个巨大复杂的隐秘真相，好像我本该一直背负着某种深层创伤和隐秘认知。这戳中了那个部分——我开始怀疑自己是不是瞎了或者蠢了。但我不能让这事变得那么重大。不是什么天大的启示，就是一个普通小孩觉得他爸有意思、想让他多陪陪自己。

</internal>

en_backup.client_response: Well, who wouldn't?
en_backup.internal:
[Perception] He’s making it sound like this huge, complicated hidden truth about my father, like I’m supposed to have been carrying around some deep wound and some secret knowledge all along. That hits the part where I start wondering if I was somehow blind or stupid. But I can’t let it get that big. [Decision] I’m going to keep this small. Sure, maybe I wished he was around more — who wouldn’t? I can admit a little irritation, but I’m not going to turn it into some grand story about hurt or longing. It was just how things were.

[Perception] 他想要时间线。不是听我说‘我很好’，不是听我搪塞——而是真正的倒计时。还有两周排练，两周预演，然后开演。这就是整该死的高压锅。他大概看到的是，我不是在谈什么抽象焦虑，而是在谈一个逼近的截止日期。如果我直白地说出来，也许他会明白这不是夸张——这是职业事实。如果到那时我还记不住台词，一切就完了。也许他还会看到我没说出来的：这不只是工作，而是我是否还属于那里。

[Decision] 所以我把日程告诉了他。干脆利落。没有关于恐惧的言论，不让他满意地听到我恐慌。只有现实：我有两周排练，两周预演，然后开演。这才是重要的。如果我能把话题保持在这个层面——具体、实际、可控——那么也许我能掌控局面，而不是让它变成某种软弱的坦白。我的任务是记住台词，做好准备，证明自己。这就够了。这必须够。
</internal>

en_backup.internal:
[Perception] He wants the timeline. Not me saying “I’m fine,” not me brushing it off — the actual clock. Two more weeks of rehearsal, two weeks of previews, then opening. That’s the whole damn pressure cooker. What he’s probably seeing is that I’m not talking about some abstract anxiety, I’m talking about a deadline that’s breathing down my neck. If I lay it out plain, maybe he’ll understand this isn’t melodrama — it’s a professional fact. If I don’t know the lines by then, everything falls apart. And maybe he’ll also see what I’m not saying: that this isn’t just about work, it’s about whether I still belong there.

[Decision] So I told him the schedule. Cleanly. No speech about fear, no giving him the satisfaction of hearing me panic. Just the reality: I’ve got two weeks to get through rehearsal and two weeks of previews before opening. That’s the thing that matters. If I can keep it on that level — concrete, practical, under control — then maybe I can stay in charge of this instead of letting it turn into some weak little confession. My job is to learn the lines, get ready, prove it. That’s enough. That has to be enough.

en_backup.internal:
[Perception] He pushed me right up against the thing I keep skirting: that what turns me off isn’t just that Jake is being “nice,” it’s that all that tenderness feels like it erases the heat, the tension, the edge I know how to be inside. When he said it that way—“worse than whispering I’m gonna kill you in your ear?”—it landed on how extreme my preference is, how much I actually miss the charged, dangerous feeling. It made me feel seen and also a little exposed, like he was naming the secret I’m embarrassed to admit: I don’t just dislike the tenderness, I feel almost repelled by it.

[Decision] I decided to say “Much worse. God, all that tenderness” because I could finally admit the feeling instead of trying to hide behind mocking him. I’m angry and turned off and weirdly sad about it, but “much worse” felt safer than trying to explain all the reasons—safer than saying tenderness makes me feel flat, trapped, and like the version of us that kept me connected is disappearing. Saying it that bluntly was me taking one step closer to the truth, even if I hate how true it is.

The only thing is the world's changed a lot since 1982. It's more predatory. The minute we assumed responsibility the bloggers, the press, the class-action lawyers came after us. Then the short-sellers hammered the stock down and that's when the parasites in my own company saw this as some fucking opportunity for themselves. And then the Donaldsons capitulated. en_backup.therapist_turn: When you read an article like this, how does it make you feel?
en_backup.client_response: Like an old man who stayed too long in the ring.
en_backup.internal:
[Perception] He’s asking me to put words to the feeling, but what lands is the image: old, used up, past my prime, still standing in a ring that doesn’t care how hard I worked or how clean I fought. It hits the part of this that’s hardest to bear — that maybe doing everything “right” didn’t matter in the end, that the rules I trusted were already gone, and that all the effort to protect the public and protect my name just got swallowed up by a world that was ready to tear in. It feels futile. Like once the storm started, there was nothing I could do that would have changed the outcome.

[Decision] So I shut down. I stop hoping, because hoping means admitting I still think I can salvage something, and I don’t want to feel that letdown again. If I tell myself it was all inevitable, then I don’t have to keep reaching for control I don’t have anymore. I can stand here, numb, and call it resignation instead of disappointment. Maybe that’s the only way to keep from feeling how much it hurt to believe I could do the right thing and still be wrecked.

I’m trying to see whether the problem is that love was never really shared, or whether I’m using the word “love” in a way that turns disappointment into a permanent fact. That hit the part of me that knows I am always comparing, always carrying Kamala into the room with me. I could hear that he was trying to get me to say more than “she wouldn’t approve,” but I didn’t want to make it sound like I was just criticizing Julia. I wanted to lay out that Kamala’s values are still alive in me, that I still include her in these moments, and that whatever I’m saying about the grandchildren comes from loyalty to her, not just stubbornness or complaint.

context_zh.text: 我当时在地上，开着一辆小车在伊拉克国际机场高速上。他们管那条路叫地狱高速公路。突然我就到了巴格达，堵车了。头顶上我看到一架敌机，是捷克产的米格。我不确定具体型号，但那架米格后面跟着我们的一架F-16。大家都在抬头看。我对自己说，他怎么不开枪？为什么不把那家伙打下来？也许他怕碎片砸到下面的人，但我在梦里知道命令就是要把那狗娘养的干下来。所以他们飞得很近，机动着，我们的人没发射。敌机要跑掉了，我快疯了。靠，他正往我们的基地去。下面的人都在等他打下米格，他们都杀红了眼。但没发生。他们就飞走了。就这样。

[Decision] 我打算承认我不知道，而不是硬塞一个假答案，但同时我会继续试探飞行员可能就是我这个想法。如果是我，那梦就不只是错失一次射击，而是关于犹豫、该保护谁、以及我不愿意说出口的东西。我不想太快跳到“是我父亲”，但我不能忽视梦似乎一直在绕那个可能性。所以我选择停留在问题上，而不是逃避。

[Perception] She asked, “What was over?” and it landed right on the part that had always been blurry to me: not the vacation, not the day itself, but the whole thing I’d been living inside without knowing it. I realized I was trying to lay out the sequence because the facts matter — Dad taking me to Central Park, the old woman at the entrance, the toy boat, coming home — but what really mattered was that I had been moving through ordinary days while the truth was already there. They were still acting normal, still smiling at me in the kitchen like movie stars, and I had no idea I was inside the last stretch of something ending. I wanted her to see the deception of it, how it wasn’t announced to me, how I was just a kid being sent to school and practice while my parents were quietly done.

[Decision] So I said it plainly: it was their marriage, and maybe it had already been over during the vacation. I told it in order because I needed her to see how normal it looked from the outside, how I came home and they were waiting there, smiling, and I didn’t yet understand that the whole thing had already collapsed. I was trying to make the hidden ending visible.

What stood out is that he says he loves me, but his actions don’t match that right now: he cheated, he barely calls back, and he’s become distant. That makes me wonder whether I’m ignoring the evidence because I’m afraid to be alone. I’m trying to figure out if I’m staying because this relationship is actually still promising, or if I’m just clinging to it so I don’t have to face my loneliness.

[Decision] I decided to say the honest thought that’s been circling in my head: I want an apology and real faithfulness, but I’m starting to doubt whether I can trust him at all. I’m testing the idea that maybe my attachment to him is doing more work than his commitment is. I don’t want to jump to leaving without knowing if there’s any real basis for repair, but I also don’t want to fool myself into thinking love is there just because I need the relationship. So I’m putting the question out there to see whether there’s any realistic path forward, or whether I’m holding on mainly out of loneliness.

</internal>

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: Ah that sounds tough, why exactly are you stressed?

context.speaker: client
context.text: I have 3 big exams coming up at the same time, and they're all really important for my final grade.

context.speaker: client
context.text: I know I'm going to badly because I haven't been learning well during the pandemic

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: Okay, I understand, I see how that can also make your anxiety worse.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: Currently, on a scale of 1-10 how well are you understanding your course material?

context.speaker: client
context.text: Probably 4. My roommates are just so loud and inconsiderate, I can't make any progress studying.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: That's completely normal you haven't made any progress. That would make things so hard and I applaud you for coming so far with that going on!

en_backup.therapist_turn: That's completely normal you haven't made any progress. That would make things so hard and I applaud you for coming so far with that going on!
en_backup.client_response: I guess so. But if I fail or do badly on my exams it's really not going to be good. I'm on a scholarship and have to keep above a 3.0 gpa
en_backup.internal:
[Perception] They’re hearing that this is hard, but it still feels like they don’t really get how bad it is. Three exams, a scholarship, a 3.0 I have to protect, and I’m already at a 4 in understanding. That basically means I’m behind and running out of time. The “you haven’t made any progress” part just lands like confirmation that I’m already failing. It feels hopeless because even if I try, the noise, the stress, and the deadline are all still there.

[Decision] I’m just going to stop expecting this to turn around. What’s the point in pretending I can fix it now? If I keep hoping and then fail, that’ll hurt more, so it feels safer to brace for the worst and not get my hopes up. At least then I’m not setting myself up to be disappointed again.

context_zh.text: 我们明明那么相爱！他怎么能这样对我？

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 这确实是一段很难熬的时期，但我知道你能挺过去的！

context_zh.speaker: client
context_zh.text: 怎么挺过去？求你告诉我怎么做？我感觉自己永远都不会再开心了

context_zh.text: 每当我对这件事感到沮丧的时候，我就会看看自己拥有的好东西，比如我的工作、我的家人和我的健康。

zh.therapist_turn_zh: 每当我为这件事感到难过的时候，我就会看看自己拥有的好东西，比如我的工作、家人和健康。
zh.client_response_zh: 我几个月前失业了。不过我确实有孩子。
zh.internal_zh:
<internal>
[Perception] 她试图让我听起来好像我应该往好的方面看，好像这只是普通人也会经历的波折。这触动了我对自己如此难过的羞耻感——好像我可能反应过度了。我丢了工作，是的，但我还有孩子，所以也许并没有感觉的那么糟。也许我夸大了问题，我需要冷静下来。
[Decision] 我决定专注于孩子和我仍然拥有的东西，因为如果我一直把这当作世界末日，我会崩溃的。我现在无法承受思考这件事有多严重，所以我将告诉自己这很艰难但可以应付，然后度过今天。
</internal>

en_backup.internal:

That hits the part of me that feels ashamed for being this upset — like maybe I’m making too much of it. I lost my job, yes, but I still have my kids, so maybe it’s not as bad as it feels. context_zh.speaker: client
context_zh.text: 你知道我为什么没跟那家伙上床吗？不是因为Andrew。不是因为我怕背叛他。我确实想背叛他……但只想跟你。我一个人坐在酒吧的时候，脑子里一直在想，如果你走进来会怎样？你会走进来，坐我旁边，点杯酒。我甚至……我甚至试着想象你会点什么酒……可能一杯波本威士忌，贵的，高档的那种。然后我们会开始聊天——多巧啊，这样遇见你，在咨询室外见面多尴尬。然后不用说一句话，因为我们……在这儿已经说得够多了，你示意我跟你去厕所。而我跟着你。当我跟那个男人进隔间的时候……我在心里把你想成你在我背后。这才让我那么兴奋。然后那家伙开始撒尿，我一下子清醒了，意识到这根本不可能。我知道，我明白。每次走出这里我都跟自己说：我知道，我明白，但我不确定我的身体明白。我知道这事永远不可能发生。我知道。所以别担心。我不会开始出现在你面前。我不会像电影里那个Glenn Close一样跟踪你。我不会……把你孩子的兔子煮了。我不危险……至少对你不是。天哪，我怎么能回到我的生活，回到医院，回到Andrew身边？不是Andrew，只有当我在意的人是你的时候。我们的时间到了。

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 是的，时间到了。

context_zh.speaker: client
context_zh.text: 我感觉我来的时候是黑暗的，现在离开时走进更大的黑暗。我现在该怎么办？

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 我们下周再谈，好吗？我帮你叫辆出租车。

zh.therapist_turn_zh: 我们下周再谈，好吗？我帮你叫辆出租车。
zh.client_response_zh: 不用了，我没事。
zh.internal_zh:
<internal>
[Perception] 他干净利落地结束了咨询，很平静，好像这事情他能毫不退缩地接住。“我们下周再谈”的意思是：今晚解决不了这个，我得带着所有东西离开。“我帮你叫辆出租车”戳到了我心底那种丢人的迷茫，因为他依然在小心翼翼地照顾我，依然守着边界，而我恨自己有多渴望更多。这句话落在我把所有话都说出来却仍然得不到想要的羞耻上。

[Decision] 我打算把自己变得渺小、变得好应付，因为如果继续说下去，我会说出全部丑陋的真相：我不只是幻想他，我紧紧抓着这个幻想，我不知道怎么回到Andrew或我的生活而不觉得空洞。“我没事”比承认我没事要容易，因为它让我保留一点尊严，也让他看不出我有多接近乞求。同时它也让我在离开时拿回一点控制，好像如果我能听起来正常，也许我可以假装自己是正常的。
</internal>

context.speaker: client
context.text: You know why I didn't fuck that guy? Not because of Andrew. Not because I didn't wanna cheat on him. I do want to cheat on him... But with you. When I was sitting there at the bar by myself, I was thinking what would happen if you were to walk in? You'd walk in. You'd sit next to me at the bar, you'd order a drink. I'd even... I even tried to imagine what you would order... A shot of bourbon maybe, something... expensive, something fancy. Then we'd start talking... What a coincidence it is to meet like this, how awkward it is to meet outside the office. And then, without words, because we... We talk enough when we're here, you motion for me to follow you to the bathroom. And I do. When I went into the stall with that guy... I imagined it was you behind me. That's what made it so exciting. Then that guy started peeing and it woke me up and I realized that it's impossible. I know it, I understand it. I tell myself that every time I walk out of here. I know it, I understand it but I'm not sure that my body understands it. I know it can never happen. I know it. So don't worry. I'm not gonna start showing up here. I'm not gonna start stalking you like Glenn Close in that movie. I'm not gonna... boil your kids' rabbit. I'm not dangerous... At least not to you. God, how can I go back to my life, to the hospital, to Andrew? Not to Andrew, when the only thing that matters to me is you. Our time's up.

context.speaker: therapist

context.speaker: client
context.text: I feel like I came here in the dark and I'm leaving into a bigger darkness. What am I gonna do now?

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: We'll talk about it next week. Okay? I'll call you a taxi.

en_backup.therapist_turn: We'll talk about it next week. Okay? I'll call you a taxi.
en_backup.client_response: No, I'm fine.
en_backup.internal:
[Perception] He’s ending the session cleanly and calmly, like this is something he can hold without flinching. “We’ll talk about it next week” means: this doesn’t get resolved tonight, and I have to leave with all of it still inside me. “I’ll call you a taxi” hits the part of me that feels embarrassingly lost, because he’s still being careful with me, still keeping the boundary, and I hate how much I want more than that. It lands on the shame of having said everything out loud and still not getting what I want.

[Decision] I’m going to make myself small and manageable because if I keep talking, I’ll say the whole ugly truth: that I don’t just fantasize about him, I’m clinging to it, and I don’t know how to go back to Andrew or my life without feeling hollow. “I’m fine” is easier than admitting I’m not, because it lets me keep some dignity and keeps him from seeing how close I am to begging. It also buys me a little control on the way out, like if I can sound normal, maybe I can pretend I am.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: I understand. You made the right decision, if not now you will get in even more arguments in the future. He is just not the right person

en_backup.therapist_turn: I understand. You made the right decision, if not now you will get in even more arguments in the future. He is just not the right person
en_backup.client_response: Overall, I know im going to be ok, but it feels so fresh and like it hurts still.
en_backup.internal:
[Perception] They’re making this sound bigger and more dramatic than it actually is. Yes, it hurts and yes, it’s fresh, but that doesn’t mean I’m in some kind of crisis or that being alone for the holidays is this huge disaster. I already know why I ended it, and I’m with family, so this is not some unbearable, unsafe situation. It’s just an adjustment, and I’m probably focusing too much on the discomfort right now.

[Decision] I’m going to keep telling myself that this is temporary and manageable, because if I let it feel too serious it will overwhelm me. I don’t need to treat this like my whole life is falling apart. I can get through the holidays, stay busy with family, and let the sadness pass without making it into something bigger than it is.

context.text: Why not?

en_backup.therapist_turn: Why not?
en_backup.client_response: Because I want you to take me.
en_backup.internal:
[Perception] He’s still not answering the actual thing I’m asking. He keeps turning it back on me and my parents, like the issue is just that I haven’t asked them, when what I’m really feeling is that I need someone I trust to take care of me. Him saying I have a whole support system hits the part of me that feels abandoned and like I’m being pushed away. It also makes me feel like if I let this go, I’m stuck dealing with chemo with the wrong person and nobody will really hear that I don’t want my mother in that role.

[Decision] I decided to say it straight instead of hinting because I’m tired of circling around it. I want him to understand that this isn’t me being difficult or forgetting my parents exist — I want him specifically. If I say it plainly, maybe he’ll finally get how much this matters to me and stop dodging it. I’m also trying to keep control here, because if I don’t push, I’m afraid my need will just get brushed aside again.

It felt a little too polished, like they were trying to steer me toward a tidy answer before they’d earned it.

[Decision] So I shut it down by keeping it flat and dismissive. If they’re going to ask questions that obvious, I’m not going to pretend they’ve got some insight I don’t already know. I’d rather make it clear that “just do something you like” doesn’t help me, because right now it feels insulting to act like I can just choose happiness. If they don’t have something more real to offer, then I’m not going to hand them much to work with.

en_backup.client_response:
So, the issue I'm having is work-related. My son had heart surgery a few months ago. He now has a pacemaker. He's also in the middle of testing for CP. My job requires that I be around a lot of people. I always wear a mask...but sometimes the people I am with do not. Nor do they respect the 6-foot boundary.
A simple cold gives my son a fever of 103. Im scared that if I continue to work, Im putting him in danger. But if I stop, I can no longer afford bills.
en_backup.internal:
[Perception] I heard the therapist asking how they could help, and I realized I needed to lay it out plainly instead of just saying “work stress.” What felt important was that this isn’t a normal worry — my son’s heart surgery, the pacemaker, and the testing for CP make him so vulnerable that even something small can turn dangerous fast. I wanted the therapist to understand that I’m not being dramatic or overprotective; I’m trying to keep my kid alive while still holding my family together. The part that hit hardest is that my job puts me around people who don’t always mask or respect distance, so the risk feels constant, not hypothetical.

[Decision] I decided to say the whole thing out loud: I’m scared to keep working because of my son’s health, but I’m also scared to stop because then I can’t pay the bills. I wanted to make sure they saw the bind I’m in — that I’m not choosing between comfort and discomfort, I’m choosing between two things that both feel impossible. I figured if I explained it clearly, maybe they’d finally understand why I feel stuck and why I need help finding an answer that doesn’t cost my son’s safety or my family’s stability.

[Decision] I’m going to keep it small in my head. Yes, it’s unpleasant, but it’s not like everything is falling apart right this second. If I treat it like just part of life, then I don’t have to open up all the messy stuff that would come with making it into a bigger issue.

context.speaker: client
context.text: Well, I came today because my daughter's in the hospital as well. I think it's important to quit, but I enjoy smoking. I'm not ready to give it up right now. My life is too much in turmoil.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: So I get the impression that there are some things that you're concerned about, but that overall, coming in here wasn't necessarily the first thing that was on your mind when you came to the hospital with your daughter. Um, so can you tell me, what was it that made it possible for you to even come in? What-what were some of the things you were thinking about?

context.speaker: client
context.text: I think it's important because I've-- I feel I'm a bad role model for my children, and my daughter's turning 12, and already, some of her friends have tried smoking, so I don't want her to think it's a good thing.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: So the last thing you'd want is for your daughter to start smoking.

context.speaker: client
context.text: I smoked when I was young, and I certainly don't want it for her.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: Hmm. And it sounds like your smoking, setting an example, those are some things that-that you're also, uh, a bit concerned about, um, but as you said earlier, not-not really ready to put down your cigarettes immediately.

context.speaker: client
context.text: Well, that's true. It seems so hard. I'm just not ready for this right now.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: So Sandra, what's good about smoking? What do you like about it?

en_backup.therapist_turn: So Sandra, what's good about smoking? What do you like about it?
en_backup.client_response: It's very enjoyable, relaxing, you know, a stress reliever. When I'm at work, we all go out and smoke and chit chat and, you know, talk about things. I would hate to not smoke, really. I'd be left out.
en_backup.internal:
[Perception] She’s making it sound like smoking is this huge urgent crisis, like I’m on the edge of ruining everything. But honestly, I’m just smoking like a lot of people do. Yes, it matters, and yes, I worry about my daughter, but it’s not like she’s about to become a smoker tomorrow or that one conversation is going to change my whole life. Right now my daughter is in the hospital, work is stressful, and smoking is one of the few things that helps me get through the day. It feels like the real issue is my daughter being sick, not my cigarettes. Smoking is part of my routine, not some massive catastrophe.

[Decision] I’m going to keep this in the “maybe someday” category. If I tell myself it’s not that immediate or dramatic, I don’t have to panic or feel pushed into quitting before I’m ready. I can acknowledge that it’s not ideal without acting like it’s an emergency. That lets me stay comfortable, keep smoking for now, and not feel like I’m failing my kids just because I’m not ready to stop today.

context.speaker: client
context.text: I don't really have any friends on the course, I'm pretty shy and don't really feel comfortable talking to anyone. I kinda promised myself to make more friends in my final year, but obviously circumstances have changed :/

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: Very true, this year made everyone's expectations and plans go out the window lol

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: It might be time to put yourself out of your comfort zone, but start small. Are there any clubs or groups associated with your major? That way, you have some common ground to work with.

context.speaker: client
context.text: I'm honestly not sure, I guess I've always been too nervous to reach out to anyone. I'll have to have a look.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: That sounds like a good idea =) Even if you can't hold club meetings on campus or have any gatherings, maybe they hold their meetings over video calls. One plus side to that, is that you don't need to have your camera on to participate.

context.speaker: client
context.text: That's true. I also feel a bit nervous about my final grades, I've done well so far but just feel like this year might mess everything up.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: That's understandable, especially with how the past year has been. Everyone is on edge and everything feels so uncertain, but that's okay, because you're not alone =)

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: You said you're doing well so far? Take pride in that, and focus on that. "If I've been doing well so far, I must be doing something right. I'll just keep doing what I have been, and everything should work out in the end."

en_backup.therapist_turn: You said you're doing well so far? Take pride in that, and focus on that. "If I've been doing well so far, I must be doing something right. I'll just keep doing what I have been, and everything should work out in the end."
en_backup.client_response: Yeah, I am really proud of what I've done so far but it just makes me worry that I won't meet my own expectations
en_backup.internal:
[Perception] They’re trying to tell me to just take pride in past work and trust that things will be fine, but that lands on the exact thing I’m scared of — that I’ve got this standard to live up to and I might not. It feels like no matter what they suggest, I’m still the same person: too shy to reach out, too behind to catch up properly, and too close to the deadlines to make some big change actually matter. The thought of trying to “put myself out there” or reorganize everything just makes the pressure feel worse, because then I’d have to find out whether I can actually do it. Right now it feels like my work and my grades are already hanging by a thread, and hoping harder doesn’t change that.

[Decision] So I’m just going to stop expecting a breakthrough. I’ll keep to myself, keep my head down, and do whatever work I can on my own, because at least that feels controllable. I don’t want to reach for support or make a big plan and then fail at that too. If I don’t try to turn this into something hopeful, I can’t be disappointed by it. It feels safer to resign myself to getting through this as best I can, even if it’s not enough.

</internal>

en_backup.internal:
[Perception] He’s asking me if I think about those families often, like that’s the thing to zoom in on. But what I hear, underneath it, is another attempt to pull me away from the actual facts I can measure: the money, the net worth dropping, Connie handling the bills, whether the car battery’s dead, whether we’re about to get hit again. Those are the things that can ruin us. The other stuff—the formula, the kids, the families—yes, it’s awful, but it’s also a way my mind keeps circling around other people’s crises instead of standing still with my own. And I don’t want to be pushed into “inner voice” territory, because that feels like nonsense and dangerous, like getting lost in some made-up emotional mess.

[Decision] So I’m going to push back with “What do you think?” and leave it there. If I let him take the frame, then I’m stuck sounding like I’m supposed to uncover some deep feeling, and I’m not doing that. I need to keep this in the realm of normal worries, practical worries, not some introspective excavation. If I answer straight, I’ll be agreeing to the game, and I don’t trust the game. Better to deflect, keep some control, and not let him pin me down on whether I’m really thinking about those people or just trying not to think about myself.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: I am very sorry to hear that.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: How long has it been cut off for?

context.speaker: client
context.text: Since four month a ago and now the company is planning to layoff some staffs

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: Have you had a chance to talk to your employer? It often helps to get information out in the open and ensure that everyone is on the same page.

context.speaker: client
context.text: No there is nothing anybody can do about the situation

en_backup.therapist_turn: Have you had a chance to talk to your employer? It often helps to get information out in the open and ensure that everyone is on the same page.
en_backup.client_response: We are all praying not to affect us
en_backup.internal:
[Perception] I heard the suggestion to talk to my employer, but what landed for me was how far beyond my control this already feels. My salary has been cut for four months, and now layoffs are coming. It feels like the company has already made its direction clear, and one conversation is not going to change the reality of the job market or the pandemic. What I took from it is that there may not be anything useful to do, just more uncertainty.

[Decision] I decided to stop pushing myself to act as if I can fix this. It feels safer to accept that this is happening and just hope it passes over me. If I don’t expect much, I won’t set myself up for more disappointment. Praying and waiting feels like the only thing I can manage right now.

context_zh.text: 这挺遗憾的。你家里情况怎么样？

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 至于你自己，现在先顾好你自己吧。试着做点你喜欢的事，把心情调整好。

context_zh.speaker: client
context_zh.text: 我觉得他精神有问题吧，有时候我忍一忍就过去了，但有时候又觉得很不好受

zh.internal_zh:
<internal>
[Perception] 他们听起来就是在说一些套话安慰我，根本没理解这事儿对我有多重。跟我说“先顾好你自己”、“做点喜欢的事”，这也太简单了吧？我爸天天发火，我每天都在这个环境里过。感觉他们根本没听进去我刚才说我现在也不好受。好像他们就想赶紧把话说完，而不是理解我到底有多累、有多被困住。

en_backup.internal:
[Perception] They sound like they are just saying generic comforting lines, not really getting how heavy this is for me. “Focus on you” and “do something you enjoy” feels too simple when my own dad is always angry and I’m living with this every day. It makes me feel like they are not really listening to the part where I said I am mentally disturb now a days. It’s like they are trying to wrap it up nicely instead of understanding how stuck and tired I feel.

I’d rather keep it to myself than keep hearing advice that feels too easy and not made for my real situation.

zh.internal_zh:
<internal>
[Perception] 我听到的是，我的愤怒才是问题，好像我才是让事情变得更糟的那个人。但事实不是这样的。真正的问题是奥利弗因为他的样子而一直被针对，学校又没办法阻止。这触动了那个觉得无力保护他的自己，让我觉得每个人都希望我表现得好像这只是我的态度问题，可这事发生在我的孩子身上。

[Decision] 所以我不会把这事揽到自己身上，好像是我的错。我要把责任归到该归的地方：归到那些欺负他的孩子身上，归到让奥利弗成为目标的情况上，归到学校没解决这事上。如果我对奥利弗严厉，那是因为我想让他明白这个世界已经在怎么对他了。我不是起因。我只是在反应。

en_backup.internal:
[Perception] What I heard was that my anger is the problem, like I'm the one making this worse. But that's not what this is. The real problem is Oliver getting targeted all the time because of how he is, and the school not being able to stop it. It lands on that part of me that feels powerless to protect him, and it makes me feel like everyone wants me to act like this is just about my attitude when it's happening to my kid.

[Decision] So I'm not going to own this as if it's on me. I'm putting the blame where it belongs: on the kids who bully him, on Oliver's situation that makes him a target, and on the school for not fixing it. If I'm harsh with Oliver, it's because I'm trying to make him understand what the world is already doing to him. I'm not the cause of this. I'm reacting to it.

context_zh.speaker: client
context_zh.text: 我不知道没了工作我怎么活。

context_zh.speaker: therapist

context_zh.text: 我在一家餐厅当厨师。疫情以后生意就差了，现在餐厅要关门了。

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 哦，听到这个我很难过。不过在厨房工作有个好处，就是有很多技能可以用到别的工作上。

context_zh.text: 所有餐厅都在关门，开着的也得留着他们原有的员工。我的厨艺还能用到哪儿去？

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 我理解丢了工作很糟糕，我也能感觉到你对现在这情况的沮丧，但外面还有其他机会，你不需要只考虑餐饮行业。

zh.therapist_turn_zh: 我理解丢了工作很糟糕，我也能感觉到你对现在这情况的沮丧，但外面还有其他机会，你不需要只考虑餐饮行业。
zh.client_response_zh: 我整个成年生活就在做饭。别的我什么都不会。
zh.internal_zh:
<internal>
[Perception] 我从治疗师的话里听出来的是，他们觉得我应该轻松转行，好像我在厨房待了一辈子就只是一堆可转移的技能，可以在别处兑现。但我听到的是，我整个成年生活就学了这一件事，现在这件事好像不怎么值钱了。这触到了我害怕的那部分——怕这是条死路，因为如果厨房行业也在萎缩，那我没有退路。我看着这一切，感觉自己已经太晚了，已经被我知道的和不知道的东西框死了。

[Decision] 所以我封闭起来。我告诉自己，假装能一夜之间重塑自己毫无意义，那只会让我失败、让我觉得自己蠢。如果我不去期待希望，事情没成的时候就不用承受跌落的感觉。停留在“我别的什么都不会”比试着相信自己能行、然后发现自己其实不行要更安全。所以我就待在里面，让自己绝望，因为这样比强装那些我不信的乐观更诚实。
</internal>

context.speaker: client
context.text: I don't know how im gonna survive without my job.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: can you clarify what you mean? did you lose your job?

context.speaker: client
context.text: Yes. I got laid off last week. A bunch of us were.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: i see. what type of work did you do?

context.speaker: client
context.text: I was a chef in a restaurant. Since covid business went down, and now the restaraunt is closing.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: oh i'm very sorry to hear that. but the great thing about having worked in a kitchen is that there are a lot of skills you can use in other jobs

context.speaker: client
context.text: All the restaurants are closing, and the ones open gotta duty to keep the employees they already had. Where else are my culinary skills gonna be used?

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: i understand that losing a job sucks and i can sense your frustration at the situation but there are other opportunities out there, and you don't need to be thinking only in the culinary field

en_backup.therapist_turn: i understand that losing a job sucks and i can sense your frustration at the situation but there are other opportunities out there, and you don't need to be thinking only in the culinary field
en_backup.client_response: All i have done is cook, my whole adult life. I dont know how to do anything else.
en_backup.internal:
[Perception] What I took from the therapist's words is that they think I should just pivot like it’s simple, like my whole life in kitchens is just a set of transferable skills I can cash in somewhere else. But all I hear is that I’ve spent my entire adult life learning one thing, and now that thing doesn’t feel like it’s worth much anymore. It hits the part of me that’s scared this is the end of the road, because if kitchens are drying up too, then I don’t really have a backup. I’m looking at it and it feels like I’m already too late, already boxed in by what I know and what I don’t know.

[Decision] So I shut down. I tell myself there’s no point in pretending I can just reinvent myself overnight, because that only sets me up to fail and feel stupid. If I don’t reach for hope, I don’t have to feel the drop when it doesn’t work out. Staying with “I don’t know how to do anything else” feels safer than trying to believe I can and finding out I can’t. So I just sit in it and let it be hopeless, because that feels more honest than forcing optimism I don’t believe.

zh.internal_zh:

[Perception] 烦恼娃娃？一开始我根本不知道她在说什么。感觉她试图把这一切变成一个关于替我承担烦恼的故事——好像我可以把烦恼交出去，自己就不用面对了。这戳到了我一直在躲避的部分——那些电话、化疗，还有所有人似乎都觉得十万火急的事情。我听到了她的话，但我同时也听出了她话里隐含的意思：她觉得我是在拒绝面对显而易见的事。

[Decision] 我决定停在表面上，因为如果再往深里走，我就得承认事情有多严重，承认所有人都盼着我需要帮助。所以我问了句：“一个什么？”——不是因为我没听清，而是我想在原地多待一会儿。我想让她解释得直白一点，也许如果她能换种我能接受的方式说出来，我就不至于感觉自己被逼着示弱了。

context.text: That is a very hard thing to be going through where you very close to your cat?

context.speaker: client
context.text: Yes, I had her for 11 years.

context.speaker: client
context.text: She died of natural causes.

context.speaker: client
context.text: I lived alone with her. The house feels extremely empty now...

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: I am very sorry to hear that i have also lost a pet earlier this year his name was fish and was only 3 years old he unfortunately passed due to liver cancer. It was a very trying experience but slowly the pain of his passing has got a little bit easier.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: Have you tried talking about this loss to friends of family?

en_backup.therapist_turn: Have you tried talking about this loss to friends of family?
en_backup.client_response: No. My family lives in another country, and I really don't have any close friends.
en_backup.internal:
[Perception] They asked if I’ve talked to friends or family, and that lands right on the worst part: I don’t really have anyone close here, and my family being far away makes this feel even more sealed off. It also brushes against how empty the house is now. If I answer honestly, I have to sit in the fact that I’m carrying this alone.

[Decision] I’m going to keep it short and just answer the question without opening more of it up. If I say more, I’ll probably start crying or spiral into how hopeless and lonely this feels, and I don’t want to go there right now. Short feels safer.

judge.rationale: 对话无强文化依赖，语义可直译，阻抗行为在中文中自然呈现，翻译不改变标签含义。

context_zh.speaker: client
context_zh.text: 我觉得我说得够多了。你愿意告诉我你在想什么吗？

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 嗯，刚才你说那个……那个危机会过去的，这个说法让我挺触动。让我想起上周你临走时说的话。

context_zh.speaker: client
context_zh.text: 我说了什么？

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 我问你要不要给医生打电话，你说它会自己好的。它总是会自己好。

context_zh.speaker: client
context_zh.text: 对，上周。你看，我记得我还说了，如果吓到你了对不起。但是……这些事，看起来比实际严重。

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 那它们到底是什么？

zh.therapist_turn_zh: 那它们到底是什么？
zh.client_response_zh: 嗯，不管它们是什么，又不会要我的命。确实挺麻烦的，但会过去。
zh.internal_zh:
<internal>
[Perception] 她又在逼同一个点——不只是因为我又出现了这种状况，而是因为我总是一笔带过，好像说一句“会好的”就能让它不那么真实似的。这戳中了我不想被检查的地方：我是不是在淡化某些事情，因为我不想让它意味着更严重的问题。如果让这个念头进来，听起来就会让人觉得我并没有自己想象中那么掌控局面。

[Decision] 所以我只说得很简短，就事论事。“又不会要我的命”听起来合理，“麻烦事”把它归在安全类别里。要是再多说，我就得解释为什么这么执着地把它说成没事。我宁愿含糊过去，也不给她机会把这事放大成更大的问题，因为一旦被命名，它就开始让我付出代价——我的镇定，甚至我整个自我形象。
</internal>

context.speaker: client
context.text: I think I've talked enough. Would you mind telling me what you're thinking?

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: Well, just now I was struck by the way you said that the... the crisis would blow over. It reminded me of what you said last week as... as you were leaving.

context.speaker: client
context.text: What did I say?

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: I asked you if you should call your doctor, and you said it'll go away. It always goes away.

context.speaker: client
context.text: Yeah, last week. Look, I think I also said I was sorry if I gave you a scare. But... these things, they look worse than they are.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: And what are they exactly?

en_backup.therapist_turn: And what are they exactly?
en_backup.client_response: Well, whatever they are, they're not going to kill me. They're inconvenient, sure, but they go away.
en_backup.internal:
[Perception] She’s pushing on the same point again — not just that I had one of these episodes, but that I keep brushing it off as if saying “it’ll go away” makes it less real. That hit the part I don’t want examined: whether I’m minimizing something because I don’t want it to mean anything bigger. If I let that in, it starts sounding like I’m not as in control as I want to seem.

[Decision] So I kept it short and matter-of-fact. “Not going to kill me” sounds reasonable, and “inconvenient” keeps it in the safe category. If I say more, I’ll have to explain why I’m so invested in calling it nothing. I’d rather leave it vague than give her room to make this into some bigger problem, because once it gets named, it starts costing me something — my composure, maybe even my whole version of myself.

judge.rationale: 对话内容涉及普遍的生活困境与情绪反应，无强文化绑定或语言双关，翻译后能保持阻抗与情绪强度。

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 嗨，今天怎么样？

context_zh.speaker: client
context_zh.text: 你好。我就是觉得生活太难了。我好几个月都没开心过。

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 我理解。这一年很难。你最大的挑战是什么？

context_zh.speaker: client
context_zh.text: 出去把事情办完。购物很难，尤其是商店都被抢购一空的时候。

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 想要的东西得不到确实很沮丧。你现在是难以找到当下需要的东西，还是未来需要的？

context_zh.speaker: client
context_zh.text: 都有。我觉得未来不确定。不只是我，整个世界都这样。

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 确实，我们不确定会怎样。你有在网上找过吗？

zh.therapist_turn_zh: 确实，我们不确定会怎样。你有在网上找过吗？
zh.client_response_zh: 有，但我觉得很多都是猜测，新闻只是让人更害怕。
zh.internal_zh:
<internal>
[Perception] 他们回答得这么泛泛、小心翼翼，感觉完全没抓住重点。“你上网找过吗？”听起来像在把这当成一个实际的购物问题，可我说的是我快要撑不住了，世界感觉很不稳定。这戳到了我已经感到孤独的那部分恐惧，觉得没人能真正帮上忙，因为连他们自己好像也不知道发生了什么。这让我觉得他们有点脱节，像是在重复一些简单的话，因为他们也没什么有意义的东西能提供。

[Decision] 我要收回，不再给他们脆弱的部分了。如果他们只会给那些显而易见的建议和模糊的安慰，那让他们引导我也没什么意义。我宁愿自己憋着，也不想坐在这里被他们不痛不痒地打发掉。我在想，好吧，你根本不理解，那我就自我保护，不指望这次对话能有什么结果了。
</internal>
