context.speaker: therapist
context.text: hi how's it going today?

context.speaker: client
context.text: Hello. I just find life very hard. I have not been happy in months.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: i hear you. it has been a hard year. what's been the biggest challenge for you?

context.speaker: client
context.text: Going out and getting things done. Shopping is hard especially when stores are picked over.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: it is frustrating not being able to get what you want when you want it. are you having a hard time finding the things you need for right now or for in the future?

context.speaker: client
context.text: Both. I feel like the future is uncertain. Not just for me but the world.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: it's true, we are not sure what to expect. have you looked for things online?

en_backup.therapist_turn: it's true, we are not sure what to expect. have you looked for things online?
en_backup.client_response: Yes, but I feel like a lot of it is speculation and news just makes people more fearful.
en_backup.internal:
[Perception] They answered in this generic, cautious way that feels like it misses the whole point. “Have you looked online?” sounds like they’re treating this like a practical shopping problem, when I’m saying I’m barely holding it together and the world feels unstable. It hits the part of me that already feels alone with this fear, like no one can really help because even they don’t seem to know what’s going on. It makes them feel a little out of touch, like they’re repeating something simple because they don’t have anything meaningful to offer.

[Decision] I’m going to pull back and stop giving them the vulnerable part of this, because if they’re just going to hand me obvious suggestions and vague reassurance, there’s no point letting them steer me around. I’d rather keep this to myself than sit here and be gently dismissed. I’m thinking, okay, you don’t really get it, so I’ll protect myself and not expect much from this conversation.

judge.rationale: 对话涉及常见经济压力话题，无强文化绑定或语言双关，翻译后可自然保留语义与情绪

context_zh.text: 你好，今天在想什么？

context_zh.speaker: client
context_zh.text: 我压力太大了，因为今年生意不好。我很担心可能得关门，付不起账单。

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 那确实很难。很多人都在经历这个，你并不孤单。

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 你做什么生意？

zh.therapist_turn_zh: 你做什么生意？
zh.client_response_zh: 我卖化妆品。我觉得很多人现在没钱买非必需品。
zh.internal_zh:
<internal>
[Perception] 我听到治疗师试图把它正常化，但让我真正感受到的是，这可能不只是我个人的失败——它跟整个经济有关，人们削减了非必需开支。这触碰到了我处境中正在努力理解的部分：这到底是一时的，还是我的商业模式真的有问题。如果人们真的没钱买化妆品，那生意不好也许不是我做错了什么，但也意味着我能控制的东西可能比我想象的要少。

[Decision] 我提起化妆品和非必需开支的问题，是因为我在试探现实情况，而不是指望它自己奇迹般好转。我想看看有没有实际可行的路，还是我需要开始做最坏的打算。有一部分我在寻找能抓住的具体东西，但另一部分我已经准备好面对市场可能已经以一种我无法忽视的方式改变了。
</internal>

context.text: hello, what is on your mind today?

context.speaker: therapist

en_backup.therapist_turn: what kind of business do you have?
en_backup.client_response: I sell cosmetics. I think a lot of people don't have money to buy non essential items right now.
en_backup.internal:
[Perception] I heard the therapist trying to normalize it, but what landed for me is that this may not be just me failing — it’s tied to the broader economy and people cutting back on non-essential spending. That hits the part of my situation where I’m trying to understand whether this is temporary or whether my business model is actually in trouble. If people truly don’t have money for cosmetics, then maybe the slump isn’t because I’m doing something wrong, but it also means there may be less I can control than I want.

[Decision] I brought up cosmetics and the non-essential spending issue because I’m trying to test the reality of my situation instead of just hoping it will magically improve. I want to see whether there’s a practical path here or whether I need to start planning for a worse outcome. Part of me is looking for something concrete to hold onto, but another part is bracing for the possibility that the market has changed in a way I can’t ignore.

judge.rationale: 内容涉及普遍的家庭期望与亲子关系，无文化专有梗或语言双关，翻译后能保持阻抗与合作，情绪自然。

context_zh.speaker: client
context_zh.text: 我爸大概想让我当个读书人吧。毕竟是家族传统嘛。但他能指望什么呢？我不知道。我觉得他早在我高中辍学那会儿就放弃对我抱希望了。

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 你觉得哪个在先——你爸期望低，还是你成绩差？

context_zh.speaker: client
context_zh.text: 你什么意思？

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 期望这东西，常常是自我实现的预言。也许你早就认定自己达不到他的期望，所以就干脆不努力了。

zh.therapist_turn_zh: 期望这东西，常常是自我实现的预言。也许你早就认定自己达不到他的期望，所以就干脆不努力了。
zh.client_response_zh: 有可能吧。我妈倒是一直想让我感兴趣。她偷偷帮我复习考试。
zh.internal_zh:
<internal>
[Perception] 他想把这事归到某个模式上——说是我先放弃的，好像是我自己不努力才搞砸了。但这忽略了一个对我很重要的事：我妈当时并没有袖手旁观，她一直在悄悄支持我。她看到我在挣扎，还是帮我，就算得偷偷摸摸——因为我爸会讨厌这样。这让事情没那么简单，不是一句“我放弃了”就能解释的，更像是家里已经分裂了——我爸在评判，我妈在拯救，我夹在中间。

[Decision] 所以我提我妈的事，是想让他看到整个局面，而不只是“我失败、我爸放弃期望”这个版本的故事。我想让他明白，确实有人在帮我，但那是藏起来的，而这种隐瞒本身就有意义。不光是成绩的事。是谁站在我这边、谁不在，还有我怎样学会在这种环境里过日子，不把它闹成一场大吵。
</internal>

context.speaker: client
context.text: My dad probably wanted me to be some kind of academic. It's the family business after all. But what did he expect? I don't know. I think he gave up the dream on me pretty early after I flunked out of high school.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: Which do you think came 1st, your father's low expectations or your low grades?

context.speaker: client
context.text: What you meaning?

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: Often with expectations, there's a self-fulfilling prophecy. Maybe you decided earlier on you couldn't match up to his expectations and so you gave up trying.

en_backup.therapist_turn: Often with expectations, there's a self-fulfilling prophecy. Maybe you decided earlier on you couldn't match up to his expectations and so you gave up trying.
en_backup.client_response: Could be. My mom was always trying to get me interested. She'd help me study for tests on the sly.
en_backup.internal:
[Perception] He’s trying to pin this on some pattern where I checked out first, like I set the whole thing in motion by not trying. But that leaves out the part that actually mattered to me: my mom wasn’t just standing by, she was quietly backing me up. She saw I was struggling and helped me anyway, even if she had to do it on the sly because my dad would’ve hated it. That makes this less like simple “I gave up” and more like there was this whole split in the house—my dad judging, my mom rescuing, and me caught in the middle of it.

[Decision] So I brought up my mom because I wanted him to see the whole setup, not just the story where I failed and my dad stopped expecting anything. I wanted him to understand that there was help there, but it was hidden, and that secrecy mattered. It wasn’t just about grades. It was about who was on my side, who wasn’t, and how I learned to live inside that without making it into a big fight.

judge.rationale: 对话核心是父子关系与内疚感，无文化特定梗或制度细节，可自然翻译为中文。

context_zh.speaker: client
context_zh.text: 我真希望我能叫你滚蛋。

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 是什么拦着你？

context_zh.speaker: client
context_zh.text: 我不知道你是怎么想我的。

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 我必须怎么想你？

context_zh.speaker: client
context_zh.text: 我在让我儿子遭受我受过的痛苦。不仅如此，我还……我还从中得到某种安慰，整夜睡得像个婴儿。我是说……我不知道你怎么还能看得下去我。

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 当我看着你，我看到一个深切关心儿子的父亲。

context_zh.speaker: client
context_zh.text: 操。操蛋。操。我20分钟后得去接马克斯。我得带他去宾州车站赶6:50的火车。他要和凯特还有史蒂夫过周末。我不知道我能不能面对他。

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 你怕什么？

zh.therapist_turn_zh: 你怕什么？
zh.client_response_zh: 怕他抬头看我，然后假装……假装什么都好，可真相是他在担心我要死了。
zh.internal_zh:
<internal>
[Perception] 他没有要我去证明我有多好。他说他看到了一个担心儿子的父亲，而不是一个怪物。这句话正好砸在我一直想藏起来的那部分：如果马克斯用那种小心翼翼的表情看我，那种“一切都好”的表情，那他肯定已经背上了我塞给他的东西。我在试图弄明白他知道什么，怀疑什么，以及我是不是已经来不及阻止他觉得我要死了或者会抛弃他。悬而未决的问题是，我的恐惧到底是因为马克斯的恐惧，还是因为我不得不面对自己一直陷在痛苦里所做的事。

[Decision] 我决定不能再拿自己的羞耻当借口躲着他。我还有二十分钟，所以下一步就是把自己收拾好，出现在他面前，老老实实地看他，而不是躲在这堆恶心后面。如果他在看着我，我需要搞清楚他到底看到了什么。我还不知道我能不能跟他说实话，但我知道，跑掉只会让事情更糟。所以我会去见他，哪怕我觉得这是走向我毁了一切的确凿证据。
</internal>

It lets me keep the heat off for a minute, keep the conversation on my terms, and avoid handing over the one thing I don’t want to say out loud: that I’m here because I can’t fully outrun what I did, even if I can still joke about the people trying to kill me. Brevity is safer because it doesn’t open the door all the way.

It ignores the reality that I do care, that I’m trying to stay within my professional limits, and that I’m scared of doing the wrong thing legally and ethically. It also sounded like she was reducing my concern to some simple boundary issue, when what I’m actually facing is that a person may die and I may still not be able to force treatment. That’s what hit me — not just the patient’s refusal, but the helplessness and the moral pressure of it.

[Decision] I decided I had to push back because I don’t want my position distorted into “you don’t care enough” or “just do more.” I needed her to understand that this isn’t about not wanting to help; it’s about the limits of my role and the fear of crossing a line. So I challenged the simplification and tried to force the conversation back to the real tension: how can I help without pretending I have power I don’t actually have?

context_zh.text: 保罗，我们不是神。救不了任何人。你确实在乎你的病人。但我得说，只要你还活在恐惧和愤怒里，你对谁都没用。

zh.therapist_turn_zh: 保罗，我们不是神。救不了任何人。你确实在乎你的病人。但我得说，只要你还活在恐惧和愤怒里，你对谁都没用。
zh.client_response_zh: 怕我救不了他们，怕他们都会死？
zh.internal_zh:
<internal>
[Perception] 怕我救不了他们，怕他们都会死？听着太简单了，但也许正因为它恰好戳中了要害。他并不是模糊地说我焦虑——他是指出背后那个规则：如果我不能阻止结果发生，就是失败。那部分感觉撑不住。这不只是这个女孩没回电话的问题，而是整个模式。如果我联系不上她，如果我不能阻止病人消失，那我还有什么用？但我又在想，我是不是混淆了责任和控制。我可以负责而不保证结果。那不是一回事，尽管情感上我觉得它们一样。

[Decision] 所以我试着跟着逻辑走而不是直接反应。如果恐惧是无论我做什么人都要死，那么一遍遍打电话可能不是帮忙，而是试图消除那种恐惧。也许我需要问：哪些部分真的是我该做的，哪些超出我的控制？因为如果我把每次损失都当作证明我没做够，我就永远停不下来。而如果永远停不下来，我也不可能清醒到帮谁。我不喜欢这个结论，但它好像比假装能拯救所有人更诚实。
</internal>

context.speaker: client
context.text: And I called her a couple of times twice yesterday. I called her three and 3 times today. She still hasn't called back. I just... You know, I have to help this girl.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: Paul, we're not gods. We can't save anybody. You really care about your patients. But I have to say you're no good to anybody as long as you are living with all this fear and anger.

en_backup.therapist_turn: Paul, we're not gods. We can't save anybody. You really care about your patients. But I have to say you're no good to anybody as long as you are living with all this fear and anger.
en_backup.client_response: Fear that I can't save them, fear that they're all gonna die?
en_backup.internal:
[Perception] Fear that I can't save them, fear that they're all gonna die? That sounds too simple, but maybe that's because it hits the nerve exactly. He’s not just saying I’m anxious in some vague way — he’s pointing at the rule underneath everything: if I can’t prevent the outcome, then I’ve failed. That’s the part that feels unbearable. It’s not only about this girl not calling back; it’s the whole pattern. If I can’t reach her, if I can’t keep patients from slipping away, then what good am I? But then I’m also wondering whether I’m mixing up responsibility with control. I can be responsible without being able to guarantee the result. Those are not the same thing, though emotionally I act like they are.

[Decision] So I’m trying to follow the logic instead of just reacting. If the fear is that people will die no matter what I do, then calling again and again may be less about helping and more about trying to cancel that fear. Maybe I need to ask: what part of this is actually mine to do, and what part is outside my control? Because if I keep treating every loss as proof that I didn’t do enough, I’ll never stop chasing it. And if I never stop chasing it, I won’t be thinking clearly enough to help anyone anyway. I don’t like that conclusion, but it seems more honest than pretending I can save everyone.

context.speaker: client
context.text: Sometimes I think if I could just... get away somewhere, the country or... maybe a lake. Just a funny thought.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: Would you care to share it?

en_backup.therapist_turn: Would you care to share it?
en_backup.client_response: With you? That's kind of what happens in here. I'm supposed to tell you everything that pops into my head? I just thought, I'll sleep when I'm dead.
en_backup.internal:
[Perception] He’s pushing me to open up the minute I mention wanting to get away, like that means I owe him the whole picture. It lands on the part of me that wants some quiet, some distance, without having to explain myself. It feels nosy, like once I give him one honest thought he’ll keep pulling until I’m laid out on the table. I don’t like being made to feel as if I’m supposed to account for every passing thought, as if that’s what this is now. I’m not here to perform my insides for somebody else. 

[Decision] No. I’m not going to hand over everything just because he asks. I’ll shut that door. If I let this turn into me talking about every little thing, I lose control, and I lose the one thing I can still count on: keeping myself together. So I’ll brush it off, make it sound small, say something blunt, and keep the rest to myself. If I can’t get away for real, then I can at least keep my thoughts to myself in here.

zh.internal_zh:
<internal>
[Perception] 她在说圣诞夜那件事不只是她伤害自己或者毁掉我的夜晚——那件事某种程度上也是冲我来的。我听到她说“惩罚你”和“如果你不照顾她”，我正试着搞清楚她是想说我也受到了威胁，而不仅仅是她让我痛苦。这部分和我一直对自己的说辞不太吻合。我一直把那看成是她做了一件戏剧性的事，但主要还是针对她自己，而我呢，就是个刚好出去开心的孩子。如果那时候我的命也受到威胁，那整件事的性质就变了。那就不仅仅是家里乱套；那是一次攻击，或者至少是冲我来的警告。

en_backup.therapist_turn: It does matter. She took your wonderful night away from you. She punished you for neglecting her. She showed you what damage she could do if you ignored her, if you didn't take care of her. And it wasn't just the threat on her life.

[Perception] She’s saying the Christmas Eve thing wasn’t just about her hurting herself or ruining my night — it was also aimed at me somehow. I heard “punished you” and “if you didn’t take care of her,” and I’m trying to figure out whether she meant that I was under threat too, not just that she was making me miserable. That part doesn’t quite fit with how I’ve always told it to myself. I’ve been seeing it as her doing something dramatic, but still mostly to herself, while I was the kid who was just out having a good time. If there was a threat on my life too, then it changes the whole shape of it. It makes it more than a family mess; it makes it an attack, or at least a warning aimed at me.

[Decision] So I’m pushing back a little to test what exactly you mean. I’m not ready to accept the whole framing as-is, because I need to know whether you’re saying she was trying to hurt me directly, or whether you mean her actions were dangerous to me in a broader way. I’m asking it this way because if I can pin down what the threat was, then I can decide whether I’m being unfair to her, or whether I’ve actually been minimizing something real. I want the logic of it before I let myself agree.

zh.client_response_zh: 他们想要被爱，哪怕是被我爱。他们想要一个孩子，或者想成为我的孩子。他们想要一个爱他们的父母。他们想要关注，想要温情。他们想要希望，想要药片，还想要性。这清单列得挺好的。但我给不了他们那些。我的病人米娅，那个律师，你知道她想要什么吗？她想要我抱着她，安慰她。但她真正需要的是一个好丈夫和一个家庭。我知道我给不了她那些。我所能做的只是让她看到，她推开了那些真正能帮她的人，却拽着那些不会帮她的人。但这只会让她感到更孤独、更不被爱。当她在周一离开时，当她离开我办公室时，她感到绝望，被家人和全世界拒绝。而我完全无话可说。
zh.internal_zh:
<internal>
[Perception] 我听到你把米娅和我的其他病人简化为那些不可能的愿望，然后下结论说，既然我满足不了这些愿望，我对他们就没用。这话戳中我最痛的地方：害怕自己的工作本质上就是让人失望，我让人感觉更糟，而且我根本没有什么真正的东西可以给他们。但这个说法太绝对了。听起来好像唯一重要的就是被爱、被抱、或者被拯救成我认为他们该有的生活。那不是全部。它忽略了一点，他们来找我还有别的原因——为了被理解，被真正看见，为了让模式被点出来，为了有人陪他们一起面对残酷的事实。我没办法修复他们的家庭，没办法娶他们，也没法给他们一个生活。但说我没给他们任何东西，这不准确。

[Decision] 我决定必须顶回去，因为如果我认了这个总结，那就等于把自己的角色全盘认成失败，看不清我实际提供的帮助。我要纠正这幅画面：没错，我给不了他们那些具体又渴望的东西，但这不代表我就是在克扣他们，或者让他们注定绝望。我得坚持说，就算没法满足每个愿望，这工作仍然有意义，而且我的局限不等于完全没用。
</internal>

context.speaker: client
context.text: That may be what I do, but it's not what people want.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: And what do they want?

en_backup.therapist_turn: And what do they want?
en_backup.client_response: They want to be loved, even by me. They want a child, or they want to be my child. They want a parent who loves them. They want attention, they want affection. They want hope, they want pills, and they want sex. It's a good list. But I don't give them those things. My patient Mia, the lawyer, do you know what she wants? She wants me to hold her, to comfort her. But what she really needs is a good husband and a family. And I know that I cannot give her those things. All I can do is show her she pushes away the very people who could help her and that she pulls on the people who won't. But that only leaves her feeling more lonely and unloved. By the time she left on Monday, by the time she left my office, she felt doomed, rejected by her family and the world. And I had absolutely nothing to say to her.
en_backup.internal:
[Perception] I heard you reduce Mia and the rest of my patients to impossible wants and then conclude that because I cannot meet those wants, I am useless to them. That landed on the most painful part for me: the fear that my work is fundamentally disappointing, that I leave people feeling worse, and that I have nothing real to offer them. But that framing feels too absolute. It makes it sound as if the only things that matter are being loved, held, or rescuing them into the life I think they should have. That is not the whole story. It ignores that they come to me for something else too — to be understood, to be seen clearly, to have patterns named, to have someone stay with them in the hard truth. I cannot fix their family, marry them, or give them a life. But it is not accurate to say I give them nothing.

[Decision] I decided I needed to push back because if I accept that summary, I collapse my role into failure and stop seeing the actual help I do provide. I want to correct the picture: yes, I cannot give them those concrete, longing things, but that does not mean I am simply withholding or leaving them doomed. I need to insist that the work is still meaningful even when it does not satisfy every wish, and that my limits are not the same as total uselessness.

zh.client_response_zh: 你是觉得我觉得我在和他竞争？保罗，我怀孕是因为那个周末我滥交没用保护措施。也许那不是最聪明的事，但也许就是那样。
zh.internal_zh:
<internal>
[Perception] 他想把这件事变成关于贝内特的理论——关于竞争、嫉妒，也许还有某种无意识的争夺——我感觉他忽略了我真正说的，把我的怀孕变成了他可以解释的问题。这正好击中了我试图不暴露的部分：我可能想要什么，冲动行事，现在不得不承受后果。如果我让他继续深入，他就会太接近那个我自己都无法完全掌控的真相。

[Decision] 所以我打算就此打住。我会用最简单、最能自我保护的方式陈述事实：我发生了性行为，没有使用保护措施，现在怀孕了。也许那是鲁莽的，也许不聪明，但我不会让他把责任推给贝内特或什么幼稚的竞争。我需要把道德和情绪上的混乱控制住，因为一旦我打开那道门，我就无法控制这件事看起来的样子——以及我自己对这件事感到多么脆弱。
</internal>

context.speaker: client
context.text: At work, Bennett... who's leaving friday, finally... he had asked me to take over this big case, assuming that I would just crush the other side as usual. But I took one look at the poor family and I cut a deal. He was pissed.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: You're sure you're not trying to punish Bennett?

context.speaker: client
context.text: He's marrying stefanie. That'll be punishment enough. I feel bad for their kid, you know? I mean, he's a double adulterer and she's a bimbo. Why are we talking about Bennett?

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: Well, you brought him up. And he is somebody that you did want to have a child with.

context.speaker: client
context.text: It's... it's not his. I did the math.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: Still, it's interesting that you found out that Bennett was having a baby and a couple of weeks later you're pregnant.

context.speaker: client
context.text: Are you saying that I'm competing with Bennett?

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: That's what you think I think?

en_backup.therapist_turn: That's what you think I think?
en_backup.client_response: that's what you think I think? Paul, I'm having a baby because I went on a sex spree that weekend without using protection. Maybe that wasn't the smartest thing but maybe it was.
en_backup.internal:
[Perception] He’s trying to turn this into a theory about Bennett — about competition, jealousy, maybe some unconscious grab for him — and that feels like he’s ignoring what I’m actually saying and making my pregnancy into a problem he can interpret. It lands right on the part I’m trying not to expose: that I may have wanted something, acted impulsively, and now have to live with it. If I let him keep going there, he gets too close to the truth that I don’t fully control the story.

[Decision] So I’m shutting it down. I’m going to name the facts in the simplest, most self-protective way: I had sex, I didn’t use protection, and now I’m pregnant. Maybe it was reckless, maybe it wasn’t smart, but I’m not going to let him pin it on Bennett or some childish rivalry. I need to keep the moral and emotional mess contained, because if I start opening that door, I lose control of how this looks — and of how vulnerable I feel about it.

en_backup.internal:
[Perception] I heard the therapist saying, basically, “Tell me what brought you here despite not being ready,” and that made me look for the part of this that actually matters enough to move me. What it hit was the conflict between what I enjoy about smoking and what kind of example I want to set for my kids. I can see the problem clearly when I think about my daughter turning 12 and having friends who are already trying cigarettes. That makes me wonder if my smoking is quietly making it seem acceptable, even if I don’t intend that. The part that still feels unresolved is whether quitting really has to happen now, given everything else going on, or whether I’m just telling myself “not yet” because I don’t want to give up something that helps me cope.

[Decision] I decided to answer with the reason that feels strongest and most defensible: I’m worried about being a bad role model and about my daughter seeing smoking as normal. That seemed more honest than pretending I’m ready to quit, because I’m not. I wanted to show that I do have a reason to think about change, even if I’m still weighing it against the benefits I get from smoking. In my head, I’m trying to figure out whether protecting my kids should outweigh my own comfort, and right now that question is still open.

[Perception] 我听到治疗师建议我女朋友的外公保持距离，但这跟实际情况对不上。让我揪心的是，大家都很痛苦，可偏偏他还是撑着整个家的人。房子是他的，他一直接济她们，现在因为痴呆他糊涂了、大喊大叫。所以那个“离开他就行了”的答案太简单了，甚至有点不公平。我在想，怎么才能既保护我女朋友和她外婆，又不背弃那个曾经撑起她们、现在还控制着她们生活稳定的老人。

[Decision] 我决定温和地反驳一下，解释为什么离开没那么简单。我想表明这不只是一个糟糕的关系能一走了之——这跟他的病、他一直以来对她们的付出有关，而且房子和钱都跟他绑在一起。我在琢磨，有没有什么办法能减少悲伤和冲突，又不背叛他，或者把全家的处境搞得更糟。
</internal>

en_backup.internal:
[Perception] I heard the therapist suggest distance from my girlfriend’s grandfather, but that doesn’t really fit the reality of the situation. The part that hit me was the tension between how miserable everyone is and the fact that he’s still the one keeping the whole thing afloat. He owns the houses, he’s been the provider, and now he’s confused and yelling because of dementia. So the obvious “just get away from him” answer feels too simple, maybe even unfair. I’m trying to make sense of how we can protect my girlfriend and her grandmother without turning our backs on a man who used to carry them and still controls their stability.

[Decision] I decided to push back gently and explain why leaving isn’t straightforward. I wanted to show that this isn’t just a bad relationship dynamic we can walk away from—it’s tied to his illness, his history of supporting them, and the fact that housing and money are wrapped up in him. I’m trying to figure out whether there’s any way to reduce the sadness and conflict without betraying him or putting the family’s situation at risk.

en_backup.internal:
[Perception] What I heard was that you were turning my mom into the problem — like her love, her support, the way she raised me somehow caused this. That hit the most protective part of me. It sounded like you were ignoring how much she gave up for us, and especially for Daniel, and instead making her sound responsible for me not leaning on anyone. That feels unfair. If there’s a problem here, it’s not her being a bad mother — it’s this situation, and maybe the pressure on her, not her character.

[Decision] I decided I’m not going to go along with blaming her or picking apart everything she did. I’m going to shut this down because I’m not going to let her be made into the reason I’m struggling. If I’m not telling her everything, it’s because I don’t want to add more to her plate — not because she failed me. The burden is already on her enough, and I’m not going to make her the problem too.

en_backup.internal:
[Perception] I heard the therapist trying to talk about coping strategies, but what stuck with me was the practical, normal part of the conversation — clothes, dresses, things that can make me feel a little more put together. That feels safer than sitting with the bigger thing underneath, which is how awful I feel about my body and how much I want to look better. Their question about feeling bad about myself landed, but it also made me aware of how much I don’t want to get pulled into a big emotional discussion where I end up exposing how bad it really is.

[Decision] I decided to steer toward something familiar and manageable: asking what they do when they feel bad about themselves. I guess I wanted to keep it conversational and reciprocal instead of making it all about me and my insecurity. If I stay on practical, relatable ground, I don’t have to fully face the part where I feel ugly and unlovable. It feels easier to ask them than to get stuck in my own spiral.

zh.therapist_turn_zh: 即使你做完测试之后也没有？
zh.client_response_zh: 我觉得你说得对，保罗。我确实想把你拉进来。当然，你知道我……我很害怕。我担心自己一个人做这些事。但我听到了你说的话。我已经不是20年前的那个人了。这里有这个新生命。我能感觉到它。而这一次，我想要它。
zh.internal_zh:
<internal>
[Perception] 当保罗说出有孩子可能意味着连片刻属于自己的时间都没有时，把我从那个“孩子会填满空虚、解决孤独”的幻想里惊醒了。我一下子听明白了，我一直渴望的其实不是某种神奇的“不再孤单”，而是进入一种新的关系——一种会要求我、改变我、又不会让我继续背负那个老样子的孤独自我的关系。最触动我的是，我一直把这胎当作我不会被抛弃的证据，可实际上它意味着我在踏进一个真实、有要求、全新的处境。

[Decision] 我决定不再求他担保我永远不会孤单，因为那不是我需要的事实。我需要的是承认自己害怕，承认无法假装自己没变，也承认无论如何我都想朝这个新生活走去。我想放下那个“我只是个孤身一人又无能为力的人”的旧故事，对那个想要成为母亲、想要尝试的我说“是”，即使我害怕。
</internal>

context.speaker: therapist

context.speaker: client
context.text: This time? No one.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: Even after you took the test?

en_backup.therapist_turn: Even after you took the test?
en_backup.client_response: I think you're right, Paul. I do want to pull you in. Of course, you know I... I'm scared. I'm worried about doing it on my own. But I heard what you said. I'm not the same person I was 20 years ago. There's just this new life. I can feel it. And this time I want it.
en_backup.internal:
[Perception] When Paul said that having a child can mean never having a moment to yourself, it startled me out of the fantasy that a baby would simply fill the empty space and fix my loneliness. I heard, all at once, that what I’ve been longing for is not really to be “not alone” in some magical way, but to be in a new kind of relationship — one that will demand me, change me, and still not leave me the same lonely person I’ve been carrying around. What hit me most was that I’ve been treating this pregnancy like proof that I won’t be abandoned, when really it means I’m stepping into something real, demanding, and new. 

[Decision] I decided to stop asking him to reassure me that I’ll never be alone, because that isn’t the truth I need. What I need is to admit that I’m scared, that I can’t do this by pretending I’m unchanged, and that I do want to move toward this new life anyway. I want to let go of the old story that I’m just someone alone and incapable, and say yes to the part of me that wants to become a mother and try, even if I’m afraid.

judge.rationale: 工作焦虑情绪通用，无文化绑定，翻译后保持合作标签与情绪强度。

[Perception] 真的要说？我从你话里听出来的是：你在试图把这弄成一个模式。你把Max来看我、音乐会、早上叫我起床这些事，跟我妈的事并列在一起，像是案件证据似的。也许这就是你说的“熟悉”的意思，但让我在意的是，这里面暗示的不只是Max发生的事——而是我据称在重复的某个旧脚本。让我觉得没搞清楚的部分是：到底真的有关联，还是你为了套理论硬把它们扯在一起？我在琢磨，Max是不是就只是Max，我是不是因为宿醉状态不好而想多了，或者我身上真的有什么东西，老是让我陷入别人接管照顾而我直到后来才意识到的局面。

[Decision] 所以我决定不为了保持房间气氛平静就简单同意你。我想看看这个关联是不是真的，如果是真的，那我需要搞清楚到底在重复什么——而不是简单贴上“我妈”的标签就过去了。但我也并不想给你一个让我听起来被动或受损的故事，因为我不确定那是不是准确的。所以我说“真的要说？”是因为我想先探探虚实：我们是在谈论我关系模式中的真实模式，还是只是在用心理学的语言粉饰一个尴尬的早晨？
</internal>

I’m trying to work out if Max is simply being Max, if I was impaired from a hangover and read too much into it, or if there really is something about me that keeps landing in situations where someone else takes over care and I don’t notice until later.

[Decision] So I’m deciding not to just agree with you to keep the room calm. I want to see whether this connection is real, because if it is, then I need to understand what exactly is repeating — not just label it “my mother” and move on. But I also don’t want to hand you a story that makes me sound passive or damaged when I’m not convinced that’s accurate. context_zh.text: 我的考试是关于合同法的。我确实有一整晚，但我学了一整天，已经累坏了。

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 我有个主意，你有没有同课程的朋友或者认识熟悉这门课的人？如果有的话，也许你可以和他们沟通，让他们给你精简一下。

zh.therapist_turn_zh: 我有个主意，你有没有同课程的朋友或者认识熟悉这门课的人？如果有的话，也许你可以和他们沟通，让他们给你精简一下。
zh.client_response_zh: 哇，这其实是个好主意。我有个朋友去年修过这门课，但我担心如果找她帮忙，她会看不起我。
zh.internal_zh:
<internal>
[感知] 她在催我去找我朋友，但真正的问题感觉是我朋友可能的评判，而不是我愿不愿意试。如果她看不起我，那会让整件事更糟。我不是拒绝帮助——而是想保护自己，免得在别人眼里显得软弱或无能。

[决定] 所以我打算先忍着，把风险归咎于情况和朋友可能的反应。我不能显得绝望或低人一等，尤其这次考试已经压在我头上。如果求助可能让我看起来糟糕，那暂时不迈出那一步感觉更安全。
</internal>

context.speaker: client
context.text: Hi. I have a big exam coming up and I am very afraid of not doing well.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: Well I can help you study if you'd like?

context.speaker: client
context.text: How are you going to help me study? I am not sure if you are familiar with my course material...

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: What is your exam about? Plus you have a whole night to study!

context.speaker: client
context.text: My exam is about contract law. I have the whole night, but I have studied all day and am exhausted.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: I have an idea, do you have any friends in the same course or know anyone that is familiar with that subject? If so, maybe you can communicate with them and they can break it down in a short version.

en_backup.therapist_turn: I have an idea, do you have any friends in the same course or know anyone that is familiar with that subject? If so, maybe you can communicate with them and they can break it down in a short version.
en_backup.client_response: Wow, that's actually a really good idea. I have a friend who took the course last year but I am worried that if I ask her for help she will think poorly of me.
en_backup.internal:
[Perception] She’s pushing me toward asking my friend, but the real issue feels like my friend’s possible judgment, not my willingness to try. If she thinks poorly of me, that would make this whole thing worse. It’s not that I’m refusing help — it’s that I’m trying to protect myself from looking weak or incompetent in someone else’s eyes.

[Decision] So I’m going to hold back for now and blame the risk on the situation and on how my friend might react. I can’t afford to seem desperate or lesser, especially with this exam already hanging over me. If asking could make me look bad, then it feels safer to not take that step yet.

judge.rationale: 对话通用，无强文化绑定，翻译后能保持阻抗与情绪

context_zh.speaker: client
context_zh.text: 我该怎么应付学业上的压力？

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 你现在是在家学习吗？

context_zh.speaker: client
context_zh.text: 对，而且因为疫情出不了门，挺压抑的。

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 嗯，确实不容易。但这样也安全啊。

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 而且你也不用开车，离冰箱也近。

context_zh.speaker: client
context_zh.text: 是啊，我公寓里是有个冰箱吧？

context_zh.speaker: client
context_zh.text: 我确实会出去玩儿，这样能放松一下。

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 那倒是真的。

zh.therapist_turn_zh: 那倒是真的。
zh.client_response_zh: 如果整天都待在公寓里，我很难保持动力。
zh.internal_zh:
<internal>
[Perception] 感觉他们在把问题说得很小，好像被困在家里只是因为“安全”和离冰箱近就该不当回事。但我真正在意的是，学业压力已经很大，独自一整天待在公寓里更难保持动力和精力。我有时会出去，那确实有好处，但这不代表待在公寓里就没事。如果我认同他们的说法，就好像我应该对一件实际上在消耗我的事感到无所谓。

[Decision] 所以不，不是这样的。我总不能因为有那么几个便利之处，就假装整天待在家里完全没问题。这依然让我感到被困住、更没动力，我需要认真对待这一点，而不是说服自己忽略。
</internal>

context.speaker: client
context.text: How can I manage the stress of school?

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: Are you studying from home?

context.speaker: client
context.text: Yes, and it's depressing not being able to go out because of covid.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: well, it is tough. But it is safe, too.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: And you do not need to drive, you are close to the fridge, too.

context.speaker: client
context.text: Yes, I have a fridge in my apartment?

context.speaker: client
context.text: I do go out for fun, it can be relaxing.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: That's true.

en_backup.therapist_turn: That's true.
en_backup.client_response: I find it difficult to stay motivated if I'm in my apartment all day.
en_backup.internal:
[Perception] It felt like they were making the problem too small, like being stuck at home is just a practical inconvenience I should shrug off because it’s “safe” and close to the fridge. But what hits me is that I’m already under a lot of pressure from school, and being alone in my apartment all day makes it harder to keep my motivation and energy up. I do go out sometimes, and that helps, but that doesn’t mean the apartment setup is fine. If I agree with the way they framed it, it sounds like I’m supposed to be okay with something that’s actually wearing me down.

[Decision] So no, that’s not it. I’m not going to pretend that being home all day is basically fine just because there are a couple of conveniences. It still makes me feel stuck and less motivated, and I need to take that seriously instead of talking myself out of it.

judge.rationale: 对话内容关于学术压力和时间管理，普遍性高，无文化专属梗或语言双关，翻译后行为标签不变。

context_zh.speaker: client
context_zh.text: 这样好多了吗？不是所有事都围着你转，保罗。

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 我知道。事实上，你上次坐在我家厨房时，我记得你告诉我小时候在你爸爸店里和他一起喝咖啡的事。你说那是你们俩瞒着你妈妈的秘密。你在想什么，米娅？

context_zh.speaker: client
context_zh.text: 没什么。我觉得没什么。我爸周日确实过来吃了早午餐。

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 所以你们俩一起过了一天。是你邀请他的吗？什么时候？

zh.therapist_turn_zh: 所以你们俩一起过了一天。是你邀请他的吗？什么时候？
zh.client_response_zh: 那天早上。我妈高高兴兴地送他过来。她大概自己去她的美容院待了一整天，她喜欢坐在那儿跟朋友聊我是怎么毁了她模特生涯的。
zh.internal_zh:
<internal>
[Perception] 他老是绕回那些跟我爸之间的小事——咖啡、早午餐、那点秘密——好像那些比我一直想讲的那个大故事更重要。这戳到了我的点：我觉得没人看到我家真正的安排——我妈控制一切，我爸顺着来，我被挤出去，我姐妹却像自己人一样被对待。如果我说“没什么”，那他就可以又把话题引到我的感受上，但我希望他理解的是这个模式：我爸过来是因为本来就这样，而就算我妈表现得大方，她还是掌控着局面。

[Decision] 所以我直截了当地摆出来了。我提到了时间、我妈送他来、早午餐、美容院——所有细节——因为我想让他看到整个布局，而不是某个他用来把事软化的温馨回忆。我故意说了她怎么跟朋友聊我毁了她模特生涯的事，因为那是我不能让它消失的关键点。如果他能理解这个，也许他就终于能明白为什么我是那个站在外面的人。
</internal>

context.speaker: client
context.text: Is this better? It's not all about you, Paul.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: I know that. In fact, when you were sitting in my kitchen, I remembered you telling me about how you shared coffee with your dad at his store when you were a girl. You said that it was a secret that you both kept from your mother. What are you thinking, Mia?

context.speaker: client
context.text: Nothing. I don't think it's anything. My dad did come over for brunch on sunday.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: And so the two of you spent the day together. Did you invite him? When?

en_backup.therapist_turn: And so the two of you spent the day together. Did you invite him? When?
en_backup.client_response: That morning. My mom dropped him off, happily. She probably went off to spend the day at her beauty parlor where she likes to sit around and talk with her friends about how I ruined her modeling career.
en_backup.internal:
[Perception] He kept circling back to the small, ordinary thing with my dad — coffee, brunch, the secret of it — like that mattered more than the big story I’m always trying to tell. It hit the part where I feel like nobody sees the actual arrangement in my family: my mother running everything, my father going along with it, me getting pushed out while my sisters are treated like they belong. If I say “nothing,” then he can make it about my feelings again, but what I want him to understand is the pattern: my dad came over because that’s how it is, and my mother still controls the scene even when she looks generous.

[Decision] So I laid it out plainly. I named the timing, my mom dropping him off, the brunch, the beauty parlor — all of it — because I wanted him to see the whole setup, not just some sweet memory he can use to soften things. And I said the part about her talking about how I ruined her modeling career because that’s the point I can’t let disappear. If he understands that, then maybe he’ll finally understand why I’m the one on the outside.

judge.rationale: COVID-19是全球话题，中文可自然表达，无文化绑定或双关，适合翻译。

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 你好，有什么可以帮你的？

zh.internal_zh:
<internal>
[Perception] 治疗师简单的“有什么可以帮你的？”让我觉得足够开放，终于可以说出压在我心里最大的事：我真的害怕新冠病毒，害怕它对我爸爸的影响。这击中了我处境中觉得自己有责任保护他的那一部分，尤其是因为他年纪大了，晚上已经在用氧气。大声说出来让那种焦虑在我心里没那么堵了。

[Decision] 我决定承认焦虑，而不是试图把它包装成一个实际担忧。我让恐惧显露出来，因为我希望这会让我感觉不那么孤单、不那么慌乱，也许能帮我开始缓解，而不是一直试图管理别人的选择。
</internal>

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: Hello there how can I help?

en_backup.therapist_turn: Hello there how can I help?
en_backup.client_response: I'm feeling so worried about the COVID-19 crisis.
en_backup.internal:
[Perception] The therapist’s simple “how can I help?” felt open enough that I could finally say the biggest thing sitting on me: I’m really scared about COVID and what it could do to my dad. It hits the part of my situation where I feel responsible for protecting him, especially because he’s older and already uses oxygen at night. Saying it out loud made the worry feel a little less trapped inside me.

[Decision] I decided to admit the anxiety instead of trying to package it as just a practical concern. I’m letting the fear show because I’m hoping it will make me feel less alone and less frantic, and maybe help me start getting relief instead of just constantly trying to manage everyone else’s choices.

context_zh.text: 我知道，我知道跟家人、跟你的孩子完全坦诚地说话可能很难，因为你要冒着进行一场痛苦对话的风险。

zh.therapist_turn_zh: 我知道，我知道跟家人、跟你的孩子完全坦诚地说话可能很难，因为你要冒着进行一场痛苦对话的风险。
zh.client_response_zh: 这就是个策略，对吧……来告诉我你懂我的感受？
zh.internal_zh:
<internal>
[Perception] 他表现得好像他已经懂我和我儿子了，好像这就是个普通的家庭问题，稍微坦诚点就能解决。这就是让人不舒服的地方。他不了解我儿子，不知道他有多封闭，不知道我已经试过什么，却说得好像我在回避什么简单的真相，而实际上我在面对的是一个根本不回应的人。这感觉像是轻飘飘地打发我，我的处境被简化成了一个理论。

[Decision] 我得顶回去，因为如果我忍了，就好像我接受了他对我生活的解读。我想纠正他，让他明白这不只是抽象的“痛苦对话”。我想说，他知道得还不够，不能假设什么方法管用，而且我不会同意谈话就能神奇地解决问题——我早就知道那不行。
</internal>

context.speaker: client
context.text: ( Speaks bengali ) ( Sighs ) I said that you are wasting my time too.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: I know, I know it can be difficult to talk to family, your children, in a completely honest way because you risk a painful conversation.

en_backup.therapist_turn: I know, I know it can be difficult to talk to family, your children, in a completely honest way because you risk a painful conversation.
en_backup.client_response: This is just a strategy, yes... to tell me you know how I feel?
en_backup.internal:
[Perception] He’s acting like he already understands me and my son, like this is some general family issue where a little honesty is the answer. That’s what felt wrong. He doesn’t know my son, doesn’t know how he shuts down, doesn’t know what I’ve already tried, and he’s making it sound like I’m avoiding some simple truth when really I’m dealing with someone who doesn’t respond. It felt dismissive, like my situation was being flattened into a theory.

[Decision] I need to push back because if I let that stand, it sounds like he’s telling me to accept his version of my life. I want to correct him and make clear that this is not just about “painful conversations” in the abstract. I’m saying he doesn’t know enough to assume what works here, and I’m not going to agree that talking will magically help when I already believe it won’t.

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 你会考虑吃点药吗？

zh.therapist_turn_zh: 你会考虑吃点药吗？
zh.client_response_zh: 不太想……然后就是，我讨厌待在人群里，会让我很焦虑。

[Perception] 他们一直就是那些老一套的解决方式——呼吸、Calm应用、吃药——就像照着清单念一样，根本没真正听到这对我有多严重。人群里的感觉才是真正的问题，而他们好像忽略了这一点，或者没当回事。这让我觉得他们根本不懂这有多吓人，尤其是我在努力解释我不只是有点紧张，我是恐慌发作。

[Decision] 所以我打算避开他们的建议，说点别的对我来说更真实的东西。因为如果他们就只会给这些基本的东西，我不想假装这就够了。我需要他们理解全貌，而且说实话，我不信这些简单的答案能有多大用。
</internal>

context.speaker: therapist

en_backup.therapist_turn: It sounds like its been really tough for you and wish you had more support from your friends and even your child's father.
en_backup.client_response: Yes, thats right. But Im having trouble accepting the fact that I have to do this alone.
en_backup.internal:
[Perception] I hear that you’re making it sound like I just need more support from my friends and my child’s father, like that’s the main issue. But that doesn’t really fit how this feels. It’s not just about missing people or wanting company — it’s that I’ve had to give up so much of who I was, and now it sounds like I’m supposed to just accept that and move on. That hits the part of me that already feels like I’ve lost my youth and my life.

[Decision] I don’t want to agree with that framing, because if I do, it feels like I’m admitting this is just my new normal and I should be fine with it. I’m not fine with it. I’m hurting, and I hate that this is what my life looks like now. I need it to be understood that this is bigger than just wishing people checked on me more.

Saying “I feel hopeless” was me touching the edge of how bad it’s been, not just talking around it.

[Decision] I decided to say it because I’m tired of minimizing it, and because this is the first small moment that feels safe enough to be honest. I don’t want to get brushed off or taken over; I just want someone to hear how bad it feels. Saying it out loud is scary, but it also feels like maybe I don’t have to keep holding it alone for one more minute.

zh.internal_zh:

</internal>

context_zh.text: 嗨，说实话我现在有点挣扎。情绪特别低落的时候，我就不停地喝啤酒。

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 嗯，我理解——我觉得疫情期间很多人都是这样。你以前有过这种问题吗？

context_zh.speaker: client
context_zh.text: 没有，其实是在疫情真正爆发、一切停摆之后大概三到六个月才开始这样的。

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 确实很糟糕，对吧？你有没有至少跟你的医生聊过，哪怕不能当面看诊？

context_zh.speaker: client
context_zh.text: 有！太恐怖了！而且我有个治疗师，每两周见一次。不过也就只能帮那么多。

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 也许是时候寻求更多帮助了？你觉得严重到需要住院治疗吗？

context_zh.speaker: client
context_zh.text: 不，我还没到那个地步。就是一堆糟心事混在一起。我老婆和我现在分居，我还在读博士，离家很远，疫情让这一切更难了。我觉得更多是环境造成的。

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 听起来过去这十八个月你过得真的很艰难。随着封锁放松，有没有什么新的消遣活动可以参与，帮你分散注意力？

zh.therapist_turn_zh: 听起来过去这十八个月你过得真的很艰难。随着封锁放松，有没有什么新的消遣活动可以参与，帮你分散注意力？
zh.client_response_zh: 嗯，我开始多和朋友一起玩了，还建立了一些每周活动比如扑克之夜。那确实有帮助。和人多待肯定更容易熬过去。我在想，痛苦的时候喝酒到底有多不好。
zh.internal_zh:
<internal>
[Perception] 我感觉咨询师在把我往“更多帮助”上推，可能觉得这问题比我想承认的严重。这戳中了那部分我自己——我知道我一直在用啤酒快速摆脱孤独、压力，还有离家远、婚姻破裂这种奇怪的感觉。同时，也激起了我害怕被当成失控的恐惧，毕竟我博士功课还在做，还在跟朋友见面。我不想被小看，但也不想被逼着承认这已经失控了。
[Decision] 所以我打算暂时保持小心和含糊一点。我会承认它在我难受的时候管用，同时继续强调环境因素，因为那感觉是真的，也能让我不至于反应过度。我还没准备好说需要什么极端治疗，因为我想保护自己还正常、还理性的感觉。但我不能忽视我居然会问这个问题，这说明有一部分我在怀疑这个“熬过去就行”的做法是不是开始让我付出越来越不想面对的成本了。
</internal>

context.speaker: client
context.text: Hi, well to be honest I'm struggling a bit right now. I keep turning to beer when I'm feeling really down.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: Ah I hear you - I think that there is a lot of that going around during this pandemic. Did you ever have a problem before?

context.speaker: client
context.text: No, this all actually started about 3-6 months after the pandemic really hit and things shut down.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: It has been horrendous hasn't it? Have you been able to at least speak to your doctor, even if you could not see them in person?

context.speaker: client
context.text: Yes! So horrible! And yeah, I have a therapist I see once every two weeks. Although that only helps so much.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: It might be time to get some more help? Do you think it is bad enough that you might need inpatient treatment?

context.speaker: client
context.text: No, I'm not quite that bad off. It's sort of a mix of too many rough things. My wife and I are separating right now, I'm in the middle of a PhD program and living far from home, and covid really made it more challenging. I think it's a bit more circumstantial.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: It sounds like you have had a really hard time the last eighteen months. As the lockdown is easing, are there any new pastimes you could get involved in that might distract you?

en_backup.therapist_turn: It sounds like you have had a really hard time the last eighteen months. As the lockdown is easing, are there any new pastimes you could get involved in that might distract you?
en_backup.client_response: Well, I am starting to hang out with friends more and establish weekly traditions like poker night. So that's definitely helping. The more I can be around others the easier it is for sure. I'm wondering how bad it is to turn to alcohol when I'm in pain.
en_backup.internal:
[Perception] I hear the therapist pushing me toward “more help” and maybe acting like this could be a bigger problem than I want to admit. That lands on the part of me that already knows I’ve been using beer as a quick way to get through loneliness, stress, and the weirdness of being away from home while my marriage is falling apart. At the same time, it also hits my fear of being treated like I’m losing it when I’m still getting my PhD work done and still showing up for friends. I don’t want to be minimized, but I also don’t want to be cornered into saying this is out of control.

[Decision] So I’m going to stay careful and a little vague for now. I’ll admit it helps me when I’m hurting, and I’ll keep pointing to the circumstances because that feels true and keeps me from overreacting. I’m not ready to say I need drastic treatment, because I want to protect my sense that I’m still functional and rational. But I can’t ignore that I’m asking the question at all, which means part of me is wondering if this “just getting through it” thing is starting to cost me more than I want to face.

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 失去最好的朋友，我想象得到你有多难过。希望聊一聊能有点帮助。我以前失去亲人时，找人聊聊天确实能让心里好受些。

context_zh.speaker: client
context_zh.text: 嗯。我们特别要好，现在有时候觉得特别孤单。

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 能感觉到你很孤单。你发小的共同朋友里，有你可以联系的没？我猜他们也有同样的感受，你们聊聊、回忆回忆，对你俩可能都有好处。

zh.therapist_turn_zh: 能感觉到你很孤单。你发小的共同朋友里，有你可以联系的没？我猜他们也有同样的感受，你们聊聊、回忆回忆，对你俩可能都有好处。
zh.client_response_zh: 有共同的朋友。我偶尔也找他们聊。但那种感觉就是消不掉。搞得我整夜睡不着。一闭眼就好像他就在旁边，像我们以前聊天那样。
zh.internal_zh:
<internal>
[Perception] 他们把这说得好像很严重很紧急一样。对，我难过、睡不好，但这不代表我出了大问题，也不代表我崩溃了。这是悲伤——很难受，但失去那么好的朋友，这样也很正常。睡不着、一闭眼就想起他，确实很糟，但也不至于要把它当成什么危机来处理。

[Decision] 我得保持分寸，不用过度反应。我可以聊这件事，但没必要恐慌，也不用往最坏处想，就算它影响睡眠。我更想就一天一天熬过去，因为感觉这我能慢慢扛得住，不是什么大得无法处理的事。
</internal>

And that hits the sore spot: the part where I worry my return already looks like failure, or like I’m trying to rewrite history and make her responsible for it. I’m also hearing something else underneath her question: she thinks I’m maneuvering, testing, maybe trying to control the frame instead of just saying what I need. context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 什么？为什么？

context_zh.speaker: client
context_zh.text: 是啊，我不觉得……拖个几年毫无意义。当一个人决定不再爱他配偶的时候，就不该推迟离开家。难道不是这样吗？结束了，已经死了。我有朋友也得出了这个结论。他们做了三年夫妻治疗，最后还是分开了。那有什么用？我说省省那些废话吧。

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 你不觉得这有点极端吗？我是说，克服危机是可能的。

context_zh.speaker: client
context_zh.text: 你知道我意识到了什么吗？我从来没爱过她——Michaela。你知道这意味什么吗？这是多可怕的醒悟？你指望我怎么做？像我爸一样找个情人？开始晚回家？我连个好借口都没了。我除了坐着看电视什么也不会做。那又怎样？你看起来很不爽。

zh.therapist_turn_zh: 不，我只是……我有点担心。
zh.client_response_zh: 行吧，别担心。我现在轻松多了。
zh.internal_zh:
<internal>
[Perception] 他还在试图为一件我已经知道结束了的事情留门。当他说“担心”的时候，我听到的是更多的拖延、更多的希望、更多那种改变不了任何东西的无休止的谈话。这触动了我内心深处，我已经厌倦了假装这个家还有未来，厌倦了假装有一个版本的我突然会爱上Michaela或者想继续活在这个谎言里。

[Decision] 我决定不再抱希望了。希望只是把事拖得更久，变得更糟。如果我留下，我会继续等待一个不会来的感觉，最后陷入困境、痛苦、虚伪。离开更干脆。至少那样我可以停止强迫一件已经死了的东西继续动下去。
</internal>

context.speaker: client
context.text: Okay, all of this just reinforces my decision to leave home.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: What? Why?

context.speaker: client
context.text: Yeah, I don't think... It's pointless to drag this out for years. When a person decides he's not in love with his spouse he shouldn't have to put off leaving home. Isn't that so? It's over. it's dead. I've had friends who've reached this conclusion. They go to 3 years of couples therapy and they end up separating. So what's the use? I say cut that shit.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: Don't you think that's a little extreme? I mean, it is possible to overcome a crisis.

context.speaker: client
context.text: Do you know what I realized? That I was never in love with her. With Michaela. Do you know what that means? What a terrible realization that is? What do you expect me to do? Find a lover like my dad? Start coming home late at night? I don't even have a good excuse anymore. I won't do anything but sit on my ass and watch tv. So what? You look upset.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: No, i'm just... I'm just a little concerned.

en_backup.therapist_turn: No, i'm just... I'm just a little concerned.
en_backup.client_response: Well, don't be. I feel a great relief.
en_backup.internal:
[Perception] He’s still trying to hold the door open on something I already know is finished. When he says “concerned,” what I hear is more delay, more hope, more of that endless talking that changes nothing. It hits the part of me that’s tired of pretending there’s some future in this house, some version of me that’s going to suddenly become in love with Michaela or want to keep living this lie.

[Decision] I decided I’m done hoping. Hope just drags things out and makes it worse. If I stay, I’ll keep waiting for a feeling that isn’t coming, and I’ll end up stuck, miserable, and fake. Leaving feels cleaner. At least then I can stop forcing something dead to keep moving.

context_zh.speaker: therapist

context_zh.text: 你妈妈怎么样了？

context_zh.speaker: client
context_zh.text: 如果不介意我问的话。

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 你的朋友可能想要支持你，别为那个有压力。他们可能只需要一些指导，知道怎么支持你。

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 我妈妈很好！还在治疗，但恢复得很好。

context_zh.speaker: client
context_zh.text: 哦，谢天谢地。真为你们俩高兴。

zh.therapist_turn_zh: 我妈妈很好！还在治疗，但恢复得很好。
zh.client_response_zh: 这真是个奇怪的年份。六个月内我的两只狗都死于癌症，然后是这个事。然后七月我表姐死于胰腺癌。还有其他一些熟人。
zh.internal_zh:
<internal>
[Perception] 我听到她说我的朋友们可能真的想支持我，他们可能只是需要指导，我知道她想帮我不要感到内疚。但我真正纠结的是今年已经经历了多少失去——我的狗，我的表姐，我周围的癌症，现在又是他的手术。那才是巨大而可怕的。关于如何依靠朋友的实际问题，相比我害怕、疲惫、一切不断累积的事实，感觉微不足道。

[Decision] 我打算抓住更宏观的画面，因为如果我现在让她聚焦在朋友上，我就得离开我实际上有多不堪重负。我不想让这一切听起来像是我在为他不够坚强，但我也需要说出一直压迫我的事：这一年太残酷了，我不知道自己还能承受多少。我在努力撑住，所以我在谈论这些失去，而不是她给我的安慰。
</internal>

context.speaker: client

en_backup.therapist_turn: My mom is doing great! Still in treatment but doing so well.
en_backup.client_response: It's just a strange year. I lost both my dogs to cancer in six months, then this. Then my cousin died of pancreatic in July. Plus some other acquaintances.
en_backup.internal:
[Perception] I heard her saying my friends probably do want to be there for me and that they may just need guidance, and I know she’s trying to help me not feel guilty. But what I’m really stuck on is how much loss this year has already had in it — my dogs, my cousin, all the cancer around me — and now this surgery with him. That’s what feels huge and frightening. The practical question of how to lean on friends feels smaller than the fact that I’m scared and tired and it all keeps piling up.

[Decision] I’m going to stay with the bigger picture because if I let her focus on friends right now, I have to step away from how overwhelmed I actually am. I don’t want to make this about me in a way that sounds like I’m not being strong for him, but I also need to say the thing that keeps pressing on me: this year has been brutal, and I don’t know how much more I can take. I’m trying to keep it together, so I’m talking about the losses instead of the reassurance she’s offering.

en_backup.therapist_turn: A good dad who shipped a 10-year-old girl off to New Jersey rather than pay for a babysitter? There had to be a way to keep you at home. I mean, families find a way of working things out.
en_backup.client_response: Well, she's probably lying about all that too.
en_backup.internal:
[Perception] She’s doing it again — taking my father, the one person who was actually there for me, and turning him into the villain. She’s not listening to what I know happened; she’s trying to rewrite my childhood like my memories can just be overwritten because she wants a story where everyone’s equally guilty. What hit me is that if I let her keep pushing, then I’m the one left with no one decent, no anchor, and I’m expected to accept that my mother’s version is the truth.

[Decision] So I pushed back the only way I could: I made it about her lying, because I’m not going to sit here and let her strip my father of being a good dad. If there was a problem, it was her dishonesty, her exaggeration, her refusal to tell the truth — not him. I’m protecting what I know is real, because I can’t afford to let her make me responsible for tearing down the person who actually showed up for me.

zh.client_response_zh: 我不确定。反正，死亡是家族遗传的。这是家族病。你妈要是死于这个，你自己也得当心。你得病的几率比其他人高五倍。
zh.internal_zh:
<internal>
[Perception] 治疗师问我姐姐还有多久，然后又问她有没有人可以倾诉。我听见了关心，但落在我心里的是我已经知道的部分：这病就是夺走我妈的那种病，现在它又回到我姐姐身上，第四期，像一个我打断不了的模式。那句“她应该找个人聊聊”让这事情显得更大了，好像人们应该得到各种各样妥当的支持，但所有这些都改变不了这个事实：病就在这儿，它该怎么样还怎么样。它击中了我内心早就相信这病是家族遗传、没人能逃掉的那个地方。

[Decision] 所以我决定转向那个数字，那个冷酷的家族规律，因为这比抱有希望更安全。如果我盯住数字，那我就不用去面对那个想要相信我姐姐也许还能好起来的部分，因为那种希望只会让摔下来更惨。我说“死亡是家族遗传的”，是我在后退，不去期待任何不同。如果我不让自己抱有希望，那我就不用眼睁睁看着希望被夺走。
</internal>

context.text: My sister is sick. She has our mother's disease. Mm.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: What's her prognosis?

context.speaker: client
context.text: Stage IV.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: I see. How long?

context.speaker: client
context.text: I'm not sure. I wanted to tell you when I called you And then later when I got here, but I couldn't.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: I understand. It's very hard

context.speaker: client
context.text: To say that kind of thing.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: Does she have somebody to talk to? I mean, is she seeing a therapist? Yes. I'm just concerned. She should be... she should be talking to somebody.

en_backup.therapist_turn: Does she have somebody to talk to? I mean, is she seeing a therapist? Yes. I'm just concerned. She should be... she should be talking to somebody.
en_backup.client_response: I'm not sure. Well, death runs in the family. It's a family disease. If your mother dies of it, watch out. You're five times more likely to get it yourself.
en_backup.internal:
[Perception] The therapist asked how long my sister might have, and then whether she has someone to talk to. I heard concern, but what landed in me was the part I already know: this is the same disease that took our mother, and now it’s back in my sister, stage IV, like a pattern I can’t interrupt. The “she should be talking to somebody” part just made it feel bigger, like there’s all this proper support people are supposed to get, but none of it changes the fact that the disease is here and it does what it does. It hit the place in me that already believes this runs the family and nobody gets to opt out.

[Decision] So I decided to go to the statistic, to the grim family rule, because that feels safer than hoping. If I stay with the numbers, then I don’t have to sit in the part that wants to believe my sister might somehow be okay, because that hope would just make the fall worse. Saying “death runs in the family” is my way of backing away from wanting anything different. If I don’t let myself hope, then I don’t have to watch hope get taken away.

I took it as: maybe these ships aren’t only decoration, maybe they’re doing something else — or maybe I’m the one treating this like it’s supposed to be simple when it isn’t. It hit the part of me that wants to keep things light and sideways, because if we stay on the surface I don’t have to say what actually bothers me.

[Decision] I decided to press it rather than let it drift. If I ask “What do you mean?” then I can force the other idea into the open and see whether there’s a real point behind the comment or just banter. I want to know if she’s talking about me avoiding the obvious, or if she thinks there’s another meaning to all this ship stuff. Either way, I’m trying to find out what game we’re actually playing before I commit to it.

zh.internal_zh:

[Decision] 我刚开始回答，又停住了，因为再说下去我就得承认自己有多孤独，也许我试图在苏尼尔身上修复的东西，正是因为我无法忍受自己面对它。说“如果……我如-如果……”更安全。这让我刚好保持在触及不到的地方。如果我说太多，我会显得软弱、需要帮助，或者好像我其实不知道怎么帮他。而我承担不起这个——不能在这里，不能在他面前，也不能在我自己面前。
</internal>

If I say I’m scared of the living room, or scared of anything at all, then I have to admit how much this has taken out of me. And if I admit that, then hope becomes a thing I’m responsible for again.

[Decision] So I shut it down. I gave the safest answer: not suicidal, don’t worry. That’s easier. It keeps the whole mess small enough to survive. If I don’t call it hopeless, I don’t have to test whether there’s actually anything to do about it. Staying in bed protected me from trying, and trying would mean risking the same empty feeling all over again — the one where you reach and nothing changes. Better to keep it contained, keep it private, and pretend getting through it is the same as being okay.

[Perception] When she said, “you might have saved him,” I felt the whole story click into place in a different way. I’d been treating my guilt like proof — proof that I caused this, proof that if I had loved differently or not at all, Alex would still be alive. But her words made me see that I was collapsing a lot of painful wishes and “what ifs” into certainty. I was holding myself responsible for everything because that felt more faithful than admitting I might not have had that kind of power.

[Decision] I’m not letting go of the guilt yet, but I can at least admit it isn’t the same thing as truth. I need to answer honestly instead of hiding behind all the noise around Laura and jealousy. If I say “yeah, I guess so,” I’m admitting that part of me believes I should have saved him — and that maybe I’ve been punishing myself as if wanting to be responsible is the same as actually being responsible.

[Decision] I decided to lay out the history plainly because I’m trying to decide whether trust can ever come back after this. If the therapist understands how it started, maybe it’ll be clearer why I feel so stuck — because I’m not just upset about one lie, I’m questioning the whole foundation of the relationship and whether I can believe anything he says now.

context_zh.speaker: client
context_zh.text: 我觉得我没法像他讲得那么好。但我试试。五十年代中期吧，对吧？俄克拉荷马州，吉姆·克劳时代。我爸因为在一个工厂组织黑人劳工，惹恼了当地那些白人佬。他们威胁他，但我爸没退缩。他是个硬骨头，这点我承认。总之，事情越闹越大。然后……一群戴头罩的暴徒袭击了他家。我罗尼叔叔拿着步枪站在前廊上。他们开枪打死了他。还打了我珍妮阿姨。然后他们进了屋。我爸带着家里其他人，跑到楼下锅炉房，躲进地下室。就在锅炉旁边，他们挤进一个隐蔽的小房间。我爷爷，也就是我爸的父亲，病得很重，肺癌晚期。他那时候……显然他那时候……喘气很重，还不停地咳。所以我爸用手捂住爷爷的嘴和鼻子，一直捂着，不松手，那些人在地下室搜查的时候，他就那样紧紧捂着。等他们终于走了，我爷爷已经死了。他是被捂死的。就是这样。

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 这……这真是个可怕的故事。

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 有可能他说这话……是因为觉得内疚很危险，是一种软弱。也许你从小到大就一直听着这种话。

context_zh.speaker: client

context_zh.speaker: therapist

<internal>
[Perception] 他这是想把我的父亲说成是个软弱的人，好像那些关于内疚的话是什么恐惧、羞耻或者他继承下来的什么信息。也许确实是，但听他这么一说，就好像我爸是在害怕、做错了、或者背负着不该有的东西。这触动了我这么多年来一直保持完整的那个部分：他活下来了。他做了他不得不做的事。如果我现在开始叫它内疚，那我就等于在评判他，也许还会评判我从小到大听着的那整个故事。

context.speaker: client
context.text: I don't think I can tell it as well as he does. But i'll try. Mid-'50s, right? Jim Crow Oklahoma. My old man had pissed off the local good ol'boys by trying to organize some black labor at this factory. They tried to threaten him but my dad didn't back down. He's a tough son of a bitch, i'll give him that. Anyway, the whole thing, it just escalated. And... this mob with hoods attacked his house. My uncle Ronnie was on the front porch with a rifle. They shot him down. Shot my aunt Jeannie too. And then they came inside. My father takes the rest of the family, they run downstairs to the boiler room, to the basement. Right near the boiler, they all crammed into this area, this hidden room. My grandfather, his father, was very sick. Dying of lung cancer. And he had this... Apparently he had this... This wheezing and this hacking cough. So my father puts his hand over his father's mouth and nose and he kept it there while they searched the basement, kept it clamped tight. Then when they finally cleared out, my grandfather was dead. He'd suffocated. There it is.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: That's... That's a horrific story.

context.speaker: client
context.text: Tells it every year on my grandfather's birthday. It's a tradition.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: And you really believe he doesn't feel guilty about it?

context.speaker: client
context.text: I'm telling you, he always used to say, leave the guilt for the white man. We can't afford it.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: It's possible that he's saying that... it's dangerous to feel guilty, that it's a kind of weakness. Maybe that's a message that... you've grown up with.

context.speaker: client
context.text: What can I say? That's just my father's way.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: But is it your way?

en_backup.therapist_turn: But is it your way?
en_backup.client_response: I don't know. Hey, it works for him.
en_backup.internal:
[Perception] He’s trying to turn my father into somebody with a weakness in him, like all that talk about guilt is some fear or shame or message he picked up. Maybe it is, but hearing it that way makes it sound like my old man was afraid, or wrong, or carrying something he shouldn’t. That hits the part I’ve kept intact all these years: he survived. He did what he had to do. If I start calling it guilt, then I’m stepping toward judging him, and maybe toward judging the whole story I grew up with.

[Decision] No. I’m not taking that frame. “Dangerous” and “weak” aren’t my father’s words, and I’m not going to make him into somebody who couldn’t bear his own life. That would feel like betraying him. So I shut it down: that’s just his way. It works for him. I don’t know if it’s mine, but I’m not letting you turn it into some problem he’s hiding under.

en_backup.internal:
[Perception] He’s pushing past the surface again. “I’ll be there for you” sounds nice, but it also lands on the part where I’d have to admit I want someone to step in, stay, and mean it. That hits the humiliating part: that I’m scared, that I don’t know what to do, and that I actually want support more than I want to act like I’ve got this handled. If I let myself say what it means, I’d have to talk about what I need from him, and then maybe feel disappointed if it isn’t there. 

[Decision] So I kept it small and practical: “I have major decisions to make.” That lets me stay in control and keeps the conversation on logistics instead of need. It’s safer to sound like I’m thinking than to admit I’m hoping. If I go deeper, I might sound needy, or find out I’m alone in this, and I can’t afford that right now.

He’s not asking me to explain the suicide or defend why I’ve moved on. He’s naming that something in me remained with her. That lands uncomfortably close to grief, and maybe guilt too — not just memory, but weight. The kind I’ve been carrying without wanting to admit it.

[Decision] I’m startled, because I’ve been telling myself this is old history, finished history. But hearing him say it that way makes me pause instead of deflect. I decide not to dismiss him immediately. I let myself sit with the question — yes, maybe there is pain still here, and maybe that’s why I’m talking about it now. If I answer honestly, I have to admit that moving on was not the same as leaving it behind.

en_backup.internal:
[Perception] It felt like they were brushing past what I actually said. I told them I get angry easily and it’s ruining my relationships, and they answered with “is there anyone you can talk to,” which sounded like they weren’t really listening or didn’t know what to do. It hit the part of me that feels alone already — like if I don’t have people, then I don’t even have a real place to start.

[Decision] So I pulled back and answered that I don’t seem to have anyone. In my head it was, “Great, so now what?” I felt irritated because it seemed useless to keep opening up if they were just going to ask me to find someone I already said I don’t have. It made me want to stop trusting the conversation and handle it myself, even though I’m asking for help because I don’t know how to fix this on my own.

[Perception] They were doing that generic “make a list, stay positive, have a win” thing like my situation is just normal low-motivation stuff. It kind of hit the part where I’m stuck because I already know I should do something, but hearing it like that makes it feel like they’re not really getting why I’m shut down in the first place. The way they skipped over the fight and went straight to productivity advice felt a little empty, like they were treating me like a lazy routine problem instead of someone who’s been avoiding my family for years.

[Decision] So I just gave the safe answer and kept it vague. If I act too serious about their advice, I’m basically letting them lead me somewhere I don’t even trust. It’s easier to stay a bit dismissive and keep the conversation on harmless stuff than pretend this is some simple “try harder” thing. That way I don’t have to explain the real reason I’m like this, and they don’t get to sound like they’ve got it figured out.

en_backup.internal:
[Perception] You heard me turn this into something soft and simple—like what I need is just to be held and soothed until I go under. And that landed right on the part of me that wants it and hates that it wants it. Because if I let that be true, then I’m not just the one who leaves first, the one in control, the one who can say “I’m difficult” before anybody else says it. Then I’m exposed. Then I’m asking to be cared for, and that means I could be denied, pitied, or seen as needy. It also means I’d have to admit there’s a real longing here, not just a problem to manage.

[Decision] So no. I’m not going there. I drew the line at being comforted like that, at being held in a way that makes me dependent or visible. I’d rather say “that would never happen” than let myself want something that tender and risk how much I’d need it. If I let that in, I lose the version of me that stays ahead of the hurt by pushing away first.

</internal>

context_zh.text: 米凯拉是谁？

context_zh.text: 我老婆。

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 她对这一切怎么看？

zh.therapist_turn_zh: 她对这一切怎么看？
zh.client_response_zh: 关她什么事？
zh.internal_zh:
<internal>
[Perception] 她现在想把我扯进米凯拉的事里。把这事变成关于我的婚姻、我的感受、她怎么想——整个那套情感角度。根本不是这回事。我要求回到那个地方是因为我感兴趣，因为这对我自己来说很重要。把米凯拉扯进来感觉她是在试探我的弱点，找故事里的裂缝，好像如果她让我谈起我老婆，她就能开始告诉我我真正的感受，或者我应该对什么感到羞耻。我不会给她这个机会。我不会让这变成对我私生活的盘问，或者把我变成需要一个管束的内疚丈夫。

[Decision] 打住。把话题留在我想谈的地方：这趟行程，事实，实际考虑。如果她想谈米凯拉，省省吧。那部分我不谈。我不会交出我的婚姻、我的事、或者我决定什么重要的权利。没有理由让她参与进来，我不会因为她想找点东西来琢磨就让她把它扯进来。
</internal>

context.speaker: client
context.text: This is where my daughter has chosen to live... some hellhole near Goma.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: And that didn't go down well?

context.speaker: client
context.text: No. At first she was... distant. Dad, I can't leave right now. I have to finish a procedure. As if she'd got some medical degree in the last month. They looked like outhouses and she was sleeping there.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: I can see how upsetting that... that might have been for you. I mean, you spent your life... providing a good home for her and... this is how she chooses to live. So what happened at the dinner?

en_backup.therapist_turn: I can see how upsetting that... that might have been for you. I mean, you spent your life... providing a good home for her and... this is how she chooses to live. So what happened at the dinner?
en_backup.client_response: Well, I didn't wait for dinner.
en_backup.internal:
[Perception] She was starting to turn it into my failure, as if this were about me “providing a good home” and me having to sit there and take in the sight of my daughter living in a shack like that. It hit the place I cannot stand: the idea that I should accept this as some kind of normal, or sit politely through dinner while she tells me she’s staying in that hellhole and I pretend that’s reasonable. That would mean admitting she knows better than I do, and I’m not doing that.

[Decision] I decided I wasn’t going to wait around and play along. I wasn’t going to sit there, be softened by the setting, and let her draw me into accepting her choice. If she wanted to stay there and call it a procedure or whatever, that was on her — but I would not endorse it by staying for dinner, nodding, and acting like this was just another difference of opinion. I drew the line there: I came to get her home, and if she wouldn’t come, then I was done with the performance.

If I let myself want sleep, or believe anything might change, then I have something to lose when it doesn’t. So I’ll stay flat, keep it as a joke, keep it at a distance. Giving up on expecting anything is the only way not to keep getting disappointed.

Then the “pandemic” comment made it feel like they were throwing in a random line instead of actually listening to what I said. It hit the part where I feel like nobody really understands how impossible my life is right now unless they’re living it.

[Decision] So I backed off and got sharp because I didn’t feel taken seriously. If they’re going to respond like that, I’d rather just keep it short and not hand over more of myself. I already feel stretched so thin, and I don’t want to spend my energy explaining everything to someone who seems like they’re just making polite comments. Saying I wish I could get a break was my way of showing the real issue without pretending the small talk is helping.

context.text: About 2 weeks ago

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: Well i'm really glad to hear that you are reaching out and communicating about it now!

context.speaker: client
context.text: I am alone and on the road so it makes it hard

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: That makes sense. There is a lot of research that look at isolation and mood. Isolation makes things a lot harder.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: While you are on the road, is there anyone in your support system that you may be able to call?

context.speaker: client
context.text: No. I am with my dog. We have been homeless of and on.

context.speaker: client
context.text: My dog is my best friend and support

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: You're doing your best for you and your dog! That is great.

en_backup.therapist_turn: You're doing your best for you and your dog! That is great.
en_backup.client_response: Yes but it i hard on us both having to move around
en_backup.internal:
[Perception] He seemed to really hear that I’m not just “on the road,” I’m alone in it. When he said isolation makes things harder, that landed because it’s true, and it hit the part of me that knows this is weighing on both me and Garbo. I felt the ache of having no one else, and the fact that my dog is carrying so much of my support. What made it possible to say now is that he wasn’t pushing me to explain everything right away — he was steady, and for a second it felt safe enough to admit that this is hard on both of us.

[Decision] I decided to say the part I usually keep tucked away: that it’s hard on us both. I’m letting myself name the strain instead of only talking around it, because I want him to understand this isn’t just logistics — it hurts. I’m still holding onto Garbo and our life together, but I can admit that being alone like this is wearing me down.

context_zh.speaker: therapist

zh.therapist_turn_zh: 不！我要你去化疗！
zh.client_response_zh: 你知道化疗是什么吗？！那是毒药，直接打进你心脏的毒药！他们把这大泵直接接到你心脏上。你知道为什么吗？因为要是只给你打一针，有些药渗到皮底下，就会把你那该死的肉都融掉！
zh.internal_zh:
<internal>
[Perception] 他听到“去做化疗”，我听到的是“去让他们毒死你，去让他们撕碎你的身体，去受苦然后管那叫治疗”。这句话击中了我心里早已知道的部分——这件事没有什么干净的版本，没有勇敢的版本，没有一条路能绕开疾病、虚弱、屈辱和痛苦。他所做的只是在那件我无法想象的事情上更用力地推，好像我的恐惧只是有待辩驳的东西。

[Decision] 所以我不再试图让这听起来充满希望。假装可以被说服去想要这个，没意义。如果这就是未来，那我就直说吧：我做不到，我不会做，你说的任何话都不会让毒药显得像一种选择。放弃争辩，保护我不必再去指望希望，然后眼睁睁看着它再次被碾碎。
</internal>

context.speaker: client
context.text: I will get sicker and sicker. I'm gonna keep passing out on your couch. I'll probably vomit on your couch. And then eventually I'm gonna die on your couch. Is that really what you want?

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: No! I want you to go to chemotherapy!

en_backup.therapist_turn: No! I want you to go to chemotherapy!
en_backup.client_response: Do you even know what chemo is?! It is poison that they administer directly to your heart! They put this big pump right to your heart. And do you know why? Because if they just gave you a shot and some of it got under your skin, it would melt your fucking flesh!
en_backup.internal:
[Perception] He heard “go to chemo” and I heard, “go let them poison you, go let them rip your body apart, go suffer and call it treatment.” It hit the part of me that already knows there is no clean version of this, no brave version, no way through that doesn’t mean sickness, weakness, humiliation, and pain. All he did was push harder at the one thing I cannot bear to imagine, like my fear is just something to be argued with.

[Decision] So I’m done trying to make this sound hopeful. There is no point in pretending I can be talked into wanting this. If this is what the future is, then I’ll just say it plainly: I can’t do it, I won’t do it, and nothing you say is going to make poison feel like a choice. Giving up on arguing protects me from having to reach for hope and watch it get crushed again.

I’m basically handing over the problem and saying: give me the medication, tell me the plan, and help me get to smoke-free in a way I can actually manage. I put it into words instead of hinting because I need real guidance, not guesses, and I don’t trust myself to fill in the gaps properly.

[Decision] So I kept it short and called him “coach,” like I was playing along instead of actually accepting it. That’s safer. If I say more, I might have to agree, and agreeing means losing the shield of sarcasm and uniqueness. I don’t want to hand over control, and I don’t want to hear myself admit he might be right. en_backup.internal:
[Perception] He keeps it plain, almost clinical: “two years ago,” “an affair,” “with one of his students.” It lands on the part of me that wants this to be simple, one clean explanation, because then I can keep standing on the high ground. I was faithful. I resisted. I did what I was supposed to do, even when I was away a lot. And yet here I am, two years later, still feeling like the whole thing was torn apart by something cheap and obvious. What I’m circling around is this: if I was the one who did everything “right,” then why does it still feel like I lost something I don’t know how to replace? And why am I suddenly thinking of telling him something I’ve never said out loud?

[Decision] I decided to say there’s something I haven’t told anyone because I want to test whether there’s more to this than just his betrayal and my outrage. If I say it out loud, maybe I can figure out whether I’m talking about the marriage, or the loneliness after it, or the fact that I’ve been acting as if I don’t need anything anymore. I’m still protecting myself by sounding sarcastic and in control, but underneath that I’m wondering if there’s a reason I’m bringing this up now — whether I’m looking for a way to explain why I’ve stayed shut down for so long, and whether I can admit that without giving up my dignity.

[Perception] I heard the therapist saying they understand, and that they’ve had to make a similar choice themselves. That landed on the part of me that is torn between caring about my friend and not wanting to keep being pulled into her boyfriend’s behavior. What still feels unresolved is whether stepping back makes me a bad friend, or whether it’s actually the clearest way to protect myself from being used, lied to, or dragged into more chaos. I’m also noticing the gap between who I thought my friend was and what her life looks like now. That’s what I’m trying to make sense of: how someone I’ve known for so long could end up in this situation, and whether I’m supposed to keep showing up anyway.

[Decision] I decided I need to keep the boundary, even if I hate it. I’m not deciding to stop caring about her; I’m deciding that caring doesn’t have to mean staying close while money, trust, and safety are being damaged. I want to stay open to the idea that she may one day get away from him, but I can’t base my actions on hope alone. Right now the more responsible choice seems to be stepping back and letting the reality of her choices be hers to live with, because I can’t fix this for her and I can’t afford to keep absorbing the consequences.

In my head, I was thinking: that may help some people, but it doesn’t touch what I’m feeling today, and I need them to understand that before suggesting another tool.

[Perception] He’s doing it again — turning my pain into a story about my family, about my father, about my mother, like I’m just a repeat of them. If I stay in this conversation, I’m going to be told that my bed, my shutting down, my anger, all of it means something ugly about me and my family. That feels intolerable.

[Decision] No. I’m not going deeper into this with him. I’m drawing the line here because I do not want my grief explained away as family pathology, and I do not want to be made to sit there and pick myself apart just to prove I’m healing. If therapy means feeling worse, feeling exposed, and losing the one thing I have left — my toughness, my distance, my ability to function — then I’m done. I can get through the day on my own. I have to.

[Decision] I’m not going to sit here and pretend this is just some simple matter of me accepting responsibility and moving on. She didn’t sign up for a husband like this. Connie is the one paying for all of it, and that’s the truth I need to keep in front of me. If there’s a problem here, it’s this situation — me like this — not some failure on my part to understand it better.

context_zh.text: 我的意思是，我做的都是体力活，通常一天大部分时间都在大太阳底下干活，所以身体里的那些不好的东西，基本上都随着汗排出来了，所以——

context_zh.text: 好的。你注意到自己体重有增加，或者有什么别的吗？

context_zh.speaker: client
context_zh.text: 嗯，有一点点，但也没什么大不了的，你知道。我没有肿，没有水肿什么的。

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 好的，好的。那去看医生呢？你最近有没有去看过医生，或者做过什么检查？

context_zh.speaker: client
context_zh.text: 嗯，有啊，我去年差不多去体检过，但——我的意思是，检查结果都正常，所以——

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 好的。那你觉得自己身体感觉还好吗？

context_zh.speaker: client
context_zh.text: 嗯。

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 好的，嗯，那……我听到的是，你觉得你老婆可能有点反应过度了，对吧？

zh.therapist_turn_zh: 好的，嗯，那……我听到的是，你觉得你老婆可能有点反应过度了，对吧？
zh.client_response_zh: 嗯，我倒不觉得她是反应过度。我知道她爱我，也知道她是想让我活得久一点，身体健康，但有时候，特别是干这么累的活，去那种地方吃顿饭吧，多少能让自己心里好受点。

<internal>
[Perception] 她说得好像这事儿有多严重似的，但我真没觉得有什么大问题。对，我是胖了一点，可我每天在大太阳底下干体力活，刚体检过，医生也说没事。我老婆是担心，但她听起来把这事儿说得太夸张了。她说的那部分好像在试图把我正常的干活、吃饭习惯说成什么大毛病，这跟我每天的感觉完全对不上。

</internal>

My wife worries, but it sounds like she’s making it into more than it is. What she’s saying hits the part where she’s trying to turn normal work-and-eat-out habits into something serious, and that doesn’t really match how I feel day to day.

[Decision] I’m going to keep taking this pretty lightly. I don’t need to treat it like I’m in bad shape when I feel okay and the doctor didn’t say anything was wrong. I can hear her out and nod along, but I don’t need to buy into the idea that I’ve got some big health issue just because I like grabbing food after a long shift.
