context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 怎么个最好法？

context_zh.speaker: client
context_zh.text: 根本不是最好。这就是一场噩梦。

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 是挺痛苦的。但从某种角度说，你也自由了……可以去好好处理……你和 Laura 之间的事。

zh.internal_zh:

[Perception] 他这是想把它包装成什么“自由”叙事，好像我老婆离开是什么让我成长、让我搞清楚自己的机会。这正好戳中我最受不了的地方——我得接受这破事，好像这是什么健康的进展，或者我竟然还能从老婆跟别人跑了这事里捞到好处似的。他听起来像是要我忽视家里四分五裂的事实，把这当作进步。这感觉像侮辱，他把这件事对我的意义——背叛、羞辱、孩子跟着遭殃——给抹平了。

[Decision] 不。我不会假装这事对我有好处，也不会把它粉饰成解放。我绝不会顺着他说我现在“自由”了，因为那就等于承认婚姻结束了，让她的选择来定义整个故事。我不接受那套说法。我就坚持真相：我要的是我老婆，我的家，不是这个。我不会帮他把她的离开重新包装成什么礼物。

[Perception] He’s trying to turn this into some “freedom” narrative, like my wife leaving is an opportunity for me to grow or figure myself out. That hits the one thing I can’t stomach: the idea that I’m supposed to accept this as if it’s some healthy development, or that I somehow benefit from my wife running off with another man. It sounds like he’s asking me to step over the fact that my family is falling apart and treat it like progress. That feels insulting, like he’s flattening what this is for me — betrayal, humiliation, and my kids getting dragged through it.

[Decision] No. I’m not going to pretend this is good for me, and I’m not going to dress it up as liberation. I won’t go along with the idea that I should be “free” now, because that means conceding the marriage is over and letting her choices define the story. I’m not accepting that line. I’m staying with the truth: I wanted my wife, my family, not this. And I’m not going to help him reframe her leaving as some gift.

context_zh.speaker: client
context_zh.text: 周五我做了一台手术，是个15岁的女孩，她脸上长了个肿瘤。没什么，良性的，就是美容性质。一切都很顺利，对吧？麻醉也没问题。结果我的主治医生被叫去会诊另一个手术，手术结束得比平时快。很简单。就剩我一个人，她还麻醉着。我从来没遇到过这种情况，病人还没醒。我就打电话问怎么办。他们让我把她送到恢复室。她还插着管，主治医生本来应该等她醒了再拔管的。她是个可爱的姑娘，挺漂亮的。叫米歇尔。手术前我跟她妈妈聊天，她说这孩子从9岁起就一直要求做这个手术，医生建议她再等等，但她不怕，就想把这东西弄掉，把这脸上的脂肪瘤弄掉。然后突然，她就不喘气了。我不知道发生了什么，保罗。我送她到恢复室，两分钟后她脸就青了。我是说，阿奇森，那个资深主治医生，他把我推开，扑上去做胸外按压。我根本不知道出了什么错，保罗。他们拔了管，她又开始呼吸了。一切都好了。没事了。

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 在那几分钟里，你感觉……

context_zh.speaker: client
context_zh.text: 棒极了，从没这么好过。我感觉糟透了。我只是看起来挺能干，保罗，你知道。白大褂，听诊器，口袋插着笔。我就像那些药品广告里的医生。你知道，手叉腰，眉头稍微皱一下表示关切，微笑很好看。我笑起来挺好看的，对吧？

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 嗯哼，你……你是不是期望病人永远不会出问题？

zh.therapist_turn_zh: 嗯哼，你……你是不是期望病人永远不会出问题？
zh.client_response_zh: 我搞砸了。
zh.internal_zh:
<internal>
[Perception] 他问我是不是期望病人永远不会出问题，可我听到的全是：你以为你在掌控，其实你根本没有。这话砸在我心里那个一直重放恢复室那几分钟的地方，那个知道“简单”不代表安全、一个错误瞬间就能变成灾难的地方。这个问题没干净的回答。我说是，那就是承认自己无能。我说不是，那就是假装我还相信自己能阻止这种事再发生。哪个我都不信。

[Decision] 所以我懒得再装出一副笃定的样子了。我搞砸了。就这样。我改不了这件事，没法让那姑娘的父母没经历过那几分钟，也没法把自己变成从不犯错的医生。我累了，懒得去找什么教训或安慰。没什么能补救这个。我只觉得空洞，如果我不再假装自己能控制一切，至少不用再骗自己了。
</internal>

context.text: So how's your week been?

context.text: Don't ask me about my week. It was terrible.

context.speaker: client
context.text: I was in surgery on friday and this 15-year-old girl, she she had this tumor on her cheek. It was nothing, benign, cosmetic. And everything's going great, right? Nothing wrong with the anesthetic. And my attending gets called away to consult on a procedure and the surgery ended faster than normal. It was simple. And I'm left with her still anesthetized. So I called to ask what to do. I'd never been in that situation before with a patient who's never woken up. And they told me to take her into the recovery room. She was still intubated, and the attending was supposed to remove the tube when she wakes up. She was a sweet girl, Pretty. Michelle was her name. Before the op, I was talking to her mom who told me that she'd Been asking for this operation since she was 9, they recommended that she put it off for a while, and how she wasn't afraid, just wanted this thing gone, this Fatty Lump off her Pretty face. And then suddenly, she wasn't breathing. I don't know what happened, Paul. I took her into recovery and two minutes later she was blue. I mean, Atcheson, he's the senior attending, he pushed me aside and pounced on her with chest compressions. I had no idea what went wrong, Paul. They extubated her, and she was breathing. Everything was fine. It was okay.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: How did you feel during those few minutes when the...

context.speaker: client
context.text: fantastic, never better. I felt like shit. I only look competent, Paul, you know. White coat, stethoscope, pen in pocket. I'm like those Doctors from the pharmaceutical ads. You know, like, hand on hip, brow a little furrowed with concern, nice smile. I have a pretty smile, right?

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: emhuh, Do... Do you expect that nothing will ever go wrong with a patient?

en_backup.internal:
[Perception] He’s asking me if I expect nothing will ever go wrong with a patient, and all I can hear is: you thought you were in control, and you weren’t. It hit the part of me that can’t stop replaying those minutes in recovery, the part that knows “simple” doesn’t mean safe, that one wrong moment can turn into a disaster. There’s no clean answer to that question. If I say yes, then I’m admitting I’m incompetent. If I say no, I’m pretending I still believe I can keep this from happening again. I don’t believe either one.

[Decision] So I’m done trying to sound certain. I dropped the ball. That’s it. I can’t un-drop it, I can’t make that girl’s parents not have lived through those minutes, and I can’t make myself into the kind of doctor who never screws up. I’m tired of reaching for some lesson or some reassurance. There isn’t one that fixes this. I just feel hollow, and if I stop pretending I can control everything, at least I won’t have to keep lying to myself.

zh.client_response_zh: 我就知道你会这么说，但我日程里根本没时间。我可抽不出一小时每天去健身房。

[Decision] 我得在他把这变成又一次泛泛的减肥说教之前反驳他。我要让他明白时间是障碍，不是动力，而且如果这方法真要有用，就必须符合现实生活。所以我要挑战他那个“增加活动量”的说法，明确告诉他去健身房对我行不通。

What bothered me was the assumption that exercise means a big, separate block of time, because that makes it sound simple when it isn’t.

[Decision] I need to push back on that before it turns into another generic weight-loss lecture. I want him to understand that time is the barrier, not motivation, and that if this is supposed to be helpful it has to fit into real life. So I’m going to challenge the “just add activity” idea and make it clear that a gym plan won’t work for me.

[Decision] 我没准备好完全接受这套说法，或者假装我能马上改变。我想给自己留点余地，因为如果投入太深又没作用，我会更难受。所以我会说应该相信自己，但心里在打退堂鼓。我保持中立，免得自己太抱希望，也避免拼尽全力却还差一截带来的羞耻感。
</internal>

context.text: I feel like a failure and I am scared my parents are going to be disappointed in me

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: From what you're saying to me, I feel that you don't believe in yourself very much.

context.speaker: client
context.text: I guess you are right, I need to believe in myself and my abilities more.

en_backup.therapist_turn: From what you're saying to me, I feel that you don't believe in yourself very much.
en_backup.client_response: I just don't know how sometimes.
en_backup.internal:
[Perception] They’re saying the problem is that I don’t believe in myself, and maybe if I just had more confidence I could handle this. That hits the most painful part: if I really try and still fail, then it means the fear is true and I really am not good enough. It also brings up my parents — I can already imagine their disappointment if I don’t pass. So yes, maybe I do need to believe in myself, but that feels impossible right now because it would mean risking even more hope.

[Decision] I’m not ready to fully buy into this or act like I can just change it immediately. I want to leave myself some room, because if I commit too hard and it doesn’t work, I’ll feel worse. So I’ll say I should believe in myself, but in my head I’m holding back. I’m staying on the fence to protect myself from getting my hopes up and from the shame of trying my hardest and still falling short.

[Perception] 我听到也许有一种实际的方法来获得帮助，而不至于一切崩溃，治疗师在指引我利用身边的支持。这戳中了我在工作中感到不堪重负和落后的那部分，尤其是我一直在和别人比较，觉得自己不够好。当治疗师问到我是否可以向主管或同事求助时，我意识到自己陷入了一种两难：既需要帮助，又因为太尴尬而开不了口。
[Decision] 我决定直接说出来，而不是只暗示，因为我需要的是实际的指导，而不仅仅是安慰。我很害怕，而且不知道该找谁，所以我想要坦诚地表示，也许我会找我的朋友兼同事讨教技巧，但这让人尴尬，也和我害怕被解雇有关。把这些话说出来，是我寻求帮助的方式，而不是假装我没事。
</internal>

context.speaker: client
context.text: I am worried about being perfect on my job.  I don't want to lose my job.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: I hear you are trying to be perfect on your job because you are worried about losing your job.  How long have you been at your job?

context.speaker: client
context.text: I have been working for about 4 months, but I just am not as fast at it as everyone else.  I'm trying so hard working late and everything but it's never enough.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: That can be hard when you are working so hard to try to do your best.  Can you consult with a supervisor or co-workers to get some help?

en_backup.therapist_turn: That can be hard when you are working so hard to try to do your best.  Can you consult with a supervisor or co-workers to get some help?
en_backup.client_response: Maybe I could ask my friend and co-worker for some tips.  I'm a little embarrassed to do so, but don't know where to turn. I don't want to get fired.
en_backup.internal:
[Perception] I heard that there might be a practical way to get help without everything falling apart, and the therapist was pointing me toward using the support around me. That hit the part of me that feels overwhelmed and behind at work, especially because I’ve been comparing myself to everyone else and coming up short. When they asked about asking a supervisor or coworker, it made me realize I’m stuck between needing help and being too embarrassed to ask for it.

[Decision] I decided to say it directly instead of just hinting because I need actual guidance, not just reassurance. I’m scared, and I don’t know where to turn, so I wanted to be honest that I might ask my friend and coworker for tips but that it feels embarrassing and tied to my fear of getting fired. Putting it into words is my way of asking for help with this without pretending I’m fine.

en_backup.internal:
[Perception] They immediately jumped in with “there’s nothing wrong with that at all,” like I needed reassurance for something that wasn’t even the issue. It felt generic and kind of performative, like they were trying too hard to be affirming instead of actually hearing that my marriage is falling apart and I’m alone in it. It hit the part of me that already feels unseen and a little irritated when people reduce this to something simple or obvious, because that’s not what hurts.

[Decision] So I kept it clipped and factual. If they’re going to lead with something that feels shallow, I’m not going to hand over the real stuff yet. I’ll just state the facts and see if they can do better, because right now I don’t trust that they’re actually tracking what matters.

context_zh.speaker: client
context_zh.text: 新冠的压力，还有照顾我残疾的姐姐，这些事真的让我有点受不了。

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 我明白这可能会让你有点焦虑。我自己也会有同样的感觉。

context_zh.speaker: client
context_zh.text: 谢了。我只是受够了新冠限制。真希望一切快点恢复正常。

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 我也一样。被封锁着，谁都会有点疯疯的。

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 你有没有家人或朋友，可以打电话跟他们聊聊？

context_zh.speaker: client
context_zh.text: 有的。我另一个姐姐总能帮很大忙。也许我应该多给她发短信？

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 对！那总是个好主意。听到亲人的声音总是让人安心。

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 我自己就很渴望家里来个电话，或者听听亲近的人的声音。总能让我笑起来。

zh.therapist_turn_zh: 我自己就很渴望家里来个电话，或者听听亲近的人的声音。总能让我笑起来。
zh.client_response_zh: 说的也是。我容易自己在那瞎琢磨。
zh.internal_zh:
<internal>
[Perception] 他们说得好像我出了什么大危机似的。没错，新冠限制和照顾姐姐是挺累人，但又不是说我要崩溃了。只是又戳到那些老痛点，说太多反而觉得更沉重。给我姐发个短信，或者出去走走，应该就够了——这也就是一段难熬的日子，不是什么大问题。

[Decision] 我要看开点，别把这事想得太严重。我可以给我另一个姐姐发短信，去散个步，深呼吸一下，而不是把它当成什么大事。简单点处理，就觉得还能应付。
</internal>

context.text: The pressures of Covid and taking care of my disabled sister are just getting to me.

context.text: i see how that could make you a bit anxious. I get the same way also.

context.text: Thanks. I'm just tired of the Covid restrictions. I can't wait for things to get back to normal.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: i feel the same. being on lockdown could make anyone a little crazy

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: do you have family or friends that you could reach out to over the phone?

context.speaker: client
context.text: I do. My other sister is always a big help. Maybe I should text her more often?

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: yes! that would always be a good idea. its always comforting to hear from a loved one.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: i myself yearn for a good call from family or even hearing someone close voice. always makes me smile.

en_backup.therapist_turn: i myself yearn for a good call from family or even hearing someone close voice. always makes me smile.

en_backup.internal:
[Perception] They’re making it sound like I’m in a bigger crisis than I really am. Yeah, the Covid restrictions and caring for my sister are stressful, but it’s not like I’m falling apart or anything. It just hits the same old nerves, and talking about it too much makes it feel heavier than it is. Reaching out to my sister or going for a walk is probably enough — this is more of a rough patch than some huge problem.

[Decision] I’m going to keep this in perspective and not let it get blown out of proportion. I can text my other sister, maybe do my walk, and try to breathe through it instead of treating it like something serious. If I keep it simple, it feels manageable.

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 你今天来是因为什么？

context_zh.text: 嗯，我有个15岁的女儿，她特别反对。还有，健康问题，你知道，我年纪——越来越大了，我有哮喘，还有慢性支气管炎，嗯，我运动的时候喘不过气来，更别提现在吸烟真的很不受待见。

<internal>
[Perception] 那句“麻风病人待在麻风病隔离区”我觉得完全不对味。它听起来好像我周围都是像我一样的人，但实际上现在感觉更像是我是个异类——被评判，尴尬，跟其他人格格不入。我不想他把我说成是跟一群烟民待在一起；这忽略了我感觉多孤独多暴露，尤其是我女儿还有现在社会对吸烟的看法。

[Decision] 我要纠正他，因为我不想让画面被扭曲。我想让他明白，不是我融入了烟民群体——而是抽烟让我觉得自己像个局外人，在一个已经往前走的世界上。所以我要用一个更尖锐的比喻来反驳，符合我真正的意思。
</internal>

And, um, health issues, you know, I'm getting-- not getting any younger and I have asthma and I have chronic bronchi-- bronchitis and, um, I'm having a hard time breathing when I exercise and not to mention it's socially unacceptable really.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: Like being a leper in a leper colony right now to be a smoker.

en_backup.therapist_turn: Like being a leper in a leper colony right now to be a smoker.
en_backup.client_response: Actually it's like being a leper in a non-leper colony.
en_backup.internal:
[Perception] That “leper in a leper colony” line felt way off to me. It made smoking sound like I’m surrounded by people like me, when actually it feels more like I’m the odd one out now — judged, embarrassed, and out of step with everyone else. I didn’t want him to frame it like I’m part of some group of smokers all together; that misses how alone and exposed it feels, especially with my daughter and the way society sees it now.

[Decision] I’m going to correct that because I don’t want the picture to be twisted. I want him to understand that it’s not that I fit in with smokers — it’s that smoking makes me feel like the outsider in a world that’s moved on. So I’ll push back with a sharper comparison that matches what I actually mean.

judge.rationale: 内容涉及普遍的父子情感与未竟之事，无文化障碍，翻译后能保持情绪与功能。

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 你希望在他走之前问他什么吗？

zh.therapist_turn_zh: 你希望在他走之前问他什么吗？
zh.client_response_zh: 我想问问他……他有没有为我感到骄傲。
zh.internal_zh:
<internal>
[Perception] 我觉得这个问题直接戳中了整个故事里缺失的那一块：不是我能为他做什么，而是我从来没能从他那里知道什么。它击中了我的某一部分，让我不断绕圈子——我父亲到底有没有真正看见过我，还是我一直只是在假设他没看见。电影里的那个画面让我先去寻找一个更简单、更象征性的版本，仿佛如果我能想象有别的儿子给了安慰，我就能靠近我自己的问题。但在这层底下，真正的未了结更简单也更难：我不知道自己是否以我需要的方式在他心里有过分量。

[Decision] 我决定把那个问题说出来，而不是待在那个更安全的绕道里。我想看看，如果直截了当地命名它，是否能让整件事更可理解——所有这些遗憾，到底是不是因为一个没问出口的问题，还是因为一生都没敢去问。如果我问“他为我骄傲吗”，那就得面对可能永远不知道结果，或者面对一个我还没准备好听的答案。但是，保持模糊一直在消耗我，我觉得我更想要这个问题的真相，而不是继续绕着它走。
</internal>

context.speaker: client
context.text: I don't know. But after he was gone I wished the whining guy in the movie could have been some kind of comfort to his father. I wished I had... done or said something more than just take the man's watch.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: Is there anything you wished you had asked him before he was gone?

en_backup.therapist_turn: Is there anything you wished you had asked him before he was gone?
en_backup.client_response: I wanted to ask him if... If he was proud of me.
en_backup.internal:
[Perception] I heard the question as pointing directly at the missing piece in the whole story: not what I did for him, but what I never got to know from him. It hit the part of me that keeps circling around whether my father ever actually saw me, or whether I just assumed he didn’t. The movie image made me search for an easier, symbolic version of that question first, like maybe if I could imagine some other son giving comfort, I could get closer to my own. But underneath that, the real unfinished business is simpler and harder: I don’t know if I mattered to him in the way I needed to matter.

[Decision] I decided to say the question out loud instead of staying with the safer detour. I wanted to see if naming it plainly would make the whole thing more understandable — whether all this regret is really about a single unanswered question, or about a lifetime of not asking it. If I ask, “Was he proud of me?” then I have to face the possibility of either not knowing, or knowing something I may not be ready to hear. But keeping it vague has been costing me, and I think I want the truth of the question more than I want to keep avoiding it.

judge.rationale: 对话无强文化绑定，语义可自然呈现，翻译后保持合作态度与情绪

zh.internal_zh:

en_backup.internal:
[Perception] They sounded too generic, like they were just saying the usual comforting line instead of really hearing what happened to me. “There is someone special out there for everyone” felt shallow after being cheated on and humiliated like that. It hit the worst part of me — that she said my body wasn’t enough — and the therapist just skipped over that like it was nothing. It made me feel like they were not taking the pain seriously, or like they didn’t know what to say.

[Decision] So I shut that down in my head. If they’re only going to give me empty talk, I’m not going to open up more or pretend it helps. I’d rather stick to what I know might keep me busy — games, friends, books — than let them talk like they understand me when they clearly don’t.

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 嗨！今晚在想什么？

context_zh.speaker: client
context_zh.text: 我觉得一个从大学开始认识了30年的朋友跟我疏远了。疫情期间她甚至还交了新朋友。

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 哦，真遗憾，这不好受，尤其是你们俩朋友这么久。

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 你有没有试过用电话、邮件或社交媒体联系她？

context_zh.speaker: client
context_zh.text: 她总是用说累来缩短我们的通话。她会回短信，但我觉得总是我在主动。

context_zh.speaker: client
context_zh.text: 她喜欢看电视，还跟我说她和她的新朋友用Facetime一起看。我特别讨厌看电视，所以不想参与。

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 嗯，她没有完全屏蔽你，这算是个积极信号。我同意，每天发短信可能会让她烦。

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 那没事！在我看来，你们俩都不该做那些不好玩、不愉快或不自在的事。

zh.therapist_turn_zh: 那没事！在我看来，你们俩都不该做那些不好玩、不愉快或不自在的事。
zh.client_response_zh: 我嫉妒她交新朋友比我成功。我已经超过10年没交一个新朋友了。
zh.internal_zh:
<internal>
[Perception] 她基本上是在说我不该做任何不自在的事，而且每天发短信只会惹她烦，所以没什么可做的。最扎心的是：总是我在主动，她在没我的情况下交新朋友，而且我连她喜欢的活动都不喜欢。感觉没有真正的办法回到以前那样。如果我不能加入她新的连接方式，又不能一直逼着找她而不成为负担，那可能这段友谊就是变了，我只能接受被边缘化。

[Decision] 我想我该少费劲了。继续主动没什么意义，她总是简短回应，我也没什么好提供的。我宁愿退后一步，也不愿再指望她更热情，然后又一次失望。不去尝试至少能让我不再因为想要更多而感到愚蠢，也不用面对我到底有多孤单。
</internal>

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: Hi! What's on your mind tonight?

context.speaker: client
context.text: I think a friend I've known for 30 years since college has drifted away from me.  Even during the pandemic she has made new friends.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: Oh, I'm sorry, that's not fun at all, especially since you two have been friends for so long.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: Have you tried reaching out to her by phone, email or social media?

context.speaker: client
context.text: She has cut our conversations short by saying she is tried. She will return text but I feel like I am always initiating.

context.speaker: client
context.text: She likes watching tv show and told me with her NEW friend they Facetime and watch TV together.  I really hate watching TV so don't want to offer to participate.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: Well, it's a positive sign that she hasn't blocked you completely. I agree, texting her each day could irritate her.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: That's okay! You shouldn't do anything that isn't fun or enjoyable or comfortable for either of you, in my opinion.

en_backup.therapist_turn: That's okay! You shouldn't do anything that isn't fun or enjoyable or comfortable for either of you, in my opinion.
en_backup.client_response: I am jealous that she is more successful in making new friends. I have not made a new friend in over 10 years.
en_backup.internal:
[Perception] She’s basically saying I shouldn’t do anything uncomfortable, and texting every day would just annoy her, so there’s not much to do. The thing it hit is the worst part: I’m always the one reaching out, she’s making new friends without me, and I don’t even like the kinds of activities she likes. So it feels like there isn’t a real path back to the way it was. If I can’t join her new way of connecting and I can’t keep pushing without being a burden, then maybe this friendship is just changing and I have to accept being on the outside.

[Decision] I guess I’ll stop trying so hard. It feels pointless to keep initiating when she cuts things short and I don’t have anything easy or natural to offer. I’d rather back off than keep hoping for something warmer and then getting disappointed again. Not trying protects me from feeling foolish for wanting more than she’s willing to give, and from having to face how alone I really am.

judge.rationale: 无强文化绑定，情绪与阻抗可清晰翻译至中文。

context_zh.speaker: therapist

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 所以你是不是觉得自己就像……在儿子家像个囚犯？

zh.therapist_turn_zh: 所以你是不是觉得自己就像……在儿子家像个囚犯？
zh.client_response_zh: 我儿子不在家。他已经走了三天了，去圣路易斯参加一个医学会议。他走之前我们一起看了那条新闻。他指着电视说，哦爸爸，还好你没在那儿。
zh.internal_zh:
<internal>
[Perception] 他试图把问题扯到我的感受上，好像问题是我在儿子家像个囚犯。但这不是真的。真正的问题是我儿子不在家，电视上在播一个孩子身处险境，而我人在布鲁克林，其他人都在外面行动。这才是问题——环境，距离，我够不到那个孩子。

[Decision] 我不会让他把这事赖到我头上，好像是我选择了无助或者找借口。我困在这里是因为情况把我困住了。如果我听起来很苦涩，那是因为这个世界让我眼睁睁看着一个孩子受苦却什么也做不了。这才是问题：分离，新闻，我在这里无能为力的事实。
</internal>

context.speaker: client
context.text: You know, a boy, perhaps three or four. He's clinging to an automobile tire, and his head barely above water and his eyes, you know... they are pleading.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: This is in the dream?

context.speaker: client
context.text: No no, this is real. It was on the news... B.B.C. News. I wanted to pass through the television and rescue that poor child. People are traveling from other areas to help. And I'm trapped in Brooklyn, useless, locked away like a prisoner.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: So is that what you feel like... like a prisoner in your son's home?

en_backup.therapist_turn: So is that what you feel like... like a prisoner in your son's home?
en_backup.client_response: My son is gone. He's been gone for three days, attending a medical conference in St. Louis. Before he left we watched the early reports together. He pointed to the television and said, oh baba, I'm glad that you are not there.
en_backup.internal:
[Perception] He’s trying to make this about my feelings, as if the problem is that I’m “a prisoner” in my son’s house. But that isn’t the real thing. The real thing is that my son is away, the television is showing a child in danger, and I’m here in Brooklyn while other people are out there doing something. That is what’s wrong — the circumstances, the distance, the fact that I cannot get to that boy.

[Decision] I’m not going to let him pin this on me, like I’m choosing helplessness or making excuses. I’m stuck because the situation has me trapped. If I sound bitter, it’s because the world is asking me to watch and do nothing while a child is suffering. That is the problem: the separation, the news, the fact that I’m powerless here.

zh.therapist_turn_zh: 这让你感到有威胁？

en_backup.internal:
[Perception] He picked up on the part where I said I was glad the boys were there, which is probably the only clean thing I can say out loud without getting dragged back into the whole mess. What hit me is the idea that my sons were watching all of this, and that whatever I made of it—whatever I understood or failed to understand about my father, about the funeral, about the family—I’m handing something down. That’s the unresolved piece: whether I’m just repeating the same blind spot I had all along, or whether there’s still a way to make sure they don’t inherit the same stupid story I did. Maybe I brought them there for comfort, but maybe I also brought them there because I needed witnesses, or because I wanted to see if they’d be smarter than I was about what kind of man a father really is.

[Decision] So I said the part I could say without sounding like an idiot: that I was glad they were there, and that maybe they won’t be as stupid as I was about it all. It’s a guess, really—a rough way of saying I don’t know what I missed, but I know I missed something important, and I don’t want my sons to miss it too. Saying it that way keeps me from having to admit I’m still trying to figure out what my father was, what I was, and what exactly got passed between us besides the obvious damage.

en_backup.internal:
[Perception] She’s asking me to say it plainly, to own whether he actually forgave himself, and that lands too close to home. It hits the place where I’m supposed to admit what I did and whether I can ever be beyond it. If I answer yes or no, I’m cornered: either I’m pretending people really can wash it away, or I’m admitting they can’t, which would mean I’m stuck with it forever.

[Decision] So I reach for the question instead of the answer. I soften it, make it general, keep it at a distance. “Do people ever forgive themselves?” lets me stay on the fence — not denying it outright, not surrendering to it either. I’m protecting myself from saying something that feels final, because final feels dangerous. If I don’t commit, I don’t have to face whether I’m unforgivable.

It’s not just “school stuff” anymore — it hits the part of me that feels like I’m watching him slip and I’m not sure if I’m helping or making it worse. I think what I’m feeling most is anxiety mixed with guilt, because he’s a good kid and I don’t want him to think school means he’s failing me. Saying it now felt possible because the therapist just gave me a simple opening, and I didn’t have to defend it or make it sound smaller than it is.

[Decision] I decided to admit the worry instead of brushing past it. I’m tired of acting like it’s fine when I can tell it’s bothering me. If I’m honest here, maybe I can sort out where I’m being supportive and where I’m just avoiding the hard part because I don’t want a fight.

en_backup.internal:
[Perception] What I heard was: "this is hard, but it gets better." And I just couldn't take that in. It hit the worst part — the feeling that I have no real control over my living situation, my privacy, or the future I used to imagine for myself. Being compared to your own experience made it sound like this is just a temporary inconvenience, but to me it feels like something bigger and heavier, like I'm already stuck in a life that keeps narrowing. The words "it will be the same for you too" landed badly because I couldn't see any solid reason to believe that. All I could feel was the pile of problems in front of me and how impossible it would be to carry them while already worn down.

[Decision] So I backed away from hoping. If I let myself believe things could improve, then I'd have to face how much I want that and how far away it feels, and that would hurt more. It feels safer to stay bleak, to call it an everlasting pile of problems, because then I don't have to risk expecting anything, planning anything, or being disappointed again. Giving up on hope protects me from the effort of trying and from the shame of failing to turn this around.

context.speaker: therapist

context.speaker: client

context.speaker: therapist

en_backup.client_response: Yes, I wonder if I will ever love again.
en_backup.internal:
[Perception] I heard the therapist saying this can happen, that it’s stressful, and maybe there’s some explanation for why it ended, but what landed for me was just how permanent this feels. Three years is such a long time, and if he could leave so suddenly, then maybe love really can disappear without warning. It hit the part of me that’s terrified this wasn’t just a bad breakup, but proof that I’m going to be left behind and that there’s no way to stop that from happening.

[Decision] I feel myself giving up on hoping right now. It seems easier to assume love probably won’t happen again than to keep reaching for something that might not come. If I don’t let myself believe in it, then I don’t have to keep feeling this sharp, humiliating hope and the fear underneath it. I’d rather stay numb and tell myself it’s probably over for me than risk wanting someone else and being crushed again.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: And did he lose interest?

context.speaker: client
context.text: No, he still wanted me. He used to come in and take pictures of me when I was nursing. He thought I looked beautiful.

context.text: And did you feel beautiful?

en_backup.therapist_turn: And did you feel beautiful?

en_backup.internal:
[Perception] He’s acting like this is a much bigger emotional catastrophe than it really was. Yes, I felt fat and not beautiful, but that doesn’t mean I was actually ruined. My body changed, sure, but that’s what pregnancy and birth do. He’s still here, he still wanted me, so maybe this wasn’t the terrible, irreversible loss I was making it out to be. It was hard, but not life-ending.

[Decision] I’m going to keep this small and practical. I don’t need to make a huge deal out of feeling unattractive, because the facts are that nothing was destroyed and my husband didn’t leave. So I can just accept that I felt less pretty for a while, without turning it into some permanent damage story. It’s uncomfortable, but not that serious.

en_backup.client_response: She's sick, Paul.
en_backup.internal:
[Perception] He wants me to make this about my hurt, as if I’m the one who needs to be careful here. But she’s the one who’s sick, the one who’s fragile, the one whose memory and condition make this delicate. What hit me was the absurdity of asking her for anything more than what she already gave me. I went there to do the decent thing, and instead I got thanked, turned into the hero, and made to feel ridiculous for even opening my mouth.

[Decision] I’m not going to lay my pain on her. That would be selfish, and it would burden someone who’s already ill. If this went wrong, it’s because the situation is impossible, because she can’t really take it in, not because I failed. So I’ll keep it to myself and protect her from my feelings — and protect myself from looking pathetic.

If I agreed with her, it would turn the whole thing into something dirty and humiliating, like I was made small by him and by my own memory of it. It would erase the feeling I still protect: that I was wanted, that I mattered, that I was the one who stepped toward it.

[Decision] So I shut that down immediately. I’m not going to let her put her story over mine. I’m not saying yes to a version where I was victimized and made stupid or used. I need to keep hold of the fact that I seduced him — that I had agency, that I knew what I was doing, that I wasn’t powerless. I’d rather be blunt and disagree than hand over that part of myself.

en_backup.internal:
[Perception] I hear the therapist trying to push me toward “moving on” and “being happy,” like it should be simple if I just decide it. But what lands for me is how impossible that sounds when I’m grieving and already so low. It hits the part of me that feels stuck in the loss — the marriage I left, the good things I miss, the life that isn’t there anymore. It makes me feel like even my sadness is something I’m failing at, because I can’t just turn it off and plan a future.

[Decision] So I shut down a little inside. If I can’t make myself happy and nothing I try seems to change how empty I feel, then there’s no point forcing it and getting my hopes up just to be disappointed again. It feels safer to stay with the grief I know than to reach for a future that may not feel real anyway. I’m not choosing this because I want to be here — I’m choosing it because I don’t see how to do anything else without hoping and then falling apart again.

It landed on the part of me that already feels exposed for coming here instead of turning it in. The look on their face was probably supposed to be neutral or curious, but all I could read was polite interest — the kind people have when they’re being careful not to embarrass you. Which makes it worse, because then I feel handled instead of understood. Like they’re about to tell me “it’s fine” when they have no idea how bad it is.

[Decision] So I went sarcastic first. If I make it sound like I don’t care, then they don’t get to be the one evaluating me, and I don’t have to sit there waiting for my work to be quietly judged. “If you’re interested in shit” is me taking the air out of it before they can. It’s easier to act contemptuous than to hand over something I already think is embarrassing and let them confirm it.

en_backup.client_response: He was nothing like me and I am nothing like him.
en_backup.internal:
[Perception] What I heard was him trying to line me up with my father, like I’m just doing some version of the same thing. That hits the worst part of it — the part where I’ve spent my whole life making sure I’m not him. If I agree with that, then all the effort, all the showing up, all the calling, all the not walking away... it starts sounding like I’m just another man making excuses. It also feels like it would give my father something he does not deserve: a place beside me in the way I try to hold my family together.

[Decision] So I shut it down. No, that’s not what this is. I am not him, and I’m not going to let you put me in the same box. If I let that comparison stand, I lose the one thing I cannot afford to lose — the truth that I am doing this differently, and that my kids know I’m there.

I hear that if I don’t make them regret it, they’ll just keep doing it, but I also hear how much stress they’re already under and how much I don’t want to be the kind of parent who makes home feel worse. It hit the part of me that is already tired and scared that nothing I do will actually stick. Talking doesn’t last, yelling doesn’t work, and taking things away feels mean. So it feels like I’m stuck either hurting them or letting my work fall apart.

[Decision] I feel like crying because I don’t know what else to do, and honestly I’m tired of trying to find the perfect response. Maybe I should just stop pushing for a solution right now and get through the day as best I can. I don’t want to make a big battle out of it if it’s just going to fail anyway. It feels safer to not hope too much, because hoping would mean facing how little control I really have.

[Perception] 她立马就把话题扯到自己被出轨的事上去了，感觉她只是透过自己的痛苦在听，根本没听到我在说什么。然后问我有没有跟他谈过，感觉完全不在状态——就好像她要么根本没抓住重点，要么就是在推着我去做我已经说过还没准备好的事。这戳到了我那种被背叛和愤怒的感觉——好像就指望我心平气和地去面对那个毁了我生活的男人，然后为了别人的舒服装出一副通情达理的样子。这让我觉得她帮不上忙，甚至还有点儿不懂我的感受，因为我的恶心就是整个问题的核心，而她好像直接跳过去了。

[Decision] 所以我就把话堵死了。如果她觉得跟他谈是顺理成章下一步，那她就根本没在听我说话。我也不打算继续解释自己，只是为了被她推着去我不想去的方向。我决定把话说绝，保持距离。我不会为了让她这对话好受一点，就放弃我恶心和愤怒的权利。
</internal>

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: Good evening.

context.speaker: client
context.text: Good evening, thanks for taking the time to talk with me.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: No problem. How can I help you tonight?

context.speaker: client
context.text: I am having issues dealing with my feelings about ending my long term relationship with my children's father.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: So just to make sure I understand, you are struggling with dealing with ending a long term relationship with your child's father.

context.speaker: client
context.text: Exactly right, after 15 years and 4 kids, he cheated on me and the affair produced a child.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: I am so sorry to hear that. My ex-fiance cheated on me and got pregnant with another man, so I know how rough this type of thing is.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: Have you been able to talk to him about it yet?

en_backup.therapist_turn: Have you been able to talk to him about it yet?
en_backup.client_response: At this point, I don't want to talk, I am so disgusted I want nothing more to do with him, regardless of the kids.
en_backup.internal:
[Perception] She immediately made it about her own cheating story, which made me feel like she was listening through her own pain instead of actually hearing mine. And then asking if I’d talked to him yet felt clueless, like she either missed the whole point or was pushing me toward something I’ve already said I am not ready for. It hit the part of me that feels betrayed and furious — like I’m expected to calmly deal with the man who blew up my life and then act reasonable for everyone else’s comfort. That made her feel unhelpful, maybe even a little tone-deaf, because my disgust is the whole issue and she seemed to skip right over that.

[Decision] So I shut it down. If she’s going to act like talking to him is the obvious next step, then she’s not really hearing me, and I’m not going to keep explaining myself just to get pushed somewhere I don’t want to go. I decided to be blunt and keep my distance, because I’m not giving up my right to be disgusted and angry just to make this conversation smoother for her.

[Perception] He’s doing that thing where he acts like he’s the only one who can see what’s “really” going on, like my life is a puzzle he gets to solve for me. He hears “breakfast” and immediately turns it into some deeper confession, then looks at me like I’m avoiding the truth. It feels patronizing — like he’s fishing for a dramatic story about Laura and jealousy because that’s more interesting than what I actually said. I’m not going to let him make me sound pathetic or predictable just because I’m here and he has a theory.

[Decision] So I’m going to call it out and make him prove it. If he wants to keep pushing this, he can stop hiding behind vague therapist voice and say what he actually means. I’m not handing him the satisfaction of nodding along while he puts words in my mouth. If he wants to reduce this to “you slept around because of Laura,” I’ll shove it back at him until he sounds as ridiculous as it is. That’s safer than letting him steer me into something I don’t want to own.

context_zh.speaker: client

zh.therapist_turn_zh: 你……是在说某件你自己无法原谅自己的事吗？
zh.client_response_zh: 什么，比如毁了我的婚姻、毁了我孩子的生活、毁了我的事业、没能救我的母亲、忽视了我父亲？
zh.internal_zh:
<internal>
[Perception] 他又来了——想把责任推到我身上，把这事变成一场关于“原谅”的规整忏悔，好像只要他说对那句话，一切就都变了。最丑陋的是：如果我说我能原谅自己，那我就是在假装那些伤害不是真的。那我就是在为自己开脱——我的婚姻、我的孩子、我的事业、我的母亲、我的父亲——所有的一切。我不能这样做。不是我不懂这个问题，而是答案感觉像谎言。

[Decision] 所以不，我不会往那走。我不会仅仅因为这会让他舒服、或让我好受一分钟，就把这事说成是可以原谅的。我画了线：我不会用一句话就把我的失败变成可以存活的事。如果我开始原谅自己，那听起来就像我在为自己的所作所为找借口——我拒绝这么做。
</internal>

context.text: You know, I hoped that... I hoped that he'd be able to forgive himself for...

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: For what?

context.speaker: client
context.text: For what he did. He dropped a bomb on a school.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: Right. And Was he able to forgive himself?

context.speaker: client
context.text: I don't know. Do people ever forgive themselves really? I know we talk about it all the time, but do people ever really do it?

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: Sometimes.

context.speaker: client
context.text: Sometimes, yeah. How long does it take?

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: Are you... talking about something you're not able to forgive yourself for?

en_backup.therapist_turn: Are you... talking about something you're not able to forgive yourself for?
en_backup.client_response: What, like breaking up my marriage, destroying my kids' lives, wrecking my career, not being able to save my mother and not paying attention to my father?
en_backup.internal:
[Perception] He’s doing it again — trying to pin this on me, to turn this into some neat little confession about “forgiveness” like if he gets the right sentence out of me, then everything changes. What it hits is the ugliest part: if I say I can forgive myself, then I’m pretending the damage wasn’t real. Then I’m letting myself off the hook for my marriage, my kids, my career, my mother, my father — all of it. And I can’t do that. Not because I don’t understand the question, but because the answer feels like a lie.

[Decision] So no, I’m not going there. I’m not going to call this forgivable just because it would make him comfortable or make me feel better for a minute. I drew the line there: I won’t turn my failures into something survivable with a word. If I start forgiving myself, then it sounds like I’m excusing what I did — and I refuse to do that.

[Decision] 我打算把这放在“能搞定，只是需要合适方法”那个盒子里，这样我就不用觉得被压垮了。这样我就能掌控住，不把这事儿闹大。我可能还会继续找简单的自助方法，除非咨询不用费什么劲、不用我什么都倒出来，才会考虑。当小事处理总比捅个大篓子容易多了。
</internal>

en_backup.internal:
[Perception] They’re making this sound like a bigger, more serious issue than it really is. I’m not collapsing or anything—I’m just stuck at the starting line and it’s annoying. The therapist is kind of treating it like I need a major intervention, but from my side it feels more like a practical hurdle with some discomfort around it, especially the cultural explanation part. It’s not that my whole situation is in crisis; it’s just that finding the right kind of help would be inconvenient and mentally tiring.

[Decision] I’m going to keep this in the “manageable, just needs the right approach” box so I don’t have to feel overwhelmed by it. That lets me stay in control and not make a huge deal out of it. I’ll probably keep looking for simple self-help ideas and maybe only consider counseling if it can be low-effort and doesn’t require me to unpack everything. It’s easier to treat it as a smaller problem than to open up a whole bigger can of worms.

[Perception] He’s reaching back into something old again — that business about me as a kid, being “on duty.” I can feel what he’s getting at: that this whole feeling of being watched now may have something to do with how I was back then. That hits a nerve because it makes it sound like I’m carrying around some old hurt or some old responsibility, and I don’t much want to go digging around in that. I’d rather keep this on the surface: Connie talking too much, Natalie keeping tabs, me wanting a little quiet. That’s simple enough. It also protects me from sounding weak or sentimental.

[Decision] So I’m going to keep it light and brush it off. Not because he’s entirely wrong, but because I’m not ready to make a whole thing out of it. I don’t want to hand over the idea that I was burdened as a boy, or that this is all stirring up something deeper. Better to say it was nothing, just part of life, not worth talking about. I can admit a little, but not too much. I need to keep my footing here.

en_backup.internal:
[Perception] They’re asking how I’m feeling, and I can hear the invitation to say more than “fine.” It lands right on the part of me that feels worn down by living here, having lost my own place, and having to carry this constant sense that things are piling up with no clear way out. If I answer too honestly, it all comes rushing in.

[Decision] So I stay a little vague. “It could be better” is enough to admit I’m not doing well, but it doesn’t pin me down or force me to unpack everything at once. I’m protecting my privacy and my sense of control by not opening the whole floodgate. Maybe I can test the water without handing over all of it yet.

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 所以不管你是不是真的感觉好点了，你都要让他们俩觉得你好了。

context_zh.speaker: client
context_zh.text: 我跟你说了，我好了。

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 所以你跟娜塔莉吃了最后一顿饭，亲了她告别，他们走了，你终于有了……你的私人空间。

zh.therapist_turn_zh: 所以你跟娜塔莉吃了最后一顿饭，亲了她告别，他们走了，你终于有了……你的私人空间。
zh.client_response_zh: 我当时就是打冷颤。
zh.internal_zh:
<internal>
[Perception] 她一直把这事说得好像我在给娜塔莉和那帮人演戏似的——好像我绷着就是为了把她们哄走。然后她说“私人空间”，说得好像那是奖品。我一下反应过来，她是想把责任全推到我身上，好像我是故意找麻烦，而不是因为病了、想要自己的房间、自己的空间、自己的生活。她们走的时候，我确实就是打冷颤——不是什么惊天动地的情绪坦白。

[Decision] 所以我就直截了当纠正她。我不会让她把那一段编成一个关于感受和好转的小故事。我就是好了，女儿陪着我，她们走了之后我就觉得冷颤。事实就是这样。她要是想编点别的，那是她的事，我可不会假装这里头有什么大彻大悟。
</internal>

context.speaker: therapist

context.speaker: client

en_backup.therapist_turn: So you had your last meal with Natalie, you kissed her goodbye, they left and you finally had... Your privacy.
en_backup.client_response: What I had was the chills.
en_backup.internal:
[Perception] She keeps making it sound like this was some kind of performance for Natalie and the others — like I was holding myself together just long enough to send them away happy. And then she says "privacy" like that was the prize. What hit me was that she was trying to pin this all on me, like I was choosing to be difficult instead of just being sick and wanting my own room, my own space, my own life back. The chills were what I actually had when they left — not some dramatic emotional confession.

[Decision] So I corrected her plainly. I wasn’t going to let her turn that into a neat little story about feelings and improvement. I was better, I had my daughter with me, and when they were gone I felt the chills. That’s the fact of it. If she wants to make something else out of it, that’s on her, but I’m not going to pretend there was some big revelation here.

en_backup.therapist_turn: How may I help you?
en_backup.client_response: Hi I am feeling quite sad today.
en_backup.internal:
[Perception] They’re inviting me to say what’s really going on, not just get through the session. “How may I help you?” lands on the part of me that’s been feeling quietly hurt and alone, like my friends don’t really notice when I’m struggling. Saying I’m “quite sad today” is me touching that sadness directly, without having to explain everything yet.

[Decision] I decided to be honest and simple instead of pretending I’m fine. I can admit the sadness because it feels safer to start here — just naming it — than jumping straight to what’s wrong with my friendships. Maybe if I say it plainly, I won’t have to carry it by myself for a moment.

en_backup.therapist_turn: No?
en_backup.client_response: What part of that word don't you understand?
en_backup.internal:
[Perception] He’s trying to make this about me again, like I’m some hidden cause behind Kevin’s letter and my dad’s reaction. That feels wrong. My dad blowing up at Karen and Kevin’s letter are not the same thing, and it pissed me off that he was reaching for some neat little theory that pins it on me. What I said about my dad actually mattered — it was about him finally showing he cared, not about me somehow shaping everything that happens around me.

[Decision] I need to shut that down because it’s not true and I don’t want him twisting it into something it isn’t. So I’m going to answer hard and keep it simple: no, that’s not what happened. I need him to hear that I’m not agreeing with some fake connection just because he’s trying to make one.

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 你经历的那件事真的很难熬，我也很难过。

context_zh.speaker: client
context_zh.text: 一份接一份申请被拒，搞得我连填表都不太想填了。

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 是啊，求职申请有时候特别让人觉得自己被贬低。我自己就烦那种重复填表又重复被拒的感觉。就好像我这个人一点价值都没有。

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 但你也得想想，选不上工作的原因有几十种，其中不少跟你这个人或者你的工作能力完全没关系。

context_zh.speaker: client
context_zh.text: 有个人知道这有多让人沮丧、多容易陷入循环，这感觉挺好的——不过我也挺抱歉，你也知道那滋味。

context_zh.speaker: client
context_zh.text: 谢谢你这么说。我觉得我投的那些工作大部分我都资历过高了，这说不通，让我觉得是不是我自己哪里有问题。

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 别那么想。我知道有好几个雇主其实公开说过，他们不想要比自己聪明的员工。因为那样成本更高、管理起来更费劲，而且不少人很乐意为了表面上的高素质人才不去操那份心。

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 具体一点，你是在投简历那一步就卡住了，还是在面试那一步？

zh.therapist_turn_zh: 具体一点，你是在投简历那一步就卡住了，还是在面试那一步？
zh.client_response_zh: 希望能碰到一个把员工素质放在其他东西前面的雇主吧，这越来越让人泄气了。
zh.internal_zh:
<internal>
[Perception] 我从咨询师的话里听出来的意思是，有那么多实际原因解释我为什么没被选上，但这些一点都没让被拒绝的感觉变得不那么针对个人。它击中了我内心那个仍然需要相信自己的经历还有点意义的部分，因为现在我看到的只是一份又一份申请消失得无影无踪。就算被告知这不一定是我的问题，也改变不了我是那个感觉不被需要、被困住的人。

[Decision] 我决定对这个过程不抱什么期待了，因为抱希望越大，每次落空就越疼。如果我表现得好像这没戏，那我就不用一直把自己暴露在同样的失望里，也不用反复怀疑自己哪里不对。麻木一点、走个流程，感觉比一直相信自己离某个东西很近但从来得不到要安全。
</internal>

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: That is an extremely tough situation to go through, I'm sorry to hear that.

context.speaker: client
context.text: Application after application I get rejected, it makes it hard to even fill out more

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: Yes, job applications can feel particularly demeaning to complete.  Personally, I get frustrated with all the repetition and then repetitive rejection.  It seems like I had no value.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: But you have to consider that there are dozens of different reasons why you don't get selected for a job, and quite a few of them have nothing to do with you , either as a person or as an employee.

context.speaker: client
context.text: It feels good someone else knows how frustrating and what a cycle it creates but I am also sorry that you do know how it is also.

context.speaker: client
context.text: Thank you for that, it seems most of the jobs I am applying for I am over qualified for which doesn't make sense to me and makes me think it is something personal about me.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: No, don't think that.  I know of several employers that have actually said they don't want employees smarter than them.  It requires more money and more management, and quite a few people are very happy to not do either of those things for ostensibly higher quality workforce.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: On an actionable level, have you been getting blocked at the application point or the interviewing point?

en_backup.therapist_turn: On an actionable level, have you been getting blocked at the application point or the interviewing point?
en_backup.client_response: Hopefully I find an employer that sees a quality workforce over other things, its getting pretty discouraging
en_backup.internal:
[Perception] What I took from the therapist's words is that there are supposed to be all these practical reasons I’m not getting picked, but none of it makes the rejection feel any less personal. It hits the part of me that still needs to believe my experience means something, because right now all I can see is application after application disappearing into nothing. Even being told it’s not necessarily about me doesn’t change the fact that I’m the one left feeling unwanted and stuck.

[Decision] I decided to stop expecting much from this process, because hoping harder just makes the drop feel worse each time. If I act like this is probably going nowhere, then I don’t have to keep opening myself up to the same disappointment and wondering what’s wrong with me. It feels safer to numb out a bit and go through the motions than to keep believing I’m close to something that never seems to come.

context_zh.speaker: client
context_zh.text: 我该怎么处理这个？

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 我们都在一起。有了适当的情感支持，我们每个人都能渡过这段动荡时期。

context_zh.speaker: client
context_zh.text: 有什么建议我可以做点什么的吗？我觉得快要撑不住了。

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 现在世界上很多地方天气变冷，可能看起来挺糟糕，但疫苗很快就要来了。

context_zh.speaker: client
context_zh.text: 我真希望如此，这算是一线希望吧。

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 想想有效疫苗的积极方面。别给自己太大压力，那些你控制不了的因素就别管了。

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 我知道有时候我们会感到无助，但试着把注意力集中在你能控制的事上——比如遵循专业健康建议：戴口罩、保持社交距离和一般消毒。

context_zh.speaker: client
context_zh.text: 没错！！口罩和社交距离真的很有用。感觉自己尽了一份力挺不错的。

zh.therapist_turn_zh: 我知道有时候我们会感到无助，但试着把注意力集中在你能控制的事上——比如遵循专业健康建议：戴口罩、保持社交距离和一般消毒。
zh.client_response_zh: 假期见不到家人，真的很难受！！
zh.internal_zh:
<internal>
[感知] 治疗师一直把我往我能控制的事情上引，那确实管用，因为我真的需要一些实实在在的东西来抓住。但最让我难受的是，这一切其实都不是我的错——是疫情、天气、限制，整个局面让我没法去上班，也没法和家人团聚。这才是让我感到崩溃和孤独的原因。

[决定] 所以我要专注于我已经做对的事：戴口罩、保持距离、努力负责任。只要我小心，至少我知道自己尽了一份力。我自己没法解决这一团糟，但我可以把责任推给外部环境，解释为什么我会这样感觉，同时继续希望事情能快点好起来。
</internal>

context.text: How do I handle that/

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: We are all in this together. With proper emotional support, each of us can overcome these turbulent times.

context.speaker: client
context.text: Any suggestions on things I can do? I feel so overwhelmed

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: It may seem pretty bad now with the cold weather setting in at many parts of the world. But there is a vaccine coming soon.

context.speaker: client
context.text: I really do hope so, it's a glimmer of hope

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: Think about the positive aspects of an effective vaccine. Do not stress too much about factors outside your control.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: I know we can feel helpless at some times, but try to focus on things under YOUR control - like following health professional advise - masks, social distancing and general sanitization

context.speaker: client
context.text: That's true!! The masks and social distancing are very ehlpful. It's good to feel like i am doing my part.

en_backup.therapist_turn: I know we can feel helpless at some times, but try to focus on things under YOUR control - like following health professional advise - masks, social distancing and general sanitization
en_backup.client_response: Not seeing family for the holidays will be very hard!!
en_backup.internal:
[Perception] The therapist kept steering me toward the things I can control, and that landed because I really do need something concrete to hold on to. But what hits hardest is that none of this is actually my fault — it’s the pandemic, the weather, the restrictions, the whole situation keeping me away from my office and my family. That’s what’s making me feel so crushed and alone.

[Decision] So I’m going to focus on what I’m already doing right: masks, distancing, trying to be responsible. If I stay careful, then at least I know I’m doing my part. I can’t fix all this mess myself, but I can blame the circumstances for why I feel this way and keep hoping things get better soon.

zh.client_response_zh: 不，我晚点打给他。
zh.internal_zh:

en_backup.therapist_turn: I'm a little confused as to why you should talk about her So... so crudely.
en_backup.client_response: Whatever, dude.
en_backup.internal:
[Perception] He’s calling me out for being crude about Ms. U, and it hits the part where I know I’m making it nasty on purpose. He’s not really talking about the joke — he’s poking at how much I actually care about her having my back, and how fast I turn it into a bit when it gets too real. That’s annoying because it lands close to the stuff I don’t want to look at: that I could lose her support, and that I’m not as chill about that as I act.

[Decision] So I kept it short and gave him nothing. “Whatever, dude” is easier than admitting I was being defensive or that I felt called out. If I keep it vague, I don’t have to explain why I’m doing this whole clown routine, and I don’t have to give him a clean shot at the part where I actually care. Brevity lets me stay in control.

context.text: Hi how are you today?

context.speaker: client
context.text: Hi, I'm stressed and anxious today

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: Oh no! I'm sorry to hear that. What's going on?

en_backup.therapist_turn: Oh no! I'm sorry to hear that. What's going on?
en_backup.client_response: Just financial problems
en_backup.internal:
[Perception] I could tell the therapist was asking me to open up, and the part that hit was how heavy everything feels right now with money. It’s not just one bill or one bad week — it’s the constant pressure of not having enough, of trying to keep up, and worrying something is going to slip. I wanted them to understand that this isn’t vague stress; it’s financial problems sitting on me all the time.

[Decision] I decided to keep it simple and say it plainly instead of overexplaining or pretending I’m okay. I’m trying to get the therapist to see the actual source of the anxiety, because if I name it clearly maybe we can talk about what to do about it. I’m also holding back a little, because once I start talking about money, it can easily turn into me feeling embarrassed or overwhelmed, and I don’t want to get lost in that yet.

context_zh.speaker: client
context_zh.text: 嗯，至少…至少有一部分是的。

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 无论你感受到什么情绪，当时你会坦率地表达出来吗？

context_zh.speaker: client
context_zh.text: 不完全是。

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 你压抑自己？

context_zh.speaker: client
context_zh.text: 你…你是这么想的吗？

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 之前，当你谈到Sunil的时候，你变得投入、兴奋，就像你自己活了过来。你说话充满活力。你身体前倾。然后你停了下来。这很引人注目。这个描述你觉得准确吗？你是否发现自己有热情或兴奋的冲动，却又阻止自己表达？几周前我也注意到你压抑自己，当时你反应很大。你记得吗？

context_zh.speaker: client
context_zh.text: 你…你在说什么啊？

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 你跟我讲过你梦的开头……沿着铁栅栏跑向敞开的大门，然后被拖下来，动弹不得。我问你是不是你自己在阻止自己，你对我很生气。你坚持说是你父亲在阻止你。

zh.therapist_turn_zh: 你跟我讲过你梦的开头……沿着铁栅栏跑向敞开的大门，然后被拖下来，动弹不得。我问你是不是你自己在阻止自己，你对我很生气。你坚持说是你父亲在阻止你。
zh.client_response_zh: 是我的学校。
zh.internal_zh:
<internal>
[Perception] 我听到的是她把所有事情都归成一个简单的故事：是我在压抑自己，是我在阻止自己的兴奋，证据就是刚才治疗中那一刻加上那个梦。让我不舒服的是那种暗示，好像这是我的选择，是我自己造成的，而父亲的压力却不是这样。我能感觉到她在站“是你自己对自己做的事”这一边，而这触动了我的那部分——我知道我有多经常被学校、被父亲、被别人期望推着走、塑造、限制。这感觉太简化了，好像她忽略了那些东西的力量，让我为那些强加给我的事情负责。

[Decision] 我决定我必须纠正这一点。我需要在那个版本的我在房间里被固定成“真相”之前推回去。所以我问：“你在说什么啊？”然后说：“是我的学校。”因为我想把责任推回它该在的地方。我不想被塑造成一个故意压抑自己的人，因为那不是我感受到的样子——我感觉是被强加的，我需要她看到这一点。
</internal>

context.speaker: client
context.text: Yeah, at least... at least in part.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: Whatever emotion you do feel, do you openly express yourself at the time?

context.speaker: client
context.text: Not entirely.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: You hold yourself back?

context.speaker: client
context.text: Is... is that what you think?

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: Earlier, when you were talking about Sunil, you became engaged, excited, as you came alive yourself. You spoke with energy. You sat forward in your seat. And then you stopped yourself. It was striking. Does that description seem accurate to you? Do you find you have passionate or excited impulses, but stop yourself from expressing them? I made a similar observation a couple of weeks ago about you holding yourself back, and you had a strong reaction. Do you remember?

context.speaker: client
context.text: What... what are you talking about?

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: You told me about the beginning of your dream... running toward open gates along a wrought-iron fence, and then being dragged down, paralyzed. I asked if you were stopping yourself and you got very angry at me. You insisted it was your father who was stopping you.

en_backup.therapist_turn: You told me about the beginning of your dream... running toward open gates along a wrought-iron fence, and then being dragged down, paralyzed. I asked if you were stopping yourself and you got very angry at me. You insisted it was your father who was stopping you.
en_backup.client_response: It was my school.
en_backup.internal:
[Perception] What I heard was that she was folding everything into one neat story: that I’m the one holding myself back, that I’m stopping my own excitement, and that the evidence is this moment in session plus that dream. What felt wrong was the implication that this is my choice or my doing in the same way my father’s pressure was not. I could feel her taking the side of “you do this to yourself,” and that hit the part of me that knows how often I’ve been pushed, shaped, constrained by school, by my father, by other people’s expectations. It felt reductive, like she was overlooking the force of those things and making me responsible for something that was done to me.

[Decision] I decided I had to correct that. I needed to push back before that version of me got fixed in the room as if it were the truth. So I asked, “What are you talking about?” and then said, “It was my school,” because I wanted to move the blame back where it belongs. I wanted to resist being made into the person who simply suppresses himself on purpose, because that’s not how it feels to me — it feels imposed, and I need her to see that.

我觉得她就是对我没兴趣了？
好几个月前的事了。真希望我能走出来。可我就是忘不掉她。她现在跟个彻头彻尾的失败者约会。

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 那很难受……你说你们是慢慢疏远了？还是你觉得更多是一方在变？

context_zh.speaker: client
context_zh.text:
多半是我的问题更多。
也许我该多做点什么让她知道我在乎她。是不是我不够浪漫？有些男的天生就不是那块料。

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 我完全理解，我觉得你不该为这事自责！

context_zh.speaker: client
context_zh.text: 有道理。我不该对自己太苛刻。我本来就不是在浪漫的家庭里长大的。那些东西我不会，但也许可以学。

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 没错，而且别忘了每个人都不一样，也许你只是不是她的那个人，而这种事双方都有可能。

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 你觉得你想改变是为了她？还是为了你自己？

context_zh.speaker: client
context_zh.text: 说得对。我真太执着于她了。我以为她完美，我们在一起完美。她不这么看。我改变不了自己是谁，她也改变不了她自己。

zh.therapist_turn_zh: 你觉得你想改变是为了她？还是为了你自己？
zh.client_response_zh: 我不知道自己能不能为了她改变。也许有些基本的东西她想要，我就是没有？我大概应该为了以后的恋爱改变才对。
zh.internal_zh:
<internal>
[Perception] 咨询师说得好像这就是一次普通的不合适，我可以吸取教训然后继续走。但那太轻巧了，根本没说到点子上。如果我同意自己应该为了以后的恋爱改变，那听起来就像是在承认，我跟她在一起时根本就是有欠缺的。也像是在说，我原来的方式不够好，她离开是对的。这戳中了我内心不想把这事变成“我得变成另一个人”的部分。我明白自己有盲点，但我并不接受就因为这一段关系结束了就得重塑自己。

[Decision] 所以我得顶回去。我不认为自己能——也不认为自己应该——为了她、或者为了某个想象中的未来人选改变自己。也许有些基础的东西某些人想要，而我就是天生没有，如果真是那样，那我硬逼自己变得更浪漫就太假了。我宁愿坦诚这一点，也不愿假装能把自己修理成别人。为了这个而改变，让我觉得是在丢掉自我，我受不了。
</internal>

context.speaker: client
context.text:
I think she just lost interest in me? 
It happened a couple of months ago. I wish I could get over it. I can't get her off my mind. She's dating this total loser.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: That's tough... so you're saying that you grew apart a little? Or do you think it was more one-sided?

context.speaker: client
context.text:
It probably was more me than her. 
Maybe I should have done more to show her that I cared for her. Am I not romantic enough? Some guys just aren't that way.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: I completely understand, and I don't think you should beat yourself up over it!

context.speaker: client
context.text: That's a fair point. I shouldn't be too hard on myself.  I didn't really grow up in a romantic family. I don't know how to do that stuff, but maybe I could learn.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: Exactly, and remember everyone is different, perhaps you just weren't her right one, and that can go both ways.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: Do you want to improve for her? or for yourself do you think?

context.speaker: client
context.text: That's true. I really got hung up on her. I thought she was perfect and that we were perfect together. She didn't see it that way. I can't really change who I am, and she couldn't change who she is.

en_backup.therapist_turn: Do you want to improve for her? or for yourself do you think?
en_backup.client_response: I don't know if I can change myself for her. Maybe there is something basic that she wants that I just don't have? I should probably change for future relationships.
en_backup.internal:
[Perception] The therapist is making it sound like this is just a normal mismatch, like I can take it as a lesson and move on. But that feels too easy, and it misses the point. If I agree that I should just change myself for future relationships, then it sounds like I’m admitting I was fundamentally lacking with her. It also feels like I’m conceding that my way of being wasn’t enough, and that she was right to walk away. That hits the part of me that doesn’t want to turn this into “I need to become a different person.” I can see that I have blind spots, but I don’t accept that I should reshape myself just because this one relationship ended.

[Decision] So I’m pushing back. I don’t think I can — or should — change who I am for her, or for some imagined future person. Maybe there are basic things some people want that I just don’t naturally have, and if that’s true, then forcing myself to become more romantic feels fake. I’d rather be honest about that than pretend I can fix myself into someone else. The idea of changing for this makes me feel like I’m losing myself, and I’m not okay with that.

en_backup.internal:
[Perception] The therapist is treating this like something that’s intense but normal, more like a rough patch I’m supposed to ride out than a serious danger. [Decision] I’m going to downshift it and try not to make a big deal out of it. I’ll tell myself it comes in waves and that I’m just having a hard spell, because that feels safer than admitting how heavy it really is. If I keep it smaller, I won’t seem like too much, and maybe I can handle it without making my family worry more.

zh.therapist_turn_zh: 我理解那种感觉。感觉没进展确实让人很沮丧。- 嗯。但你不觉得，光是倾听这个行为本身就有价值吗？

zh.internal_zh:
<internal>
[Perception] 我听到治疗师提到了沮丧感，但只是轻轻带过，然后转到倾听有价值的想法。这正好打中了我内心那种被抹消的感觉——当杰西回到他的生活，所有努力似乎都消失的时候。也触动了我的另一部分：我希望自己的付出能以一种可衡量的方式发挥作用，而不仅仅是房间里美好的瞬间。如果我停留在那里，我就得承认，感到连接不足以改变房间外的事情，这有多伤人。

[Decision] 所以我从杰西身上移开，转到“我最近有个新来访者……”因为这样我待在更安全的地方。我可以保持职业性，把焦点放在另一个案例上，避免说出更暴露的东西：我不只是在谈论一个病人的进展，我担心自己的工作可能不够。如果继续深入，我可能不得不面对失望、无助，以及我无法像自己希望的那样控制结果的可能性。说得少一点比冒险感受那种感觉更安全。
</internal>

If I have no future right now, at least I can say this is because of what happened to me, not because I am refusing to try.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: Hi there, how is this season treating you?

context.speaker: client
context.text: It's alright. Definitely not as cold as last year which is something to be slightly thankful for.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: Well let's be grateful for small mercies :). How are you feeling in yourself though? Is there anything you'd like to talk about?

context.speaker: client
context.text: I'm worried about grad school

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: Ah I am sorry to hear that. Please try not to worry too much as it's a common worry to have. Do you want to tell me the details?

context.speaker: client
context.text: Sure. One of my classes is extremely difficult and the professor has not been responsive at all. The TA is kind enough to make time to help me with homework, but my grades are still not great. It makes me feel really dumb and undeserving to be in that class

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: So you are feeling as though you are in the wrong place? Do you feel as though you might fail your class completely?

context.speaker: client
context.text: I want to be in the program, it's just that I feel like everyone is so much smarter than me and my performance in that class makes me question my admission into the programs sometimes. When I feel like this after submitting homework, I end up crying because I just want to do well. I enjoy this field, just not this  class in particular.

en_backup.therapist_turn: So you are feeling as though you are in the wrong place? Do you feel as though you might fail your class completely?
en_backup.client_response: I'm afraid of failing, but I'm not sure if that should be a concern either. Over the past 3 years, no one has gotten a grade lower than a B.
en_backup.internal:
[Perception] The therapist is basically asking if failing is actually the thing I’m afraid of, but that doesn’t quite fit. Yes, I’m stressed about the class, but the bigger hit is how the class makes me feel about myself — like maybe I’m not smart enough, maybe I don’t belong here. Still, I also know the grade situation isn’t as dire as it feels; if no one has gotten below a B in years, then maybe I’m not actually in immediate danger. It’s hard to say that out loud because it sounds like I’m overreacting, and I don’t want to make the problem bigger than it is.

[Decision] So I’m going to stay a little on the fence. I’ll admit I’m afraid of failing, but then I’ll soften it and point out the grade trend, because that lets me acknowledge the fear without fully committing to it. That way I don’t have to face the possibility that this is really about my self-worth, and I don’t have to look too needy or like I’m panicking over something that might be manageable. I want to protect the part of me that still believes I belong in the program, even if I’m struggling right now.

context_zh.text: 我爸爸是我中学的训导主任兼篮球教练。他管着我跟我哥的一举一动。我们表现好的时候，他觉得那是理所当然。要是搞砸了……这么说吧，他这人没什么同情心。

context_zh.speaker: client
context_zh.text: 你会这么想。我上初一那年，他开始周末一个人开车出去。我跟我哥骑车在附近转，找他的车。结果在一栋小房子的车道上找到了。我哥让我去按门铃。门开了，是我爸的秘书，那个以前给我们糖的好心女士。然后我爸从她浴室出来，冲着我们大吼。

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 你们当时怎么办？

zh.therapist_turn_zh: 你们当时怎么办？
zh.client_response_zh: 我们能怎么办？骑车回家了。那天晚上我躺在床上睡不着，突然发现我爸秘书家的客厅跟我们家一模一样。每件家具都一样。肯定是他给她买的。我哥告诉我妈，事情就闹大了。她收拾东西，我们搬走了。后来只有每个月收到他的支票时才听到他的消息。钱这块他倒是不含糊，这点我得承认。但我们不想见他。我是说，他肯定也不想见我们。他从没见过贝丝和奥利弗。他死的时候，感觉就像走个形式。
zh.internal_zh:
<internal>
[Perception] 他让我停留在事实和顺序上，好像如果我讲得够清楚，他就能看清全貌。最冲击我的是，当我大声说出来时，这一切听起来那么平常：开车、按门铃、糖果女士、家具、支票。而在那之下，是我终于努力想让他看见的东西——这不只是他严厉或疏远，这是背叛，然后整个生活都围绕着不去直视它而构建。我想让他看到，我父亲不是以戏剧性的方式缺席；他出现在每月的支票、手续、金钱里，而真正的家庭却被留下来承受伤害。

[Decision] 所以我直截了当地摆出来，几乎像呈递证据，因为我不知道还有什么别的办法能让人理解而不被它吞没。我讲了细节：他付钱，他不来看我们，他从没见过贝丝和奥利弗，他死的时候感觉像走程序。我想让治疗师最终看到它冰冷坚硬的轮廓——能抓住的东西那么少，以及我学会通过绕着说痛苦来保持距离。也许如果我讲得平淡，他就不会再以为有什么更温和的版本。
</internal>

context.speaker: client
context.text: My father was the dean of students and basketball coach at my middle school. He was in charge of every breath my brother and I took. When we did well, that's just what he expected of us. And when we screwed up, well, let's just say he was a man of limited sympathy.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: That's quite a lot to live up to.

context.speaker: client
context.text: You'd think that. The year I was in the seventh grade, he started taking long drives on the weekends by himself. My brother and I got on our bikes and we rode around the neighborhood, looking for his car. And we found it in the driveway of this little house. My brother made me ring the buzzer. The door opened, and there was my father's secretary, this nice lady who'd give us candy. Then my dad came out of her bathroom and started screaming at us.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: What did you guys do?

en_backup.therapist_turn: What did you guys do?
en_backup.client_response: What could we do? We got on our bikes and we rode home. And then I was lying awake that night in the bed and I realized my father's secretary's living room looked exactly like our living room. Every piece of furniture was exactly the same as ours. He must've bought it all for her. My brother told my mother and shit hit the fan. She packed us up and we left town. We only ever heard from him when he sent his check every month. He was good about the money, I'll give him that. But we didn't wanna see him. I mean, he sure didn't wanna see us. He never met Bess or Oliver. And when he died, it was like a formality.
en_backup.internal:
[Perception] He kept me in the facts and the sequence, like if I told it clearly enough he’d see the shape of it. The part that hit was how ordinary it all sounded when I said it out loud: the drives, the buzzer, the candy lady, the furniture, the checks. And underneath that was the thing I think I was finally trying to make visible — that this wasn’t just him being strict or remote, it was betrayal, and then a whole life organized around not looking at it too directly. I wanted him to see that my father wasn’t just absent in a dramatic way; he was there in the monthly check, in the formalities, in the money, while the actual family was left to absorb the damage.

[Decision] So I laid it out straight, almost like evidence, because I don’t know how else to make people understand it without getting swallowed by it. I said the details: he paid, he didn’t visit, he never met Bess or Oliver, and when he died it felt procedural. I wanted the therapist to finally see the hard, cold outline of it — how little there was to hold onto, and how I learned to keep my distance from the hurt by talking around it. Maybe if I said it plainly, he’d stop assuming there was some softer version of the story.

The plant is in trouble, the phones are exploding, and people are getting sick. If I’m not there, things fall apart. What felt wrong was the implication that I’m choosing work over her, or that I can just step away from this and be “all right.” He was missing the scale of the crisis and the fact that I’m the one holding it together.

[Decision] I need to correct that immediately. I’m not going to let him reduce this to me being absent or avoidant. I need him to understand that this is an emergency and that my place is with the company right now. So I push back and remind him: my daughter may manage, but the plants and everyone depending on me can’t. I’m the glue, and if I don’t go, everything gets worse.

If I let myself believe this is fixable, I’m just setting myself up to be disappointed again, and I don’t think I can take that. It feels safer to let it go numb, to stop pushing for certainty I’m probably never going to get. Because if I keep asking whether he loves me, and the answer is no, then there’s nothing left to protect. Better to assume the worst and be done with waiting.

[Decision] So I’m not going to let them steer this into some pep-talk about resilience or staying put for the long run. If they’re going to ignore the real problem, I’ll keep pushing back and naming what’s actually happening: the reward for competence is punishment. I need them to stop pretending this is just about my attitude and deal with the fact that the job is squeezing me dry.

zh.therapist_turn_zh: 很多书里说，在和朋友的关系中，我们有权选择分享什么。所以如果有些事你不想跟朋友说，可以告诉他们，他们应该也会接受。不过我也理解你不想重新联系朋友。
zh.client_response_zh: 他们会接受我，但我不愿意跟他们分享我的负面情绪。
zh.internal_zh:
<internal>
[Perception] 我听到她说重新联系朋友可能有用，但这件事戳中了我的羞耻感。他们也许能接受我，但我不希望他们看到我这个样子，或者知道我分手后有多破碎。分享我的负面情绪感觉像是在暴露一些太赤裸、太丢人的东西，我也不想把那种沉重带进我的友情。我仍然觉得，如果我以这种状态回到他们身边，我就再也不是他们认识的那个人了。

[Decision] 所以我在这里划条线：我不会跟我的朋友分享我的负面情绪。我想保护自己，不被评判、不被可怜、不成为别人的负担，我也不想让我的痛苦公开化，就为了让自己好受一点。如果这意味着我现在得保持距离，那我就这么做。
</internal>

[Perception] I hear that reconnecting with friends could help, but what it hits is my shame. They might accept me, but I don’t want them to see me like this or know how broken I feel after the breakup. I still feel like if I go back to them in this state, I won’t be the same person they know.

[Decision] So I’m drawing a line there: I will not share my negative mood with my friends. I want to protect myself from feeling judged, pitied, or like a burden, and I don’t want to make my pain public just to try to feel better. If that means I stay away for now, then that’s what I’ll do.

en_backup.internal:
[Perception] She’s hearing me make it sound like I’m talking about a child being doomed, but what hit me was the same old thing: that number, that stupid 87 percent, sitting there like a verdict. It lands right on the part of me that feels trapped between two terrible outcomes — cancer or a mutilation that doesn’t even promise safety. It all feels pre-decided, like I’m just waiting for my turn.

[Decision] I’m not going to let myself hope, because hope would mean I have to imagine choosing something and possibly losing anyway. If it’s fate, then at least I don’t have to fight with myself about it. I can stay numb, stay resigned, and not risk being disappointed by trying to control something that feels uncontrollable.

context_zh.speaker: client
context_zh.text: 嗯，你觉得呢？

context_zh.speaker: therapist

context_zh.text: 不……不，我说错了。你不是父亲。你是一个父亲。

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 尽管如此，你确实想和我们一起庆祝，你问我如果你怀孕了我是否会陪着你，然后你想象了我们私奔结婚。所以，如果你要组建新家庭，Mia，很可能你想让我也在场……在画面里或房间里。

zh.therapist_turn_zh: 尽管如此，你确实想和我们一起庆祝，你问我如果你怀孕了我是否会陪着你，然后你想象了我们私奔结婚。所以，如果你要组建新家庭，Mia，很可能你想让我也在场……在画面里或房间里。
zh.client_response_zh: 我们现在就在这儿。
zh.internal_zh:
<internal>
[Perception] 他在点破我一直在绕来绕去、努力不说出口的事：这不只是实际层面的问题。我可以雇人帮忙，可以负担更大的房子，可以把实际的方面安排好。真正让我难受的是做这件事的时候身边没有人，哪怕只是在想象里，我也想让他出现在画面里。当他说出那句话，它击中了。它让孤独变得真实，不再是那种我能一直躲着的东西。

[Decision] 所以我没再反驳。我就在这儿，不再假装这只是关于有没有准备好。我愿意留在这个对话里，说出我真正想要的，哪怕它很尴尬、很痛苦。如果我要做一个关于家庭的决定，我需要面对自己是否能接受独自承担这件事——我愿意在这儿面对，而不是逃开。
</internal>

[Perception] He’s naming the thing I keep circling around and trying not to say out loud: that this isn’t just about logistics. I can hire help, I can afford a bigger place, I can figure out the practical side. What really hurts is the idea of doing this without anyone beside me, and of wanting him in the picture even if only in my imagination. When he said that, it landed. It made the loneliness feel real instead of something I could keep dodging.

[Decision] So I stopped arguing with it. I’m here, and I’m not going to keep pretending this is only about being prepared. I’m willing to stay with this conversation and tell the truth about what I want, even if it’s embarrassing and painful. If I’m going to make a family decision, I need to face whether I can accept doing it alone — and I’m willing to work that through here rather than run from it.

zh.internal_zh:
<internal>
[Perception] 治疗师问我心里在想什么，这直接把我带到那些我通常会打理得井井有条、说“处理好了”的旧事门口。这个问题击中了我心里那个还想弄明白的部分——背叛到底会不会永久改变一个人，还是说真的有可能从另一边走出来，变得没事。如果我直接说自己的事，我就得承认这里还有个谜团：事情有多少是因为她，有多少是因为我，以及真正能保护我以后不再受伤的是什么。我还注意到，我很好奇治疗师有没有这方面的真实经历，因为我在判断他们能不能理解出轨、离婚、共同抚养孩子这一整套情况，还是只会泛泛而谈。

[Decision] 所以我决定先问问治疗师的经历。一部分是想看看他们能不能共情，一部分是想试探这场谈话安不安全、值不值得敞开心扉。如果他们经历过类似的事，也许他们能理解其中的复杂性，我就不用一下子把所有事都摊开。如果他们没经历过，那我还可以决定要拿出多少自己的事来说。这是我保持控制同时又把对话往前推的方式。
</internal>

en_backup.client_response: Have you experienced your partner cheating on you?
en_backup.internal:
[Perception] The therapist asked what’s on my mind, and that puts me right at the doorway of the old stuff I usually keep tidy and “handled.” The question lands on the part of me that still wants to figure out whether betrayal is something that changes a person permanently, or whether it’s really possible to come out the other side and be okay. If I talk about myself directly, I might have to admit there’s still a puzzle here: how much of what happened was about her, how much was about me, and what actually protects me from getting hurt again. I also noticed I’m curious about whether the therapist has any real-life reference point for this, because I’m trying to gauge whether they’ll understand the whole cheating/divorce/co-parenting situation or just talk in generalities.

[Decision] So I decided to ask about the therapist’s experience first. Partly to see if they can relate, partly to test whether this conversation is safe and worth opening up in. If they’ve been through something similar, maybe they’ll get the complexity without me having to lay everything out all at once. And if they haven’t, then I can still decide how much of my own stuff I want to put on the table. It’s my way of staying in control while still moving the conversation forward.
