en_backup.internal:
[Perception] What I heard was her turning my frustration into some kind of strategic maneuver, like I'm sitting here plotting or “making moves” instead of actually trying to ask for help. That felt off because what’s happening is simpler and more humiliating than that: I already feel on the back foot, and every time she circles back to why I left or what I felt before, it sounds like she’s building a case against me. It hits the part of me that feels judged as disloyal, immature, or disappointing, and then she talks like I’m being manipulative for reacting to it.

[Decision] I decided I needed to push back on that framing right away. I didn’t want her to keep treating my response like some kind of game or hidden agenda, because that lets her avoid the actual point: I’m telling her this feels accusatory and makes it harder to be here. So I challenged her wording, to force the conversation back to what’s actually happening between us instead of accepting her interpretation as if it were neutral.

</internal>

en_backup.client_response: We've been running together for a long time, between six and 10 miles... Depending on whether one of us is on his period. Only this time i chalenged him a little. There's no real good running in the middle east. Not for the US military, unless you want a roadside bomb to blow your balls off. So I wanted to do some serious running. I said, let's go for 15. Then after 15 miles, I said, 20. Now he didn't want it, but I said, okay, i'll go on my own. So he followed. I said, You know, only six more and it's a marathon. Let's do it. He wanted to stop. en_backup.internal:
[Perception] The therapist wasn’t letting me stay in the joke or the trash talk. He wanted the actual person in the story, not just “my fairy friend” or the running numbers. So I laid out the whole thing: Daniel and I always run hard, this time I pushed it way past what he wanted, and I kept escalating because I wanted to see how far we could go. I wanted the therapist to see that it wasn’t just a run — it was me testing him, testing myself, and not backing off even when he was clearly done. 

[Decision] So I told it straight, from six to ten miles to fifteen to twenty to marathon, because I wanted him to understand what I did before he starts talking about feelings. I’m not trying to look weak in here. I’m trying to show that I’m still the guy who can push, lead, and keep going. If Daniel can’t hang, that’s on him. But I know I’m the one who took it too far, and I’m trying to get that across without sounding soft.

context_zh.text: 另外，要是他们当中有人先动手打我怎么办？

context_zh.text: 你在这个问题上还需要更多建议吗？或者你还有其他担心？霸凌者是问题，不是你。有没有人能跟你一起面对他们，给你支持？

context_zh.text: 有。在我们结束前再给点建议吧。我有我未婚夫支持我。

zh.therapist_turn_zh: 你在这个问题上还需要更多建议吗？或者你还有其他担心？霸凌者是问题，不是你。有没有人能跟你一起面对他们，给你支持？
zh.client_response_zh: 我就想知道我怎么才能跟那些霸凌者对抗。
zh.internal_zh:
<internal>
[Perception] 他们一直在给那种宽泛、显而易见的建议，比如“叫他们停手”和“找支持”，但根本没回答我真正害怕的部分：如果他们发火或者打我怎么办。感觉他们根本没听明白这事儿有多危险，或者我有多走投无路。我早就知道霸凌者是问题。我需要的是真实、安全的东西，不是在咨询室里听着好听的一句套话。这让我觉得他们太敷衍了，根本没理解我面对的到底是什么。

[Decision] 我打算无视那些空洞的建议，继续追问更实际的东西，因为我仍然需要帮助，而且他们给的远远不够。我不想就重复一句“霸凌者是问题”然后就算了。我想要一个真正保护自己、不让情况更糟的办法，所以我不会把他们的回答当成是够用了。
</internal>

context.speaker: client
context.text: Thank you. That is good. I feel I am depressed because I have been bullied and it is still continuing today.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: I am sorry to hear that. How can I help you deal with the bullies? Can you stand up to them in a safe way?

context.speaker: client
context.text: Well, to be honest, dealing with these bullies are pretty tough, Is there a safe way I can handle them?

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: I understand your concern, but I feel you have to tell them that you do not deserve to be bullied and they need to stop now.

context.speaker: client
context.text: Okay. I will do that. Thank you.

context.speaker: client
context.text: Also, what if one of the bullies starts a fight with me?

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: Do you need any more advice on this matter or do you have any other concerns? The bully is the problem, not you. Do you have anyone who can stand up to them with you for support?

context.speaker: client
context.text: I do. One more piece of advice before we part ways. I have my fiance for support.

en_backup.therapist_turn: Do you need any more advice on this matter or do you have any other concerns? The bully is the problem, not you. Do you have anyone who can stand up to them with you for support?
en_backup.client_response: I would want to know how I can stand up to these bullies.
en_backup.internal:
[Perception] They keep giving me broad, obvious advice like “tell them to stop” and “have support,” but that does not actually answer the part I’m scared of: what happens if they get angry or try to fight me. It feels like they’re not really hearing how dangerous this could be or how trapped I feel. I already know the bullies are the problem. What I need is something real and safe, not a simple line that sounds good in a session. That made me feel like they were being too generic, like they didn’t fully get what I’m up against.

[Decision] I’m going to push past the vague advice and keep asking for something more practical, because I still need help and I’m not getting enough from this. I don’t want to just repeat “the bully is the problem” and leave it there. I want an actual way to protect myself without making things worse, so I’m not going to treat their answer as sufficient.

He was asking whether I’m actually letting the reality of it land, or whether I’m hiding behind “options” so I don’t have to feel how serious this is. [Decision] I need to stop using alternatives as a way to avoid the fear underneath all this. I can still want control and have preferences, but I have to face that this is real. So I said it plainly: I know I have cancer. That’s me admitting the truth, not surrendering my judgment. It’s me starting from reality instead of from resistance.

[Perception] I heard the “opportunity for growth” part, and all I could think was: growth doesn’t help when your whole life just got ripped apart. It hit the part of me that still has to get up tomorrow and keep functioning while feeling like everything I built was for nothing. The idea of “starting over” lands like proof that I lost too much time, and that I’m already behind in a way I can’t fix.

[Decision] I’m shutting that hope down because hoping feels dangerous right now. If I let myself believe I can rebuild, then I also have to face the possibility that I can’t, and I can’t take that hit. So I’m going back to the story that I’m too old and something must be wrong with me — at least that explanation keeps me from reaching for something I’ll just lose again.

So when he says “other things,” I hear a question: if I cannot change the larger situation, what exactly is left? That is the puzzle. I keep feeling as if I am only observing my life from the outside, but perhaps he is asking whether I am mistaken about how little choice I have.

[Decision] I decided to press him for specifics, because if he wants me to consider change, I need to know what kind of change he means. I cannot accept vague advice. I need the problem reduced to something concrete: what can be changed, where, and at what cost? If it is something that threatens my dignity or depends on money I do not have, then it is not really an option. So I ask, “Other things, meaning what?” to force the idea into a form I can examine instead of drifting in this helpless feeling.

zh.internal_zh:

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 啊，这种人最难应付。要是太过了，你跟你老婆有没有考虑过搬走？

zh.therapist_turn_zh: 啊，这种人最难应付。要是太过了，你跟你老婆有没有考虑过搬走？

zh.internal_zh:
<internal>
[Perception] 他抓住了“搬走”这个点，好像那真是个选项似的，而且刚好戳中我最不愿意放弃的东西：我的房子，我的地，我经营起来的整个局面。我还觉得他在把我引向一个方向，好像这事是个大问题，我非得把生活连根拔起去解决，但对我来说这顶多就是个烦人的邻里琐事。我不想被他推着去讨论放弃这个院子，或者承认我搞不定。

[Decision] 我要直接堵住这条路，简单明了。不，我不会搬，也没什么好绕圈的。我想保护我建立起来的生活，不想让这事变成一场讨论要不要放弃我的家，或者把我的情况说得好像很严重。
</internal>

[Perception] He latched onto the part about “moving away” like that was a real option, and it hit the one thing I’m not willing to give up: my house, my land, the whole setup I’ve built. It also felt like he was steering me toward making this into some big problem I’m supposed to uproot my life for, when to me it’s mostly just an annoying neighborhood thing. I don’t want to get pushed into talking about giving up the compound or admitting I can’t handle it.

[Decision] I’m going to shut that line down and keep it simple. No, I’m not moving, and there’s no point circling around that. I want to protect the life I’ve built and not let this turn into a discussion about surrendering my home or making my situation sound more dire than it is.

[Decision] 所以我说“我不知道”，这样我不用承诺什么我不确定能不能做到的事。它保护我，让我不用保证能修复什么，也保护我内心里那个还觉得亲近应该自然发生，不该靠我去硬拉的地方。只要我含糊着，就不用承认我害怕主动伸手，怕发现其实也没剩多少感情了。
</internal>

zh.internal_zh:

I already know how this gets twisted when people decide there’s “something in it.” That’s the part that hits me: not the pictures, but the idea that my own memory and intention don’t count unless it fits his interpretation.

[Decision] I’m not going there. I’m not going to say there was some secret meaning in those pictures just because that’s what he wants to hear. I’m not going to turn my own experience into evidence for somebody else’s story. If he wants “the truth,” then the truth is that I was a kid doing a school project, and my mother reacted badly. That’s it. I’m drawing the line there because I’m not letting him make me betray what I actually remember or pretend I saw something I didn’t.

[Perception] 他一直逼我把话说完，正好撞上我不想碰的那块。感觉他让我站在那个我消失的地方，没法再用含糊、开玩笑或者“我想聊点别的”来躲。我觉得被逼到墙角了。那个“溜走的感觉”说起来好像很小事，但其实是想被人喜欢、安全，但又不想被完全看见。他不让我绕开的时候，我觉得暴露了，还有点生气，好像他不明白我多需要另一扇门离开。

[Decision] 所以我就问他女儿。我问她是因为我想把压力从我身上挪到更安全、更人畜无害的地方。我也想看看他会不会让我进去一点，在他那儿接住我，而不是让我继续扒在我自己的事情边缘。我不想再旁敲侧击或者绕圈子了。我想要个喘息，也想有连接，但不用承认我害怕自己要说的话。直接问比继续躲闪、假装我只是好奇要容易。
</internal>

context.text: You don't get it.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: What don't I get?

context.speaker: client
context.text: The slipping away thing. It's a girl thing, The wanting to be liked. To be there, but not to be there. It's like... Can we talk about something else?

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: Finish the thought.

context.speaker: client
context.text: No, I wanna talk about something else.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: Okay, What would you like to talk about then?

en_backup.therapist_turn: Okay, What would you like to talk about then?
en_backup.client_response: How's your daughter?
en_backup.internal:
[Perception] He kept pushing me to finish the thought, and that landed right on the part I was trying not to touch. It felt like he was asking me to stand still in the exact place where I disappear, where I can’t hide behind being vague or funny or “just wanting something else.” I could feel myself getting cornered. The “slipping away” thing is hard because it sounds small, but it’s really about wanting to be liked and safe without being fully seen. When he wouldn’t let me move away from it, I felt exposed and a little angry, like he wasn’t getting how much I needed a different door out.

[Decision] So I went to his daughter. I asked about her because I wanted the pressure off me and onto something safer and more human. I also wanted to see if he’d let me in a little, if he’d meet me there instead of making me stay on the edge of my own stuff. I didn’t want to keep hinting or circling. I wanted a break, and I wanted connection without having to admit I was scared of what I was about to say. Asking directly felt easier than trying to keep dodging and pretending I was just curious.

If I focus on whether it’s hard to do and how it works, I can avoid the bigger argument about my friends not respecting my distance and the fact that virtual contact still feels like a poor substitute.

[Perception] My therapist is asking me to look at the relationship itself, not just the blow-up with my friend or the awkwardness with my ex. What stands out is that this is not straightforward: he broke up with me, then stayed in my orbit, then said “friends,” then asked me out again. That pattern makes me think his intentions are unclear on purpose or at least not fully settled. I’m noticing I’m still trying to figure out whether this is him actually wanting me back or just liking the attention and access without committing. The part that hits hardest is that I don’t want to be in a situation where I’m waiting around decoding signals while he keeps the comfort of me being available.

[Decision] I’m deciding that I need clarity, not hints. If he wants a real relationship, he should say that directly and act like it. If he can’t do that, then I’m going to protect myself by not treating this like a relationship in progress. I’m weighing whether I should ask him plainly what he wants, because that would force the issue and stop me from guessing. I don’t want to keep reopening the door just because I hope he means something more. If he’s serious, he can be clear; if not, I need to step back instead of getting pulled into games.

context_zh.text: 那太好了。在这种时候保持人际联系很健康。我难过的时候就会和朋友搞个虚拟 happy hour。

context_zh.speaker: client
context_zh.text: 听起来不错。

zh.internal_zh:
<internal>
[Perception] 他们一直在暗示我没事，因为我还能跟一个朋友聊天，或者因为“大家”都很难。但那根本触及不到我痛的那个点。我真正错过的，是我以为我现在会过的整个大学生活——那些日常的、随性的、让一切感觉真实的东西。听到“这很健康”“那总是有帮助的”，反而让我的感受变得渺小了，好像我应该感激一些残渣剩饭，而我自己还在眼睁睁看着整个生活在别处进行。这戳中了那个觉得被困在家里、而生活正在他处展开的我。

[Decision] 所以我干脆不再指望这件事很快会有什么不同。如果我一直希望它不再痛，只会一次次失望。接受自己难过、接受这就是我现在的处境，比不断追寻一个我其实根本实现不了的更好版本要容易。我不想再假装我可以“正常过日子”了，当我觉得我根本没过上什么生活。还不如就此打住，省得一直希望，然后觉得自己像个傻子。
</internal>

context.speaker: client
context.text: With covid and everything, college hasn't been the same at all. I'm missing out on a lot of experiences and that makes me sad.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: I can imagine, it's so tough right now for everyone. You aren'y alone. Are you in school or at home?

context.speaker: client
context.text: I'm currently a sophomore in college but I'm on break so I am at home.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: Are you able to connect with friends while on break even virtually? That always helps!

context.speaker: client
context.text: Yes. thankfully my friend and I from college facetime around 3 times a week

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: That's so great. It's so healthy to keep up human contact in these times. When i am feeling sad, I do a virtual happy hour with my friends.

context.speaker: client
context.text: That sounds fun

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: It is! IS there anything else bothering you?

en_backup.therapist_turn: It is! IS there anything else bothering you?
en_backup.client_response: I just wish I wouldn't be so sad about missing things. I wish I could just live my life ya know
en_backup.internal:
[Perception] They keep trying to make it sound like I’m okay because I still talk to a friend or because “everyone” is having a hard time, but that doesn’t touch the part that hurts. What I’m actually missing is the whole college life I thought I’d be living right now—the normal stuff, the spontaneous stuff, the stuff that makes it feel real. Hearing “it’s healthy” and “that always helps” just makes it feel smaller, like I’m supposed to be grateful for scraps when I’m still watching the whole thing pass me by. It hits the part of me that feels stuck at home while my life is happening somewhere else.

[Decision] So I’m just going to stop expecting this to feel different anytime soon. If I keep hoping it’ll stop hurting, I’ll just keep getting let down. It feels easier to accept that I’m sad and that this is what my life is right now than to keep reaching for some better version of it that I can’t actually make happen. I don’t want to keep pretending I can “just live my life” when it feels like I’m not really getting one. Better to shut that down than keep hoping and feeling stupid for it.

</internal>

<internal>
[Perception] 他一直逼我，好像我该交出什么东西似的。“怎么了？”“你为什么摇头？”好像我得把自己变得让他能读懂。然后他直接捅到压力那事上，戳中了我最不想被碰的地方——那个已经被逼到角落、被盯着看的部分。噪音很大，因为我他妈很生气，而且我正努力不让他看到任何真实的东西。左撇子这事给了我一个更安全的关注点，把注意力放到看得见的事情上，而不是他拼命想从我这里挖出来的那些东西。

[Perception] He kept pushing like there was something I was supposed to hand over. “What is it?” “Why are you shaking your head?” Like I’m supposed to make myself readable for him. Then he went straight at it with the pressure thing, and that hit the part I don’t want touched — the part that already feels cornered and watched. The static is loud because I’m pissed off and trying not to show him anything real. And the left-handed thing gave me somewhere safer to put my attention, on something observable instead of whatever he’s trying to drag out of me.

[Decision] I gave him the smallest thing that still counted as an answer because that’s the safest way through this. If I say more, he’ll start making it mean something, and then I’m stuck either agreeing or fighting him. I’d rather keep it short, keep control, and let him have the noise instead of the rest of me. The less I say, the less he gets to use.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: The pandemic has been hard on many people, those in relationships and those looking for new ones! Have you tried to develop a new hobby or interest that you can do with others once the pandemic is over?

context.speaker: client
context.text: Well, I've been writing enough poetry to publish a book, so I'll certainly do that. I know the pandemic has been rough for everyone. Hopefully my doctor will say I qualify for the vaccine soon.

en_backup.therapist_turn: The pandemic has been hard on many people, those in relationships and those looking for new ones! Have you tried to develop a new hobby or interest that you can do with others once the pandemic is over?
en_backup.client_response: Getting my stimulus check in the next week or so would certainly make me a bit happier, too.
en_backup.internal:
[Perception] They’re trying to make this about “finding hobbies” and future social stuff, but what’s really loud in my head is how stuck I am right now. I miss my friends, I miss being around people in person, and I’m also waiting on the vaccine and money so I can even think about anything safely or practically. The poetry thing is what I can actually do today, and it feels more concrete than talking about future hobbies when I’m still boxed in by the pandemic and my disability.

[Decision] So I went to what felt safer and more real: my poems, my doctor, my stimulus check. That’s the stuff I can hold onto without pretending I’m ready to fix the loneliness part yet. If I stay with those practical things, I don’t have to sit in the uncomfortable feeling that I’m isolated and don’t know how to change it.

context_zh.speaker: client
context_zh.text: 没有！满脑子都是她，我爱她，真希望她没做过那种事。

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 你觉得你们还能复合吗？还有希望吗？她愿意和你一起努力，弥补她的错误吗？

zh.therapist_turn_zh: 你觉得你们还能复合吗？还有希望吗？她愿意和你一起努力，弥补她的错误吗？
zh.client_response_zh: 我希望我们能，但我就是忘不掉。
zh.internal_zh:
<internal>
[Perception] 她在问我有没有希望，能不能复合，好像这件事我可以凭决定就做到似的。但我脑子里一直响的都是我发现的那一刻，我感觉整个人都被撕碎了。再信任她，感觉根本不可能。哪怕试着想象和她在一起的未来，胸口都会发紧。这正好戳中了我已经破碎、已经厌倦了拼命撑下去的那部分。

[Decision] 我觉得我现在什么都做不了，没法强迫自己抱有希望，也没法让这件事在脑子里停止回放。所以我只能就这么待着，哪怕感觉糟透了，因为试图修复它或想象什么出路都没有意义。比起继续期待一个答案然后又受伤，不如干脆放弃寻找答案来得容易。
</internal>

[Decision] So I just shut it down. I said I didn’t love my dad because it feels safer to make it flat and final than to keep hoping and finding out I’m wrong. zh.therapist_turn_zh: 不，其实不怎么亲。
zh.client_response_zh: 为什么不是？
zh.internal_zh:
<internal>
[Perception] 他说他父亲去世了，但又说他们其实不怎么亲近，这在我脑子里拼不到一块儿。要是不亲近，为什么感觉这事挺大的？而且他能这么平静地讲出来，我该怎么理解——是我漏掉了什么，还是他故意说得含糊在保护我？我一听到就马上想，他跟他爸的距离是不是就像他在这里保持的距离一样，也许他就是这么对人。这让我怀疑他到底能给我什么样的支持，我是不是看错他了。

[Decision] 我问“为什么不是？”是因为我想知道缺掉的那块。我在试图弄明白这里的规则：什么算亲近，什么算在乎，他的回答是不是透露了他的某些东西，而我在更信任他之前需要知道。如果他打算保持情感疏离，我需要现在就搞明白，而不是以后瞎猜。如果他不跟父亲亲近是有原因的，也许他对我小心翼翼也是有原因的。我在试图解开这个谜，免得再往前走一步然后被打个措手不及。
</internal>

en_backup.therapist_turn: No, not really.
en_backup.client_response: Why not?
en_backup.internal:
[Perception] He said his father died, but then he also said they weren’t really close, which doesn’t fit together cleanly in my head. If they weren’t close, why does it feel like such a big thing? And if he can talk about it so calmly, what am I supposed to make of that—did I miss something, or is he protecting me by keeping it vague? I heard that and immediately wondered whether his distance from his father is somehow like the distance he keeps here, like maybe that’s just how he handles people. That makes me question what kind of support he can actually give, and whether I’m reading him wrong.

[Decision] I asked “Why not?” because I want the missing piece. I’m trying to figure out the rules here: what counts as closeness, what counts as caring, and whether his answer means something about him that I need to know before I trust him more. If he’s going to be emotionally detached, I need to understand that now instead of guessing later. If there’s a reason he wasn’t close to his father, maybe there’s a reason he’s careful with me too. I’m trying to solve that puzzle before I step any further in and get blindsided.

What really hit was the image of “real life” starting again — because that’s what I’ve been waiting on. Not some abstract future, but the actual normal stuff: class in person, doing the work with my hands, seeing people, having a beer at a bar like before. The unresolved puzzle is whether I’m supposed to just endure this weird holding pattern, or if there’s some way to keep moving toward my trade even while everything’s still half-broken.

[Decision] I decided to keep my eye on the return to normal, but not pretend this setup is good. I want to believe the vaccine and the lockdown ending actually mean something, because otherwise this year feels like a total loss. At the same time, if I just sit there stewing, I’m going to go nuts. So my best move is probably to keep my head down, do what I can with school, and hang onto the idea that this isn’t permanent — that there will be a point when I can get back to doing it for real. That’s the only thing that makes the waiting feel survivable.

en_backup.internal:
[Perception] She kept sounding like she was skipping over how awful this was and jumping straight to “move on” advice. First it was “maybe that’s not all bad,” then “have a glass of wine and celebrate you,” like this is some breakup movie where I just need a pep talk. It hit the part of me that feels blindsided and kind of humiliated — I’m trying to say I’m scared and untangling ten years of my life, and she’s acting like I should either wait for him to come back or toast to being single. It made her feel a little careless, like she wasn’t really taking in how messy and insulting this actually is.

[Decision] So I’m not going to hand her the soft, vulnerable version of this. If she’s going to keep brushing past the real hurt, I’d rather keep it practical and a little detached. I’ll talk about being alone, the logistics, the cat, whatever — anything but let her turn this into some neat little self-love moment. I don’t need another person telling me what I “deserve” like that solves the fact that I got blindsided and have to rebuild my whole life.

I’m not giving up the question; I’m shifting back toward the safer ground he wants, while keeping the real puzzle in play. en_backup.internal:
[Perception] She wanted me to keep going, to put the car back in my face and make it real. That hit the part where everything goes blank and I can feel my throat tighten again. If I start describing it, I might have to admit what it felt like inside the bike, inside my body, and that it wasn't just an accident — that something in me was already going toward death. [Decision] So I gave her almost nothing. “I don't remember” is safer. It shuts the door without sounding like I'm shutting her out, and it keeps me from falling back into that moment. If I stay brief, I don't have to feel it, and I don't have to say the worst part out loud: that some part of me wanted to disappear.

en_backup.internal:
[Perception] She’s telling me to step away and focus on healing, like I can just put my life on pause. But that hits right at the part I can’t ignore: my family depends on me. My siblings are struggling, my parents aren’t in great health, and if I back off, who picks up the slack? It feels like she’s asking me to choose my pain over their stability, and I can’t do that.

[Decision] No — I’m not leaving my obligations behind. I can’t afford to stop being the one who holds things together. My breakup hurts, but my responsibilities are real, and if I step away, people I care about could suffer. I’ll deal with the loss while still showing up, because that’s what has to happen.

[Decision] 我要把这事放在“它很不幸，但未必对我或所有人有巨大含义”的盒子里。这样我就能保持冷静，不至于崩溃。也许她就是选择不沟通，这很粗鲁也让人失望，但没必要现在把它变成什么改变人生的大判断。
</internal>

context_zh.text: 我没那么想。但你父亲一直是你重要的慰藉。只要你还是他的宝贝，你就永远不会孤单。我感觉这种紧密的联系并不完全舒服。

zh.therapist_turn_zh: 我没那么想。但你父亲一直是你重要的慰藉。只要你还是他的宝贝，你就永远不会孤单。我感觉这种紧密的联系并不完全舒服。
zh.client_response_zh: 你什么意思？
zh.internal_zh:
<internal>
[Perception] 他没说我父亲对我做过什么性方面的事。他说的是这种联结本身对我有作用——当他的宝贝让我不再感到孤独。这话说到我心坎上了，因为这让我想到为什么我一直被那些得不到的男人吸引。也许不是因为他们在某种普通意义上“更好”。也许是因为被选中的感觉，就像那种联结一直让我感到安全和特别。但我不确定他是不是对的，因为这听起来像是要我放弃唯一一直稳定的关系。

[Decision] 在同意之前，我得先搞清楚他到底什么意思。如果关键是我在重复一个模式，那我想知道我到底在重复什么——是婚姻的部分、得不到的部分、还是当别人宝贝的部分。我还没准备好说我父亲有问题，但我可以承认，在最紧密的联结中感到最安全，和我选择那些我根本没法拥有的男人之间可能有联系。我想继续搞清楚我是在保护自己，还是只是原地踏步。
</internal>

context.speaker: client
context.text: The problem is I can't find anybody as good as him. You think there's something wrong with that , don't you?

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: For one thing, your father's married to your mother. Do you think there's any connection between that and your picking married men?

context.speaker: client
context.text: I said that I was done with that.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: You did, but you also asked me what that pattern was about.

context.speaker: client
context.text: Now you're gonna tell me that my father molested me? Because he didn't.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: I didn't think that. But your father has been an essential comfort for you. For as long as you are his favorite, you won't ever be alone. I'm getting the feeling that the tight bond isn't entirely comfortable.

en_backup.therapist_turn: I didn't think that. But your father has been an essential comfort for you. For as long as you are his favorite, you won't ever be alone. I'm getting the feeling that the tight bond isn't entirely comfortable.
en_backup.client_response: What do you mean?
en_backup.internal:
[Perception] He’s not saying my father did something sexual. He’s saying the bond itself is doing something for me — that being his favorite keeps me from feeling alone. That lands because it makes me think about why I keep getting pulled toward unavailable men. Maybe it’s not about them being “better” in some normal sense. Maybe it’s about the feeling of being chosen, the way that bond has always made me feel secure and special. But I don’t know if he’s right, because that sounds like he’s asking me to give up the one relationship that has always been steady.

[Decision] I need to understand what he means before I agree with it. If the point is that I’m repeating a pattern, then I want to know what exactly I’m repeating — the marriage part, the being unavailable part, or the being someone’s favorite part. I’m not ready to say my father is the problem, but I can admit there may be a connection between feeling safest in a tight bond and choosing men I can’t really have. I want to keep figuring out whether I’m protecting myself or just staying stuck.

context_zh.speaker: client
context_zh.text: 我睡在办公室。白天我们都装作没事，但到了晚上，我……我就睡在沙发上。

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 从什么时候开始的？

context_zh.speaker: client
context_zh.text: 最近四个晚上。我带了毯子和衣服过去。

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 孩子们怎么看这件事？

context_zh.speaker: client
context_zh.text: 罗茜星期二没回家。她说她会晚回来，但……早上的时候她不在。她说她在某个朋友家过夜。伊恩大学放了一周假。他连电话都没打，也没回来。昨天我下班回来，凯特宣布说……你知道，嘿，我要出去。我说，行，你爱干嘛干嘛。然后……我去做晚饭，厨房里什么吃的都没有。我打开冰箱一看……空的。连个鸡蛋都没有。我和麦克斯叫了披萨，然后哄他睡觉。我本来打算睡在办公室，后来又想：万一出事怎么办？你知道？他一个人在楼上，孤零零的。我……实在没法睡在那间卧室里。哪怕为了他我也做不到。我觉得那间卧室有点……恶心。我睡了一会儿，不知道几点，然后……我醒来听到一个声音叫“爸爸”。麦克斯就在那，你知道，就站在门口。他问我能不能陪他睡……我说，当然。他自从五岁以后就没这样过。我猜，这就是你问题的答案：孩子们什么都知道。总之，她三天后就走了……也许这样最好，真的。

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 怎么就是最好了？

context_zh.speaker: client
context_zh.text: 不是最好。简直是噩梦。

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 很痛苦。但在某种程度上，你自由了……可以去处理……你和劳拉之间的事了。

zh.therapist_turn_zh: 很痛苦。但在某种程度上，你自由了……可以去处理……你和劳拉之间的事了。
zh.client_response_zh: 我想要我老婆为了一个销售员离开我？
zh.internal_zh:
<internal>
[Perception] 他试图把我的生活变成一个干净的治疗故事——好像因为凯特要走了，我就该把这看作“自由”，也许我应该坦然接受和劳拉继续下去。这正好戳中了最糟糕的部分：羞辱。不光是我老婆出轨，而是我居然要冷静地接受被一个销售员抢走，然后表现得好像这是个机会。这话听起来好像问题出在我的态度，而不是她做的事。

[Decision] 不。我不会把这称为自由，也不会假装我想要任何一部分。我不会把被背叛重写成一个整洁的下一步，就因为在这里更容易谈。我的立场很简单：我不会参与让这件事变得“好起来”。我不会粉饰它，也不会同意那种我应该为此感恩或者走向劳拉就是自然答案的想法。不是的。这是噩梦，我不会把它变成进步。
</internal>

context.speaker: client
context.text: I sleep in the office. During the day, we act like everything is fine, but at night, I'm... I'm on the couch.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: Since when?

context.speaker: client
context.text: Last four nights. I brought in my blankets and my clothes.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: How are the kids taking this?

context.speaker: client
context.text: Rosie didn't come home on Tuesday. Said she'd be back late, but... In the morning, she wasn't there. She said she slept over at some friend's. Ian had a week off from college. He didn't even call, didn't come back. Got back after work yesterday and Kate announced that... you know, Hey, I'm going out. I said, Fine, do whatever you want. So... I went to make dinner and... There's no food in the kitchen. I went to the fridge, I look in... Nothing. Not even an egg. Max and I ordered pizzas, then I put him to bed. I was gonna sleep in the office, then I thought: What if something happens? You know? He's upstairs by himself, he's all alone. I... couldn't bring myself to sleep in that bedroom. Not even for his sake. I find that bedroom kind of... repulsive. I was asleep for while. I don't know what time it was, and... I wake up and I hear this voice saying, Daddy. And Max is there, you know, just standing at the door. He asked me if I could sleep with him and... I said, Sure. He hasn't done that since he was 5 years old. My guess, that's the answer to your question: is the kids know everything. Anyway, she's leaving in 3 days, and... Probably for the best, really.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: How is it for the best?

context.speaker: client
context.text: It's not for the best. It's a nightmare.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: It's painful. But in a way, you're free... to go through... whatever it is with Laura.

en_backup.therapist_turn: It's painful. But in a way, you're free... to go through... whatever it is with Laura.
en_backup.client_response: I wanted my wife to leave me for a salesman?
en_backup.internal:
[Perception] He’s trying to turn my life into some kind of clean, therapeutic story — like because Kate is leaving, I should see this as “freedom” and maybe I should be okay moving on with Laura. That lands right on the worst part of it: the humiliation. Not just that my wife cheated, but that I’m supposed to calmly accept being left for some salesman and then act like this is some opportunity. It makes it sound like the problem is my attitude, not what she did.

[Decision] No. I’m not going to call this freedom, and I’m not going to pretend I want any part of it. I’m not going to rewrite being betrayed into some neat next step just because that’s easier to talk about in here. My line is simple: I will not participate in making this okay. I won’t dress it up, and I won’t go along with the idea that I should be grateful for it or move toward Laura like that’s the natural answer. It’s not. It’s a nightmare, and I’m not turning that into progress.

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 你父亲去世前，你跟他说上话了吗？

zh.therapist_turn_zh: 你父亲去世前，你跟他说上话了吗？
zh.client_response_zh: 你知道，对男人来说，失去就是……一种失败。在比赛或打架中，输了会让你生气。你想跟那个人扯平。就像那个起诉我的人，亚历克斯的父亲。这家伙气到满脑子只想找我算账。好像那样能有用似的。
zh.internal_zh:
<internal>
[Perception] 他问我有没有在父亲去世前跟他说上话，而我意识到我一直绕着没说出来的事：我没得到最重要的东西。不是那次对话，不是那种完结感，不是一个干净的结束。只有这场拖泥带水、丑陋的后续，我还得从中找出意义，可它根本感觉不到任何意义。听到自己谈论男人、失败和扯平，听起来可怜又毫无意义——好像失去这件事，男人根本没能力应对，包括我在内。如果这是真的，那这里就没有隐藏的答案。只有伤害。

[Decision] 所以我决定不再去够他试图引导我去的地方。待在这种冷嘲热讽里更安全，因为它对我没有任何要求。如果我让自己相信有办法处理好这件事，那我就得面对自己做得有多糟糕、有多么无知、有多么暴露。还是保持硬气，保持泛泛而谈，谈男人女人和官司这些吧。这样我就不用承认自己迷失了，或者我可能没法修复这件事，或者说也许根本就没法修复。
</internal>

context.speaker: client
context.text: Women really liked my dad, as you know. Then too, women live longer than men so when you get to a certain age, there are always going to be more women at funerals. You know what I've decided? Women are really good at loss. Men don't really... They haven't got a fucking clue.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: Did you get to speak to your father before he died?

en_backup.therapist_turn: Did you get to speak to your father before he died?
en_backup.client_response: You know, for men loss is... It's a defeat. In a game or a fight, losing makes you mad. You want to get even with the guy. Like this man who's suing me, Alex's father. This guy is so angry that all he can think of is coming after me. Like that's gonna help.
en_backup.internal:
[Perception] He asked whether I got to speak to my father before he died, and what landed was the obvious thing I’ve been circling around without saying it: I didn’t get what mattered most. Not the conversation, not the closure, not the clean ending. Just this dragged-out, ugly aftermath where I’m supposed to make meaning out of something that doesn’t feel meaningful at all. And hearing myself talk about men, defeat, and getting even, it all sounded pathetic and pointless — like the whole terrain of loss is something men are simply unequipped for, including me. If that’s true, then there isn’t some hidden answer here. There’s just damage.

[Decision] So I decided to stop reaching for whatever he’s trying to get me toward. It feels safer to stay with the cynicism because at least it doesn’t ask anything of me. If I let myself hope there’s a way to do this well, then I have to face how badly I’m doing it, how much I don’t know, how exposed I am. Better to keep it hard, keep it general, keep it about men and women and lawsuits and all the rest. That way I don’t have to admit I’m lost, or that I might not be able to fix this, or that maybe there’s no fixing it at all.

What puzzles me is that it doesn’t feel obviously panicked in the moment; it feels distant, almost calm, even a little affectionate in a weird way. So if it was fear, I want to know fear of what exactly — Kyle seeing the real me, me wanting him, being wanted, losing control, or maybe realizing something about the relationship that I don’t want to face.

[Decision] I decided not to let “fear” stay vague. If I’m going to understand why this happens, I need to test the possibilities instead of just accepting the label. I asked, What was I afraid of? because I want the missing piece — the thing underneath the detachment — and because if I can name what the dissociation is protecting me from, maybe I can tell whether it’s still necessary or whether it’s keeping me cut off from something I actually want.

zh.therapist_turn_zh: 关于丢工作的事，别太担心。随着疫情慢慢消退，每天都有新公司开张。你会有很多工作机会的。同样，随着你更多地与社会互动，你也会重新获得自信和社会地位。

zh.internal_zh:
<internal>
[Perception] 我听到治疗师说得好像只要我一直往前走、等着世界重新开放，事情自然会变好。这直接戳中了我的恐惧——我背着案底、工作履历毁了，整个系统都在把我筛掉。我感觉真正的障碍是背景调查、疫情，还有社会对我的评判——根本不是我不够努力。

[Decision] 所以我用“恶性循环”来反击，还指出了背景调查的问题，因为我不想让问题被简化成“再努力一点就行”。如果我把焦点放在外部障碍上，那我就不用面对过去的羞耻，也不用觉得自己什么都搞不定。这样还能保护那个相信自己是奋斗者、只是被阻碍了的我，而不是一个失败者。
</internal>

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: Do you think your mood is related to any current or recent events in your life?

context.speaker: client
context.text: Yes. To handle my previous depression I self medicated and ended up going to prison. Made my situation worse. Now trying to adjust but depression is worse having lost job and social stauts

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: Feeling down after an experience like that is certainly understandable, and I suspect that might be the main cause of your depression.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: Regarding losing your job, I wouldn't worry too much. New businesses are opening each day as the pandemic slowly goes away. You will have plenty of job opportunities. Similarly, you will also regain your confidence and social status as you interact with society more.

en_backup.therapist_turn: Regarding losing your job, I wouldn't worry too much. New businesses are opening each day as the pandemic slowly goes away. You will have plenty of job opportunities. Similarly, you will also regain your confidence and social status as you interact with society more.
en_backup.client_response: Yes, but its a vicious circle. Get blue and find it hard to strive. Unfortunately many jobs require background checks these days. Even Amazon!
en_backup.internal:
[Perception] I heard the therapist make it sound like things will naturally get better if I just keep moving and wait for the world to open back up. That lands right on the part of me that’s scared I’m stuck with a record, a ruined job history, and a system that keeps screening me out. It feels like the real obstacle is the background checks, the pandemic, and the way society judges me — not some simple lack of effort on my part.

[Decision] So I pushed back by framing it as a vicious circle and pointing to the background check issue, because I don’t want it reduced to “just try harder.” If I make it about the outside barriers, then I don’t have to sit with the shame of my past or feel blamed for not being able to fix everything. It also protects the part of me that still wants to believe I’m a striver who’s being blocked, not someone who failed himself.

What lands for me is that my sleep, food, and overall health are starting to slip, and that probably feeds back into the stress. I also notice myself framing it as something “we all go through,” which maybe means I’m trying to make sense of whether this is just a normal pandemic adjustment or whether I’m letting it become a bad pattern. The unresolved question seems to be: am I simply coping as best I can in difficult circumstances, or am I stuck in a routine that is making me worse?

[Decision] I decided to keep the conversation grounded in the practical reality of my life instead of treating it like an abstract complaint. I want to sort out what is actually caused by the pandemic and what I may be reinforcing through habit, because if I can tell those apart, then I can figure out where change is possible without feeling like I’m betraying my reasons for being careful. I’m also noticing that if I keep saying “this is just how things are,” I may avoid facing the part of me that does want things to improve. So I’m trying to examine the pattern more closely rather than defend it automatically.

And I don’t want to hand over the impression that I’m weak or that I’m accepting their version of me. At the same time, I’m not ready to say I refused it on purpose either, because that sounds too final, too much like giving up on myself.

[Decision] So I’m going to stay in this middle place for a second. I’ll say I don’t know, because that keeps me from having to choose between looking defeated and looking like I’m pretending nothing’s wrong. I need to protect my self-respect. I need to keep the door open in case there’s still a way to handle this without me having to kneel to anybody.

[Perception] 治疗师只是认可了一下情况，没逼我，这正好戳中我最烦的那部分：我并不是一直这样。今年刚开始其实还行，所以现在这个低谷更让人憋屈，因为又不是从来没起色。让我放不下的是为什么夏天之后掉得这么狠——到底是季节原因、运气不好，还是自己方法上有什么地方没及时察觉。我还注意到“圣诞节手头紧”不光是钱的问题，是年末本来希望翻盘的对比，结果没成。

</internal>

en_backup.internal:
[Perception] The therapist is just acknowledging the situation, not pushing me, and that lands on the part that’s been bothering me most: I wasn’t always in this position. The year actually started okay, which makes the current slump feel more frustrating because it’s not like I never had traction. What feels unresolved is why it dropped off so hard after summer—whether it was just the season, bad luck, or something in my approach that I didn’t catch in time. I’m also noticing that “broke for Christmas” isn’t just about money right now; it’s the end-of-year contrast I had hoped would turn around, and it didn’t.

[Decision] I’m deciding to say more than just “yeah, it’s tough,” because that doesn’t explain the real problem. I want to figure out what changed between the good start and the weak finish, since that’s the only way I can tell whether I need a small adjustment, a whole new plan, or just to accept that I need to get through a rough stretch. I’m trying to sort out whether this is a temporary dip or proof that the current setup isn’t working, because those lead to different next steps.

zh.internal_zh:
<internal>
[Perception] 他们还在陪着我聊这个，但如果我继续聊房子，我就能待在安全、想象的那部分里。治疗师大概是想让我把这事当真——去想真人真事，真的联系，可能回一封信，可能这对我意味着什么。可那触及了我根本不想面对的部分：这不只是一个奇怪的故事，这是真实的、活生生的联系，而且我不知道如果打开那扇门会怎样。

[Decision] 所以我问了房子的事，因为这样我就能在远处徘徊。我可以聊他们，却不用回答那个更大的问题，不用做选择，不用完全感受如果真回应会怎样。简短一点回答更安全，因为要是说得少，我就能控制住——控制情绪、控制节奏、控制玛莉莎可能翻我东西的可能性，或者控制我生活中熟悉的一切在我准备好之前就开始变动。我想再多琢磨一会儿。这比说“我害怕”要容易。

The therapist is probably trying to get me to make this real — to think about actual people, actual contact, maybe a letter back, maybe what this means about me. That hits the part I don’t want to face: that this isn’t just a strange story, it’s a real, living connection, and I don’t know what happens if I open that door.

[Decision] So I asked about the house because it lets me hover at a distance. I can talk about them without having to answer the bigger question, without having to choose, without having to feel the full weight of what it would mean to respond. A short answer feels safer because if I keep it brief, I can keep control — over the feelings, over the pace, over the possibility that Marisa might get into my things, or that everything I know about my life could start shifting before I’m ready. I want to stay in the wondering a little longer. It’s easier than saying I’m scared.

context_zh.speaker: client
context_zh.text: 听起来是个好建议。

context_zh.speaker: client
context_zh.text: 也许我会试试按你说的去建立信心。

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 我敢说，你一重新开始，那些东西都会回来的。有时候最难的就是开头。

context_zh.speaker: client
context_zh.text: 我觉得你说得对！

zh.therapist_turn_zh: 我敢说，你一重新开始，那些东西都会回来的。有时候最难的就是开头。
zh.client_response_zh: 你相信我吗？相信我能考好？
zh.internal_zh:
<internal>
[Perception] 她又在搞那种治疗师的一套了，说着鼓励的话，其实根本不了解我的情况。“都会回来的”感觉像是在猜，不是她真有什么依据才说的。她没见我上过微积分课，没看我卡壳的时候是什么样，也不知道我以前的B到底意味着我学得还行还是我已经落后了。所以她这么说的时候，太轻易了，好像只是在掩盖我到底有多害怕。这让我觉得，她安慰我只是因为治疗师该这么做，而不是因为她懂这事对我有多重要。

[Decision] 我问她信不信我，是因为我想要点实在的东西，不只是礼貌性的乐观。但我心里也有点抵触——靠她的信心来做决定，那算怎么回事。如果她只是随便抛点鼓励的话出来，那我还不如自己搞定。我不想把“我能不能做成”这个权力交给她。所以她的建议有用的话我就听，但我不会当她是真知道我会不会过。那是我自己要证明的事，不是她说了算的。
</internal>

context.text: There seem to be some really good online courses out there. It might be worth sending out enquiries to a number of tutors, asking them to get in touch as soon as they are free, and in the meantime working through something online to help build up your confidence?

context.speaker: therapist

context.speaker: client

en_backup.therapist_turn: I bet once you get into it again it will all come back to you. Sometimes getting started is the hardest part.
en_backup.client_response: Do you believe in me? That I will pass well?
en_backup.internal:
[Perception] She’s doing that therapist thing where she sounds encouraging without really knowing my situation. “It will all come back to you” feels like a guess, not something she actually has reason to say. She hasn’t seen me in a calculus class, hasn’t sat with me when I blank out, and she doesn’t know whether my old B means I’m fine or whether I’m already behind. So when she says it like that, it lands a little too easy, like she’s smoothing over how scared I actually am. It makes me feel like she’s being reassuring because that’s what therapists are supposed to do, not because she understands the stakes for me.

[Decision] I asked if she believes in me because I want something solid, not just polite optimism. But part of me is also bristling at the idea of leaning on her confidence like it means anything. If she’s just going to toss out generic encouragement, I might as well figure this out myself. I don’t want to hand her the power to decide whether I can do this. So I’m going to take the advice if it helps, but I’m not going to treat her as if she really knows whether I’ll pass. That’s mine to prove, not hers to announce.

en_backup.internal:
[Perception] He’s saying the silence itself matters, but he’s not giving me the exact rule for when he would step in. That lands on the part of me that wants to know the boundaries before I decide whether to risk saying something real. If I can figure out the mechanics — how long is “too long,” whether there’s a record, whether he’ll always eventually rescue the session — then I can test the room without having to jump straight into the vulnerable stuff. I’m noticing I’m more focused on the procedure than on whatever I’m actually avoiding.

[Decision] So I’m going to keep probing the edges first: ask about the longest silence, ask how he decides when to intervene, and see what he does with discomfort. I want to understand whether this is a space where I’m allowed to stall, whether he’ll tolerate it, and whether he’ll take over if I don’t. If I can map that out, then maybe I’ll know how much control I still have here before I have to say the thing I’m trying not to say.

context_zh.text: 大约三个月前

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 那时候有什么特别的事情开始发生吗？

context_zh.speaker: client
context_zh.text: 因为疫情我丢了工作，我老公不得不去干另一份活儿，我在家陪儿子上网课。

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 在史无前例的时期，那确实是艰难又煎熬的情况。不过这是暂时的，会慢慢好起来的。

context_zh.speaker: client
context_zh.text: 我不太确定，但我祈祷会好。谢谢你。

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 谁也没想到事情会变成这样，我们不得不这样做。

context_zh.speaker: client
context_zh.text: 是啊，简直疯了，但我一路祈祷着撑过去。

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 你想过跟你老公聊聊你的感受吗？

zh.therapist_turn_zh: 你想过跟你老公聊聊你的感受吗？
zh.client_response_zh: 我聊过，但我觉得他根本就不在乎，不想改变。
zh.internal_zh:
<internal>
[Perception] 感觉咨询师又把问题推回给我，好像我应该主动去表达感受、让情况变好。但我最强烈的感受是，我老公根本不在乎改变。这一点最伤人，而且现在看起来就是事实——我已经尽了全力撑着这个家，他却没有朝我迈出半步。

[Decision] 我不会把错都揽在自己身上。我已经试过沟通了，真正的问题是他没有在情感上回应我。我可以继续祈祷、继续撑，但这段婚姻不能只靠我一个人努力。如果他在乎，我就不会坐在这里觉得自己不被需要、孤零零一个人。
</internal>

en_backup.internal:
[Perception] It feels like the therapist is putting this back on me, like I should be the one to bring up feelings and make things better. But what I hear most is that my husband just doesn’t care enough to change. That’s the part that hurts and the part that seems true right now — I’m doing all I can to hold things together, and he’s the one not meeting me halfway.

[Decision] I’m not going to take all the blame for this. I’ve already tried talking, and it feels like the real problem is that he’s not showing up for me emotionally. context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 分手确实很痛苦！

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 我能问问她为什么甩了你吗？

context_zh.speaker: client
context_zh.text: 是的。而且这次分手对我打击特别大。我没胃口，也睡不好觉。

context_zh.speaker: client
context_zh.text: 她说“我们就是不合适”，听着像扯淡。我觉得她当时就出轨了。

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 听起来你挺抑郁的。不过可以理解。

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 如果她出轨了，那她也不算个好女朋友。如果她说你们不合适，我听着像是她心里有别人了。

context_zh.speaker: client
context_zh.text: 嗯，但我真的很喜欢她。我觉得也许我们就是需要更多时间。她还不够了解我。

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 虽然现在很难很孤单，但这是好事。你看起来真的很好，你值得更好的！

context_zh.speaker: client
context_zh.text: 谢谢！我也一直这么跟自己说，但我担心下一任女朋友又会这样。

zh.therapist_turn_zh: 虽然现在很难很孤单，但这是好事。你看起来真的很好，你值得更好的！
zh.client_response_zh: 谢谢！我也一直这么跟自己说，但我担心下一任女朋友又会这样。
zh.internal_zh:
<internal>
[Perception] 感觉每个人都说着正确的话——说我值得更好的，说这是最好的结局——但这些都改变不了我内心的空虚。最让我难受的是，想到我可能又要跟别人再经历一遍这一切。别人说“再相信一次”，而我只想到：万一我敞开心扉，那么在乎，然后又回到这里，孤零零的，吃不下饭，睡不着觉，拼命把自己拼回去。这让“抱有希望”这件事都变得危险。

[Decision] 所以我暂时不抱那个希望了。假设它不会成功，比抱有期待然后再次被击碎要容易得多。如果我不让自己相信下一段关系会不一样，那我就不会以同样的方式失去它。我讨厌这种挫败感，但现在放弃可能性，能保护我不再承受更多痛苦。
</internal>

en_backup.therapist_turn: as hard and lonely as it is right now, it was a good thing. yiu seem really great, and you deserve way better than that!
en_backup.client_response: Thanks! I keep telling myself that, but I'm worried that the same thing will happen with the next girlfriend.
en_backup.internal:
[Perception] It feels like everyone keeps saying the right things — that I deserve better, that this was for the best — but none of it changes how empty this feels. What hit me hardest is the idea that I could go through all of this again with someone else. I hear “just trust again” and all I can think is: what if I open up, care that much, and end up right back here, alone, not eating, not sleeping, trying to piece myself back together. It makes the whole idea of hoping feel dangerous.

[Decision] So I’m backing off from that hope for now. It feels easier to assume it won’t work out than to get my expectations up and be crushed again. If I don’t let myself believe the next relationship could be different, then I can’t really lose it the same way. I hate feeling this defeated, but right now giving up on the possibility protects me from risking more pain.

zh.therapist_turn_zh: 当然。
zh.client_response_zh: 你有没有想过……自杀？
zh.internal_zh:
<internal>
[Perception] 我听到了那个问题，它正好砸在我一直试图不去看的那个地方。其实跟吉娜没什么关系——在我脑子里，它击中了我内心一直在绕着戴维、绕着四月、绕着所有那些我试图成为那个撑住一切的人却总是太迟、做错、或无法修复我碰过的东西的部分。它让整件事变得简单又丑陋：我保护不了所有人，我无法撤销发生的事，我甚至不知道该怎么说我心里的那部分——它在想这一切有没有意义。希望现在太昂贵了。如果我允许自己渴望解脱，我就得承认自己有多疲惫和绝望。

[Decision] 所以我退缩了。我决定不去那个地方，真的不去。保持模糊比较安全，从侧面问，把问题变成“你有没有想过？”而不是说出我真正害怕对自己说的那些。如果我能保持距离，我就不用冒险让人看到我破碎，也不用相信处理这种感受还有什么用。放弃一点感觉上像是解脱——不是因为我想要这样，而是因为现在试图抱有希望只会让我觉得自己又要失败。
</internal>

context.speaker: client
context.text: Can I ask you something, Gina?

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: Sure.

en_backup.therapist_turn: Sure.
en_backup.client_response: Have you ever thought about... suicide?
en_backup.internal:
[Perception] I heard the question and felt it land right on the place I’ve been trying not to look at. It wasn’t really about Gina, not in my head — it hit the part of me that’s been circling around David, around April, around all the ways I’ve been trying to be the one who holds everything together and still ending up too late, or wrong, or unable to fix what I touched. It made the whole thing feel stripped down to something simple and ugly: I can’t protect everyone, I can’t undo what happened, and I don’t even know how to talk about the part of me that wonders if any of this matters. Hope feels expensive right now. If I let myself want relief, I have to admit how exhausted and hopeless I am.

[Decision] So I pulled back. I decided not to go there, not really. It feels safer to stay vague, to ask it sideways, to make it about “have you ever thought about it?” instead of saying what I’m actually afraid to say about myself. If I keep it at a distance, I don’t have to risk being seen as broken, or have to believe there’s anything useful to do with this feeling anyway. Giving up a little felt like relief — not because I want this, but because trying to hold hope right now just feels like setting myself up to fail again.

en_backup.therapist_turn: I am so sorry to hear that. I understand, things can be tough sometimes.
en_backup.client_response: I don't know how to be happy
en_backup.internal:
[Perception] They heard me say I feel hopeless, but what I really took from it was that they were being gentle because they don’t have anything concrete to offer. “Things can be tough sometimes” just landed like a soft, distant acknowledgment of something that has already gone too far. It hit the part of me that feels exhausted by trying to imagine a better life and finding nothing there. The whole idea of learning how to be happy feels impossible, almost childish, like I’m being asked to build a bridge with no materials. 

[Decision] I decided to stop reaching for an answer because it only makes the emptiness feel sharper. If I keep hoping, I’ll just have to face the fact that nothing changes and I still can’t make myself into someone who wants to live. So I said I don’t know how to be happy, because that feels truer than pretending I can figure it out. Giving up on trying protects me from the humiliation of failing at even the simplest thing: feeling okay. It’s easier to stay with the bleakness I understand than to risk believing in something that probably isn’t there.

[Decision] I decided to answer directly instead of just going along with small talk because I need support, not a performance. Saying “I just need someone to listen to me” is me trying to make room for my own feelings without having to explain everything all at once. Then I asked how she is almost automatically, because that’s my habit, but the real request was already there: please stay with me and let me talk.

en_backup.therapist_turn: Does this feel like a nightmare... Having to sit here with me now?

en_backup.internal:
[Perception] He heard the “nightmare” part and pushed it right back at me: is this what it feels like with me now? That hit the exact thing I was trying not to let in — that I’m sitting here, exposed, being looked at, and I don’t really know what to do with that. I also noticed he didn’t let me escape into the shaman story or the work excuse. He brought it back to me, to this room, which is exactly what makes me bristle and also why Patricia said he was good.

[Decision] So I softened it on purpose. I didn’t want to sound like I was bolting, but I also didn’t want to admit outright that I was feeling cornered. “Not a nightmare” gave me some room, and “vague anxiety dream” kept it from sounding too dramatic. Then I added that Patricia was right and he’s easy to talk to because I was asking, without exactly asking, for him to stay easy. I was basically saying: keep going, but don’t pin me down too hard. I need this to feel less like interrogation and more like conversation, or I’m going to shut down.

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 当然！我每次锻炼完都倒头就睡。但你要是做不到，简单点也行，比如每天晚上同一时间关掉所有灯，躺在床上，这会有帮助。能调节你的生物钟！

zh.therapist_turn_zh: 当然！我每次锻炼完都倒头就睡。但你要是做不到，简单点也行，比如每天晚上同一时间关掉所有灯，躺在床上，这会有帮助。能调节你的生物钟！

zh.internal_zh:
<internal>

[Decision] 我不会假装那些泛泛的建议就是答案，我的心思卡在一种真实威胁感上。我必须继续说到底是什么让我睡不着，因为如果让对话滑向常规的自我照顾，就好像我在无视危险。我想要帮助改善睡眠，但不是通过假装这种担忧不理性，或者光靠改变习惯就能洗掉它。
</internal>

context.speaker: therapist

context.text: Thanks!  What other ideas do you have?

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: Of course! I always knock right out after a workout. But if you aren't able to, just simple things like turning all the lights off at the same time every night and laying in bed will help. It will align your circadian rhythm!

en_backup.therapist_turn: Of course! I always knock right out after a workout. But if you aren't able to, just simple things like turning all the lights off at the same time every night and laying in bed will help. It will align your circadian rhythm!
en_backup.client_response: Great, but I wake up frequently thinking about the recent events surrounding police and how they treat black people.
en_backup.internal:
[Perception] I heard the suggestions about water, vegetables, meditation, workouts, and turning the lights off, but none of that touched the real reason I’m not sleeping. What’s in my mind is the fear and anger that keep coming back when I think about police and Black men in my family, especially my son. That feels urgent and bigger than sleep habits. It hit the part of me that stays on guard because I don’t feel like I can afford to relax.

[Decision] I’m not going to pretend those general tips are the answer when my mind is stuck on something that feels like a real threat. I need to keep saying what’s actually keeping me up, because if I let the conversation drift to routine self-care, it feels like I’m ignoring the danger. I want help with sleep, but not by acting like the worry is irrational or can just be washed away with a habit change.

[Perception] I heard the therapist reading back a version of me that sounds polished and almost too neat: “impressive,” “sensitive,” “mature,” “intelligent,” “highly independent.” That hit the exact place I’m always watching — whether people are actually seeing me, or just making something up that sounds good on paper. The part that stayed unresolved was whether those words are real observations or just the kind of thing adults say when they want to be reassuring. And if they are real, what exactly did she see that I didn’t mean to show? The accident, my mom, the fact that I’m not just fine? I also heard her leave out the messy part, which makes me wonder if she doesn’t know it, or if she does and just didn’t say it out loud.

[Decision] I decided to ask directly because I need to know whether she actually means it. If she says yes, then maybe she’s really paying attention and I can decide whether to trust that. If she hesitates, then I’ll know to be careful and not hand over too much. I’m trying to figure out whether this is a place where I can be understood without being treated like I’m fragile. And I said the thing about my mom because I wanted to test whether I’d get pushed, or whether I could mention it and still stay in control. Saying “Do you really think those things you wrote?” is my way of checking if she’s being honest with me before I let myself believe any of it.

[Perception] He’s asking me to go back toward the part of me that broke, the part that didn’t hold up when everything got too much. He talks like there’s something living back there that can be found and repaired, but all I hear is the same old thing: open the door, look at the wreckage, and call it healing. I don’t see how digging around in that darkness changes anything. If that part of me fell apart once, what makes anyone think it’s suddenly going to come together now? It feels like being asked to stare at what was ruined and pretend it still matters.

[Decision] I’m not going to pretend I can just reach into that and make it whole. I can’t afford to believe in something that might not exist, or that might only leave me worse off. Better to keep my distance, keep it where it is, and not set myself up for hoping this will fix what never got fixed. If I don’t go there, then at least I’m not watching it fail all over again.

en_backup.internal:
[Perception] I hear the therapist noticing that I’m hurt, but their question is framing this mostly as “he didn’t tell you.” That lands on the practical betrayal, but it also misses the bigger thing I’m wrestling with: even if he had told me, I still would’ve been hurt, because then I’d have to face that the relationship I thought was still in limbo was already moving on without me. What feels unresolved is how to square two versions of him — the person I believed was honest and decent, and the person who can look me in the eye and say one thing while doing another. I’m also trying to figure out what I’m supposed to do with his lack of accountability. If he won’t acknowledge that I’m entitled to be hurt, do I keep explaining it, keep hoping he’ll “get it,” or do I accept that I may never get validation from him?

[Decision] I decided I need to stop trying to solve this by getting him to agree with my perspective, because that keeps me stuck in the same argument. I’m thinking I may need to focus on what his behavior means for my next move: whether this “sort of” breakup is actually over, whether continued contact is helping or just prolonging the damage, and whether I can protect myself even if he never takes responsibility. I don’t want to let go of the relationship, but I also can’t keep building on a version of him that his actions are contradicting. So the question I’m trying to answer is: what boundaries make sense if I can’t count on honesty or accountability from him?

zh.client_response_zh: 没，手机没电了，所以我得先打回去，然后再挂断。能借你手机用一下吗？求你了，就两分钟。我根本没法集中注意力。她不能占最后一句话，保罗。我不能死，她却能继续活下去，和唯一我爱过的人过上完美生活。
zh.internal_zh:
<internal>
[Perception] 他还是没明白。他以为这只是个抽象误会，但他那句话戳到了我感觉被逼到墙角、被暴露的地方。凯尔故意告诉她。西耶娜打电话意味着他们联手了，如果我接，就会失去仅存的一点控制。我快崩溃了，因为我现在就需要做点什么，而不是坐在这里解释为什么受不了。我无法集中注意力，我能感觉到她已经“赢了”，除非我阻止她。

[Decision] 我提出要用电话，因为我需要立刻行动，而不是被继续盘问。我要打回去，亲自结束这件事，这样我就不至于坐在这里毫无还手之力，让他们占最后一句话。把话说清楚是唯一能让我把事情变得具体的方法。如果我直接说出我需要什么，也许他就不会试图说服我放弃，而是让我去做。
</internal>

[Decision] I asked to use the phone because I need immediate action, not more probing. I want to call her back and end it myself so I’m not just sitting here powerless while they get the last word. Saying it plainly is the only way I can force this into something concrete. If I say what I need directly, maybe he’ll stop trying to talk me out of it and just let me do it.

If I let this become a story about losing interest, then I’m admitting the thing that held me together is slipping away too.

[Decision] No. I’m not going to go there with him. I’m not going to treat this like some clean, healthy letting-go when it feels like losing the only safe thing I ever had. He can ask all he wants, but I’m drawing the line here: I’m not giving up gymnastics as the center of who I am just because he thinks I should “explore” it. If I name it, it gets real, and if it gets real, then I have to face what it cost me to need it this much. I won’t do that right now.

context.text: I work a dead end job with no potential and it is depressing being there for 9 hours a day. Thats why I am on here instead of working.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: That sounds really exhausting. You work longer hours than a normal job and must feel really burned out.

context.speaker: client
context.text: Yeah the burn out isn't the worst I experienced. I previously worked jobs that I was at for 12 hours a day but they were more rewarding.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: You are definitely a hard worker and I hope you know that. You make a great employee puttin in som many hours.

en_backup.therapist_turn: You are definitely a hard worker and I hope you know that. You make a great employee puttin in som many hours.
en_backup.client_response: I am there for 9 hours. I probably only work for 1 hour a day. The rest of the time I am killing time.
en_backup.internal:
[Perception] He’s making it sound like I’m under a huge amount of strain, but that’s not really what this is. Yeah, the job is boring and depressing, but it’s not like I’m drowning in work or barely surviving it. I’m mostly just sitting there killing time. The “burned out” thing feels exaggerated, because compared to the 12-hour jobs I had before, this is pretty manageable. The part it hits is the idea that I’m in some serious crisis — I’m not.

[Decision] I’m going to keep it in perspective and not make this into a bigger problem than it is. If I tell myself it’s severe, then I’ll feel pressured to do something drastic, and I don’t want that. Right now the safest move is to treat it as an annoying but tolerable situation and just get through the day. It’s not ideal, but it’s not enough of a disaster to justify shaking up everything.

context.speaker: client
context.text: The boys used to spy on me the same way... when I worked on weekends. They'd want to play or... go swimming, and... I always had work to do. I probably gave them the same look. Maybe that's why we don't have anything to talk about now.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: You know, it's not too late for you to get to know them and for them to get to know you.

en_backup.therapist_turn: You know, it's not too late for you to get to know them and for them to get to know you.
en_backup.client_response: I don't think they'd be interested.
en_backup.internal:
[Perception] He’s trying to tell me it can still be fixed, like all I have to do is reach out and they’ll want me. But that hits the worst part: if I go there and they don’t care, then it means I really did the same thing my father did. It means this distance isn’t just bad luck or work or timing — it’s me. And I can’t sit with that right now. I can’t hand him that kind of truth, and I can’t pretend I believe it.

[Decision] So I shut it down. “I don’t think they’d be interested” feels safer than letting him talk me into hoping. If I agree with him, I have to want something I may not get, and then I’d have to feel the rejection all over again. Better to keep it where it is than reach for my boys and find out they don’t want me.

context.speaker: client
context.text: Yes, but my whole life was upended. My living situation, my friend circle is broken up over this. I don't know how to move on. Any suggestions?

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: Getting over a breakup will take time? Have you ever heard of DABDA? Denial (I can't believe this happened!) Anger (we all know that) Bargaining (If only I had done that, or if only - trying to make it FEEL better by imagining other scenarios - doesn't really work) Depression - sadness, then Acceptance -- we go in and out of these emotions and sometimes it can make us feel crazy, but all of them are normal in varying degrees and we don't know when they will happen.

context.speaker: client
context.text: No, but those sound like the typical stages of grief. I guess I'm in anger. I have no interest in barbagining.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: I would make a list of things you have always wanted to do and then just BRAINSTORM any idea, no idea is too out there -- learn to ice skate, learn to play the ukulele, sign up for dance lessons, join the gym, go to a singles group at church, visit the elderly, volunteer somewhere.

context.speaker: client
context.text: I think I need to focus on exercise. Just get my body and mind healthy and full of energy. What do you think?

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: I also find it helpful not only to limit how much I dwell on my pain, but make sure I reach out to help someone else. I will tell you, that is the secret to happiness. Maybe help a neighbor with groceries or hanging lights. Old people (me) love help, bake something or call your aunt or uncle.

context.speaker: client
context.text: True, but it's hard not to dwell. It's not like I have a choice. It overcomes me.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: I agree, get healthy and try to help others. One thing about feelings is that if you change your mind, you can change your feelings, it might happen slowly, but if you put your mind off of it, it will help. Not saying NEVER feel the emotions, but feelings are the tail of the dog, not the dog itself, You do not have to be ruled by them. You don not have to FEEL like going for a walk to go for a walk.

en_backup.internal:
[Perception] They keep talking like this is something I can just manage with the right list, the right mindset, the right walk, the right helping-other-people routine. But what I hear is how far away that feels from where I am. My whole life got broken apart — my home, my people, my sense of who I was — and “just go for a walk” lands like they don’t really get how heavy this is. The booze and weed are the only things that seem like they can turn the volume down, even for a little while. Staying numb feels safer than sitting there and hoping for some better version of me that might not show up.

[Decision] So I’m probably going to do the thing that shuts this off fastest, because I don’t have it in me to try and fail at being healthy right now. If I don’t reach for anything, I have to feel how wrecked and alone I am, and I don’t want to open that door. Giving up on the “fix it” advice protects me from getting my hopes up and then feeling stupid when it doesn’t change anything. Right now, numb is easier than hopeful.

[Perception] 他在把我的问题定义成我的边界、我的越界，好像核心问题是我想要对亚历克斯的生命拥有过多权威。但事实不是这样。亚历克斯把我放到了那个位置上。他直接问我他该不该飞，然后让我承担这个决定的分量。真正的问题是，他到底还是飞了，海军也没能保护他不受他自己的伤害。我能看出治疗师想把责任推到我角色上，但真正沉重的是，我未能使用我剩下的唯一正式渠道。
[Decision] 我需要把责备转移到该去的地方：亚历克斯的选择、他的冒险，以及那个没有干预的制度。如果我一直揽在自己身上，我会被‘我本该掌控无法掌控之事’这个念头压垮。所以我告诉自己，我本该提交那份评估，因为那至少让失败变成程序性的而不是道德性的。那是一个更安全的真实：我漏了一步。我没有杀他。
</internal>

context.speaker: client
context.text: He gave me the chance to stop him from flying.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: Literally? Did he really offer that or are you projecting?

context.speaker: client
context.text: He asked me directly, Should I fly?

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: What did you say?

context.speaker: client
context.text: I told him I was very concerned about his... About his state of mind.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: You said that clearly?

context.speaker: client
context.text: But he wanted me to say it unequivocally. Do not fly.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: It's not your place, Paul. A patient can't ask you to take his life into your hands. It's not your place to say; Don't fly. Anymore than it's your place to say to that couple, Have an abortion. Or to Laura, Marry or don't marry your fiancé.

en_backup.therapist_turn: It's not your place, Paul. A patient can't ask you to take his life into your hands. It's not your place to say; Don't fly. Anymore than it's your place to say to that couple, Have an abortion. Or to Laura, Marry or don't marry your fiancé.
en_backup.client_response: I should have sent the Navy an evaluation. Guilt-ridden. Wants to punish himself. Shouldn't fly.
en_backup.internal:
[Perception] He’s making this about my limits, my overreach, as if the central issue is that I wanted too much authority over Alex’s life. But that isn’t what happened. Alex put me in that position. He asked me directly whether he should fly, and then left me to carry the weight of the decision. The real problem is that he flew anyway, and the Navy didn’t protect him from himself. I can see the therapist trying to pin this on my role, but what landed was that I failed to use the one formal channel I had left.

[Decision] I need to move the blame outward to where it belongs: Alex’s choice, his risk-taking, and the institution that didn’t intervene. If I keep this on me, I’ll be crushed under the idea that I was supposed to control the uncontrollable. So I’m telling myself I should have sent the evaluation, because that at least makes the failure procedural instead of moral. That’s the safer truth: I missed a step. I didn’t kill him.

context_zh.speaker: client
context_zh.text: 这是社区卫生项目。是论文不是考试。而且是小组作业。我们已经在收容所里实施了一个课程好几个月了，正在衡量这个项目对成年男性群体的成效。

context_zh.speaker: client
context_zh.text: 而且我们一直在找研究文献来支持我们的项目。

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 论文压力很大，尤其是小组作业。我读研究生的时候，72小时内要完成4篇不同主题的全篇论文。

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 你觉得你在找必要信息上有进展吗？

context_zh.speaker: client
context_zh.text: 是的，我明白压力大。对，我们有进展。

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 我相信只要每个人都努力，你们论文会成功的。有什么我能帮忙的吗？

context_zh.speaker: client
context_zh.text: 我受不了小组合作，因为总有人不干活，最后都是我兜底。一想到这个我就特别焦虑。

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 我看得出你很焦虑，小组项目确实很难。也许你们可以一起制定个计划，分配任务，确保每个人都承担自己那份工作？你考虑过这个吗？

zh.therapist_turn_zh: 我看得出你很焦虑，小组项目确实很难。也许你们可以一起制定个计划，分配任务，确保每个人都承担自己那份工作？你考虑过这个吗？
zh.client_response_zh: 是啊，我试过了。但还是有人不按计划来。
zh.internal_zh:
<internal>
[Perception] 她表现得好像问题只是我们需要一个更好的计划，好像只要大家都组织好了就一切顺利。但让我觉得被困住的根本不是这个。我已经试过分配任务了，结果还是有人不执行，最后又落到我头上。如果我顺着她的话说，就好像我在假装一切尽在掌控，可我知道最后兜底的人还是我。

[Decision] 我不会再附和另一个忽略实际情况的简单解决方案了。我已经试过了，结果还是我一个人焦虑、收拾烂摊子。在我考虑其他任何事之前，我需要她明白这不只是计划的问题。
</internal>

context.speaker: client
context.text: It's community health. It's a paper not a test. And it's a group project. We have been implementing a class in a homeless shelter for months and we are measuring the success on that implementation for the adult male population.

context.speaker: client
context.text: And we have been finding research articles to support our project.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: Papers can be very stressful, especially when it is a group project. When I went to graduate school I had to complete 4 full papers on different subjects in 72 hours.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: Do you feel like you've made progress in finding the necessary information?

context.speaker: client
context.text: Yes I understand it's stressful. And yes we've made progress.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: I'm sure that if everyone puts in the effort, you will all be successful with your paper.  Is there anything I can do to help?

context.speaker: client
context.text: I can't stand working in groups because there is always someone who doesn't pull their own weight and it usually falls on me to make up for it. I just get so stressed out every time I think about it.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: I can tell you're stressed about it and group projects are very hard.  Perhaps you can all put a plan together an allocate tasks to make sure that everyone puts in their share of the work? Is that something you've considered?

en_backup.therapist_turn: I can tell you're stressed about it and group projects are very hard.  Perhaps you can all put a plan together an allocate tasks to make sure that everyone puts in their share of the work? Is that something you've considered?
en_backup.client_response: Yes. I've done that. But still have people who don't seem to stick to the plan.
en_backup.internal:
[Perception] She’s acting like the problem is just that we need a better plan, like if everyone is organized enough then it’ll all work out. But that’s not the part that’s making me feel trapped. I’ve already done the allocating-tasks thing, and it still ends up on me when people don’t follow through. If I just agree with her, it feels like I’m pretending this is under control when I know I’m the one who gets stuck carrying it.

[Decision] I’m not going to nod along to another simple solution that ignores what actually happens. I’ve already tried it, and I’m still the one left stressed and picking up the slack. I need her to understand that this isn’t just a planning issue before I even think about anything else.

en_backup.therapist_turn: Have you ever talked to your friends about this? Have you expressed how it made you feel?

en_backup.internal:
[Perception] What I took from the therapist was that the problem might be that I’m not speaking up, but what hit me more was the feeling that I keep getting let down by people I thought I could trust. They say it’s “just joking,” but it still lands as judgment and makes me feel like I’m the one being picked on. It feels like my friends are the ones creating the hurt, not me.

[Decision] I’m deciding that if I keep hanging around them, I need to be careful and not assume they’ll suddenly be different on their own. The issue is really how they’re treating me, so if anything changes, it has to come from them too. I don’t want to be the only one trying to fix something they’re causing. For now, I’ll keep my guard up and see whether they can actually be supportive before I risk opening up too much.

context_zh.speaker: client
context_zh.text: 韦斯顿先生，你有儿子吗？

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 有的。

zh.therapist_turn_zh: 有的。
zh.client_response_zh: 那如果是另一个人，一个来自不同文化的人，每周都给他提建议……建议你心里清楚会对你儿子有害……你会怎么做？
zh.internal_zh:
<internal>
[Perception] 他说他有儿子，所以他不是坐在那儿跟我保持距离、光会评判我的人。我在试探他，看他会不会像我保护亚历克斯一样保护自己的孩子。戳中我的地方在于，有人能把“建议”说成“帮助”，但实际上那东西越帮越糟，还指望我因为那是专家说的、或者来自一个跟我不同的文化、我就得站在旁边看着。我想看看他是不是真的明白，一个父亲不能只看话本身——他得看话带来的后果。

[Decision] 我要逼他做这个对比，因为我要一个直截了当的回答，不是那种包装好的。如果他能告诉我他会为自己的儿子怎么做，那我就能知道他对我儿子是不是公平。我也在逼着他把问题摆到台面上，因为我不相信那个观念——别人管它叫治疗、我就该一直接受那些看起来有害的建议。我需要他的回答能表明他理解我为什么反抗，而不是光叫我要开放点。
</internal>

context.speaker: client
context.text: Do you have a son, Mr. Weston?

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: Yes, I do.

en_backup.therapist_turn: Yes, I do.
en_backup.client_response: And if another man, someone from a different culture, started giving him advice... Every week... Advice that you were pretty sure would be harmful to your son... What would you do?
en_backup.internal:
[Perception] He says he has a son, so he’s not just sitting there judging me from a distance. I’m trying to test whether he’d protect his own child the way I’m trying to protect Alex. The part that hits is the fear that somebody can call advice “help” when it’s actually making things worse, and then expect me to stand by and watch it because it comes from an expert or from some culture that sounds different from mine. I’m trying to understand whether he really gets that a father has to judge more than the words — he has to judge the effect.

[Decision] I’m going to press him into the comparison because I want a plain answer, not a polished one. If he can tell me what he would do for his own son, then maybe I can see whether he’s being fair to mine. I’m also trying to force the issue because I don’t trust the idea that I should just keep accepting advice that looks harmful while somebody else calls it therapy. I need him to answer in a way that shows he understands why I’m resisting, not just telling me to be open-minded.

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 那专业心理咨询呢？有些组织会提供一定次数的免费咨询。

zh.internal_zh:

[Perception] 我听到治疗师试图让我不感到那么孤独，还提到了实际帮助。真正戳中我的是我感到多么被困住：我确实有可能会关心我的朋友，但我害怕成为“负担太多的人”，而且我厌倦了成为别人想到我时就联想到的那个悲伤的人。当他们提到专业治疗时，感觉好像真的有一条前进的路，而不是我一直在为成为负担道歉。住在乡下这一点也很重要，因为在这里获得帮助并不简单。

[Decision] 我决定说出我已经在排队了，因为我想诚实，也想表明我确实想要帮助。我有点像是在寻求建议，但又不必完全开口，因为我不习惯直接说“我需要支持”——那对我来说很自私。但我确实想让治疗师明白我在努力，而且我需要一些实际可行的东西，比如短信或视频，因为我住的地方面对面咨询的选择很有限。
</internal>

[Perception] I heard the therapist trying to move me toward not feeling so alone in this, and also toward practical help. The part that hit was how stuck I feel: I do have friends who would probably care, but I’m scared of being “too much,” and I’m tired of being the sad one people think of when they think of me. When they mentioned professional therapy, it felt like maybe there was an actual path forward instead of me just apologizing for being a burden. The rural part matters too, because getting help here doesn’t feel simple.

[Decision] I decided to say that I’m already on a waiting list, because I wanted to be honest and also signal that I do want help. I was kind of asking for ideas without having to fully ask, because I’m not used to directly saying “I need support” — that feels selfish to me. But I did want the therapist to understand that I’m trying, and that I need something realistic, like maybe text or video, since in-person options feel limited where I live.

[Perception] She’s making it plain: saying it out loud is awful, but not saying it is worse. And I can hear that she means me — that this is not about some abstract daughter, it’s about me being the one who has cancer and has to tell my mother. It hits the part of me that wants to be the good daughter, the one who doesn’t drop something unbearable into her mother’s life. It also hits the part that knows this is real and can’t be postponed forever.

[Decision] I’m not saying no. I can’t quite do that, because I know she’s right in some terrible way. But I also can’t let myself commit, because if I do, I have to step straight into the horror of it. So I stay on the edge — agreeing in theory, holding back in practice — because that lets me protect my mother from hearing it, and protect myself from having to become the person who says it.
