[Perception] She’s acting like this is mostly about organizing the work better or making the case clearer, and honestly that makes it sound more manageable than it feels. Yeah, the workload is annoying and my manager is dismissive, but maybe it’s not some huge crisis — just a stressful project with a bad supervisor. If I keep framing it as a work issue instead of a bigger problem, I don’t have to face how stuck I feel or how much this is affecting me.

[Decision] I’m going to keep it in the “just deal with this project” box for now. I’ll stay practical, send the spreadsheet, maybe mention it again if needed, but I’m not going to make a big thing out of it or act like everything is falling apart. It feels safer to treat it as manageable, because if I admit how serious it is, then I’d have to do something bigger that I’m not ready for.

[Decision] So I pull back. I decide not to fully hope in any direction, because hoping would mean risking proof that I can’t follow through. If I stay uncertain, at least I’m not trapped by a choice or embarrassed by failing at it. It feels safer to keep everything provisional than to commit and discover I really am someone who can’t make a life out of anything. Maybe that’s all I can do right now — not choose, not trust, just wait and keep myself from being wrong in a way that would hurt too much.

context_zh.speaker: client

context.text: So you shared that you're, um, here today because you're having some dissatisfaction with your body and your confidence and your mood and your energy. Um, but first, I'd love to hear what are your philosophies about health and wellbeing?

context.speaker: client
context.text: Um, I definitely, uh, you know, I-I strive to be physically healthy, but I also have in my life seeing how that impacts me mentally. Um, so I think if I'm- if I'm able to do the things that I wanna do and, um, you know, that I'm feeling good about where I'm at mentally, then that's kind of my end goal, always. Um, yeah, so this body dissatisfaction piece has really just kinda thrown a wrench in that and it's been enough of a challenge that I thought I should seek out someone who can really help me through that piece.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: Yeah. Well, I'm so glad that you reached out for help, um, and just know that you're not alone. And-and so, yeah, is that okay if I share a little bit about, um, how I tend to work with clients on that topic?

context.speaker: client
context.text: Yes, please.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: Yeah. Well, um, first of all, I really am passionate about looking at the whole picture, um, physical health and emotional wellbeing and what I found in working with clients in the past is when, um, we make a focus of weight loss, sometimes, uh, physical health improves, but at the cost of emotional wellbeing.

context.speaker: client
context.text: Mm-hmm.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: Um, many people find that when then- when they are restricting their intake or starting some, uh, ac-activity patterns that are really rigorous, that, um, a piece of their mental health suffers because they start to obsess, um, more than they'd like to be about those things. So, my approach with clients is just a more holistic approach. Looking at certainly some behavior changes that you could make to be more physically active, improve your energy levels.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: Um, and also look at activities that enhance your mood. We can also take a look at some dietary patterns and see if-if there are ways you could tweak how you're fueling your body throughout the day, but at the same time, sort of letting go of what happens on the scale. Letting go of, um, the final, you know, weight outcome of that, and really focusing instead on healing your relationship with food and also adopting sustainable physical activity patterns. What do you make of all that?

A set meal plan feels like something concrete I can follow, and I’m worried that without that I’ll lose control or not know what I’m supposed to do. I also heard the part about not getting too focused on the scale, and honestly that makes me feel a little uneasy, because the scale is still the part I’m most attached to.

[Decision] So I went with a question about a meal plan because it lets me test where this approach is going without fully agreeing to it yet. I’m trying not to say too much about how strongly I want weight loss, because I don’t want to get into a back-and-forth or feel judged for it. zh.internal_zh:
<internal>
[Perception] 他们把这孤独和不出门说得像是天大的紧急情况，但对我来说更像是一个可以应付的暂时阶段。是的，我感到孤单，工作比之前更重，但那不代表现在有什么糟糕的事发生。出门的风险仍然比待在家里的不适要大，所以我告诉自己我是小心，不是被困住。

[Decision] 我会继续做目前最安全的事——待在家里，用娱乐和做饭分散注意力，度过这段时间。我不需要在情况还不确定的时候做大的改变或强迫自己社交。我可以小范围地处理孤独和工作压力，不用反应过度。
</internal>

context.speaker: therapist

context.text: i have lot of colleagues and friends. to the best of my knowledge, i don't think that the people who are healthy will die.

context.text: I have found that being in isolation lowers my immunity, and if I want to be healthy, fresh air, loving friends, exercise, good healthy food is the way to do it, not isolation and loneliness. Yes, I feel alone and work is heavier than before, but that doesn’t mean something terrible is happening right now. The risk of going out still feels bigger than the discomfort of staying in, so I can tell myself I’m being careful, not stuck.

[Decision] I’ll keep doing what feels safest for now — stay home, distract myself with entertainment and cooking, and just get through this period. I don’t need to make a big change or force social plans when the situation is still uncertain. I can handle the loneliness and work stress in small ways without overreacting.

If I’m being honest, it also hit the part that feels exposed when I don’t know the expectations. Saying “I’m a customer” was my way of putting a frame around it—reminding both of us that this is supposed to have boundaries, a process, and some accountability.

[Decision] I decided to say it out loud instead of pretending I was fine with the vagueness. If he won’t define the rules, then I will at least define the relationship as a transaction for now. That keeps me in control and prevents me from having to admit that I’m not comfortable just walking in here and being open-endedly seen. So I named the customer role because it’s safer, and because I want to see whether he can handle that before I decide how much of myself to actually bring into this.

[Decision] So I ask him straight whether he believes it, because if he doesn’t, then at least we’re both standing in the same dark. If he does, maybe he’s just feeding me lines. en_backup.internal:
[Perception] The therapist is telling me to do yoga, but I don’t really know how that would help with the pain, the sleeplessness, or the feeling that everyone is talking about me. [Decision] I decided to ask how yoga helps because I want a real explanation, not just another vague answer. If I understand why it might work, I can tell whether it’s actually useful for me. I’m trying to get practical guidance for my sleep and stress, since I’m too upset to figure this out on my own right now.

What lands hardest is the implied accusation that if I feel anything at all, I’m already in the wrong. That hits my autonomy, my competence, and the way I see myself as a therapist who doesn’t turn every feeling into a mandate.

[Decision] I’m not going to hand her that opening. I’m going to shut this down before she turns it into a moral verdict on me or my work. I need to protect my professionalism, keep the focus on my judgment rather than my feelings, and refuse the premise that attraction automatically means I have to surrender my role. If I let her keep pressing, she gets to define the terms — and I’m not giving her that.

zh.therapist_turn_zh: 所以我想你俩都在同一条……同一条船上，可以这么说。

zh.internal_zh:

[Decision] 所以我就直接同意了。“绝对。”我不想让这一刻变成什么沉重的告白，但也想承认，没错，我们都在做同样的尴尬、有点羞愧的舞蹈——装成没事人一样。如果我直说出来，也许这事儿就没那么沉重了。也许它就是个事实，而不是我在保护的一个秘密弱点。

context.text: You know what a life coach is. They give advice. It's not... Look, people don't have families anymore that they can talk to, and friends are quickly going the way of families. So if you were Mia's life coach, what would you tell her to do? I would tell her to quit her job. I would tell her to grow her hair, I would tell her to move somewhere where she's outside in the sunshine, like Napa Valley. I would tell her to take up biking, not wear heels for a year. And I'd tell her, Get a dog.

context.speaker: therapist
context.text: Do you think that she would take your advice?

en_backup.therapist_turn: Do you think that she would take your advice?
en_backup.client_response: She just wants me to give her love and support.
en_backup.internal:
[Perception] What I hear is that they’re asking whether any of this actually changes anything, whether Mia would really do what I tell her. And it lands on the part I don’t want to look at: that maybe I’m not helping in the way I keep telling myself I am. Maybe I’m just handing out instructions to fill the silence. Maybe “love and support” is all she can take because there’s nowhere else for her to go, and that means my advice doesn’t actually matter as much as I want it to.

[Decision] So I’m done arguing the point. I’m going to let it be what it is and stop pretending I can fix people by telling them what to do. If she wants support, that’s what she gets. If she wants to leave, she’ll leave. If I keep reaching for some bigger outcome, I’m just setting myself up to be disappointed again. It’s easier to just step back and stop hoping my advice will change anything.

context_zh.text: 我感觉我什么都抓不住了

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 好，我明白。你想聊聊为什么会有这种感觉吗？

context_zh.speaker: client
context_zh.text: 我另一半那么拼命工作，我总觉得自己不够好，怕他会直接走人

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 我想让你知道，你不是一个人。我之前也经历过一段很难的时候。

context_zh.speaker: client
context_zh.text: 而且我们还流产了小柔，不到五个月又流了一对双胞胎，这根本帮不了什么

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 说出来会好受些。我很抱歉。把情绪说出来会帮你去掉一些负担。

context_zh.speaker: client
context_zh.text: 人们是怎么从流产里走出来的？

context_zh.speaker: therapist
context_zh.text: 最终一切都会好起来的。你只需要积极想，活下去。上帝对你的双胞胎另有安排。上帝想让他们成为你的两位天使。

zh.therapist_turn_zh: 最终一切都会好起来的。你只需要积极想，活下去。上帝对你的双胞胎另有安排。上帝想让他们成为你的两位天使。
zh.client_response_zh: 我知道这就是命该如此，但一想到我们现在的这个孩子也可能保不住，我就疼得不行
zh.internal_zh:
<internal>
[Perception] 我听到的都是人们不知道还能说什么时才会说的那套话——积极想，会好起来的，上帝有安排。没有一句能真正碰触到我现在正在经历的东西。它戳中了我心里已经害怕得不行的那部分——怕这个孩子也会流产，怕我不得不在还没从之前的失去中恢复过来时再扛一次。也戳中了另一部分——觉得自己对不起伴侣，因为我没法稳定、没法有用、没法坚强，而他们那么拼命为我们付出。这一切都让我觉得自己更渺小了，好像说再多也没用，我爱的每一样东西随时都会被夺走。

[Decision] 所以我决定暂时不去够那个希望。希望太危险了，每次我让自己相信事情可能会好，最后都被摔得粉碎。如果我不期待任何好事，也许最坏的结果来临时，就不会那么痛。我知道这意味着我在封闭自己，但这比敞开心扉去冒险再次失去这个孩子、失去伴侣、失去剩下的那点我，要安全得多。
</internal>

en_backup.therapist_turn: in the end things will work out. you just have to think positive and live. God had other plans for your twins. god wanted them to be your two angels

en_backup.internal:
[Perception] I heard the same kind of words that people always say when they don’t know what else to offer — think positive, it will work out, God has a plan. None of that touches what I’m actually living with. It hit the part of me that is already terrified that this pregnancy could end too, and that I’ll have to survive another loss on top of the ones I still haven’t recovered from. It also hit the part of me that feels like I’m failing my partner because I can’t be steady, useful, or strong when they work so hard for us. All of it just makes me feel smaller, like no amount of talking will change the fact that everything I love can still be taken away.

[Decision] So I decided to stop reaching for hope for now. Hope feels dangerous because every time I let myself believe things might be okay, I end up shattered again. If I don’t expect anything good, maybe it will hurt less if the worst happens. I know that means I’m shutting down, but it feels safer than opening my heart and risking losing this baby, my partner, and whatever is left of me all at once.
